## ABV
id="mc-main-content">
ABV
ABV contains assay troubleshooting data for these runs:
- Good Run
- Invalid Run ebl Flags
- Invalid Run FLSOR Flags
- Invalid Run Due to 'cce,p' Flag on Calibrators
Good Run
Invalid Run ebl Flags
Recommendations for Invalid run ebl flags :
Technical Support: dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
FSE instructions:
- Perform RTF measurements RTF2 range = 10-600. This can be done with and without MTU over the RTF.
- Remove Amp incubator’s shield underneath the incubator.
- Remove RTF 2. Check lens for debris. If there is debris, confirm what it is (i.e. glove, from incubator).
- Photograph debris, bag and send it back to us if possible.
- * Measure RTF. If there is no debris, shake it lightly and listen carefully for rattling. Replace if rattling sound.
- Important: Carefully remove the RTF from the instrument - from underneath - so that you do not dislodge any dirt or debris from RTF, and carefully inspect it.
- Make sure to follow all procedures from Panther Service Manual as applicable.
- Replace RTF if nothing apparent or issue continues after cleaning.
Invalid Run FLSOR Flags
Logs review for Invalid run FLSOR flags :
Message logs show several of the following errors on 2/6:
2/6/2021 21:43:57 Message 034.004.00165 RTF error (Signal out of range at the RTF 2)
2/6/2021 20:18:43 Message 034.004.00165 RTF error (Signal out of range at the RTF 2)
Output logs show that LED1 went > 600 on 2/6, and went back in range, but is still close to 600 (high 500rds).
RTF = RTF2 selectedChannel = 0 LED = 1 MessageID = 137769 Result=650
Recommendations for Invalid run FLSOR flags :
TS: FSE dispatch
FSE resolution: FSE Replaced RTF #2. Performed required calibrations and alignments. Verified proper.
Invalid Run Due to 'cce,p' Flag on Calibrators
Logs review for Invalid run due to 'cce,p' flag on calibrators :
Logs show:
WL0507-02 TCR00143 is a failed BV run due to cce flag on 2 calibrator replicates that invalidated the entire kit.
Output logs show:
2020-05-07 12:22:02,224|[TOS]|RuntimeType|DataReduction|Info|Normal|LogChannelResults, Channel FAM 11250, Reason: Calibrator replicate invalid: FAM does not meet the RFU range, TTime or emergence rate specification, RFURange: 1482.744, TTime: NaN, EmergenceRate: NotComputed
Same kit was then loaded with new cals/controls (WL0506-32) and failed again due to negative control failure.
Output logs show:
2020-05-07 00:40:53,927|[TOS]|RuntimeType|DataReduction|Info|Normal|LogTubeResults, 11220, Reason: Negative Control tube is invalid due to Lacto concentration is out of specified range.
Recommendations for Invalid run due to 'cce,p' flag on calibrators :
TS: Both runs show failure to amplify on FAM channel (lacto), likely a kit preparation issue. Will recommend customer to discard this kit, prepare a new one following P.I. instructions, and monitor the next run till PAS review.
PAS: Agree it appears to be reagent preparation issue. Recommend customer discard the kit (TCR# 00143). Ensure customer follows PI instructions and changes gloves at appropriate times
The first run failed due to both controls not meeting spec.
The second run failed due to calibrators not meeting spec.

## HSV
id="mc-main-content">
HSV
Below are sample runs of HSV 1 and HSV 2 assays in different reagent preparation conditions, their results, and comments or resolution.
- So far the only known reagent prep issue that causes invalidation of the run is when IC is not added to the TCR. This guide will be updated as we see other instances of failed runs in the future.
- Runs below are sample PQ runs:
Panel A is dual negative
Panel B is HSV1 positive, HSV2 negative
Panel C is HSV2 positive, HSV1 negative
Table below shows results for sample runs:
Reagent Prep Condition
Run Result
Sample PQ Run
Comments/Resolution
Normal Run
Valid
Positive
control is dual positive for HSV1 and HSV2.
Typical
Positive Control TTime: ~ 19-22 min for both HSV1 and
HSV2.
Amp not mixed
Valid
No observable difference from a
normal run. Positive control TTime is ~19-22 min.
Enzyme not mixed
Valid
Positive
control is elevated in TTime (~25-30
min). Run is still valid; results
are reportable.
No IC added
Invalid
Discard the kit. Prepare a new kit, make sure the IC is
added into the TCR.
Promoter not
mixed
Valid
No observable
difference from a normal run. Positive
control TTime is ~19-22 min.
Reconstituted for less than 15
min
Valid
The PI specifies to wait at least 15 min for lyophilized
reagents to go into solution. In the
sample run here, the reagent was reconstituted for only 1 minute.
No observable difference from a
normal run. Positive control TTime is
~19-22 min.
Note: Dual HSV1 and HSV2 positive samples are rare.

## How to Check Reagent Kit Inventory Onboard Stability
id="mc-main-content">
How to Check Reagent Kit Inventory Onboard Stability
There is an onboard stability calculation.
We need to check against all the reagents, though.
Line 23373: 2021-01-11 17:12:32,531|[PI.ReagentBayManager:.#0]|AssayReagentKitViewItem|PantherUI|Info|Normal|OnReagentUpdate[1717]: updateType=Updated reagent=(564,201627917015082202170,3,0,Amplification,Valid,54,54,2.15:48:00), kit=113

You have it correct, and it is time remaining.
Day.Hour:Min:seconds
To find onboard stability information:
- Find a Barcode which belongs to the reagent kit in question.
- Query the logs by reagent barcode.
-
Depending on the string to inspect… The remaining stability time is in minutes (can also be in ticks) or days.Hours:Minutes:Seconds.
For the Assay type 48 = CV/TV kit, remaining time reflects a new kit as the PI for CV/TV shows 5 days.
7200 minutes * (1 hr/60 min) * (1 day/24 hrs) = 5 days.
72 hours sounds right, but I would have to check PI.
I think this is the master lot expiration date: 2016279170 150822 02170 = 15 day , 08 month, 2022 year.

To find the recon expiration you can use the frequently seen UI update logs (e.g. from another set of logs that I was reviewing):
OnUpdate[1620]: updateType=Updated kit=(181,63,04-Feb-21 02:26:43,163,223,Valid,InUse) ARKVI=(181,1,63,SARSCoV2,04-Feb-21 02:26:43,163,223,Valid,InUse)
Technically this date is the closest of the master lot and recon expirations (OBS is not considered) but as you can imagine this will most often be the recon expiration.
I found it easiest to open view log, find the kit expiration error in EventLogEntries, double click the error to find the error in the Low level log, then search that log for: "updateType=Updated kit=(xxx" (xxx= the kit number of interest, in the example below it would be 113).

- Negative Controls are identified by 2814231697150220.

FAM (RTF1)
- Negative Control and Panel A should lie flat and should not fluoresce.
- LPC, Panel B, and Positive Calibrators should fluoresce around the same ttime, in this case between 14 and 15 minutes.
- HPC should fluoresce with a ttime 3 - 5 minutes earlier.
HEX
- Negative Controls and Panel A lie flat, and do not fluoresce.
- LPC, Panel B, and Positive Calibrators should fluoresce with ttimes between 20 and 24. All curves should follow a similar pattern.
- HPC will fluoresce earlier with ttimes around 17 in this example.
ROX
All samples fluoresce somewhat equally and consistently, as ROX is the Internal Control.
BV and CV/TV
FAM
Positive Controls, Panels A, C and D All do not fluoresce on the FAM channel and their ttime curve is flat.
Negative Controls and Positive Calibrators should fluoresce with a Ttime around 20mins.

BV CV/TV
CY5.5 is the Internal Control RTF. All samples, Panels, Controls, and Calibrators should fluoresce with a ttime around 18-20 minutes.
For Hex
Panel A, Negative Control, and Negative Samples should not fluoresce and lay flat on the graph.
Positive Control, Positive Calibrators, and Positive Sample should fluoresce with a tTime around 18-20 Minutes.
Negative Control, Panel A, and Negative Samples will not fluoresce.
Positive Sample, Positive Control will fluoresce at around 12 minutes
Positive Calibrator will fluoresce around 18 Minutes

## Curves Introduction
id="mc-main-content">
Curves Introduction
Curves Introduction contains these sections:
- What are curves and curve files?
- Where are curve files stored?
- What is in a curve file?
-
How do I view curve files?
- Graphing with CurveTrend
- Graphing with Excel
What are curves and curve files?
Curves and Curve files refer to the recorded sensor readings for process control data of specific modules.
These recorded readings are used to set new limits for new assays or change existing limits. These sensor readings are also useful in diagnosing and confirming issues. Flags are generated when the readings or calculated limits are outside the acceptable limits.
Limits are set for each specific assay to account for differences in formulation and volume needs. The process limits are saved in the assay definition or “sequence” file. These files are added/removed with the Diagnostic Assay Software installer. If inspection of process limits is required, this can be done by opening the sequence file. These files are located on the local workstation directory: C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\input . Best practice is to copy a set and inspection on your personal computer. If files are accidently corrupted, repair or reinstall assay software.
Where are curve files stored?
Curves refer to the folder where the curve files are stored. These files are located locally on the workstation, and persist until the workstation is reimaged.
When Send Logs is performed across a given time period, the curves are retrieved, and packaged with the logs package. The data are retrieved from the following location on the local machine:
C:\Panther\Software\PC\Persistance\Curves\YYYY_MM_DD_HH-mm-ss
Figure 1 – Example of curve folders containing curve data.
Curve files are the files within the timestamped folders. These files end in *.curve file extension. As of software version 7.2.1.37, a Panther Fusion Plus with RTFs will generate the following curve files.
What is in a curve file?
Curve files contain sensor readings of process control data.
Curve data is only recorded when the process step has completed.
Errors that occur during the process can result in no data generated as the command is interrupted before data is sent from the module to COP and back to the PC.
Image below shows an example of curve file content and file structure using Notepad++. Notepad++ is a text editor program like Notepad.
Line 1 is the header and explains what is in each column.
All curve files should have in the header:
- Date Time or Timestamp: month/day/year hh:mm:ss (this is in UTC time, most will need to adjust for local time zone).
- TestOrder Id: test order value assigned to test order.
- SampleID: sample id that is physically assigned to sample tube.
- MTUID: MTU barcode value.
- Tube Number. Tube number in MTU.
The remaining header data is unique to the curve file.
For additional information, refer to the module curve data entry.
Lines 2 and on: actual process control data. if line 2 is blank, no information was recorded.
How do I view curve files?
Curve files are delimited files and can be viewed using a variety of methods.
- Text editor, such as Notepad, or Notepad++.
- Specialized program, such as Panther Dashboard, or CurveTrend.
- Spreadsheet program, such as Excel.
Note: Always unzip the compressed *.gpz file before manipulating files with other programs.
To open file in text editor, right-click on file, then click Open with... in pop-up menu.
Graphing with CurveTrend
Refer to module curve data entry for more in-depth information.
Launch CurveTrend.
Data Tab
To view data in curve file:
- Use magnify glass to select files (can also drag and drop directly into the region as shown).
- Click Load Data .
- Click Continue >> .
Parameters Tab
-
Click Show Curves >> .
You can also uncheck Available Run s, and select Available Curve Files if desired.
Curve Plots Tab
- Select A Curve Type : choose relevant process curve for your issue.
- Select Command : different commands measure different things, reagents, or steps.
- These are additional ways to sort data. Assay, MTU number and Tube number are always available. While Flags, Sensors are file dependent.
- Curve column header (CurveID,|Flag|RunName|Assay|ProcessStep|…) with process data.
- Data by Curve ID.
- Graph colors by… Tube, Assay, etc.
Summary Plots
Sometimes it is easier to analyze specific process parameters using the Summary Plots tab.
-
For example, compare all Pmax (peak of curve values) – this is somewhat difficult.
Note: Curve Plots tab > Select A Curve Type = DispensePressure, Select Command=Amplification.
-
View the same data using Summary Plots tab, reporting Pmax only by MTU. Colored by assay. Now it is easier to compare Pmax (max pressure by MTU over time).
Note: Summary Plots tab
Select A Curve Type = DispensePressure
Select Command = Amplification
Measurement = Pmax
Graphing with Excel
To launch Excel:
Select , File > Open > Navigate to folder. If folder is empty, in file type selector change to All files (*.*), select File , click Open .
Excel may launch Text Import Wizard. If this option is not provided, select column A, then select Data > Text to Columns in the ribbon.
Text Import Wizard opens to Step 1 of 3. Select Delimited , then click Next .
Text Import Wizard, Step 2 of 3 opens. Check Semicolon at upper left, and leave Treat consecutive delimiters as one unchecked.
Click Finish . Click Next to format additional columns.
Find the values column, and select the data to be graphed.
Use line graph. Excel can handle only 255 lines.

## Pipettor Curves
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor Curves
Pipettor Curves contains these sections:
-
Background
-
AspirationPressureCurve, DispensePressureCurve, ShearingPressure, and SideCarPressure
-
C-LLD, C-LLD1, C-LLD2, PostDispCapLLD, and SidecarCLLD
-
LLDValues, SidecarLLDValues, and SidecarHardstopValues
Background
Pipettor curves are recorded readings of sensor outputs for specific processes.
Limits are set for each specific assay, to account for differences in formulation and volume needs.
The pipettor collects data and analyzes it in real time, then transmits it from the pipettor to the COP and over to the local workstation. Then the data is written into the curve file.
Short version: Pipettor curves are generated when pipettor is performing level sense, aspirate, and dispense.
Long version: A pipettor will pick a tip, move to aspirate location, performs level sense fluid (C-LLD, LLDValues). A shearing step (ShearingPressure) is performed for capped sample tubes, aspirates fluid (AspirationPressureCurve), spits back to prime dispense (DispensePressureCurve), pulls a travelling air gap, then moves to dispense location.
-
For reagent, fluid will be dispensed (DispensePressureCurve) in tubes with tests.
-
For sample, a bubble pop (C-LLD1) then TCR|FCR (C-LLD) will be measured, then sample will be dispensed another bubble pop (C-LLD2) and final measurement(PostDispenseCapLLD).
Pipettor then moves to tip eject location and ejects tip into tip chute.
Processes performed with Fusion reagent pipettor will have a “Sidecar” prefix.
References for detailed explanation:
-
MDD_FW_APP_6319
-
CDD_FW_6319_APE_ZSPip-EC
-
MTU Storyboard
List of curve files for Panther and Fusion Pipettors.
Figure 1 - Curve folder view of pipettor related curve files.
“x” indicates reagent type. E.g. TCR, TER, FCR, FER, Amplification, Probe, Promoter, Sample, etc.

Fusion pipettor aspiration and dispense
AspirationPressureCurve, DispensePressureCurve, ShearingPressure, and SideCarPressure
X-axis is time scale. Pipettor firmware will maximize data collection, so shorter aspiration times can have longer traces as the firmware is acquiring data more quickly. In these instances, it’s better to inspect the final pressure. Y-axis is pressure units. Each pressure unit is 0.57 Pa. “RDV” (reagent dispense verification) parameters define the pressure trace and are set by assay. While “D” represents dispense; the term “RDV” parameters applies to both aspiration and dispense. The following parameters can be tested against:
Figure 2 - Dispense signal and thresholds , see MDD for full details.
Figure 3 - Time stamps at pipette plunger move profile . TStop = TPumpStop
RDV parameters can be set for AspirationPressureCurve, DispensePressureCurve and SideCarPressure. RDV parameters can not be set for ShearingPressure. Shearing pressure monitors the shearing step for sample tubes with caps.
Aspiration begins after a successful level sense or successful move to set aspiration depth and shearing step has completed (e.g. pierceable sample tube). Aspiration pressure curve is recorded and processed at the pipettor.
During aspiration, the process control at this step is not tightly regulated to prevent excessive flagging. The only processing flag directly related to aspiration pressure event is the CLT flag. This flag is triggered when the pressure exceeds -28,672 counts (a pressure count unit is 0.57 Pa) and exists to protect the pressure sensor.
The next two figures display the same data, using two different groupings methods.
Figure 4 - Aspiration curve, default view is colored by Tube Number in MTU. As most MTUs will use all 5 tubes, the majority of the traces are black.
Figure 5 - Same data set as Figure 4, aspiration curve color grouped by "assay" reveals inconsistent aspiration pressure with AC2 assay. As the variability is within assay, the issue could be kit related or caused by tip issue. Amplification reagent happens to mix easily so reagent prep is not the issue, which leaves the consumable tip.
Dispenses, include spitbacks. Spitbacks are performed to prime the pipette tip after reagent aspiration with reagent specific process control disabled. Spitbacks are expected to not be as uniform as actual dispense in MTU. Here are the parameters for AC2 – TCR dispense found from an assay definition file or “sequence” file:
<RDVParams>
<PMaxMax>6000</PMaxMax>
<PMaxMin>0</PMaxMin>
<PRampDownMin>0</PRampDownMin>
<PStopMin>0</PStopMin>
<PStaticMin>0</PStaticMin>
<PStaticMax>0</PStaticMax>
<PMeanMin>2200</PMeanMin>
<TRiseMaxStartDelay>0</TRiseMaxStartDelay>
<TDownMinStopDelay>0</TDownMinStopDelay>
<THalfMaxPeriodMin>0</THalfMaxPeriodMin>
<PRefType>Undefined</PRefType>
</RDVParams>
Each of the parameters are assigned a bit value. If the parameter is triggered the bit is enabled. Pmax error = RDV2, Pmean error = RDV64. It is possible to trigger multiple parameters. From the above set RDV parameters notice only PMaxMax and PMeanMin are defined. PMaxMax = maximum pressure value cannot exceed 6000. PMeanMin = minimum mean pressure must be greater than 2200. Below is an example of Pmax triggered, generating RDV 2 flags. (Dispense Flag 2, InstrFlag 2 are synonymous with RDV 2).
Figure 6 - Pmax triggered for AC2, when Pmax values exceed 6000. By scanning the Pmax column in curve trend it's easy to determine the cutoff without opening the assay definition XML file.
Figure 7 - Summary plot view of dispense pressure – TCR – Pmax. Can clearly see a transition around MTU = 42.
The first line of data is the header line, which explains the data within the column. Commonly used columns:
CurveID: is not a column present in raw data. This value is assigned by curve trend software.
Assay: as previously mentioned process parameters are tied to assay formulation.
ProcessStep or CommandDescription: determines fluid type
DateTime: UTC time
TestOrderID: test order of sample
SampleID: barcode of sample tube
MTUNumber: MTU # since PantherMain was started
MTUID: MTU barcode
InstrFlag: RDV code
Pmax: Peak pressure
Pmean: Average pressure from from time of TRampEnd through TPumpStop
C-LLD, C-LLD1, C-LLD2, PostDispCapLLD, and SidecarCLLD
Liquid level detection can be performed using barometric or capacitive sensor. Capacitive is normally used as it increases pipettor life span as it reduces the number of plunger cycles. Barometric is used for oil which cannot be detected using capacitance. Normal frequency values of capacitive sensor when pipettor is at z-home is shown in service software. A normal value is in the range of 9,000Hz to 14,000Hz. The closer the diti is to ground plane, the higher the frequency reading. The maximum value is 24,000Hz
Figure 8 - Basics of any capacitive curve.
Figure 9 - Basics of any barometric curve.
The first line of data is the header line, which explains the data within the column. Commonly used columns for LLD values.
CurveID: is not a column present in raw data. This value is assigned by curve trend software.
Assay: as previously mentioned, process parameters are tied to assay formulation.
ProcessStep or CommandDescription: determines fluid type.
DateTime: UTC time.
TestOrderID: test order of sample.
SampleID: barcode of sample tube.
MTUNumber: MTU # since PantherMain was started.
MTUID: MTU barcode.
LLDValues, SidecarLLDValues, and SidecarHardstopValues
These values represent z-axis motor steps (20 steps = 1mm, a step is the minimum movement unit of measure). LLDValues are used to determine if reagent inventory levels are acceptable range otherwise reagent volume too high, reagent volume too low errors or bottle empty errors are generated. For open tube assays, a minimum fill height in sample tube is required, if not, a quantity insufficient (QNS) error will be generated. It is important to note, the implementation of liquid detected height reporting before aspiration is as follows:
Liquid not detected: detected height of fluid fails inventory. reported height is where fluid was detected. No aspiration step is performed.
Liquid detected: detected height of fluid meets inventory requirement. Pipettor will track down into fluid during aspiration. Reported height is final pipettor position after aspiration and not the initial height where fluid was detected.
This rule also applies to reagents.
LLDValues also record the pre- and post-sample dispense heights within the MTU to help determine if enough fluid was dispensed; a VVFS error will be generated when this is incorrect. SidecarLLDValues, does the same but for the Fusion side of the instrument.
SidecarHardstopValues is used when capacitive and barometric level sensing are ineffective. Fusion pipettor will detect the bottom of the MTU or cartridge by driving to a hard stop. The pipettor will then move away a set distance and aspirate fluid.
The first line of data is the header line, which explains the data within the column. Commonly used columns for LLD values:
CurveID: is not a column present in raw data. This value is assigned by curve trend software.
Assay: as previously mentioned, process parameters are tied to assay formulation.
ProcessStep or CommandDescription: determines fluid type.
DateTime: UTC time.
TestOrderID: test order of sample.
SampleID: barcode of sample tube
MTUNumber: MTU # since PantherMain was started.
MTUID: MTU barcode.
LldResultType: reports if level detection was successful or not.
LldHeight: measured fluid height from software defined bottom of container.

Click the Pipettor tab, then click the LLD Right Arm tab.

Important: Select bar under LLD at lower left.

Important: Select Log under LLD at lower left.

In this example, script is asking for 10 sample tips to be loaded in Tray1 and Drawer 1. Refer to image below.

The script launches. Sample Pipettor picks a sample tip, then applies Barometric Liquid Level Detect at TCR bottle position 1.

When the script completes, it creates files in the following folder: C:\Panther\Panther Service Software\Log\ .

## Pipettor – Pmax – RDV 2
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor – Pmax – RDV 2
RDV 2 flag is an overpressure error that is generated when dispense or aspiration pressure exceeds Pmax threshold.
Dispense Side – RDV 2
Figure 1 – RDFA flag with RDV 2 code. Curve Plot - Dispense Pressure - Amplification reagent by Assay type. (1) sort “Color By” field by “Assay” to differentiate processing curves (2) ”Dispense Flags” 0 = successful dispense, no flagging ; 2 = Pmax exceeded. (3) Sort or scan “InstrFlag” field for “Dispense Flag” code. (4) “Pmax” field reports Pmax value of individual process curves.
Figure 2 – Another way to look at data from Figure 1, the Summary plot allows graphing of the specific columns. Notice the other assays there is less variance MTU to MTU (e.g. tip to tip as 1 tip per MTU).
Figure 3 – Same run as Figures 1 and 2, Enzyme dispense for CT/GC only. Notice the InstrFlag column values flips between 0 and 2. For CT/GC assay version 2.6.5, Enzyme Pmax threshold = 4000. For most assays, tips which are made properly should be at least 10% below flagging threshold (e.g. max value in Pmax column for CT/GC – enzyme should around 3800).
Aspiration Side – RDV 2
Figure 4 – Fusion Internal control flagged with RDV 2 during aspiration.

Second peak approximately 75 on x-axis is peak pressure. This peak value should be at least 2000 (y-axis). As the pressure profiles are similar between peak 1 and peak 2, it’s likely these tips are missing aerosols filters.

## Magnetic Wash Station Processing Curves
id="mc-main-content">
Magnetic Wash Station Processing Curves
ProcessControlData_MagWash2_XXXXXX
ProcessControlData_MagWash1_XXXXXX
These curves are useful for identifying a problematic Wash Solution Pump, diagnosing a mild or severe aspirator clog, or determining if there are early triggers caused by foam or bubbles.
Columns of Interest
Column
Description
Tube Number
Identifies the tube within the MTU— O is the tube closest to the barcode.
Magwash_id
Identifies the Magnetic Wash Station module— 0 is the module on the left (Magnetic Wash Station 1), 1 is the module on the right (Magnetic Wash Station 2.
Note —Magnetic Wash Station 1 and Magnetic Wash Station 2 process control data are stored in separate files.
Cmd
Identifies the following process control commands:
34 = Tiplet sense after tiplets are picked
35 = Tiplet sense after tiplets are stripped
45 = Wash dispense verification
46 = Residual wash detection
47 = Empty check (only during prime)
51 Tiplet sense immediately before tiplets are stripped off
FIR max
The maximum capacitive signal spike detected.
FIR motor position
The encoder position where the maximum capacitive signal spike occurred.
Threshold
The FIR maximum cutoff limit.
ErrorCode
Displays 0 if no error occurred during the step. It displays a number if an error occurred.
Result0
Only informative if ErrorCode is not zero. This column indicates on which of the aspirators the error occurred.
Convert the number in this column from decimal to binary to indicate the problematic tube. For example, if Result0 is 11 , it converts to 1011 in binary. This indicates errors on tubes 1, 2, and 4 of the MTU.
Tiplet Detection (Cmd = 34, 35, and 51)
- The value in the FIR max column is compared to the value in the Threshold column.
- If FIR max > Threshold , no tiplets were detected on this aspirator.
- If FIR max < Threshold , tiplets were detected on this aspirator.
- If tiplet sense ( MT1 ) problems are occurring, note whether there are any trends from MTU to MTU.
For example, check to see if the same tube in each MTU has an abnormal value. Also, note if any FIR max values are closer than 10 to the Threshold value.
Wash Dispense Verification (Cmd = 45)
- If the value in the FIR max column is greater than the Threshold value, the Magnetic Wash Station did not detect fluid in the MTU tube, as it should during this part of the process.
- If FIR max > Threshold , then the FIR motor position column is related to how much volume was detected in the tube.
- If FIR motor position ≤ 8475 , then more than 1,200 µL of Wash solution was detected in the MTU tube.
- If FIR motor position ≥ 9170 , then less than 800 µL of Wash solution was detected in the MTU tube.
- If ML2 or ML3 flags are occurring, note whether the same trends are seen on Magnetic Wash Station 1 and Magnetic Wash Station 2. If similar patterns are seen on both stations, this indicates a problem with the shared Wash Pump, as opposed to problems with the Magnetic Wash Stations.
- Problems detected at this step are typically caused by one of the following conditions:
- An under-dispensing Wash Pump ( ML3 )
- Clogs of the aspirator ( ML2 )
- Bubbles or foam caused by a bad wash injector ( ML2 )
- An empty or disconnected Wash bottle ( ML3 )
- Leaks in the Wash fluid line ( ML3 )
- Low vacuum pressure ( ML2 )
Residual Wash Check (Cmd = 46)
- If the value in the FIR max column is greater than the Threshold value, the Magnetic Wash Station detected fluid in the MTU tube. The majority of the time at this step, the Magnetic Wash Station will not detect any fluid (i.e., FIR max < Threshold ). However, it is not unusual for the Magnetic Wash Station to detect the presence of some residual fluid (i.e., sometimes you will see FIR max > Threshold ).
- If FIR max > Threshold , then the FIR motor position column is related to how much volume was detected in the tube.
If FIR motor position ≤ 10716 , then more than 50 µL of Wash solution was detected in the MTU tube.
- If FIR max > Threshold , then one should typically see associated FIR motor position values > 10840 .
- If residual wash ( ML5 ) flags are occurring, note whether there are any trends from MTU to MTU. For example, check to see if the same tube in each MTU has an abnormal value.Also not if any FIR max values are closer than 10 to the Threshold value.
- Problems detected at this step are typically caused by a clogged aspirator or low vacuum pressure. Remove and inspect aspirators, and note nature of substance, if any, removed from the aspirator.

## TCR too Low
id="mc-main-content">
TCR too Low
Error Code
262.000.00044
Refer to these sections:
-
Data from Sequence Files
-
Liquid Level too Low in Q1
Data from Sequence Files
Both AC2 (250tk) and TMA-covid use the same fill volume calculation.
Volume 46798, initLL 4592
42206 is the InitLL 1st LLD
42206 volume/ 1884.2 (cross sectional area)= 22.399 ht in mm. * 20steps/mm = 448 steps
The lowest of the retries = 431 steps, so 17 steps below the LL threshold (0.85mm).
The AC2 kit I see from the curve data suggests they are using 100 TK.
As they are running 5.3.2, I do not have access to the coo file.
Resolution
When you reteach:
- Grab coo file beforehand.
- Use the correct teach tool. The sn suggests they may have a machined tcr carousel.
-
This can cause 40 steps bias in wrong direction.
-
If pipettor z is too high, e.g. needs to be taught lower, then the problem will be fixed after teaching.
Additional troubleshooting
-
Teaching changed by five steps in y-axis and 24 steps in z-axis.
<<Coordinate_before (tcr too low).coo>>
<<Coordinate-after.coo>>
- Different tips were being used – unlikely root cause of tcr too low, but could cause RDV errors.
Reagent handling
Liquid Level too Low in Q1
11/06: X-axis 100-130, capacitive tracking profile is different: x = 100, y = 11400.
Aspriation: not well mixed.
Dispense: RDFT errors, removing the under dispense curve Pmax range is 4700-5000.
12/02: To me, this trace does look like a bubble.
Also, notice along x-axis 100-130, the tracking profile: X = 100, y = 11500.
Aspiration: tip appears damaged.
Dispense: Pmax range 4500-5000
This looks like a pipette/tcr alignment issue.
Things to check:
-
Bubbles or foam
-
Correct tcr cup holder is being used
-
tcr carousel/pipettor alignment
-
tcr carousel

## Event Logs Viewer
id="mc-main-content">
Event Logs Viewer
The Dashboard Event Logs module provides the ability to view and analyze PANTHER System Log files. The overall PANTHER System Log files can be referred to as ‘PMains’ and are considered the super set while the ‘Event Logs’ and ‘Activity Logs’ are considered the sub sets.
A PANTHER Log file is a recording of important user and application activity that occurs on the instrument. Each entry in the PANTHER Log contains a date/time stamp. This allows the information to be chronologically ordered to assist with problem troubleshooting. If something should malfunction within the complex PANTHER system, there may be no other way of identifying the problem so that when the problem occurs it is easier to pinpoint and fix.
The Event Logs module displays Event Log and Activity Log information which includes PANTHER instrument diagnostic messages as well as their severity levels. Main Log entries that correspond to the same time frame as a selected Event Log entry can be viewed. Once the Events and or Activity records are populated in the Event and/ or Activity grid, the user can select an Event or Activity record and generate a detailed log file search to get the PANTHER Log, or PMains, detailed information related to the selected entries.
Event Logs and Activity Logs are displayed in the upper section of the screen while the PANTHER Logs , or PMains , are displayed at the bottom of the screen.
To open a open a PMains file, click on the “Record Creation Time” column and the corresponding PMains file will display at the bottom of the screen.
Event Logs – Module Components
- Event Logs – Module Components
Column Headers
Column
Description
Record Creation Time
The time the record was created. It is displayed by local date, hour, minute, seconds and milliseconds.
Description
Describes the message details for Event Log(s) or Activity Log(s).
Event #
Event number.
Severity
Lists the severity of a log, i.e. Message, Warning, Problem, Critical, or Fatal.
Module
PANTHER component name.
Source
PANTHER source name.
- Event Logs
-
Event Log messages can be viewed for each hardware module.
-
A maximum of 500 Event Log records can be displayed.
-
Event Log sorting, conditional formatting, and grouping can be done by right-clicking the column header .
-
To sort columns in ascending or descending order, right-click the column header, then select Sort Ascending or Sort Descending.
-
To undo the column sort, right-click the column header, then select Clear Sorting .
-
Conditional Formatting can be done by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘Conditional Formatting’ . This feature assists with the creation of rules for customized formatting. The following can be controlled: text alignment, row alignment, case sensitive, row color, and cell color .
-
Columns can be grouped by an existing column by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘Group by this column’ . Grouping can be used to consolidate non-numeric data values into more general group values; these group values can be mapped into a new column within the data set.
-
Columns can be removed from the current view by right-clicking on the column header and s electing ‘ Column Chooser .’ Drag a column header into the gray area in the ‘Column Chooser’ dialog box to remove the column.
-
Columns can be hidden from the Event Logs screen by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘Hide Column’ . To unhide the column, right-click on any column header and select ‘Column Chooser,’ then drag the hidden column header back out to the ‘Event Logs’ screen.
-
Columns can be ‘pinned’ so that they remain at the ends of the screen (left or right side); this keeps the column headings visible as the data bar is scrolled up and down. To pin the column, right-click on the column header and select ‘Pin Column’ ; to reverse this, right-click on the same column header and select ‘Unpin Column’ .
-
Columns do not automatically accommodate to fit the information they contain. However, by right-clicking and selecting ‘Best Fit’ , the column automatically expands and contracts to fit the data enclosed.
- Events Logs can also be grouped by holding the left-click mouse button down and dragging a column to the row named “ Drag a column here to group by this column ".
The Event Logs are grouped by 'Module' and 'Severity '.
- Event Log Search
-
Search for Event Logs by selecting a date range and checking-off ‘ Severity ,’ ‘Log Type ,’ and ‘ Include Diagnostic Messages ’ as preferred.
-
Use the 'Description' text box to type description notes.
- Panther Log Search
To search Panther logs by date, select the desired date in the Search Date drop-down list in Panther Log Search. Then click Search .
-
Click Clear to reset the search date to the present date.
-
Search results appear at the bottom of the Event Logs screen, in the following columns:
Column
Description
Date/Time
Local date and time of the PMains Log.
Content
Describes the instrument message details.
Category
Classifies PMains information, e.g. Data Manager, PANTHER UI, RS232 Communication.
Error Level
Describes the severity of the error.
Thread
Thread number; it is PANTHER system generated.
Class Name
Message class, e.g. Event Logs, Activity Logs.
Log File
Displays the PANTHER Log or PMain log file this entry derives from.
- Bookmarks
Bookmarks can be set or reset on any of the detailed grid log entries to allow the user to return to the selected locations during the log file evaluations. A current Event Log or PANTHER log entry can be marked in order to easily return to it by using the ‘Bookmarks’ tab.
-
Setting Bookmarks – from the ‘ Events Log ’ screen, select an Event Log or PANTHER Log by clicking on a desired log row, then right-click and select ‘ Set Bookmark '.
-
Displaying the Bookmarks list – click the Bookmarks tab, then select ‘Event Log’ or ‘PANTHER Log’ to see the appropriate list.
-
Finding a Bookmark from the Logs list – from the Bookmarks tab, select the desired log , then click Find Bookmark .
- Event Log Breakdown
Locate Event Log Breakdown on the far right side of the Event Logs tab. Logs are displayed by individual module, with the number of messages, warnings, problems, critical, fatal and unknown frequencies.

## Flags by Worklist
id="mc-main-content">
Flags by Worklist
The Flags by Worklist module provides the ability to analyze test flags from Test Order within a set of work lists. The work lists are retrieved from the DM database and displayed in a master grid by providing a start-date and end-date range. Overall, this module determines the number of pipetted tests per work list by counting the number of sample replicates aspirated. It also determines the number of MTUs processed per work list from the Panther test order table.
- Flags by Worklist List – Module Components
Column
Description
Start
Local date and time that the work list began to run.
End
Local date and time that the work list was completed.
Worklist ID
Worklist Identification.
Duration
Total time it took to complete a work list.
Pipetted Tests
Number of pipette tests completed per work list.
MTUs Processed
Number of MTUs/ Multi-Tube Units processed per work list; 1 MTU = 5 disposable reaction tubes.
Flags
An error message.
- Flags by Worklist
To display Result and Assay flags by worklist, select a Start Date and an End Date under Work List Filter Criteria, then click Search .
Click Reset to adjust the Start Date and End Date to the past seven days, to end with the current date.
To sort Result and Assay flags by column – click the filtering arrow next to the column head: Start, End, Work List ID, Duration, Pipetted Tests, MTUs Processed. Click the column head to display the arrow .
Refer to Flags By Work List below:
To open a menu for copying, sorting, conditional formatting, and grouping Result and Assay flags, right-click the column head.
Refer to Flags By Work List below:
To expand Result and Assay flag columns, place the cursor between the columns, hold down the left-click mouse button, and drag the bi-directional arrow in the desired direction.
To move and reorganize Result and Assay flag columns, place the cursor on the column head, hold down the left-click mouse button, and drag the column to the desired location.
To view Test Order Information on the right, select the desired Work List ID row on the right.
- Test Order Information – Column Headers
Column
Description
Tube #
Tube number.
Completion
Local date and time that the test order is completed.
MTU Pos
Multi-Tube Unit position number; 1 MTU = 5 disposable reaction tubes.
MTU ID
Multi-Tube Unit Identification number.
RLU
Relative Light Unit, it is a measurement used by Luminometers to quantify light emitted.
Flags
Error message.
Test Order Look Up columns can be organized by sorting, conditional formatting, and grouping by right-clicking the column header and selecting the listed functionality.
-
Columns can be sorted in ascending or descending order by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘ Sort Ascending ’ or ‘ Sort Descending '.
-
Column sorting can be reversed by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘ Clear Sorting '.
-
Conditional Formatting can be done by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘ Conditional Formatting ’. This feature assists with the creation of rules for customized formatting. The following can be controlled: text alignment, row alignment, case sensitive, row color, and cell color.
-
Columns can be grouped by an existing column by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘ Group by this column ’. Grouping can be used to consolidate non-numeric data values into more general group values; these group values can be mapped into a new column within the data set.
-
Columns can be removed from the current view by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘Column Chooser’ . Drag a column header into the gray area in the ‘ Column Chooser ’ dialog box to remove the column.
-
Columns can be hidden from the Event Logs screen by right-clicking on the column header and selecting ‘ Hide Column ’. To unhide the column, right-click on any column header and select ‘Column Chooser,’ then drag the hidden column header back out to the ‘Event Logs’ screen.
-
Columns can be ‘ pinned ’ so that they remain at the ends of the screen (left or right side); this keeps the column headings visible as the data bar is scrolled up and down. To pin the column, right-click on the column header and select ‘ Pin Column ’; to reverse this, right-click on the same column header and select ‘ Unpin Column '.
-
Columns do not automatically accommodate to fit the information they contain. However, by right-clicking and selecting ‘ Best Fit ’, the column automatically expands and contracts to fit the data enclosed.

Health reports consist of a series of sub reports. The date and time range you specify for the report determines its content. Each health report type contains a specific set of sub reports. Health reports consist of the following grouped sections:

## Panther Remote Dashboard
id="mc-main-content">
Panther Remote Dashboard
Introduction
The Panther Remote Dashboard is a software application that provides instrument runtime diagnostics, analytics, and reports to allow Field Service Engineers and technicians the ability to analyze instrument health, accuracy, and test results.
The application is composed of individual modules, or mini-applications, that allow Field Service Engineers to analyze and diagnose various system errors and warnings, or test anomalies that may have occurred during an Assay procedure. The application supports compatibility across all Panther releases to date, which include SPx (Diagnostics code branch) and Blood Bank / Real-Time code branch.

User Guide
Refer to PANTHER Remote Dashboard User Guide (PDF)
Health Reports
Types of Graphs on Dashboard

## LIS Monitor
id="mc-main-content">
LIS Monitor
The LIS Laboratory Information System. Log File monitoring software module provides the technician the ability to view LIS log messages as they are being created by PANTHER from the LIS system. This tool exposes any possible malformed messages that may cause invalid or erroneous data that PANTHER may not be able to handle properly. After turning on the LIS logging features located on the PANTHER system LIS Configuration screen, the LIS Monitor will display all LIS / ASTM American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) is an international standards organization that develops and publishes voluntary technical standards. traffic. This allows the FSE Field Service Engineer. to determine if connectivity has been properly configured and allows the FSE to work with the LIS Vendor on the ASTM message formats.
Use the log file monitor to view two different types of transport message files: RS232 and TCP/IP. Typically one of the two transports will be set up by the technician but never both at the same time. The output display of the monitor shows the last 500 or less messages that were received by PANTHER and will ignore any older messages. The monitor adds new messages received and removes older messages from the 500 message buffer to ensure that the buffer limit is never exceeded.
The top view displays any TCP messages, while the bottom view displays any RS232 messages. A green monitoring button, File Monitor On turns the monitor on or off. It uses the FileWatcher event service, to minimize system CPU overhead when monitor is not in use.
Table below lists buttons in LIS monitor:
LIS Monitor Buttons
Description
Load Logs
Load LIS log messages created by Panther from the LIS system.
File Monitor Off
Turns the monitor on or off.
Clear Logs
Removes displayed logs.

## PRO360° Connectivity Tester Feature
id="mc-main-content">
PRO360° Connectivity Tester Feature
The PRO360° Connectivity module has additional functions that allow the FSE Field Service Engineer. to:
- View the Network Interface Card (NIC) configuration settings.
- Test TCP/IP address and port connectivity. It is used to ensure LIS Laboratory Information System. connectivity has been configured properly.
- Determine if DNS resolution occurs properly.
- Ensure EFT connectivity exists. EFT connectivity is needed for RSL.
- Perform a basic test to ensure that the Panther NIC has been configured correctly.
- PRO360° Connectivity Tester
The PRO360° Connectivity module displays information of any RDXM server configuration as network addresses are tested. When this test is run, it produces a status result of each connection by executing a network request to each address that is listed. Overall, this module enables:
- Viewing the Network Interface Card (NIC) configuration settings.
- Testing TCP/IP address and port connectivity. It is used to ensure LIS connectivity has been configured properly.
- Determines if the DNS resolution occurrs properly.
- Ensures EFT connectivity exists. EFT connnectivity is needed for RSL.
- Performs a basic test to ensure that the Panther instrument NIC has been configured correctly.

- Network Connectivity Tester
The Network Connectivity Tester module is used to determine if a network route exists, if a server is accepting network connections, and optionally if DNS can be resolved. For example, this tester can be used to verify that the LIS is accessible and accepting connection to the LIS Host. Another use of this tester is to determine if the Panther has the ability to access the RDxM servers.

If you enter an IP address, tester tries to establish a network connection to the address over the port number entered

## Quantitative Graphing
id="mc-main-content">
Quantitative Graphing
The Quantitative Analysis software module provides the technician a view into the general pressure or command curve data over a designated range of time. This curve data is similar to the curve data reported by the Graphing module. The result plots, however, are a composite of curve data over the designated time range.
The software retrieves the curve data from the database in incremental requests and provides a continuous plotted update as the data is retrieved. The plotting report controls automatic scaling of the output as new data arrives until the final data retrieval and update is completed for that user’s designated time range. After you enter a specific WorklistID or selectable date range, additional filter criteria become available.
This additional filter criteria selection helps build the final query for the successive curve type requests. Some of these selections are listed below. AC2 PQ
The AC2 PQ (Aptima Combo CT/GC Assays Performance Qualification) module is responsible for validating and verifying the luminescence acceptance criteria for proper PANTHER system operation. The software module processes the luminescence data similarly to the SysCheck and FlashCheck modules, in that statistical calculations are performed to verify compliance to the requirement specifications. The AC2 PQ module retrieves a specific population of panels (Panel A – Panel E) information from the database, based on a user selected run. Allowable invalid reactions per assay run for APTIMA COMBO 2 Assay:
- 1 – VVFS or VVFT
- 1 – Cap Pierce Failure if caused by a double foil
- Up to 2 Equivocal Panel E results (> 25,000 RLU)
- Verify % CV and Average RLU of Panel B / Panel C ratio between 0.5 < Ratio < 2.0 for all valid results.
The output report displays the results of the calculations and whether there is an overall pass or fail of the complete test based upon the allowable invalid reactions.

## RLU Evaluations
id="mc-main-content">
RLU Evaluations
RLU Evaluations are conducted in following four modules:
-
Flash-Check
-
System-Check
-
HPV-PQ
-
AC2-PQ
- FLASHCHECK
The Flashcheck Reagent is intended for use in performing Quality Control verification of the Auto Detect fluid pumps and injectors in the PANTHER Luminometers as part of new instrument Manufacturing and existing instrument Service/Maintenance procedures. The PANTHER Luminometers are self-contained microprocessor based instruments that measure Relative Light Unit (RLU) values and report raw data for further analysis. The software in these instruments allow protocol programming, perform quality control calibration, acquire RLU values and monitor various sensors to warn the user of possible invalid conditions. The instruments contain pumps and injectors that dispense detection reagents (Auto Detect Reagents) that create chemiluminescent reactions. The Flashcheck Reagent is a chemiluminescent oligonucleotide complex dissolved in an acidic buffered detergent-based solution. Flash Check shall be developed as a system check to measure the performance of High Count and Chiron Luminometers to ensure that assay results are consistent within an instrument and from instrument to instrument.
Flashcheck is a chemiluminescent formulation that generates a signal on PANTHER instruments by sequential mixing with a hydrogen peroxide reagent (Auto Detect 1) and a sodium hydroxide reagent (Auto Detect 2).
The Flash Check software module is responsible for displaying the results of a Flashcheck Assay reagent test(s). The results of these tests consist of measuring luminescence from 4 PANTHER MTU (Multi Tube Unit) x 5 replicates totaling 20 replicate samples. Each replicate luminescence measurement consists of 200, 10–msec RLU ( Relative Light Unit ) sample measurements from the Luminometers found in each of the 4 MTUs of the PANTHER RT Incubator. The 200 sample measurements are then converted into fifty intervals containing 40-msec RLU values by summing every four cells and storing the values. From there, average and variant statistical values are calculated to determine acceptance criteria. The system shall also indicate whether there are outliers or no outliers.

- SYSCHCK
The System Check software module is responsible for verifying that PANTHER luminometer is in compliance with performance validity and acceptance criteria defined in the Software Requirements Specification document. The software will run several statistical evaluations with the Syscheck Assay of 12 replicates. The result report displays the test demographics along with the user input data. It also includes a calculated calibration factor with a listing of all the test-orders Raw RLU and Calibrated RLU values. The last page of the report displays additional calculated statistical results such as “ Average Calibrated RLU ”, “ Standard Deviation ”, “ Covariance ”, “ Dark Counts ” among others. The software module follows a similar processing methodology as the FlashCheck module.

# Section: Firmware

## Communication Error During Instrument Setup
id="mc-main-content">
Communication Error During Instrument Setup
Possible reasons: new PCB has been installed, communication.
Instrument setup stalls when trying to communicate to the Luminometer, like this:
Then, either the Lumo board has an issue, or something upstream. So, take a look in the troubleshooting guide for CAN-Bus, and in this case, looking at the communication, you can see that the OQ is just before the Luminometer. So, try swapping the Lumo cable with the OQ cable on the AUX COP board. Does the Lumo now initialize?
**Make sure to swap cables back after troubleshooting.
[Image!!]

## Firmware – Instrument Setup Stalls
id="mc-main-content">
Firmware – Instrument Setup Stalls
During Firmware install, Instrument Setup Stalls and FSE Field Service Engineer. receives ERROR OCCURED! message below. To find the message, you may need to drag the Instrument Setup window aside, to view the error message behind it.
Error Code
RS232S32.EXE : Internal : 81, Win : 0, DDE : 0
Error text : server cannot open communication – COM3 may be busy
Resolution 1
Click OK .
Resolution 2
FSE had skipped step 5 (Rename the Com Port) from TB-01772.
Resolution 3
Panther Fusion, FSE had skipped step 5 and could not rename COM port. Had to reimage.
We have received reports during Software 7.2 upgrades, instrument setup will sometimes stall.
Please check if there is a dialog box open behind the Instrument Setup screen.
Resolution 4
- Drag the Instrument Setup window to the side. (Alt + Tab will not work)
- Click OK , instrument setup will resume.

## Firmware – FSE Selected Fusion on a Panther
id="mc-main-content">
Firmware – FSE Selected Fusion on a Panther
While pushing firmware to a Panther, FSE Field Service Engineer. accidentally selected Fusion, and then ran firmware. Instrument Setup failed. FSE realized her mistake, and reran firmware correctly, but then the GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. would not start.
Error
"Timeout at connecting to Sidecar COP"
Resolution
Navigate to folder named C:\panther\software\PC\bin\configuration.
In that folder, locate file named ChangedUserSettings.xml . Cut the file and move it to a USB drive, as a backup.
Test
Restart the GUI.

## Firmware – FSE Selected Incorrect Pipettor
id="mc-main-content">
Firmware – FSE Selected Incorrect Pipettor
APP is APP (old).
APE is BLDC (new).
The FSE Field Service Engineer. in the second example mentioned the blue LEDs on the pipettors.
BLDC have blue LEDs.
APP have green.
This error is selecting BLDC in FW and having APP.
Getting an error while doing the Panther firmware download. It appears the left and right air pipettors are not taking firmware.
ERROR: device APE0 [6319,60,1] @ CAN1 not found!
ERROR: device APE1 [6319,60,2] @ CAN1 not found!
Resolution
Select correct pipettor configuration in Instrument Setup.

id="mc-main-content">
Firmware Instrument Setup Error 7.x
We are running into an issue pushing firmware to the sidecar on SW 7.1 and 7.2. The program runs normally until about 130 seconds, at which point it freezes and pops up a serial number page. Refer to image below.
Resolution
-
Need to allow Active X in dialog box prompt.
-
Then enter Thermocycler Serial Number.
-
Press Submit.
Note: Nothing will happen when SUBMIT is pressed. Move on to the next step.
-

-
Press Submit.
Note: When you press Submit after you enter sidecar serial number, firmware flashing resumes.
Note: In the picture below, instrument setup appends -01 to the end. This is normal.

## Firmware Instrument Setup Would Not Pass
id="mc-main-content">
Firmware Instrument Setup Would Not Pass
FSE Field Service Engineer. Replaced Reagent Pipettor, and then Instrument Setup would not pass. FSE said firmware update would fail about seven minutes in. Stratec logs show that IS was able to download all parameters, but then was not able to push any parameters.
Reviewed the C:\Stratec\InstrumentSetup\log folder. In the 5-00-00-18-0_before_2021-01-28_11-50-3 folder, opened the ParameterLog.txt file, and found the following error:
Copy
Message: File C:\Program Files\STRATEC\Download\Uniload3\log\Uniload_Panther_Complete_1.txt does not exist
Message: File C:\Program Files\STRATEC\Download\Uniload3\log\Panther_Complete.log exists, the fie contents are copied to
C:\Stratec\InstrumentSetup\log\5-00-00-18-0_before_2021-01-28_11-50-3\Uniload_Panther_Complete_1.txt
ERROR: DOWNLOAD_FW not done as Uniload_Panther_Complete_1.txt file contains 'ERROR:' string. See for details:
C:\Stratec\InstrumentSetup\log\5-00-00-18-0_before_2021-01-28_11-50-3\Uniload_Panther_Complete_1.txt
Opened the Uniload_Panther_Complete_1.txt file, and found this error:
Copy
firmware release: 02.01 2210 0X Kernel
software release: 03.0021.1 2090 COP
ERROR: device CPX [ 2210, 1, 1] @ CAN 2 not found!
error occured!
download could not be carried out!
Resolution
FSE was able to perform full HW Reset in both SSW and Panther GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. , but still could not pass IS. FSE replaced the COP Slave board, and firmware would then pass.
Suspect this could be the difference between pass-through and non-pass-through mode. Sounds like the only time we request information from the slave (AUX) board is during IS. At other times, it is just a pass-through.

## APV – Assay Process Verifier Detected an Issue with Assay Process
id="mc-main-content">
APV – Assay Process Verifier Detected an Issue with Assay Process
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
The Assay Process Verifier (APV) detected an issue with the assay process.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Possible Hardware Failure
-
Field Service
- Mix frequency, duration out of range
- Assay Reagent pipetting to the MTU is not initiated
- Software APV flag
Technical Support
Possible Hardware Failure
- Look for the hardware failure information in the logs/messages.
- Check for initial hardware failure.
Resolution
Follow procedure for identified hardware failure.
Field Service
Mix frequency, duration out of range
- Using the PANTHER Dashboard, launch Event Log and identify flag assignment.
- In Service Software, use OQ Procedure and look for rough MTU positioning to stations or slots.
Resolution
Clean, re-teach, or even replace the device that was identified causing the problem during isolation procedure.
Assay Reagent pipetting to the MTU is not initiated
Assay Reagent pipetting to the MTU is not initiated within 15 seconds after the MTU is inserted into the Reagent Load Station.
Using the Dashboard, launch the Graphing feature to identify abnormalities during reagent pipetting.
Resolution
Clean, re-teach, or replace the device that was identified as the cause of the problem during the evaluation procedure.
Software APV flag

## FDF1 – Oil Dispense Failure Detected
id="mc-main-content">
FDF1 – Oil Dispense Failure Detected
Description
Fluid Dispense Failure – Oil dispense failure was detected.
Technical Support
Empty Oil Bottle
Check to make sure there is fluid in the oil bottles.
Replace the Universal Fluids if necessary.
Note— Inventory control can sometimes be circumvented with various service procedures.
Leakage on Fitting Connection (Oil Dispense Path)
Check to be sure the oil bottle connection and tubing are connected, and the straw is connected to the cap.
Kinks in Fluid Tubing
- Open the Universal Fluids Drawer and look for any kinks in the fluid lines.
- Open the right-side access panel and look for any kinks in the fluid lines.
Field Service
Empty Oil Bottle
Verify oil bottles contain fluid.
Note— Inventory control can sometimes be circumvented with various service procedures.
RESOLUTION:
Replace the Universal Fluids kit, if necessary.
TEST:
Perform Prime in Panther.
Kinks in Fluid Tubing
Open the Universal Fluids drawer and look for any kinks in the fluid lines.
Open the right-side access panel and look for any kinks in the fluid lines.
RESOLUTION:
Straighten or replace any kinked tubing.
TEST:
Perform Prime in Panther.
Damaged Fitting or Tubing in the fluid line from the bottle to the injector
Follow tubing and fitting connections between Magnetic Wash modules and the fluid bottle connector and check for leaks.
Using Service Software prime the oil into an MTU in both Magwash stations. Check for any abnormality (leaking from any fitting or tubing).
RESOLUTION:
Replace defective fitting.
Replace Pump if identified as defective.
TEST:
Verify prime in Service Software.
Perform Prime in Panther.
A/B Valve on Universal Fluid Drawer
Using Service Software prime the oil into an MTU (default is Bottle A). Check for any abnormality (bubbles, or uneven dispense).
Switch to Bottle B and dispense into a new MTU. Check for any abnormality.
RESOLUTION:
Ensure the solenoid wiring is securely attached to the PCB connector.
Tighten fitting connectors on the valve.
Replace valve if identified as defective.
Replace Pump if identified as defective.
TEST:
Verify prime in Service Software.
Perform Prime in Panther.
Defective Magnetic Wash Station Solenoid Valve
Using Service Software prime the oil into an MTU in both MagWash stations. Check for any abnormality (no liquid dispensed).
RESOLUTION:
Replace the defective solenoid valve.
TEST:
Verify prime in Service Software.
Perform Prime in Panther.

## FDF3 – Auto Detect 1 Dispense Failure Detected
id="mc-main-content">
FDF3 – Auto Detect 1 Dispense Failure Detected
Description
Fluid Dispense Failure – Auto Detect X dispense failure was detected.
Technical Support
Leakage on Connection
If only affected one sample in the run, continue processing.
If frequent or recurring, check to be sure the Auto Detect bottle connection and tubing, and the straw is connected to the cap.
Incorrect Tubing/Connection
Check to be sure the Auto Detect bottle connection and tubing are properly connected.
Field Service
Inventory Mismatch
Check AD inventory
Check bottle cap connections
Using Service Software dispense the AD into an MTU (default is Bottle A). Check for any abnormality (foam, or uneven dispense).
Switch to Bottle B and dispense into a new MTU. Check for any abnormality.
RESOLUTION:
Tighten fitting connectors
Replace bottle cap and straw if identified as defective
Replace valve if identified as defective
TEST:
Perform Prime in Panther
Auto Detect Pump
Follow tubing and fitting connections between AD bottles and the injector.
Using Service Software dispense the AD into an MTU. Check for any abnormality (foam, or uneven dispense).
RESOLUTION:
Replace defective component
TEST:
Perform Prime in Panther
A/B Valve on Universal Fluid Drawer
Using Service Software dispense the AD into an MTU (default is Bottle A). Check for any abnormality (foam, or uneven dispense).
Switch to Bottle B and dispense into a new MTU. Check for any abnormality.
RESOLUTION:
Ensure the solenoid wiring is securely attached to the PCB connector.
Tighten fitting connectors on the valve.
Replace valve if identified as defective.
Replace Pump if identified as defective.
TEST:
Perform Prime in Panther
Damaged Fitting or Tubing in the fluid line from the bottle to the injector
Follow the tubing between AD bottles and the injector.
Using Service Software, dispense the AD into an MTU (default is Bottle A). Check for any abnormality (leaking from any fitting or tubing).
RESOLUTION:
Tighten fitting connectors.
Replace any defective tubing or fitting.
Replace Pump if identified as defective.
TEST:

Occlusion in the fluid line from the bottles through the injector
Follow the tubing between AD bottles and the injector.
Using Service Software dispense the AD into an MTU (default is Bottle A). Check for any abnormality (no liquid dispensed).
RESOLUTION:
Flush lines with warm water.
Replace any defective tubing or fitting.
Replace Pump if identified as defective.

## FLSOR – Fluorometer Has an Off-Target Error
id="mc-main-content">
FLSOR – Fluorometer Has an Off-Target Error
Assay Processing Flag: FLSOR
Complaint Description
AMP incubator
Flag: FLSOR
FLSOR flag affects all assays, as it is difficult to decouple firmware on/off target check during assay processing.
Technical Support
Auto Dispatch FLSOR (fluorometer has an off-target error) as a Severity 2. Dispatch as a Severity 1 if customer only runs Real-Time assay. Perform troubleshooting as normal. If instrument restart is successful, customer may process TMA and Fusion assay samples. Inform customers not to run Real-Time assays until service is provided.
Troubleshooting:
-
Restart the instrument.
Field Service
Log Review
Keyword: Off-Target | On -Target
2019-12-12
23:14:05,101|[ProcessEvent]|SpecialInformationHandling|ProcessManagement|Info|Error|Off-Target measurement problem started for Rtf2 channel 5
Rtf2 channel 5 = RTF 677, 5th LED having issues.
From logs, determine if range exceeds high or low end...
filter for >>> CommandID=0x99 >>> ignore other commands (e.g. 0xa6)!
2019-12-16
13:32:09,701|[ProcessEvent]|SpecialInformationHandling|ProcessManagement|Info|Normal|Received target data: RTFTargetDataEvent - Device=Incubator3 CommandID=0x99 Severity=Message EventID=0x0 original sender=0x22 time=107541 RTF=RTF2 selectedChannel=0 LED=3 MessageID=4603 Result=249
RTF = RTF2 // RTF = fluorometer installed RTF1,2,3,4,5,6
selectedChannel=0 // measurement location on target or off target, 0 = off target, 1 = RTF 1 on target, 2 = RTF 2 on target, etc.
LED=3 // led is tube# or channel in array.
MessageID=4603 //ignore
Result=249 //fluorometer reading
Off target values should coincide with nominal ranges during install.
Inspect ranges in FW:
RTF ranges are defined using parameters 34, 35, 36, 37.
This Regex returns par.22, 34, 35,36,37 >>> FWP: Rtf[1-6]: (22|(3[4-7]))
RTF1
P00022d=0, rfu offset
P00034d=600, max on target
P00035d=5, min on target
P00036d=300, max off target
P00037d=0, min off target
RTF2
P00034d=5000
P00035d=5
P00036d=600
P00037d=0
RTF3
P00034d=5800
P00035d=200
P00036d=2260
P00037d=0
RTF4 and RTF6
currently not implemented by HOLX as of IS 6.2.1.8
RTF5
P00022d=0
P00034d=550
P00035d=5
P00036d=300
P00037d=0
If FW values do not match, run IS again.
Zip folders:
c:\Stratec
c:\Panther\Panther Service Software\Logs\session
Upload to EFT.
If FW values match, then proceed to ssw:
-
Initialize RTFs and perform single RTF measure test. e.g. this is same measurment to verify RTF is within range when installing RTFs.
-
If 1 is okay, verify if target/off target slot error by introducing MTU into Amp incubator.
-
- Move slot 1 to door position.
-
- Pick MTU from IQ and place in AMP incubator (use MTU sensor to verify mtu picked and placed).
-
- Move slot 1 to RTF# in question.
-
- Perform read and check measurements. check behavior is as expected note: MTU doesn't fluoresce for all fluorometers.
-
DO NOT FLIP/INVERT - AMP incubator in the event debris landed on the fluorometer. Remove fluorometer and inspect for debris.
- If debris found, attempt to capture and return debris to San Diego. Run ssw check again.
- If no debris found, likely RTF failure. Also return to San Diego.

## HB – Luminometer High Background
id="mc-main-content">
HB – Luminometer High Background
Error Code
Dec
Hex
098.000.00xxx
Complaint Description
High Background (HB) flags are caused when the reading before the Auto Detects are dispensed (aka Dark Count) is too high.
Technical Support
Check Bleach and Wash Connections in the Universal Fluids Drawer
Check if the Bleach and Wash fluid connectors were swapped in the Universal Fluids Drawer.
If swapped, correct the line orientation and force three full primes.
Review Logs
Review Results Reports for patterns in the run or reagent prep related issues such as probe gradient.
Review logs for the Dark Count values.
- Open the FlashCurve file in CurveTrends.
- Scroll sideways to the Dark Count column.
- Review the Dark Count values.
- General Values:
- Normal: 100-500
- Borderline: 600-900
- High: 1000+
- Upper Limit for HB flags:
- AC2: 1000
- HPV: 1200
- HPV GT: 1500
- If Dark Count values are high, notify FSEs.
Next Steps
Review cases history for previous High Background errors. Notify FSE Field Service Engineer. is there were recent cases.
Instruct customer to monitor.
Field Service
Injector Light Leak
Using Service Software perform a 2 second Dark Count check with the shutter closed then with shutter open (an MTU should be present in the lumo in any position 1-5 for this test). If the dark count is only high >500) with the shuttler open then a light leak is the problem. This could be at the injector (most likely) or in the lumo case. Look for damage or gaps in the black sleeve over the injector. Look for cracks in the injector.
Resolution:
Replace injector.
Test:
In SSW perform the 2 second Dark Count with and without an MTU.
Monitor customer runs.
Bad PMT
Using Service Software perform a 2 second Dark Count check with the shutter closed then with shutter open (an MTU should be present in the lumo in any position 1-5 for this test). If the dark count is high with and without an MTU present, even with the shutter closed, then it is a bad PMT.
Resolution:
Replace the PMT.
Test:
In SSW perform the 2 second Dark Count with and without an MTU.
Monitor customer runs.
Luminometer Casing Light Leak
Using Service Software perform a 2 second Dark Count check with the shutter closed then with shutter open (an MTU should be present in the lumo in any position 1-5 for this test). If the dark count is only high >500) with the shuttler open then a light leak is the problem. If the injector is not the source of the light leak, look for loose or cracked casing parts, such as the lid not being secured or a crack in the lid.
Resolution:
Secure loose casing.
Replace the Luminometer.
Test:
In Service Software, perform the two-second Dark Count with and without an MTU.
Monitor customer runs.

## IDF – Incubator Door Failure
id="mc-main-content">
IDF – Incubator Door Failure
Assay Processing Flag
Description
Incubator Door Failure – Accompanied by associated module Event ID: 032.01.00121 for Incubator 1 (High Temperature), 033.001.00121 for Incubator 2 (Transition), and 034.01.00121 for Incubator 3 (Amp).
Tier 1
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support/Customer Action
Reference
- Mechanical obstruction that prevents the Incubator door from closing properly
Instruct the customer to complete the following steps:
- Restart the instrument and allow the system to unload MTUs.
- Wait to see if the error recurs.
- Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem and will require an FSE Field Service Engineer. service call.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual
- Faulty/dirty sensor
- Faulty door board PCB
- Distributor/Incubator misalignment that causes poor MTU placement
FSE
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Mechanical obstruction that prevents the Incubator door from closing properly
- Diagnose and remove obstruction.
- Faulty/dirty sensor
- Faulty door board PCB
- Distributor/Incubator misalignment that causes poor MTU placement

## IFF1 – Incubator 1 Fan Failure
id="mc-main-content">
IFF1 – Incubator 1 Fan Failure
Assay Processing Flag
Description
Incubator Fan Failure – At Incubator 1 (High Temperature). Accompanied by associated module Event ID: 032.001.00117 .
Tier 1
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support/Customer Action
Reference
Faulty Incubator fan system
Instruct the customer to complete the following steps:
- Restart the instrument and allow the system to unload MTUs.
- Wait an hour to see if the error quickly recurs during start-up.
- If the error recurs during start-up, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual
FSE
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Fan RPM is outside specified range/fan RPM failure
- Remove the Incubator cover.
- Verify the fan impeller moves smoothly.
- If there is undue friction, the fan is faulty.
- Replace the Incubator fan.
- See Incubator Fan Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- Faulty cable/cable to fan
- Remove the Incubator cover.
- Inspect the fan connections.
- Diagnose the integrity of the connections and resolve accordingly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual
- Wrong Incubator fan is installed
- Remove the Incubator cover to expose the fan Part Number.
- The the P/N for the correct fan for Incubator 1 (High Temperature) is PMD2412PTB1-A11.8W .
- If the wrong fan is installed, remove and replace with the correct fan.
- See Incubator Fan Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- Fan is connected to the wrong port on the Incubator Main PCB.
- Remove the Upper Bay Front Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB.
- Connect the fan to the correct port on the PCB, labeled PWR fan .
- See Upper Bay Front Cover Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- See Incubator Main PCB Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .

## ITF1 – Incubator 1 Thermistor Failure
id="mc-main-content">
ITF1 – Incubator 1 Thermistor Failure
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Incubator Thermistor Failure – The Incubator 1 (High Temperature) dual thermistors have exceeded the allowable range. Accompanied by associated module Event ID: 032.001.00122 .
Tier 1
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support/Customer Action
Reference
Incubator temperature sensor failure
Instruct the customer to complete the following steps:
- Restart the instrument and allow the system to unload MTUs.
- Wait to see if the error quickly recurs during start-up.
- If the error quickly recurs during start-up, the error is not intermittent. Dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- If the error recurs within an hour after startup, dispatch an FSE.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual
FSE
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
Firmware not upgraded
- Upgrade to 3.2.2.18 (SP2) or higher, if applicable
- See Installing Firmware in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- Faulty Incubator Door PCB
- Using Service Software, initialize the failed Incubator.
- Observe the Temperature Difference of the Incubator and verify the difference remains less than 0.5 °C.
- Replace the Incubator Door PCB.
- See Starting Service Software in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- See Incubator Door PCB Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- Faulty cable/connection between the Incubator Door PCB and the Main PCB.
- Remove the front panel to expose the Incubator Main PCB.
- Remove the Incubator cover and fan to expose the Door PCB.
- Inspect/reseat wires and connections between the Incubator Door PCB and the Main PCB.
- Correct the faulty connections, if possible. Otherwise, replace the Incubator Door PCB.
- See Upper Bay Front Cover Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- See Incubator Fan Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- See Incubator Door PCB Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .

- Faulty Incubator Door PCB
- Using Service Software, initialize the failed Incubator.
- Observe the Temperature Difference of the Incubator and verify the difference remains less than 0.5 °C.
- Replace the Incubator Door PCB.
- See Starting Service Software in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- See Incubator Door PCB Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- Faulty cable/connection between the Incubator Door PCB and the Main PCB.
- Remove the front panel to expose the Incubator Main PCB.
- Remove the Incubator cover and fan to expose the Door PCB.
- Inspect/reseat wires and connections between the Incubator Door PCB and the Main PCB.
- Correct the faulty connections, if possible. Otherwise, replace the Incubator Door PCB.
- See Upper Bay Front Cover Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- See Incubator Fan Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
- See Incubator Door PCB Removal and Replacement in the PANTHER System Service Manual .
