## ML2 – Liquid Level Sense Too High After Wash Dispense
id="mc-main-content">
ML2 – Liquid Level Sense Too High After Wash Dispense
ML2 – Assay Processing Flag
Error Codes
Magnetic Wash 1
Magnetic Wash 2
Dec
Hex
Dec
Hex
048.000.00040
0x30.0x00x0.28
049.000.00040
031.0x00x0.28
Complaint Description
Magnetic Wash Level 2 reported a liquid level sense too high after wash dispense.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
- Possible Root Causes
- Troubleshooting
Field Service
- Vacuum System Shutdown
- Low Vacuum Pressure
- Clogged Aspirators
- Damaged Magnetic Wash Station Vacuum Tubes
- Air Bubbles or Foam Built Up During Wash Dispense
- Anomalous Signal Spikes Caused By a Sporadic Bubble in the Wash
- Wash Pump Dispense Inaccuracy
- Clogged Aspirators Due to Incorrect Proteinase K
Technical Support
Possible Root Causes
-
Low vacuum pressure
-
MagWash aspirator clogged
-
Air bubbles or foaming built up during wash dispense
-
Bad wash pump or Faulty MagWash
Troubleshooting
-
Troubleshoot for low vacuum.
-
Perform back-to-back MagWash clean.
-
If the error repeats, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
To troubleshoot ML2 errors that occur during an Aptima qCMV assay run:
-
Confirm whether ML2 error occurred during a qCMV run.
-
Document sample type (plasma, whole blood, or other?).
-
Ask customer to perform back-to-back MagWash cleanings.
-
Recommend customer not to retest the ML2 flagged sample(s), as this could cause repeat errors (one or both MW stations out of service) per CTB-01171.
-
Invalid samples due to MOS (MW Station out of service), or any other processing flag are not impacted, and should be retested per the package insert.
-
If MagWash cleaning fails, or if one or both MW stations are out of service, or if customer requests, dispatch an engineer.
-
Collect logs.
-
Escalate case to QA, and notify appropriate internal teams.
-
Inform customer that someone from Hologic may follow up to obtain additional sample or patient-related information.
Possible root cause: sample related issue.
Field Service
Vacuum System Shutdown
During some fatal errors, the vacuum system shuts down, but the Magnetic Wash stations complete their cycles. Without vacuum, those tests will fail process control checks.
Resolution
-
Check the Messages screen, Diagnostic Log and/or Eventlog Entry file for critical or fatal errors that immediately preceded this code.
-
Resolve the issue that caused the original problem.
Low Vacuum Pressure
Low vacuum pressure may cause an overfill of the MTU tube.
Resolution
Refer to Vacuum Pressure Errors section.
Clogged Aspirators
Clogged aspirators will cause an overfill of MTU tube, possibly due to highlighted cotton pile.
Resolution
-
Perform an automated Magnetic Wash Cleaning procedure.
-
Perform a prime for the system.
Test
Observe whether any additional errors are displayed.
Damaged Magnetic Wash Station Vacuum Tubes
The clamps holding the vacuum tubes onto the aspirators sometimes damage the tubes.
-
Check the tubes for crimps or pinches.
-
Check the tubes for cracks or distortions around the metal clip that holds the tubes to the aspirators.
Resolution
-
Replace the vacuum tubes. If the vacuum tubes are not immediately available, perform steps 2–4 until the vacuum tubes can be replaced.
-
Pull of the metal clamps.
-
Using a razor, cut approximately 2 cm from the bottom of the vacuum tubes.
-
Re-seat the clamps onto the freshly cut porting of the tubing.
-
Carefully re-install the tubes into the aspirators.
Air Bubbles or Foam Built Up During Wash Dispense
Anomalous signal spikes caused by a sporadic bubble in the wash. This could be the cause if the error is sporadic and none of the above conditions are present.
Resolution
Replace the faulty injector, if possible.
Test
-
In Service Software, perform a Visual Dispense Verification.
-
Check for the presence of foam or bubbles in the wash.
Anomalous Signal Spikes Caused By a Sporadic Bubble in the Wash
Note: This could be the cause if the error is sporadic and none of the above conditions are present.
Resolution
-
Check all fittings for leaks.
-
Tighten all wash injection fittings from the bottle to the Magnetic Wash Station Module.
Wash Pump Dispense Inaccuracy
A bad Wash Pump may cause an over-dispense in one or more tubes.
Resolution
-
Calibrate the Wash Pump.
-
Replace the Wash Pump.
-
Replace the Magnetic Wash Station.
Test
-
In Service Software, perform a Visual Dispense Verification.
-
Check to see if fluid levels are even across all five tubes.
Clogged Aspirators Due to Incorrect Proteinase K
Proteinase K is used in the Fusion LDT assays. When the customer uses the incorrect type of Proteinase K, it will cause gelling and clogging in the MagWash aspirators. Symptoms include frequent clogs, in both MagWashes, and random aspirators. In this case, it could easily be traced to the LDT:
Date
Assay
MLS/MOS
3/24
LDT-QCMV UNCAP
Y
3/25
qHIV
N
3/25
LDT-QCMV UNCAP
Y
4/04
qHCV
N
4/04
qHBV
N
4/04
LDT-QCMV UNCAP
Y
4/06
SARSCoV2
N
4/06
qHIV
N
4/06
LDT-QCMV UNCAP
Y
Resolution
-
Instruct the customer to review our package insert. Customer should be using Proteinase K, Qiagen Cat No 19131.
-
Run MagWash Advance Clean.
-
Clean affected aspirators with fishing line, as necessary.
Test
-
In Service Software, perform a Visual Dispense Verification.
-
Reinsert the MTU in the MagWash, and aspirate fluid. Verify all fluid is aspirated.

## ML3 – Liquid Level Sense Too Low After Wash Dispense – Magnetic Wash Level 3
id="mc-main-content">
ML3 – Liquid Level Sense Too Low After Wash Dispense – Magnetic Wash Level 3
ML3 – Assay Processing Flag
Error Codes
Magnetic Wash 1
Magnetic Wash 2
Dec
Hex
Dec
Hex
048.000.00041
0x30.0x00x0.29
049.000.00041
0x31.0x00x0.029
Complaint Description
Magnetic Wash station failed a fluid level check, due to liquid level too low after wash buffer was dispensed.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Possible root causes
- Troubleshooting
-
Field Service
- Kinks in fluid tubing
- Missing, disconnected, or cracked aspirator tube (straw) inside bottle
- Leaky or disconnected fluid fittings
- Aspirators not sufficiently tightened
- Faulty Solenoid Valve
- Poorly aimed wash injectors
- Improperly routed Wash Injector nozzles
- Wash Pump dispense accuracy
- TSE Review
Technical Support
Possible root causes
- Empty or disconnected Wash Bottle
- Kinks in wash fluid tubing
- Missing, disconnected, or cracked straw inside wash bottle
- Bad wash pump most likely if both MagWash showing ML3 error
- Faulty MagWash
Troubleshooting
- Check wash buffer bottle caps and connections are clean and intact.
- Straighten kinked tubing.
- Replace Empty Wash bottle.
- Tighten/Replace straw inside wash bottle.
- If the error repeats, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
Kinks in fluid tubing
- Open the Universal Fluids Drawer and look for any kinks in the fluid lines.
- Open the right-side access panel and look for any kinks in the fluid lines.
Resolution
Straighten any kinked tubing.
Missing, disconnected, or cracked aspirator tube (straw) inside bottle
- Verify that the aspirator tube is present in the bottle cap/fitting assembly and is not cracked.
- Replace the aspirator tube in the cap assembly or order a new cap assembly.
Resolution
- Empty wash bottle. Inventory control can sometimes be circumvented during various service procedures.
- Check to be sure there is fluid in the wash bottles.
- Replace the Universal Fluids Kit, if necessary.
Leaky or disconnected fluid fittings
Leaky or disconnected fluid fittings will cause low fluid levels in the Magnetic Wash Station.
- Look for the presence of air bubbles in the lines.
- Check to see that the bottle fittings are connected.
Resolution
- Look for the presence of any fluid leaks.
- Tighten, connect, or replace fittings as necessary.
Aspirators not sufficiently tightened
Aspirators not sufficiently tightened to make good electrical connection to the Magnetic Wash Station LLS PCB.
Resolution
- Use a 4.5 mm wrench to check for any loose aspirators.
- Carefully tighten any loose aspirators.
Faulty Solenoid Valve
Ensure that the solenoid wiring is securely attached to the PCB connector.
Resolution
Replace the solenoid.
Test
Verify that the solenoid valve is properly switching between bottle A and B.
Poorly aimed wash injectors
Poorly aimed wash injectors that dispense fluid outside the MTU.
- In Service Software, perform a Visual Dispense Verification.
- Look for the presence of fluid on the outside of the MTU tube.
Resolution
- Re-align the problematic injector, if possible.
- Otherwise, replace the Magnetic Wash Station.
Improperly routed Wash Injector nozzles
Injectors have been installed onto the wrong location and fill the wrong tube of the MTU.
- In Service Software, perform a Visual Dispense Verification.
- Look to see if fluid is injected into the correct tube.
Resolution
- Re-route the problematic injector, if possible.
- Otherwise, replace the Magnetic Wash Station.
Wash Pump dispense accuracy
A bad Wash Pump can cause an under-dispense in one or more tubes.
- In Service Software, perform a Visual Dispense Verification.
- Look at how even the fluid level is across all fiver tubes.
- Observe and note whether the ambient temperature has had large recent fluctuations or has been outside the 15–30 °C range.
Resolution
- Re-calibrate the Wash Pump.
- If necessary, replace the Wash Pump. If the Wash Pump serial number is -276 or lower, replace the pump regardless.
TSE Review
Acceptable range of mag wash volume is 0.8ml -1.2ml.
ML3 = when MW detects less than 0.8ml.
Based on the image, tube 0 looks okay for now.
Also, when MW pump is replaced the fitting should be replaced at the same time as a precaution.
Do not use wrench and do not over torque.
Once a fitting is damaged, it can damage a new pump.
The fitting on the right broke 2 MW pumps before the fitting was replaced.

id="mc-main-content">
MT1 – Aspirators Not Functioning at the Start of the Wash Cycle
MT1 – Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Aspirators not functioning at the start of the wash cycle. This may be due to a hardware problem or defective MTU.
Technical Support
Operator Error
Visually inspect the area around the Input Queue and Lower Bay for stray tiplets. A hasty user may cause tips to fall out of the MTUs during loading.
RESOLUTION:
- Visually inspect the area around the Input Queue and Lower Bay for stray tiplets.
- Train the user to load MTUs carefully, and to check for stray tiplets.
Field Service
Operator error
Visually inspect the area around the Input Queue and Lower Bay for stray tiplets. A hasty user may cause tips to fall out of the MTUs during loading.
RESOLUTION:
- Visually inspect the area around the Input Queue and Lower Bay for stray tiplets.
- Train the user to load MTUs carefully and to check for stray tiplets.
Service Drawer not fully engaged
Check to see if the Service Drawer is fully closed.
RESOLUTION:
Close the Service Drawer.
Improperly Taught Distributor may place the MTU improperly
Check Distributor teaching at the Magnetic Wash Station.
RESOLUTION:
Teach the Distributor.
Improperly Installed Module may allow the MTU to be placed improperly
- Check for improperly installed module.
- Look at the front-lower foot of the Magnetic Wash Station Module.
- Observe whether the module is fully seated onto the alignment pin.
RESOLUTION:
Loosen the 4 mm screw on the top of the Magnetic Wash Station Module, then re-seat the module onto the alignment pin.

## PCL1 – Auto Detect 1 and PCL2 – Auto Detect 2
id="mc-main-content">
PCL1 – Auto Detect 1 and PCL2 – Auto Detect 2
Auto Detect Process Control Failure
Complaint Description
Process control failure for Auto Detects.
Note: Refer to AD1 and AD2 – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves > Process Control Data: Luminometer .
Technical Support
Check Auto Detect Bottles in the Universal Fluids Drawer
Check the Auto Detect 1 bottles for PCL1 flags.
Check the Auto Detect 2 bottles for PCL2 flags.
Empty Bottle
Check to make sure there is fluid in the bottles.
Replace the empty Auto Detect bottle. The entire Fluids kit, A or B, must be replaced.
Disconnected Bottle
Verify the quick-connect fitting is connected to the bottle.
Connect the fitting.
Bottle Cap Connectors are crusty or crystalized
Check for crust or crystal formation on bottle cap connectors.
Clean cap connectors with DI water.
Send replacement caps if needed.
Prime the instrument and check for air bubbles in the detect fluid line after prime.
Missing or Defective Bottle Fitting O-Ring
Verify o-rings on the male fitting are intact.
Inform FSE Field Service Engineer. if damaged or missing.
Missing, disconnected, or cracked straw inside the bottle
Verify that the straw is present in the bottle cap/fitting assembly and is not loose or cracked.
Send replacement straw assembly.
Refer customer to CTB-00256 for bottle straw replacement procedure.
Review Logs
Review Luminometer Curves in logs. Compare Normal to Abnormal curves. Troubleshoot accordingly. [insert link to curves]
If the site is at an altitude >2000’ (600m) and the Luminometer Curves show pullback approaching 3000, inform the FSE.
Next Steps
Review case history for previous PCL errors. Notify FSE if there were recent cases.
Instruct customer to monitor.
Field Service
Empty Bottle
Verify the AD bottles contain fluid. [insert links to Normal and Air curves]
Resolution:
Replace Auto Detect if necessary.
Test:
Perform Prime in Panther
Disconnected Bottle
Verify the quick-connect fitting is connected to the Auto Detect bottles.
Resolution:
Connect the bottle fitting.
Test:
Perform prime in Panther.
Bottle Cap Connectors are Crusty or Crystalized
Check for crust or crystal formation on the bottle cap connectors.
Resolution:
Clean the caps with DI water.
Replace the connectors if necessary.
Test:
Prime the instrument and check for air bubbles in the detect line after prime.
Missing, disconnected, or cracked straw inside the bottle
Verify that the straw is present in the bottle cap/fitting assembly and is not loose or cracked.
Resolution:
Replace the bottle straw.
Test:
Perform Prime in Panther.
Leaky Fitting, Fluid Line, pump, or valve
Check for leaks at all fittings, fluid lines, the pump, and the solenoid valve in the fluid path (from the Auto Detect bottles to the injector).
Resolution:
Correct the leak. Replace parts as needed.
Test:
Prime lines and verify no leak.
Kinks in the fluid tubing
Inspect all Detect fluid lines for a kink.
Resolution:
Straighten or replace any kinked tubing.
Test:
Perform Prime in Panther.
Faulty OLV Sensor Circuit Board
Plot the OLV sensor traces. If the trace has a near zero signal, the PCB may be faulty. [insert links to Normal and OLV LED Failure curves]
Inspect the PCB for moisture and/or dried fluid deposits.
RESOLUTION:
Replace PCB.
TEST:
Verify prime in Service Software and plot the traces.
Perform Prime in Panther.
Luminometer Injector
Plot the OLV sensor traces and compare against normal. [insert link to Good vs Bad Curves for AD]
Check for kinks in the injector fluid lines.
Check the affected AD pump connections are not under or over tightened.
Check the affected AD pump ports are not cracked.
Verify the OLV sight holes in the injector are clear and free of debris.
Inspect the injector housing for cracks or leaks.
Resolution:
Tighten fittings.
Replace injectors.
Replace pump if found to be defective.
Check screws on Luminometer lid and tighten if necessary.
Replace Luminometer if injector housing is compromised.
Test:
Perform Prime in Panther
Run Flashcheck
Delayed Dispense
Confirm site altitude – if over 2000 ft (600m) elevation pumps are replaced with vacuum sealed pumps at install.
Confirm temperature in lab is within specifications (15°C – 30°C).
Plot OLV sensor traces. (Insert link to Good vs Bad curves for ADs.)
Resolution:
If OLV curve shows the transition from air to liquid or from liquid to air is delayed, replace the pump. (If errors occurring on initial installation and site is at altitude above 2000 ft (600m) – replace both AD pumps.)
Test:
Confirm OLV curves in Service Software are normal.
Perform Prime in Panther.
Run Flashcheck.
A/B Valve on Universal Fluid Drawer
Using Service Software prime the affected Auto Detect into an MTU (default is Bottle A). Check for any abnormality (bubbles, or uneven dispense).
Switch to Bottle B and dispense into a new MTU. Check for any abnormality.
Resolution:
Ensure the solenoid wiring is securely attached to the PCB connector.
Tighten fitting connectors on the valve.
Replace valve if identified as defective.
Test:
Verify prime in Service Software.
Perform Prime in Panther.
Run Flashcheck.

## QNS—Quantity Not Sufficient in Sample Tube
id="mc-main-content">
QNS—Quantity Not Sufficient in Sample Tube
Uncapped / Open Tube – Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
QNS = quantity not sufficient in the sample tube.
QNS requires level sense, so it only applies to open tube (uncapped) work flows.
QNS will be applied to the test order when fluid level is too low in sample tube, which is measured at the sample bay.
It is normal for LLDHeight associated with QNS to be greater than a successful aspiration. The reason for this is due to implementation: during assay processing, pipettor aspiration and level sense commands are tied together.
Pipettor will detect level of fluid and immediately determine if enough fluid is present:
- Not enough fluid, then immediately report height of detected fluid. Aspiration is cancelled.
- Enough fluid, then report final position of pipettor at the end of aspiration.
Data should be generated as follows:
-
C-LLD curve file, as sensor is turned on as pipettor moves towards fluid.
-
Based on detection result, fluid height is checked by software and recorded in both:
- C-LLD
- LLDHeight
-
Aspiration curve file, if fluid level was acceptable.
QNS failure modes
- Insufficient fill volume
- Too many replicates assigned to sample
- Damaged tip, inconsistent tip length or non-conductive
- Pipettor teach
QNS - fill volume
She is using the open cap workflow, and they pipette the lysis buffer and sample into the tube. She mentioned that they look at the samples, and volume looks okay. This happened the other day too, with a different operator, so she doubts it is pipetting issue.
Samples with QNS flag are here (see bold circles below), which seem to be in the middle of those that are acceptable.
If one looks, there are samples which are showing lower, and they are not flagged. Can someone explain this?
Answer: Liquid level height is reported as follows:
1. If detected liquid level meets software minimum acceptable volume, then report final pipette position after aspiration is completed.
2. If detected liquid level is less than software minimum acceptable volume, then report detected volume.
Looking at the following table, sorting by LldHeight:
All of the LldPositive values are reporting final pipette position AFTER aspiration of sample.
While the NotEnoughLiquid is reporting the liquid level BEFORE aspiration occurs.
Inspecting the LldHeight closely, software is likely using 106 as the cutoff as LLDResult = NotEnoughLiquid is reported with LLDHeight = 105.
Scrolling through the remaining values, the lowest reported LldHeight value is 7.
For this assay version, build the inferred minimum amount of liquid aspirated from the sample tube in steps is 106 -7 = 99.
That means fluid is detected around 99 steps above the reported LLDHeight for LLDPositive results.
Also, I note that samples are checked twice. Please see the associated error in messages. What are the actual checks that are performed in the sample tube? Note: I also see that in many cases, the sample is retested, and gets a valid result afterwards (see run report attached). Can someone shed any light on this?
Lastly, here are the c-lld curves for TCR and sample, in case this assists. C-lld for TCR looks fine, so likely not instrument HWF…
Here is the c-lld for SARS samples. I am noticing that each sample has two curves (see example in second curve below).
Any assistance understanding this would be great. How are we supposed to say whether issue is instrument, or volume too low? One thing we can ask is that they are using correct tubes, that is, according to the specs, as this might make a difference.
ALL SARS samples
Liquid level height is reported as follows:
- If detected liquid level meets software minimum acceptable volume, then report final pipette position after aspiration is completed.
- If detected liquid level is less than software minimum acceptable volume, then report detected volume.
Looking at the following table, sorting by LldHeight:
All of the LldPositive values are reporting final pipette position AFTER aspiration of sample.
While the NotEnoughLiquid is reporting the liquid level BEFORE aspiration occurs.
Inspecting the LldHeight closely, Software is likely using 106 as the minimum required LldHeight.
The lowest LldHeight value is 7.
This suggests the amount of liquid aspirated for the sample reaction is 106-7 = 99.
So for LldHeight for LldPositive results, the actual detected liquid level height BEFORE sample is aspirated is approximately 99 steps higher than reported.
Also, there will be some error in measurement – this mean the NotEnoughLiquid = 105 is measured say 5 times can give a range from 10 steps [0.5mm] (due to minute differences in tip length, software timing, motor/pipette meshing). In other words, that is the likely reason running the sample again, the instrument is able to pipette the sample.
- C-lld traces looks the way they do because the “C-LLD” graph doesn’t break out the Aspirate v Dispense measurements. Also, the measurements are performed roughly 12 seconds apart.
There are two sets of C-LLD curves, because for the uncapped work flow, the Sample pipettor does two cLLDs for each sample - the first one is in the sample tube before aspiration, and the second one is after the dispense in the MTU. The smaller group on the left is the level senses after dispense in the MTU. The other set is the level sense in the Sample Tube.
- I agree, the TCR c-lld traces look good, which means not a HW issue. And yes, tube variation and different pipette tips can affect volume.
Question, did customer inspect volume before loading sample on, or after running sample on the instrument?
Because if inspected after running sample on the instrument, it would be difficult to tell.
Using the rough 99 steps is pipetted volume suggests customer would be looking for roughly 5mm difference in fill volume.
QNS - too many replicates
For this customer, inspection of LLDValues curve file showed multiple test orders assigned to same sample ID.
Sample ID is a unique tube identifier and customer is not running samples with same barcode.
Sample ID = 11111, has five test orders 134,147,160,161 and 187 assigned.
When LldResultType = LldPositive , aspiration step is performed and LldHeight is reflects after fluid has been aspirated.
When LldResultType = NotEnoughLiquid, QNS flag is assigned and aspiration not performed.
Correct by setting appropriate number of replicates:
Technical Support
Sample Tube Empty
Resolution
-
Check intended sample replicates matches setting in software.
-
Inspect fluid volume in sample tube with QNS errors.
- Customer inspection of QNS sample tube against sample tubes with no errors, verify fluid.
- Inspect LLDvalues curve file.
-
Check tips:
- Approved tips
-
Damaged tips

- Inspect tip packaging for damage.
- Inspect sample bay cover causing bent tips.
Test
Verify QNS issue has been resolved by running new samples.
Field Service
- Check sample bay cover.
- Save coordinate.coo file and verify pipettor sample bay teach points.
- Correct teach and transfer coordinates.
- Verify QNS issues has been resolved by running new samples.

## RBEA, RBEE, RBEP, RBESL
id="mc-main-content">
RBEA, RBEE, RBEP, RBESL
Assay Processing Flags
Complaint Description
Topic covers troubleshooting procedures for these Assay Processing Flags:
- RBEA – Reagent Bottle Empty Amp – the Amp Reagent bottle is empty.
- RBEE – Reagent Bottle Empty Enzyme – the Enzyme Reagent bottle is empty.
- RBEP – Reagent Bottle Empty Probe – the Probe Reagent bottle is empty.
- RBESL – Reagent Bottle Empty Selection – the Selection Reagent bottle is empty.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Questions for customer
- How to review logs
- Possible causes of RBEE
- Q & A
-
Field Service
- RBEA, RBEE, RBEP, RBESL
Technical Support
Questions for customer
- How many times was the kit used? The more times kit was loaded/unloaded, the higher the chance reagent was lost in between runs.
- Was the reagent spilled?
- How does customer pop bubbles? Recommend to use non-absorptive end of swab.
- Low lab humidity? (high altitude, cold area)
- Logs are needed to verify the issue. Ask for logs for every day the kit was used.
How to review logs
Pipettor issue? Check c-LLD curves.
Reagent issue? Check LLDvalues curves.
RBEE in the middle of the run? Enzyme reagent is probably not really empty.
RBEE at end of the run? Enzyme is probably close to empty.
Possible causes of RBEE
-
Initial kit volume on the lower end of the valid range (due to popping bubbles, spilling, not allowing all reagent to poor in recon bottle).
100 kit
250 kit
TCR
~398 steps
~496
steps
RT:05
Amp
~1115 steps
~1091
steps
RT:16
Enz
~634 steps
~ 516 steps
RT: 17
Probe
~1267 steps
~1384 steps
RT: 18
Select
~749 steps
~1068 steps
RT: 04
In the example below, the LLDheight for the new SarsCov2 TMA run is too low (460). The LLDheight should have been around 516 (in most cases, usually above 480 is pretty good).
-
Enzyme volume lost between runs (mixing, warming up, lost in grooves of cap).
Compare the LLDheight of the last use with the first use the next time kit was used.
-
A lot of MTUs have fewer than 5 samples/MTU.
Issue Description: The main problem is that for every MTU that gets processed, the total volume withdrawn is the reagent (enzyme =25 uL) plus an additional constant of 33 uL of “waste” volume.
Depending on the number of samples per MTU, the instrument will pipet: 1 sample/ MTU= 58 uL / 2 samples = 83ul / 3 samples = 108ul / 4 samples= 133ul / 5 samples = 158 ul.
So for every MTU, the instrument pipets an additional 33 ul, regardless of the number of samples in that MTU.
If this is done in too many MTU, that will eventually deplete the enzyme and cause RBEE towards the end of the kit.
Which curve to check? Refer to LLD Values, and Tube number column.
For example:
- 0,1,2,3,4 = 5 samples/ MTU
- 0,1 = 2 samples/per MTU
- 0 = 1 sample/MTU
Q & A
Q: There are RBEE towards the end of the run, but the last 2 - 3 samples are valid?
A: Usually that means there was enough enzyme for 2 - 3 samples, but not enough for an entire MTU with five samples.
Field Service
TSE Review
Below is some more data from the time the instrument reported RBEE flags and invalidated the reagent. It looks like you should have 28 remaining tests in the kit. The log entry below shows the time increments about 5 minutes between each attempt until failure at date : 2020-12-18 15:09:08,080

message : 12/18/2020 05:54:11 (18 14:54:11) [D] (Message , Info ) [InventoryManagement] Liquid level detected: lane=1, position in rack=2, reagent type=17, expected volume=2925 ul, fill height=132, lld status=LldPositive correlated volume=0. [262.000.00011]
date : 2020-12-18 14:54:11,827
message : Removed 5 tests (162 microliters) from the reagent Enzyme Reagent from kit 0 ardbid 92.New status: Reagent: Type/Code=Enzyme/17,RTP=18,RTR=43,RVP=2164,RVR=2925
date : 2020-12-18 14:59:11,940
message : Removed 5 tests (162 microliters) from the reagent Enzyme Reagent from kit 0 ardbid 92.New status: Reagent: Type/Code=Enzyme/17,RTP=18,RTR=38,RVP=2164,RVR=2763
date : 2020-12-18 15:04:11,928
message : Removed 5 tests (162 microliters) from the reagent Enzyme Reagent from kit 0 ardbid 92.New status: Reagent: Type/Code=Enzyme/17,RTP=18,RTR=33,RVP=2164,RVR=2601
date : 2020-12-18 15:09:08,080
message : Lower liquid level detected by reagent 'Enzyme Reagent' from kit 0 ardbid 92. New status: Reagent: Type/Code=Enzyme/17,RTP=18,RTR=0,RVP=2164,RVR=0.
Some suggestions:
- Service both pipettors as mentioned in my original email.
- Continue running, and record lost test count.
- Record kit and bottle id, submit complaint.
- Inspect fluid level of enzyme, before and after recon.

## RBET – Reagent Bottle Empty TCR
id="mc-main-content">
RBET – Reagent Bottle Empty TCR
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Reagent Bottle Empty TCR – The Sample Pipettor has detected the level of TCR is at or below the lowest allowable limit. The inventory is set to zero for this kit.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Bottle is empty
- Bottle is not seated completely
- Damaged or incorrect tips used
- Spill on Tip Drawers
- Sample Bay cover is not installed correctly
- Ask the Customer if the DiTi was cleaned or became wet due to Operator interference
-
Field Service
- Bottle is empty
- Bottle is not completely seated
- Damaged or incorrect tips used
- Spill on Tip Drawers
- Sample Bay cover is not installed correctly
- Ask the Customer if the DiTi was cleaned or became wet due to Operator interference
- Check Z-motor engagement
- Verify the DiTi is not wet
- DiTi Thumbscrew is not sealing completely
- Teaching to the TCR Carousel is Off
- DiTi O-ring Failure
-
Technical Support
- Bottle is empty
- Bottle is not seated completely
- Damaged or incorrect tips used
- Spill on Tip Drawers
- Sample Bay cover is not installed correctly
- Ask the Customer if the DiTi was cleaned or became wet due to Operator interference
-
Field Service
- Bottle is empty
- Bottle is not completely seated
- Damaged or incorrect tips used
- Spill on Tip Drawers
- Sample Bay cover is not installed correctly
- Ask the Customer if the DiTi was cleaned or became wet due to Operator interference
- Check Z-motor engagement
- Verify the DiTi is not wet
- DiTi Thumbscrew is not sealing completely
- Teaching to the TCR Carousel is Off
- DiTi O-ring Failure
Technical Support
Bottle is empty
Resolution
If the bottle is empty, reconstitute a new kit. The bottle may be empty due to a spill or leak.
Test
Verify the bottle is not empty.
Bottle is not seated completely
Resolution
Ensure the TCR bottle is fully seated in the TCR Carousel at the proper location for the loaded reagent rack.
Test
Verify that the bottle is fully seated in the TCR cup.
Damaged or incorrect tips used
Resolution
Ensure the tips are the correct type and have not been damaged.
Test
- Verify the tips are the correct type (eppendorf 1 mL Capacitive tips with filters).
- Verify the tips are not damaged.
Spill on Tip Drawers
Resolution
If a spill occurred on the Tip Trays, stop the instrument immediately — the Pipettor arms may already be damaged.
Test
Verify there is no evidence of a spill on the Tip Trays.
Sample Bay cover is not installed correctly
Resolution
Reinstall the Sample bay cover correctly.
Test
Verify the sample bay cover is installed properly and the tip does not come into contact with the cover during TCR aspiration.
Note: The sample tip can become occluded. If this happens, the barometric Liquid Level Detection (bLLD) of TCR will not be able to sense a state change (outside liquid to inside liquid) and will then drive to the maximum pipettor depth, setting the TCR bottle inventory to zero).
Ask the Customer if the DiTi was cleaned or became wet due to Operator interference
Resolution
If the arm is suspected as having become wet, stop use immediately as further use may cause more damage.
Test
If the DiTi (Disposable Tip interface) becomes wet, sensitive components in the Pipettors can become irrecoverably damaged.
Field Service
Bottle is empty
Resolution
If the bottle is empty, reconstitute a new kit. The bottle may be empty due to a spill or leak.
Test
Verify the bottle is not empty.
Bottle is not completely seated
Resolution
Ensure the TCR bottle is fully seated in the TCR Carousel at the proper location for the loaded reagent rack.
Test
Verify the bottle is seated fully in the TCR cup (the bottle is originally loaded higher at the TCR cup, then eventually slipped down to the correct position).
Damaged or incorrect tips used
Resolution
Ensure the tips are the correct type and have not been damaged.
Test
- Verify the tips are the correct type (eppendorf 1 mL Capacitive tips with filters).
- Verify the tips are not damaged.
Spill on Tip Drawers
Resolution
If a spill occurred on the Tip Trays, stop the instrument use immediately—the Pipettor arms may already be damaged.
Test
Verify there is no evidence of a spill on the Tip Trays.
Sample Bay cover is not installed correctly
Resolution
Reinstall the Sample bay cover correctly.
Test
Verify the sample bay cover is installed properly and the tip does not come into contact with the cover during TCR aspiration.
Note: The sample tip can become occluded. If this happens, the barometric Liquid Level Detection (bLLD) of TCR will not be able to sense a state change (outside liquid to inside liquid) and will then drive to the maximum pipettor depth, setting the TCR bottle inventory to zero.
Ask the Customer if the DiTi was cleaned or became wet due to Operator interference
Resolution
If the arm is suspected as having become wet, stop use immediately as further use may cause more damage.
Test
If the DiTi (Disposable Tip interface) becomes wet, sensitive components in the Pipettors can become irrecoverably damaged.
Check Z-motor engagement
Resolution
Correct the Z-motor engagement and re-teach the pipettor arm to the appropriate modules.
Test
Using the corresponding Service manual installation procedure (Z-Motor/Pipettor Meshing Adjustment), verify the Z-motor is properly engaged with the pipettor arm.
Verify the DiTi is not wet
Resolution
If the Capacitive level is significantly above 11000 (19000 or greater), replace the arm (as the DiTi is wet) and further use may damage the Pressure sensor.
Test
In the SSW, verify the Capacitive level is approximately 11000 when idle.
DiTi Thumbscrew is not sealing completely
Resolution
Tighten the DiTi thumbscrew.
Test
Verify the DiTi thumbscrew is tight.
Teaching to the TCR Carousel is Off
Resolution
Reteach the Sample Pipettor to the TCR carousel.
Test
Verify the teaching is correct. In the SSW, load a TCR bottle onto the TCR carousel; pick the tip and move the sample pipettor to Z-max at the TCR carousel position 1. The TCR bottle should be able to be lifted about 1cm (not pinned against the TCR carousel bottom).
DiTi O-ring Failure
Resolution
If the Pressure Integrity test fails, replace the arm.
Test
Perform the Pressure Integrity test in the SSW to verify the DiTi (or O-ring) is not damaged.

## RBETR – Reagent Bottle Empty TER
id="mc-main-content">
RBETR – Reagent Bottle Empty TER
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Reagent Bottle Empty TER – The Sample Pipettor has detected the level of TER is at or below the lowest allowable limit. The inventory is set to zero for this kit.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Bottle is Empty
- Bottle Not Seated Completely
- Damaged or Incorrect Tips Used
- Spill On the Tip Drawers
- Sample Bay Cover Is Not Installed Correctly
- Ask If DiTi Was Cleaned or Became Wet Due to Operator Interference
-
Field Service
- Bottle is Empty
- Bottle Not Seated Completely
- Damaged or Incorrect Tips Used
- Spill On the Tip Drawers
- Sample Bay Cover Is Not Installed Correctly
- Ask If DiTi Was Cleaned or Became Wet Due to Operator Interference
- Check Z-motor Engagement
- Verify the DiTi Is Not Wet
- DiTi Thumbscrew Is Not Sealing Completely
- Teaching to TCR Carousel Is Off
- DiTi O-ring Failure
Technical Support
Bottle is Empty
Resolution
If empty, reconstitute a new kit. May be empty due to a spill or leak.
Test
Verify the bottle is not empty.
Bottle Not Seated Completely
Resolution
Ensure the TER bottle is fully seated in the TCR Carousel at the proper location for the loaded reagent rack.
Test
Verify the bottle is seated fully in the TER cup (the bottle was originally loaded at the TER cup, then eventually slipped down to the correct position).
Damaged or Incorrect Tips Used
Resolution
Ensure the tips are the correct type and have not been damaged.
Test
Verify the tips are Eppendorf 1mL Capacitive tips with filters. Verify the tips are not damaged.
Spill On the Tip Drawers
Resolution
If the spill occurred on the tip trays, stop instrument use immediately, as the pipettor arms may already be damaged.
Test
Verify there is no evidence of a spill on the tip trays.
Sample Bay Cover Is Not Installed Correctly
Resolution
Reinstall the Sample Bay Cover correctly.
Test
Verify the Sample Bay cover is installed properly, and the tip does not come into contact with the cover during the TER aspiration (the sample tip can become occluded. If this happens, the barometric Liquid Level Detection (bLLD) of the TER will not be able to sense a state change (outside liquid to inside liquid) and will then drive to the maximum pipettor depth, setting the TER bottle inventory to zero).
Ask If DiTi Was Cleaned or Became Wet Due to Operator Interference
Resolution
If the arm is suspected as having become wet, stop use immediately; further use may cause more damage. NOTE: If the DiTi (Disposable Tip interface) becomes wet, sensitive components in the Pipettors can become irrecoverably damaged.
Field Service
Bottle is Empty
Resolution
If empty, reconstitute a new kit. May be empty due to a spill or leak.
Test
Verify the bottle is not empty.
Bottle Not Seated Completely
Resolution
Ensure the TER bottle is fully seated in the TCR Carousel at the proper location for the loaded reagent rack.
Test
Verify the bottle is seated fully in the TER cup (the bottle was originally loaded at the TER cup, then eventually slipped down to the correct position).
Damaged or Incorrect Tips Used
Resolution
Ensure the tips are the correct type and have not been damaged.
Test
Verify the tips are Eppendorf 1mL Capacitive tips with filters. Verify the tips are not damaged.
Spill On the Tip Drawers
Resolution
If the spill occurred on the tip trays, stop instrument use immediately, as the pipettor arms may already be damaged.
Test
Verify there is no evidence of a spill on the tip trays.
Sample Bay Cover Is Not Installed Correctly
Resolution
Reinstall the Sample Bay Cover correctly.
Test
Verify the Sample Bay cover is installed properly, and the tip does not come into contact with the cover during the TER aspiration (the sample tip can become occluded. If this happens, the barometric Liquid Level Detection (bLLD) of the TER will not be able to sense a state change (outside liquid to inside liquid) and will then drive to the maximum pipettor depth, setting the TER bottle inventory to zero).
Ask If DiTi Was Cleaned or Became Wet Due to Operator Interference
Resolution
If the arm is suspected as having become wet, stop use immediately; further use may cause more damage. NOTE: If the DiTi (Disposable Tip interface) becomes wet, sensitive components in the Pipettors can become irrecoverably damaged.
Check Z-motor Engagement
Resolution
Correct the Z-motor engagement and reteach the pipettor arm to the appropriate modules.
Test
Using the Z-Motor/Pipettor Meshing Adjustment installation procedure (in the Service manual), verify the Z-motor is properly engaged with the pipettor arm.
Verify the DiTi Is Not Wet
Resolution
If the Capacitive level is significantly higher than 11000 (19000 or greater), replace the arm as the DiTi is wet and further use may damage the pressure sensor.
Test
Using the SSW, verify the Capacitive level is approximately 11000 at idle (not touching anything).
DiTi Thumbscrew Is Not Sealing Completely
Resolution
Using the Tightening the Pipettor DiTi Knurl Nut procedure (in the Operator’s manual), tighten DiTi thumbscrew.
Test
Verify the DiTi thumbscrew is tight.
Teaching to TCR Carousel Is Off
Resolution
Using the Auto-Teaching Sample Pipettor procedure (in the Operator’s manual), reteach the Sample Pipettor to the TCR Carousel.
Test
Verify teaching is correct. In the SSW, load a TER bottle onto the TCR Carousel; then pick the tip and move the sample pipettor to the Z-max at TER carousel position 1. The TER bottle should be able to be lifted ~1cm (not pinned against the carousel bottom).
DiTi O-ring Failure
Resolution
If the Pressure Integrity test fails, replace the Pipettor arm (per the Pipettor Arm Removal and Replacement procedure in the Operator’s manual).
Test
Perform the Pipettor Integrity Pressure Integrity test in the SSW (per the Pipettor Integrity Pressure Test procedure in the Operator’s manual) to verify the DiTi (or the O-ring) is not damaged.

## RDFA, RDFE, RDFP, RDFSL
id="mc-main-content">
RDFA, RDFE, RDFP, RDFSL
Assay Processing Flags
Complaint Description:
Topic covers troubleshooting procedures for these Assay Processing Flags:
- RDFA = RDV Failure Amp
- RDFE = RDV Failure Enzyme
- RDFP = RDV Failure Probe
- RDFSL = RDV Failure Select
RDV Failure Amplification — RDV indicated a failure during the dispense of Reagent. There is an RDV error type message associated with each dispense failure; either 2, 64, 128, or a sum of any of these. For example, error type 192 means error type 64 and error type 128 both occurred.
- Error Type 2: Maximum pressure threshold exceeded.
- Error Type 64: Minimum mean pressure threshold not met.
- Error Type 128: Minimum pressure down time threshold not met.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Foam reagent (typically error type 128)
- Pipettor tips damaged/wrong type (typically error type 2)
- Pipettor tips lack filter (intermittent but persistent error type 64)
- Fluid viscosity (can be any of above three error types)
-
Field Service
- Precipitate in sample
- Foam reagent
- Pipettor tips damaged
- Pipettor tips lack filter (intermittent but persistent error type 64)
- Fluid viscosity
- Sticky Pipettor Plunger
- No liquid aspirated
- Leaky Pipettor
Technical Support
Foam reagent (typically error type 128)
Resolution
Pop the bubble(s).
Test
Visually check for bubbles in the bottle.
Pipettor tips damaged/wrong type (typically error type 2)
Resolution
-
Fix the hardware obstruction (reseat reagent bay lid and reinitialize instrument).
-
Use the correct tips (1mL Tecan or Biorear capacitive with filter).
RDFA and RDFP due to tips (these are examples using a known bad lot of tips):
(Notice the banding of the curve near Pmax.)
Example 1, RDFA:
Example 2 (RDFP):
What the Dispense Pressure Curve should look like (very little banding):
Alternately, data can be sorted by PMAX in the Summary Plots tab:
Example 2 (RDFP):
Test
- Visually verify damage to Pipettor tips.
- Determine where the obstruction occurs (typically reagent bay lid).
- Verify tips are not wrong type.
Pipettor tips lack filter (intermittent but persistent error type 64)
Resolution
Use the correct tips (1mL Tecan capacitive with filter).
Test
Visually verify the pipettor tips have the white filter.
Fluid viscosity (can be any of above three error types)
Resolution
Check if the reagent is “chunky” or contains particulate matter.
Test
Compare the dispense pressure against a good dispense curve (un-flagged dispense event).
Field Service
Precipitate in sample
TBD
Foam reagent
Resolution
Verify the customer's reagent preparation workflow.
Test
Use the Dashboard tool to check the dispense curves.
Pipettor tips damaged
Resolution
- Re-teach the Pipettor.
- Fix the hardware obstruction.
Test
- Visually verify the damage to the Pipettor tips.
- Determine where the obstruction occurs.
Pipettor tips lack filter (intermittent but persistent error type 64)
Resolution
Use the correct tips (1mL Tecan capacitive with filter).
Test
Visually verify the pipettor tips have the white filter.
Fluid viscosity
Resolution
- Check to see if the sample was properly stored.
- Check to be sure the reagent type matches the assay.
- Check to be sure the customer properly reconstituted the reagent.
Test
- Use the Dashboard tool or CurveTrend to check the aspiration and the dispense pressure curves.
- Compare the dispense pressure against a good dispense curve (un-flagged dispense event).
- Check the reagent for uniformity.
Sticky Pipettor Plunger
Resolution
-
Check the curve files for “Sticky Plunger” Curve profiles. Refer to the following examples.
Normal Aspiration:
Aspiration with a Sticky Plunger:
Normal Dispense:
Dispense with a Sticky Plunger - variation in the pull back section of dispense curve:
-
Perform testing for a sticky plunger by performing a bLLD test in SSW. Instructions to perform a bLLD test can be found in the Service Manual. Search for bLLD .
Sticky plunger in SSW bLLD trace:
- If verified, replace the Pipettor.
Test
Follow the instructions in the Panther Service Manual for replacing the Pipettor.
No liquid aspirated
Resolution
- Replace the reagent with a new reagent kit (possibly below the volume requirements).
- Re-teach the Pipettor.
- Replace the Pipettor.
Test
- Use the Dashboard tool to check the aspiration and the dispense curves.
- Verify the LLD height.
Leaky Pipettor
Resolution
- Tighten the Pipettor Ditty.
- Replace the Pipettor.
Test
- Check the Reagent Bay cover for drips.
- Check the Load Station for drips.
- Use the Dashboard tool to check aspiration curves.
- Check to see if the Pipettor DiTi is loose.
- Perform a pressure integrity test using the Service Software.

## RDFS
id="mc-main-content">
RDFS
Volume Verification failed for sample.
Complaint Description
Reagent Dispense Sample Failure —RDV indicated a failure during dispense of Sample. There is an RDV error type message associated with each dispense failure; either 2, 64, 128, or a sum of any of these (e.g. error type 192 means error type 64 and error type 128 both occurred).
Error type 2— Maximum pressure threshold exceeded
Error type 64— Minimum mean pressure threshold not met
Error type 128— Minimum pressure down time threshold not met
Table of Contents
Technical Support
Questions to Ask Customer
Log Review
Example Curves
RDFS/VVFS Pierceable Cap Left on the Controls
Field Service
Precipitate in Sample
Foamy Reagent
Pipettor Tips Damaged or Wrong Type
Pipettor Tips Lack Filter
Fluid Viscosity
No Liquid Aspirated
Leaky Pipettor
VVFS Due to Cap Sealing Around Pipettor Tip
Sample Aspiration Pressure Curves
Sample Dispense Pressure Curves
Technical Support
Questions to Ask Customer
- RDFS on samples or controls? If on samples only: which sample type?
- Only in one particular assay or multiple assays?
- If in HPV run or on controls: check curves for a cap venting issue
- Which tips are on the instrument? (Validated or alternative, document Ref number + lot.)
- Request logs for review.
Log Review
- 1-2% is considered normal (likely viscous samples/precipitate in urine)
- Rare in HPV runs since Thinprep samples are usually not viscous
- If >2% RDFS, or RDFS in HPV runs or on controls, check curves
- Check the following curves: cLLD TCR, Sample aspiration and dispense curves
- Sometimes invalids have both VVFS/RDFS. See more curves under VVFS.
Example Curves
- RDFS due to viscous sample :
-
RDFS due to cap venting can be caused by:
-
Sample rack clip broken – sample is moving up.
-
Sample not pushed all the way down in the rack.
-
Cap foil delamination. Have customer check the shape of the piercing hole. It should be square or ‘D’ shaped, not perfectly round.
RDFS/VVFS Pierceable Cap Left on the Controls
Resolution
For Covid uncapped workflows, the controls (which have pierceable caps) must be uncapped. Customers at times will forget this, since the cap is pierceable.
If the RDFS occurred on a Covid control, ask the customer which workflow they are running.
Example
SarsCov2 WL 000877-20201209-23 Version: 3.1.11.5 (For Emergency Use Authorization) ML: 286020 Exp: 07/15/2021 TCR: 03254
SarsCov2 WL 000877-20201209-28 Version: 3.1.11.5 (For Emergency Use Authorization) ML: 286020 Exp: 07/15/2021 TCR: 03254
Both runs failed due to RDFS and VVFS on both positive and negative controls.
Confirmed cap is on using C-LLD and LLDValues:
Field Service
Precipitate in Sample
Resolution
Remove the mucous, then transfer to a new sample tube and retest the sample.
Test
Verify the sample does not have a mucous cap, or cotton pile in the tube.
Foamy Reagent
Typically error type 128.
Resolution
Pop the bubbles
Verify the customer's reagent preparation workflow.
Test
Use CurveTrend or the Dashboard tool to check the dispense curves.
Pipettor Tips Damaged or Wrong Type
Typically error type 2.
Resolution
Fix the hardware obstruction
Fix the hardware obstruction (reseat sample bay lid).
Use the correct tips (1mL Tecan capacitive with filter).
Test
Visually verify damage to Pipettor tips.
Determine where the obstruction occurs
Verify tips are not wrong type.
Pipettor Tips Lack Filter
Intermittent but persistent error type 64.
Resolution
Use the correct tips (1mL Tecan capacitive with filter).
Test
Visually verify the pipettor tips have the white filter.
Fluid Viscosity
Resolution
Check to see if the sample was properly stored.
Check to be sure the reagent type matches the assay.
Check to be sure the Customer properly reconstituted the reagent.
Check sample quality for mucoidal particles or particulate matter.
Test
Use CurveTrend or the Dashboard tool to check the aspiration and the dispense pressure curves.
Compare the dispense pressure against a good dispense curve (un-flagged dispense event).
Check the reagent for uniformity.
No Liquid Aspirated
Resolution
Replace the reagent with a new reagent kit (possibly below the volume requirements).
Re-teach the Pipettor.
Replace the Pipettor.
Test
Use CurveTrend or the Dashboard tool to check the cLLD, Aspiration and dispense curves.
Verify the LLD height.
Leaky Pipettor
Resolution
Tighten the Pipettor Diti.
Replace the Pipettor.
Test
Check the Reagent Bay cover for drips.
Check the Load Station for drips.
Use CurveTrend or the Dashboard tool to check aspiration curves.
Check to see if the Pipettor DiTi is loose.
Perform a pressure integrity test using the Service Software.
VVFS Due to Cap Sealing Around Pipettor Tip
If the Cap seals around the Pipettor Tip during aspiration, this will cause a pressure spike during aspiration, and the incorrect volume of sample will be aspirated. This will lead to a short shot of sample being dispensed. This can be caused by:
- The customer not pushing the sample all the way down in the tube (most likely).
- Wet cotton pile (likely if multiple reps taken from the same tube).
- Poor caps (rare). Note- this is not a frequent issue but captured here to raise awareness that it is possible.
Resolution
Observe the Sample Aspiration and Dispense Curves.
Plot the aspiration curves, and find the curve with the elevated pressure trace. Note the Test Order ID and Sample ID for that curve.
Sample Aspiration Pressure Curves
Sample Dispense Pressure Curves
Plot the dispense curves, and find the corresponding to the Test Order ID noted in the first step.
Test
Compare the dispense pressure against a good dispense curve (un-flagged dispense event).

## RTL – Reagent Tip Loss
id="mc-main-content">
RTL – Reagent Tip Loss
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Reagent Tip Loss — Reagent pipettor lost a tip.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Tip Loss
-
Field Service
- Tip Loss
- Tip Sensor Malfunction
Technical Support
Tip Loss
Resolution
- Remove a sample tip.
- Load a new kit, as there is possible reagent cross contamination.
- Clean the area where the drips or the spillage occurred.
- Ask the customer what type of tips they are using. Verify they are either Tecan or Biorear.
Test
- Look for the dropped tip in any of the bottles.
- Ensure that the tips are actually off of the pipettor.
Field Service
Tip Loss
Resolution
- Remove the sample tip.
- Load a new kit, as there is possible reagent cross contamination.
- Clean the area where the drips or the spillage occurred.
- Fix the hardware obstruction.
- Re-teach the Pipettor.
Test
- Identify the source and the destination when the RTL error was generated.
- Visually verify any sources of obstruction between the source and the destination.
- Use the Service software to recreate the problem if an obstruction cannot be found – pick tip, move down, move up, move to your destination .
Tip Sensor Malfunction
Resolution
Replace the Pipettor arm if the sensor is defective.
Test
Manually move the DiTi sleeve up and down. Verify that the status changes in the Service software when the DiTi sleeve is moved.
Other Items to Check
-
Tip Type matters. Customer should be using Biorear PN C30A0014-B13 or -B17 or Tecan PN 10612513 or 30180117. If tips other than these are being used, this may be the issue.
-
Check the Eject Sleeve. If Eject Sleeve has not been upgraded, do so. TB-01627.
-
Verify the Service Drawer is Closed.
-
Check Teaching of the pipettor.
-
Check Pipettor V and L white Slide bearings.
-
Check Z-Motor.
-
If at the Reagent Bay, check the Reagent Bay Shutter is moving correctly.
-
Review logs and look for Pipettor X, Y or Z movement errors.
-
Look for obstructions. One example, ribbon cable in the tip drawer interfering with the tips:

## RVHA, RVHE, RVHP, RVHSL
id="mc-main-content">
RVHA, RVHE, RVHP, RVHSL
Assay Processing Flags
Complaint Description
Topic covers troubleshooting procedures for these Assay Processing Flags:
- RVHA = Reagent Volume High Amp
- RVHE = Reagent Volume High Enzyme
- RVHP = Reagent Volume High Probe
- RVHSL = Reagent Volume High Select
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Questions to Ask Customer
- Log Review
- Example Curves
-
Field Service
- Reagent Bay cover
- Enzyme Bottle not properly seated
- Enzyme Bottle Cap
- Excess Fluid
- Air Bubble(s)
- Spill on Tip Tray
- Poor Z-motor Engagement causes excess noise during bLLD event
- Early Trigger
Technical Support
Questions to Ask Customer
Request Logs
Log Review
- Check c-LLD, reagent aspiration and dispense curves to determine if the issue is related to the reagents or the instrument.
- If there are no c-LLD curves for some of the reagents, it is likely instrument is still on a lower SW version using b-LLD instead of c-LLD. See example curves below.
Example Curves
- RVHSL due to bubbles in selection reagent (not a pipettor issue).
- Enzyme reagent curves are shown as comparison of a ‘good’ curve.
-
RVHP after tip related errors with instrument still on bLLD (SW 5.2.0.50).
Since the SW is still on the bLLD level sense, it is behaving much like the pipettor in the Fusion side for Oil. Basically, what happens is, the filter density is higher. This causes the slow response, resulting in lower volume detected. The inventory adjusts lower. Then a normal tip measures the correct height, which is higher than the previous level sense. At this point, the kit is invalidated.
TSE Technical Service Engineer. recommendation: Dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. to upgrade customer to current SW.
Normal Trend for Reagent LLD
Normal cLLD Curve for Amp Reagent
Field Service
Reagent Bay cover
Resolution
Reseat the Reagent Bay cover.
Test
Check if the Reagent Bay cover is properly mounted.
Reference
Enzyme Bottle not properly seated
Resolution
Push the Enzyme bottle down until it is fully seated in the Reagent Rack.
Test
Visually verify the bottle is fully seated in the Reagent Rack.
Enzyme Bottle Cap
Resolution
Inform the Customer to remove the reagent cap prior to Reagent Rack insertion.
Test
Check if the cap has been removed from the reagent bottle.
Excess Fluid
Resolution
Inform the Customer to follow the directions in the appropriate package insert.
Test
Use the Dashboard tool to view the LLD heights.
Air Bubble(s)
Resolution
Pop the bubbles and reinsert the kit.
Test
Verify there are no bubbles present in the Enzyme.
Spill on Tip Tray
Resolution
Discard any tips/tip trays where the spill occurred.
Replace the arm(s) if the frequency is >19000 when idle.
Test
Look for signs of a liquid spill on the tip tray.
Verify the DiTi for both arms are not wet by checking the LLD frequencies - "Pipettors" "Main" "Sensors".
Poor Z-motor Engagement causes excess noise during bLLD event
Resolution
Adjust the Z-motor engagement according to the Service manual.
Test
Verify the sample pipettor Z-motor engagement is correct (1 sheet of paper gap).
Early Trigger
Resolution
Verify the LLD early trigger event occurred.
If the bLLD traces show consistent early trigger in one piston location, replace the arm.
If the "delta Z" exceeds 30 steps, replace the arm.
Test
Use the Dashboard tool to view the LLD heights.
Use the Dashboard to view the aspiration and dispense curves for noise.
Try to replicate the event in the Service Software using the "LLD Right Arm" tab and the "Log" checkbox activated for 15+ cycles.

## SRR – Sample Rack Removed
id="mc-main-content">
SRR – Sample Rack Removed
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Sample pipetting operation was aborted.
Technical Support
Sample Rack was Removed while the samples were being pipetted
Resolution:
If the sample rack was removed, the rack can be reloaded. If the sample rack was replaced, all samples that have been pipetted will need to be pipetted again.
Test:
Determine if the customer removed the rack while the sample was being pipetted.
Field Service
Sample Rack Optical Flag is Broken
Resolution:
Replace the sample rack, then remove the defective rack from customer use.
Test
Visually verify the sample rack in question has the Optical flag feature.
Sample Lane Optical Flag is Broken
Resolution:
- Replace the Optical flag if defective.
- Replace the sample bay.
Test:
- Using SSW, verify the sample bay Optical flag for the corresponding lane is functional then verify the sample rack flag feature can be detected.
- If the new Optical flag is not functional, the sample bay PCB may be defective.
- Replace the sample bay PCB is defective following testing.

## STL – Sample Tip Loss
id="mc-main-content">
STL – Sample Tip Loss
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Sample Tip Loss – Sample pipettor lost a tip.
Technical Support
Tip Loss
Resolution:
- If the tip loss occurred in a sample tube, follow the instrument’s on-screen instructions to minimize possible contamination.
- Advise the Operator (or the FSE Field Service Engineer. ) to take great precaution as the dropped tip can lead to or cause contamination.
Important: If the lost tip is not carefully or properly removed, contamination can easily spread.
- Cannot rerun the specimen tube as the sample is now considered contaminated (or lost) as it is unknown how the dropped tip will affect the test results.
Test:
- Determine if there is dropped tip in any of the bottles.
- Ensure the tips are not on the pipettor.
Field Service
Tip loss
Resolution:
- If the tip loss occurred in a sample tube, follow the instrument’s on-screen instructions to minimize possible contamination.
- Advise the Operator (or the FSE) to take great precaution as the lost tip can lead to or cause contamination.
Important— If the lost tip is not carefully or properly removed, contamination can easily spread.
- Fix or remove any hardware obstruction.
- Re-teach the Pipettor.
Test:
- Identify the source and destination when the STL error was generated. Consider the following scenarios: for example, (A) Did the tip hit something and fall off the pipettor? (B) Was the pipettor properly picked?
- Visually verify any sources of obstruction between the source and the destination. NOTE:
Note— Determine actions that the instrument was performing with the pipettor when the tip fell off. Consider the following scenarios: (A) Did the instrument just “pipette” a reagent prior to dispensing it in a tube?
- Use the Service software to recreate the problem, if an obstruction was not found ( Pick tip, move down, move up, move to your destination ).
Tip Sensor Malfunction
Resolution:
Replace the Pipettor arm if the sensor is defective.
Test:
Monitor the tip presence sensor using the Service software while manually moving the DiTi sleeve up and down to determine the proper functioning of the sensor.
Other Items to Check
-
Tip Type matters. Customer should be using Biorear PN C30A0014-B13 or -B17 or Tecan PN 10612513 or 30180117. If tips other than these are being used, this may be the issue.
-
Check the Eject Sleeve. If Eject Sleeve has not been upgraded, do so. TB-01627.
-
Verify the Service Drawer is Closed.
-
Check Teaching of the pipettor.
-
Check Pipettor V and L white Slide bearings.
-
Check Z-Motor.
-
If at the Reagent Bay, check the Reagent Bay Shutter is moving correctly.
-
Review logs and look for Pipettor X, Y or Z movement errors.
-
Look for obstructions. One example, ribbon cable in the tip drawer interfering with the tips:

## TC – Temperature Chiller
id="mc-main-content">
TC – Temperature Chiller
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Temperature Chiller – The Chiller Ramp temperature was out of range while processing an MTU.
Technical Support
More Sensitive when closer to the extremes (Note)
Resolution:
- Adjust the Room temperature.
- Do not add new samples until the temperature is back in range.
- Retest any affected specimens.
- If the problem recurs, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Test:
- Check the Environmental conditions for the lab (within the recommendations) including the temperature and the humidity. Ensure the Room temperature is between 15 and 30 C.
- Verify the back of the instrument is not blocked/obstructed (including the instrument’s ventilation system).
- Request that the Customer check the temperatures ( The Temperature icon is displayed on the instrument screen).
Field Service
Faulty Thermistor
Resolution:
Replace the faulty thermistor.
Faulty Peltier
Resolution:
Replace the faulty Peltier.
Faulty PCB
Resolution:
Replace the faulty PCB.
Improperly Installed or faulty fan
Resolution:
Properly install or replace fan.

id="mc-main-content">

TABLE OF CONTENTS

Field Service

Technical Support
Troubleshooting
Panther:
-
Check waste bottle cap and tighten it.
-
Replace waste bottle.
-
Grease or replace o-rings. Vacuum grease and extra o-rings are in spare parts kit.
-
Change filter. Refer to instructions in Panther Operators Manual. Most likely part number: 903401 (T8), but this part could be upgraded to ASY-11890 (Odorcarb) filter. Ask customer if filter is small or large, and refer to CTB-01016. Ensure flow arrow is pointing up!
-
If male vacuum fittings in drawer are cracked, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. . Ask customer to move or wiggle fittings, as crack may be at base.
Panther Plus:
-
Change filter. Refer to instructions in Panther Operators Manual. Use part number ASY-11890 (Odorcarb) filter. Ensure flow arrow is pointing up!
-
If pressure remains low, dispatch FSE.
Possible root causes:
(Normal vacuum pressure reading: 4.0-12 Hg target 7.0 Hg.)
Vacuum pressure below 4.0 mmHg
-
Loose waste bottle cap.
-
Cracked or damaged waste bottle or fittings.
-
Broken, or unlubricated O-rings.
-
Wet vacuum filter.
-
Coalescing bottle is full.
-
Loose or kinked vacuum hose.
Vacuum pressure negative or close to 0 mmHg
-
Vacuum pump not working.
-
Vacuum manifold sensor tube clogged.
Normal vacuum pressure reading: 6.0 - 12 Hg, target 7.0 Hg.
Questions:
-
When did this happen?
-
What did they do today?
-
Ask customer to check the vacuum pressure.
-
Is instrument Standard Panther or For Panther Plus ?
For Standard Panther
Possible Root Cause
Troubleshooting
Loose waste bottle cap
Check waste bottle cap and
tighten it.
O-rings
Lift the bottle, and inspect for cracked fittings or
missing o-rings.
Grease or replace o-rings.
Vacuum grease and extra o-rings are in spare parts kit.

If male vacuum fittings in
drawer are cracked, dispatch FSE. Ask customer to move or wiggle fittings. Crack may be at base.

Check for cracks or other damage. Replace waste bottle as needed.

Left: SY-11890
(Odorcarb)
Right: 903401
(T8)
- Verify if filter is wet inside. See Wet Filter
step above.
- Notice
a wet filter will have discoloration, compared to a new dry filter.
- If yes, replace it.
- Ask customer if filter is small or large. Refer to CTB-01016.
Ensure flow arrow is pointing
up.

If vacuum hoses behind drawer
are kinked, unkink or dispatch FSE if not possible

vacuum manifold

key 2.5mm

personnel. Field Engineer may need to be dispatched.

is wet)

Note: This step is to only be performed by trained
personnel. Field Engineer may need to be dispatched. This procedure is only
found in the Panther Service Manual “Draining the Coalescing Trap”.
Check if all tubing is
well screwed in the manifold.
Make sure the instrument is off. Securely insert
aspirator tubing at the Vacuum Manifold.
Note: This step is to only be performed by trained
personnel. Field Engineer may need to be dispatched.
Check if all tubes
connected to the magwash aspirators are in place.
Make sure the instrument is off. Securely insert
aspirator tubing at the Magnetic Wash Stations.

personnel. Field Engineer may need to be dispatched.

Remove waste bottle. Verify
if you feel the negative pressure, and if you hear the noise.
If pump is not working, dispatch
FSE.

flow arrow is pointing up.

Dispatch FSE.
All fittings should be "finger
tight".
Make sure the instrument is off. Securely insert
aspirator tubing at the Vacuum Manifold.
Note: This step is to only be performed by trained
personnel. Field Engineer may need to be dispatched.
Check if all tubings
connected to the magwash aspirators are in place.
Make sure the instrument is off. Securely insert
aspirator tubing at the Magnetic Wash Stations.
Note: This step is to be performed only by trained
personnel. Field Engineer may need to be dispatched.
Cracked permanent bottle, requires an FSE to replace the bottle.
Note: It is normal for a foamy residue to build up in the Removable Liquid Waste Bottle when customers have Waste-to-Drain. FSEs will clean the Removable Liquid Waste Bottle as part of their Total Service Call and PM activities.
Customer can:
-
Discard the foamy residue like normal liquid waste.
-
Add bleach or water to the waste bottle, and swirl to help remove the residue.
Field Service
O-rings
Stretched, broken, or unlubricated O-rings at waste bottle quick connects.
Resolution:
- Replace stretched or broken O-rings.
- Lubricate O-rings at the waste bottle quick connects.
Test:
Check for stretched, broken, or unlubricated O-rings at the waste bottle quick connects.
Kinked Hose
Resolution:
Un-kink or replace hoses as needed.
Test:
Visually inspect for kinked hoses.
Hose Connection
Resolution:
Tighten loose hose locks or re-connect hoses, if necessary.
Test:
Check for loose vacuum hoses.
Cracked Fitting
Resolution:
Replace fittings as needed.
Test:
Visually inspect for cracked fittings.
Coalescing Bottle is Full
Resolution:
Empty coalescing bottle.
Test:
Visually inspect coalescing bottle.
Vacuum Muffler
Resolution:
Clear the vacuum muffler as needed.
Test:
Make sure the muffler is not occluded or blocked in any way.
Aspirator Tubing
Loose aspirator tubing at the Magnetic Wash Station and/or Vacuum Manifold.
Resolution:
Check to see if aspirator tubing are loose at the Magnetic Wash Stations and at the Vacuum Manifold.
Test:
Securely insert aspirator tubing at the Magnetic Wash Stations and Vacuum Manifold.
Aspirators
Clogged aspirators or tubing from the Magnetic Wash Station, or clogged tubing from the Output Queue.
Resolution:
Unclog or replace aspirators or tubing.
Test:
Check tubing or aspirators for clogs.
Vacuum Manifold
Clogged Vacuum Manifold ports (especially the port leading to the pressure transducer).
Resolution:
Unclog the Vacuum Manifold ports.
Test:
Check the Vacuum Manifold ports for clogs.
Pressure Transducer
Resolution:
Replace the Vacuum pressure transducer
TEST:
Make sure the Vacuum pressure transducer does not show signs of leaks or shorted components.
Communications Cable
Disconnected communication cable for one of the Vacuum Pumps from the power break away PCB.
Resolution:
Connect the communication cable from the power break away PCB to the Vacuum Pumps, if necessary.
Test:
Check to see if the communication cable from the power break away PCB is not connected to one of the Vacuum Pumps.
PCB
Bad Vacuum Pump power break away PCB.
Resolution:
Replace the Vacuum Pump power break away PCB.
Test:
Make sure the Vacuum Pump power break away has no shorted components or signs of dry fluid on it.
Control Cable
Vacuum Pump control cable disconnected from the Liquid Cooling/Vacuum Module PCB.
Resolution:
Re-connect the Vacuum Pump control cable to the Liquid Cooling/Vacuum Module PCB.
Test:
Make sure the Vacuum Pump control cable is connected to the Liquid Cooling/Vacuum Module PCB.
Wiring
Wire touching the Vacuum Pump body.
Resolution:
Replace the Vacuum Pump if any of its wires are exposed.
Test:
Check to be sure wire insulation is intact.
Vacuum Pump
Resolution:
Replace the Vacuum Pump.
Test:
Use Service Software to make sure the vacuum pump is operating properly.
Vacuum Duty Cycle Too Low (Quad)
Problem:
Vacuum pressure operating at higher end of range, but vacuum would intermittently shut off.
Isolation:
Check if vacuum duty cycle in SSW lower than 50%, this can cause vacuum to cut out.
Service manual search: Ported Vacuum Manifold Cover.
Resolution:
Vacuum speed control is determined by flow rate using two threaded ports on vacuum manifold cover. In this case, the ports were not tapped through.
-
Add or remove screws.
-
If not enough screws are present, verify the ports are tapped through.
-
Left/Right ports are not the same size.
Vacuum Pressure Low for Liquid Waste on the Fly
-
Vacuum filter is wet.
-
Permanent Waste Bottle is not holding the vacuum pressure.
Note: It is normal for a foamy residue to build up in the Removable Liquid Waste Bottle when customers have Waste-to-Drain. FSEs will clean the Removable Liquid Waste Bottle as part of their Total Service Call and PM activities.
- Customer can discard the foamy residue like normal liquid waste.
- Customer can add bleach or water to the waste bottle, and swirl to help remove the residue.
Customer can:
-
Discard the foamy residue like normal liquid waste.
-
Add bleach or water to the waste bottle, and swirl to help remove the residue.

## VVFS  – Volume Verification Failure Sample
id="mc-main-content">
VVFS – Volume Verification Failure Sample
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Volume Verification Failure Sample – The volume verification check for the TCR + Sample indicates the volume was either too low or too high.
The difference in the LLD values for the "Pipettor Dispense Sample PreLLD" and the "Pipettor Dispense Sample PostLLD" does not fall within the appropriate range for a Sample Dispense.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Questions for the Customer
- Log Review
- Example 1: VVFS Due to Viscous Sample
- Example 2: Cap Left on Sample (SarsCov2 TMA Uncapped WF)
- Example 3: TCR in MTU (Left) and TCR in Sample Tube (Right)
- Examples of Pipettor Issues ( = Dispatch)
-
Field Service
- Particulate in Sample
- Foam in the MTU
- Leaky DiTi
- Improper Tip Pick
- Faulty LLD sensor
- Pipettor Gold leads
- VVFS Due to Sample Quality Examples
- Instructions to Graph cLLD Tests Performed in SSW
Technical Support
Questions for the Customer
- Does the VVFS flag correspond to the Sample or to the Control? If the VVFS error corresponds to the Sample – which Sample type?
- Is the VVFS flag applicable to one specific assay or to multiple assays?
- If the VVFS flag corresponds to SarsCov2, is there a capped or uncapped WF? If there is an uncapped WF, was there a pierceable cap left on it?
- Which tips are currently used?
Note: If the tips are validated or an alternative type, document the Tip reference number and the Lot number).
- If customer inquires about a VVFS flag, customer logs will be required for review purposes, to determine if the issue is related to the Sample (i.e., bubbles, viscous, cap was left on) or if this is an instrument-related problem.
Log Review
- Review the Run reports. What is the percentage of VVFS?
Note: <1-2% - this percentage is normal and is likely attributed to viscous samples.
- Review the following Panther curves: Sample - Aspiration and Dispense curves. / c-LLD TCR, CLLD Sample.
Example 1: VVFS Due to Viscous Sample
Example 2: Cap Left on Sample (SarsCov2 TMA Uncapped WF)
Example 3: TCR in MTU (Left) and TCR in Sample Tube (Right)
Examples of Pipettor Issues ( = Dispatch)
Scenario: c-LLD TCR looks bad.
Examples 1 and : Normal c-LLD TCR (for Comparison)
Example 3: c-LLD TCR (Brushless Pipettor Problem)
Example 4: Normal C-LLD (with Bad c-LLD Sample)
Bad capacitive contact leading to noisy Sample pipettor Level Sense
Example 5: Bad Capacitive Circuit Contact
Example 6: Normal C-LLD (Left) and Bad c-LLD Sample
Field Service
Particulate in Sample
Resolution:
Remove the mucoid from the sample, then transfer to a new sample tube and retest the sample.
Test:
Verify the sample does not have a mucoid cap or cotton pile in the tube.
Foam in the MTU
Resolution:
- Do not shake the sample. Invert the sample gently.
- Replace with a new sample (or sample tube).
- Rerun the sample.
Test:
- Ensure there is no foam or air bubbles in the sample tubes.
- Verify the RDFS flag was triggered.
- Verify that the sample has a sufficient level of fluid.
Leaky DiTi
Resolution:
- Replace the DiTi then repeat the Pressure Integrity test.
- Replace the pipettor arm then repeat Pressure Integrity test.
Test:
Perform the Pressure Integrity check using the Service software.
Improper Tip Pick
Resolution:
Re-teach the pipettor.
Test:
Verify the Sample pipettor alignment using the Service software.
Faulty LLD sensor
Resolution:
Replace the Pipettor.
Test:
Check the LLD curve then verify the slope is not “zeroed”.
Pipettor Gold leads
Resolution:
- Clean the gold leads of the Pipettor.
- Adjust the gold leads of the Pipettor.
Test:
- Ensure the gold leads of the Pipettor are not dirty.
- Ensure the gold leads are making good contact with the DiTi.
VVFS Due to Sample Quality Examples
Example 1: VVFS (Due to Sample Quality)
Example 2: VVFS (Due to Sample Quality)
Looking at your sample cLLD curve, you can see that tube 0 of the MTU is the tube that is frequently triggering early, and you can see that the frequency it is starting at is much lower than the other tubes. If I take out SARS (which has the extra level sense in the open tube), I think it looks even clearer:
TCR level sense looks normal, so I do not think it is an issue with the electronics within the pipettor (although, it wouldn’t hurt to reteach the sample pipettor to the TCR mixer, verifying the correct tool is being used, the slope to the level sense line could mean the pipettor is too close to the edge of the TCR bottle):
I think what might be happening is the pipettor is too close to the edge of the MTU tube, and so it is throwing off the LLD frequency at the beginning of the cLLD move.
I would tell the FSE Field Service Engineer. to go in and check the following:
-
Verify the cLLD upgrade has been completed (TB-01684)
-
Sample Dispense Slot: Is the MTU being held in place, or is the spring allowing the MTU to “walk” when the sample mixer is going.
-
Look at the LD to Sample Dispense Slot teaching. Is the MTU being pushed far enough back into the sample dispense slot (or too far back)?
-
Perform a cLLD test at the Sample dispense slot, position 1, and watch the pipettor- does it look like it is getting too close to the edge of the MTU?
-
Reteach the sample pipettor to the sample dispense slot
-
Reteach the LD to the sample dispense slot.
-
Run another cLLD test at sample dispense slot 1. Did the performance improve?
Instructions to Graph cLLD Tests Performed in SSW
-
To get your results, navigate to C:\Panther\Panther Service Software\Log
Search for files named Right-LLD-ZPos.log and Right-LLD-Values_TCR Carousel-Track1-Tube1.log . Refer to image below:
-
Graph the LLD signal with the first file.

## VVFT – Volume Verification Failure TCR
id="mc-main-content">
VVFT – Volume Verification Failure TCR
Assay Processing Flag
Complaint Description
Volume Verification Failure TCR – The volume verification check for TCR indicates the volume is too low or too high which may be due to a hardware problem or the presence of bubbles in the TCR.
Technical Support
Hardware Problem
Resolution:
Perform a re-test of the sample.
Test
- Verify the TCR is in a solution/at room temperature before loading.
- The sample will not be processed and must be retested.
Bubbles
Resolution:
Perform a re-test of the sample.
Test:
Check for the presence of bubbles in the TCR line.
Field Service
VVFT Due to SP Clipping Sample Shield
Message the customer sees:
"Rescheduling tests due to error. Reagents already added to the invalidated MTU have been deducted from the available inventory. Test orders will be pipetted with the next MTU."
Confirmed in logs, RDV error 2 during TCR dispensing. RDFT errors are causing the message regarding rescheduling tests to occur.
TCR Dispense curves look as follows (note that tube 5 is always affected):
Resolution:
Have the customer check if the sample shield is installed correctly (and/ or is not warped)? Suspect that it may be up just enough that the SP is clipping the Sample Shield when moving from the TCR bottle to the Sample Dispense slot. Then, a drop of TCR falls out, and results in the 5th dispense being short. Customer performed Sample Shield maintenance between the good and bad TCR dispenses.

## Distributor Hook Motor Step Loss or Stall at Sample Dispense Slot (Position 25)
id="mc-main-content">
Distributor Hook Motor Step Loss or Stall at Sample Dispense Slot (Position 25)
Distributor Module – Observational Error
Event Description
MTU still in Sample Dispense Slot and the Distributor attempts to insert another MTU.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
An MTU from a previous run was not removed during the clear MTU operation at initialization.
If possible, visually verify if there are MTUs in the Sample Dispense Slot.
- Re-start the instrument and allow it to complete the MTU clearing process.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
An MTU from a previous run was not removed during the clear MTU operation at initialization.
If possible, visually verify if there are MTUs in the Sample Dispense Slot.
Using Service Software, clear MTUs.
N/A
Distributor is not able to pick up an MTU.
Visually verify if the Distributor cannot grab an MTU.
Re-teach the Distributor.
PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Teaching Procedure
The MTU retainer clip inside the Sample Dispense module was not correctly installed and allows the MTU to move further into the module.
Visually verify if the MTU is too far in.
Replace the Sample Dispense Slot module.
PANTHER System Service Manual —Sample Dispense Slot Removal and Replacement

## a
id="mc-main-content">
a
Result Processing Flag
Description
Invalid kinetic profile. The result calculation for the flasher analyte curve fit has failed.
Tier 1
Possible Root Cause
