id="mc-main-content">
fb
Result Processing Flag
Description
Invalid kinetic profile. The front-to-back ratio is out of range for the assay.
Tier 1
Possible Root Cause
Outcome
Technical Support/Customer Action
Reference
Front to back ratio is calculated from the total RLU between interval 10 and 25 (front) divided by the total RLU between interval 30 and 50 (back). The ratio must be ≥ 1.63. Samples with calculated values below 1.63 receive this flag and are marked invalid.
Sample is invalid.
This flag can be induced from Probe gradient due to the long tail off.
- Ask the operator if other runs, with other AR kits, have been affected, as well.
- Check to see if RLU values are high for negative results and lower than usual for positive results.
- For multiple flags in a worklist or over multiple kits, collect the Logs files and analyze kinetic files.

## p – Assay Processing Error
id="mc-main-content">
p – Assay Processing Error
p – Result Processing Flag
Event IDs
Dec
Hex
261.000.00013
261.000.00014
261.000.00015
261.000.00016
261.000.00017
261.000.00018
261.000.00019
261.000.00020
0x105.0x00x0.0D
0x105.0x00x0.0E
0x105.0x00x0.0F
0x105.0x00x0.10
0x105.0x00x0.11
0x105.0x00x0.12
0x105.0x00x0.13
0x105.0x00x0.14
Description
The Software has reported an assay processing error.
This Flag is generic and not related to any specific fault mode. The “p” flag will be displayed on the Results report to notify the user that the software has flagged and/or invalidated one or more results in the report.
The trouble shooting approach for “p” flags should include a further review of any additional reported flags or logs review. See examples below.
Example 1
The instrument is unable to validate the Positive Calibrators due to a Channel error most likely due to an RTF failure. The instrument assigns a cce and then p flag. Subsequently controls are invalidated for the same reason (x flag) and thus the rest of the run is invalidated each result assigned f flag, x flag, and p flag.
In the logs:
04/01/2022 16:50:56 (01 09:50:56) [E] (Warning , Low ) [TestOrderManagement] cce flag assigned to Calibrator ID 462431447715012405712 for BV assay in rack 717-04. [261.000.00018]
04/01/2022 16:50:56 (01 09:50:56) [D] (Warning , Low ) [TestOrderManagement] p Flag assigned to SID 462431447715012405712 for BV assay in rack 717-04. [261.000.00020]
Resolution:
Troubleshoot the cce Flag.
For this example, cce flag was generated in the FAM channel, where some Controls were fluorescing unexpectedly.
Example 2
A “p” flag is assigned to a single result in the results report of a CV/TV run. No other results are flagged and no other errors are logged otherwise the run was valid.
04/01/2022 17:55:58 (01 10:55:58) [E] (Warning , Low ) [TestOrderManagement] Invalidated Sample ID 12358872 for CV/TV assay in rack 046-06 due to p flag. Sample will need to be retested. [261.000.00016]
Resolution:
For this example, the internal control did not fluoresce in the RTF. Troubleshooting should focus on the reagent prep process.

## Handheld Barcode Scanner Does Not Scan or Misreads
id="mc-main-content">
Handheld Barcode Scanner Does Not Scan or Misreads
Error Code
Dec
Hex
None
None
Complaint Description
- Handheld Barcode Scanner does not scan.
- Handheld Barcode Scanner misreads, reads only symbols, not numbers – can happen if Shift key is held down.
Technical Support
Possible root causes
- Loose connection.
- The Shift key is pressed down.
- Failing barcode scanner.
Troubleshooting
- Check and ensure USB cable properly connected to instrument.
- Make sure the Shift key is not stuck down.
- Replace the barcode scanner. FSE Field Service Engineer.  must install softare driver.
Unable to Scan Master Lot
Resolution
When operator navigates to a different tab in the software, it nicely scans the correct numbers – for example, into the search bar of the Help tab.
Handheld scanner was not programmed correctly. FSE reprogrammed the scanner, and it worked as expected.

## Processing Curves OLV – Luminometer
id="mc-main-content">
Processing Curves OLV – Luminometer
Error Code
Flag
PCL
Technical Support
N/A
Field Service
Reading the Luminometer Process Control Curves offline:
- Navigate to the curve folder for the associated Panther Run.
- Right click on the “ProcessControlData_Luminometer_XXXX.curve” file and open with EXCEL.
- Highlight Column A:
- On the Data Tab, Select “text to Columns” to open the text to columns dialog box.
- Select The Delimited and then NEXT.
- Step Two on the Text to Columns Options, Select Semicolon as the Delimiter
- Select Finish.
Explanation of the Process Control Data Curve File: Luminometer
- TimeStamp : Pretty self explanatory… is the timestamp of when the process control curve was generated.
- TestOrderID : Test order ID assigned by the system. ID numbers that are -1 occur on curves generated during System Prime.
- SampleID: An ID generated from the barcode scanned into the system during sample loading. ‘Unknown’ ID numbers occur on curves generated during System Prime.
- MTUID: The ID of the MTU scanned when scanned by the input queue MTU barcode scanner.
- Tube Number: This is the tube number of the MTU (ranges from 0 to 4 for tubes 1 to 5). Tube 1 is closest to the MTU barcode and tube 5 is closest to the MTU tab for the distributor hook.
- Sensor ID: The sensor ID indicates which OLV channel generated the curve (0 or 1). The injector only goes in one way… Channel 0 measures the Auto Detect 1 dispenses. Channel 1 measures the Auto Detect 2 dispense.
- USER TIP: Use the sort or filter functions available in excel to look for trending in the data.
A note on sections of the process control curve known as regions 1 through 4: The Luminometer has 4 regions of interest which are defined by the headers in the curve file.
- The region at the beginning of the curve where air is seen before fluid is dispensed. (high)
- The region of the curve while fluid is being dispensed. (low)
- The region of the curve which has undergone fluid pull back by the LCMP and air is observed. (high)
- The transition region, where fluid is seen during pullback and then transitions to air as the fluid travels back up the injector past the sensor. (low then high)
- Region 1 must pass if region 3 or 4 of the previous injection did not fail.
- For luminometer either region 1, 2, 3 or region 4 need to pass. If region 3 or 4 fails ignore region 1 on the next dispense.
Region 1: Defined by columns labeled Parameter 1, Parameter 2, Parameter 3 and Parameter 4.
- Parameter 1: Value that defines the measurement point of the start of Region 1.
- Parameter 2: Value that defines measurement point of the end of Region 1.
- Parameter 3: Binary number that defines if the region is looking for a high (1/air) or low (0/liquid) signal, which represents the sensor reading from air or fluid, respectively.
- Parameter 4: Value that defines how many points in the region specified by parameter 1 and 2 need to be measured as whatever Parameter 3 specifies (either a high or a low signal) to pass.
Region 2: Defined by columns labeled Parameter 5, Parameter 6, Parameter 7 and Parameter 8.
- Parameter 5: Value that defines the measurement point of the start of Region 2.
- Parameter 6: Value that defines the measurement point of the end of Region 2.
- Parameter 7: Binary number that defines if the region is looking for a high (1/air) or low (0/liquid) signal which represents the sensor reading from air or fluid, respectively.
- Parameter 8: Value that defines how many points in the region specified by parameter 5 and 6 need to be measured as whatever Parameter 7 specifies (either a high or a low signal) to pass.
Region 3: Defined by columns labeled Parameter 9, Parameter 10, Parameter 11 and Parameter 12.
- Parameter 9: Value that defines the measurement point of the start of Region 3.
- Parameter 10: Value that defines the measurement point of the end of Region 3.
- Parameter 11: Binary number that defines if the region is looking for a high (1/air) or low (0/liquid) signal which represents the sensor reading from air or fluid, respectively.
- Parameter 12: Value that defines how many points in the region specified by parameter 9 and 10 need to be measured as whatever Parameter 11 specifies (either a high or a low signal) to pass.
Region 4: Defined by columns labeled Parameter 13, Parameter 14, Parameter 15 and Parameter 16.
- Parameter 13: Value that defines the measurement point of the start of Region 4.
- Parameter 14: Value that defines the measurement point of the end of Region 4.
- Parameter 15: Binary number that defines if the region is looking for a high (1/air) or low (0/liquid) signal which represents the sensor reading from air or fluid, respectively.
- Parameter 16: Value that defines how many points in the region specified by parameter 13 and 14 need to be measured as whatever Parameter 15 specifies (either a high or a low signal) to pass.
Result 1: This value represents the number of passing points in Region 1. Parameter 4 defines the number of points required in each result to pass.
Result 2: This value represents the number of passing points in Region 2. Parameter 8 defines the number of points required in each result to pass.
Result 3: This value represents the number of passing points in Region 3. Parameter 12 defines the number of points required in each result to pass.
Result 4: This value represents the number of passing points in Region 4. Parameter 16 defines the number of points required in each result to pass.
Graphing the results is a good way to determine where the failed dispenses occurred.
Example: The following chart shows one dispense for Result 2 that fell below the defined number of points required for a good dispense (Parameter 4).

Example 4: Air Bubbles in Auto Detect
Example 5: This PCL flag is due to a poor-quality pullback of the air/liquid interface in the injector.
According to the OLV curve, the final air region (Region 3) of the prior dispense to marginally low, but not a failure. The next dispense then started with a low initial air region (region 1), which was flagged as a failure.
Example 6: Leaky Fittings, small leak
Leaky fittings appear to extend Region 1 and often the air will work its way out of the system only to return when a time delay is introduced. Solution is to check all fittings and bottle connections for leaks.
Example 7: Slow Pump Pullback
Pumps with a slower Pullback are characterized by having extended Region 3 and Region 4. In these cases the Pump fails to pull back the meniscus past the OLV window in the injector in the correct amount of time. Solution is to replace the pumps.
Example 8 blocked Sight Holes

Luminometer Dispense Verification System
Luminometer Procecess Control Overview:
The Luminometer uses an optical sensor to verify that the dispensing of AD1 and AD2 has occurred correctly. The sensor assembly is installed in the top part of the Luminometer housing. The injector passes through an opening in the sensor assembly. The sensor assembly consists of two sensors and two emitters attached to a small PCB. The tubing of the injector assembly extends down into the injector and there are four small windows in the injector through which infrared (IR) light passes. The IR generated by the emitter is passed through one window, the injector tubing, and out of the opposite window to the sensor. The amount of IR that passes through the injector varies with the presence of liquid in the tubing. Prior to an injection the fluid in the injector tubing will not extend down to the area adjacent to the dispense verification sensor. After the dispense, a "pullback" occurs where the LCMPs briefly pump in the opposite direction so that the fluid in the tube is again pulled up above the sensor level. This functionality allows dispense verification. The sensor signal contains three distinct time regions: initial air (from previous pullback), liquid dispense, final air pullback. The signal is analyzed in each region to determine if the signal substantially matches the expected air/liquid signal. Small signal discrepancies are allowed, but larger discrepancies will generate an error. The specific region parameters and the acquired sensor signal for each dispense are logged in the ‘luminometer.curve’ file. The air/liquid threshold value is determined by sensor calibration that is performed as part of the system “full prime” routine.
Luminometer Process Control Description:
The OLV system incorporates a liquid/air sensor near the injector orifice. Each dispense is followed by an airgap pullback. This pulls air back up past the sensor after each dispense. Therefore, the subsequent dispense starts with air in the tubing in front of the sensor. The sensor signal for a “good” dispense will start with air (a high signal), then transition to liquid (a low signal) as fluid is dispensed, then remain sensing liquid as the pullback begins, and finally transition to air as the air/liquid interface is drawn up past the sensor. It is important that the sight holes in the injector body remain free from debris, fluid, and dried salt solutions, as any visual obstruction in these holes will result in erroneous failure flags.
The algorithm splits this “air-liquid-air” signal into 4 distinct regions. These regions are each defined by 4 parameters: Start point, end point, criteria (air or liquid), and minimum number of points required to meet the critera. A threshold defined during sensor calibration, as part of full-priming, is used to determine if each data point is considered as “air” or “liquid”. The threshold calculation sets the threshold at 1/3.5 of the way from the liquid value to the air value.
For a dispense to be considered “good”, the following conditions must be met:
-
Region 1 check passes (this is the initial air check)
-
Region 2 check passes (this is the liquid phase check)
-
Region 3 and/or 4 passes (this is the final air pullback check)
If region 3 fails, then region 1 is ignored on the subsequent dispense. This is to eliminate a false failure mode where the air/fluid interface does not pullback cleanly and instead leaves droplets on the inside of the tubing in front of the sensor.
The specific region parameters and the acquired sensor signal for each dispense are logged in the ‘luminometer.curve’ file. Sensor ID “0” corresponds to AD1 and Sensor ID “1” corresponds to AD2.
Luminometer Process Control Troubleshooting
Typically, the process control system will generate failure flags when the system is dispensing air instead of liquid. This may be observed in the curve file data as Region 2 failures. In this case, the instrument should be inspected for:
- An empty AD1 or AD2 bottle
- A disconnected AD1 or AD2 bottle
- Loose fitting in the fluid line from the bottles to the injector
- Damaged fitting or tubing in the fluid line from the bottle to the injector
- Air or occlusion in the fluid line from the bottles to the injector
- Leaky AD1 or AD2 pump
If the injector is dispensing properly and the failure is a false flag due to a problem with the process control system, then the instrument should be inspected for:
- Wet or damaged process control circuit board in the luminometer lid
- Damaged or unplugged process control cable in the luminometer (from the main PCB to the process control PCB)
- Debris in the sight holes of the injector
If the instrument has a luminometer process control system failure, this failure may occur while performing full-prime because the process control system is calibrated during full-prime and is used to check that the bottles are correctly connected during full-prime. The process control system is not exercised during mini-prime.
Output Queue Dispense Verification System
Output Queue Processes Control Overview
The Output Queue uses an optical sensor to verify that the dispensing of bleach and deactivation buffer has occurred correctly. The sensor assembly is installed in the top part of the Output Queue injector housing. The injector passes through an opening in the sensor assembly. The sensor assembly consists of two sensors and two emitters attached to a small PCB. The tubing of the injector assembly extends down into the injector and there are four small windows in the housing through which infrared (IR) light passes. The IR generated by the emitter is passed through one window, the injector tubing, and out of the opposite window to the sensor. The amount of IR that passes through the injector varies with the presence of liquid in the tubing. Prior to an injection the fluid in the injector tubing will not extend down to the area adjacent to the dispense verification sensor. After the dispense, a "pullback" occurs where the peristaltic pump briefly pumps in the opposite direction so that the fluid in the tube is again pulled up above the sensor level. This functionality allows dispense verification. The sensor signal contains three distinct time regions: initial air (from previous pullback), liquid dispense, final air pullback. The signal is analyzed in each region to determine if the signal substantially matches the expected air/liquid signal. Small signal discrepancies are allowed, but larger discrepancies will generate an error. The specific region parameters and the acquired sensor signal for each dispense are logged in the ‘Output Queue.curve’ file. The air/liquid threshold value is determined by sensor calibration that is performed as part of the system “full prime” routine.
Output Queue Process Control Description
The OLV system incorporates a liquid/air sensor near the injector orifice. Each dispense is followed by an airgap pullback. This pulls air back up past the sensor after each dispense. Therefore, the subsequent dispense starts with air in the tubing in front of the sensor. The sensor signal for a “good” dispense will start with air (a high signal), then transition to liquid (a low signal) as fluid is dispensed, then remain sensing liquid as the pullback begins, and finally transition to air as the air/liquid interface is drawn up past the sensor.
The Output Queue Process Control algorithm splits this “air-liquid-air” signal into 3 distinct regions. These regions are each defined by 4 parameters: Start point, end point, criteria (air or liquid), and minimum number of points required to meet the criteria. A threshold defined during sensor calibration, as part of the full-priming routine, is used to determine if each data point is considered as “air” or “liquid”. The threshold calculation sets the threshold at 1/3.5 of the way from the liquid value to the air value.
For a dispense to be considered “good”, the following conditions must be met:
- Region 2 check passes (this is the liquid phase check)
- Region 1 and/or 3 passes (these are the initial and final air pullback check)
The “Non-Deactivated waste” message will only appear to the instrument operator after 4 dispense failures in a row or 6 failures out of 20 dispenses.
The specific region parameters and the acquired sensor signal for each dispense are logged in the ‘Output Queue.curve’ file. Sensor ID “0” corresponds to Buffer and Sensor ID “1” corresponds to Bleach.
Output Queue Process Control Troubleshooting
Typically, the process control system will generate failure flags when the system is dispensing air instead of liquid. This may be observed in the curve file data as Region 2 failures. In this case, the instrument should be inspected for:
- An empty bleach or buffer bottle
- A disconnected bleach or buffer bottle
- Loose fitting in the fluid line from the bottles to the injector
- Damaged fitting or tubing in the fluid line from the bottle to the injector
- Kinked or crushed tubing in the fluid line from the bottle to the injector (** This tubing is very thin walled and can easily kink and occlude, particularly when routed through grommets and clips.)
- Air or occlusion in the fluid line from the bottles to the injector
- Old or worn peristaltic pump tubing
If the injector is actually dispensing properly and the failure is a false flag due to a problem with the process control system, then the instrument should be inspected for:
- Wet or damaged process control circuit board in the Output Queue injector mount assembly
- Damaged or unplugged process control cable in the Output Queue (from the main PCB to the process control PCB)
- Poor quality of the air/liquid meniscus in the injector tubing during pullback. Droplets left behind on the inner wall of the tubing in front of the sensor.
If the instrument has an Output Queue process control system failure, this failure may occur while performing full-prime because the process control system is calibrated during full-prime and is used to check that the bottles are correctly connected during full-prime. The process control system is not exercised during mini-prime.

## Magwash and PumpMonitor
id="mc-main-content">
Magwash and PumpMonitor
Magwash (tiplet and wash buffer) and PumpMonitor (oil) curves are used to assess processes associated with the magwash module.
ProcessControlData_Magwash1 and ProcessControlData_Magwash2 files uses a capacitive circuit to monitor tiplet pick, tiplet check and tiplet eject, magwash fluid heights.
ProcessControlData_PumpMonitor uses a pressure transducer to measure the oil dispense in the magwash once cleaning step has completed. It is important to note for Fusion assays, oil is not dispensed into the MTU after magwash cleaning.
Curve folder view of magwash related curve files (tiplet sensing, wash buffer and oil)
MTU workflow inside Magwash
Actual process cutoffs may vary by assay. For example, RTF assays use less oil and for Fusion assays, oil is not introduced at Magwash.
References for detailed explanation:
- MDD Firmware MagWash
- MDD Firmware PumpMonitor
- MTU storyboard
Magwash commands
Command (Decimal)
Movement
34 - PickTips
Picks the tiplets and checks presence. After picking is done all drives are driven to init position.
35 - EjectTips
Eject the tiplets and checks presence. After eject is done all drives are driven to init position.
45 - VerifyLiquidLevelFIR
(LLV) Liquid Level Verification – Verifies liquid is at the expected level using a FIR differentiator. After check probes are driven to home position and magnet is in work position.For each tube a flag is set it the liquid level is invalid.
46 - CheckResidualLiquid
Check residual liquid command checks presence of liquid at the bottom of tube. After the check probes and magnet are driven to home position.
47 - CheckEmptyMTUFIR
Empty Check - Prime sequence only, final check that all priming fluid has been aspirated from MTU
51 - CheckTips
Tip Still On Check – after tiplet pick, before eject, checks if tiplet is present
The first line of data is the header line, which explains the data within the column. Commonly used columns:
- CurveID: is not a column present in raw data. This value is assigned by curve trend software.
- Assay: as previously mentioned process parameters are tied to assay formulation.
- ProcessStep or CommandDescription: determines fluid type
- DateTime: UTC time
- TestOrderID: test order of sample
- SampleID: barcode of sample tube
- MTUNumber: MTU # since PantherMain was started
- MTUID: MTU barcode
- RFID: bottle A/B and rfid barcode value
- InstrFlag: RDV code
- Magwash_id: 0 = Magwash 1, 1 = Magwash 2
- FIR max : The maximum capacitive signal spike detected.
- FIR motor pos: The encoder position where the maximum capacitive signal spike occurred.
- Threshold or Treshold : The FIR maximum cutoff limit.
- Result0: Only informative if ErrorCode is not zero. This column indicates on which of the aspirators the error occurred. Convert the number in this column from decimal to binary to indicate the problematic tube. For example, if Result0 is 11, it converts to 1011 in binary. This indicates errors on tubes 1, 2, and 4 of the MTU.
Curve plots* (*in sw7.x additional columns were added, so curve file will require reformatting to render correctly in curve trend.)
Example of curve file and curve trend mismatch. Commands field show wrong information
Tiplet Detection (Cmd = 34, 35, and 51)
- The value in the FIR max column is compared to the value in the Threshold column.
- If FIR max > Threshold , no tiplets were detected on this aspirator.
- If FIR max < Threshold , tiplets were detected on this aspirator.
- If tiplet sense ( MT1 ) problems are occurring, note whether there are any trends from MTU to MTU.
- For example, check to see if the same tube in each MTU has an abnormal value. Also, note if any FIR max values are closer than 10 to the Threshold value
PickTips (command 34), check tiplets are present after picking
EjectTips (command 35), check tiplets are removed after eject
CheckTips (command 51), checks tiplets have not dropped off. Checks tiplets are present after picking and prior to ejecting.
Microsoft Excel visualization of elevated FIR values causing false tiplet missing during CheckTips and PickTip commands
In this situation, the level sense board (loose aspirators or damage) and flex cable should be inspected and reseated at both ends.
Wash Dispense Verification (Cmd = 45)
- If the value in the FIR max column is greater than the Threshold value, the Magnetic Wash Station did not detect fluid in the MTU tube as it should during this part of the process).
- If FIR max > Threshold , then the FIR motor position column is related to how much volume was detected in the tube.
- If FIR motor position ≤ 8475 , then more than 1,200 µL of Wash solution was detected in the MTU tube.
- If FIR motor position ≥ 9170 , then less than 800 µL of Wash solution was detected in the MTU tube.
- If ML2 or ML3 flags are occurring, note whether the same trends are seen on Magnetic Wash Station 1 and Magnetic Wash Station 2. If similar patterns are seen on both stations, this indicates a problem with the shared Wash Pump, as opposed to problems with the Magnetic Wash Stations.
- Problems detected at this step are typically caused by one of the following conditions:
- An under-dispensing Wash Pump ( ML3 )
- Clogs of the aspirator ( ML2 )
- Bubbles or foam caused by a bad wash injector ( ML2 )
- An empty or disconnected Wash bottle ( ML3 )
- Leaks in the Wash fluid line ( ML3 )
- Low vacuum pressure ( ML2 )
VerifyLiquidLevelFIR (command 45). Process control will general ML2 (too high) and ML3 (too low).
Residual Wash Check (Cmd = 46) and Empty Check (Cmd = 47)
- If the value in the FIR max column is greater than the Threshold value, the Magnetic Wash Station detected fluid in the MTU tube. The majority of the time at this step, the Magnetic Wash Station will not detect any fluid (i.e., FIR max < Threshold ). However, it is not unusual for the Magnetic Wash Station to detect the presence of some residual fluid (i.e., sometimes you will see FIR max > Threshold ).
- If FIR max > Threshold , then the FIR motor position column is related to how much volume was detected in the tube.
- If FIR motor position ≤ 10716 , then more than 50 µL of Wash solution was detected in the MTU tube.
- If FIR max > Threshold , then one should typically see associated FIR motor position values > 10840 .
- If residual wash ( ML5 ) flags are occurring, note whether there are any trends from MTU to MTU. For example, check to see if the same tube in each MTU has an abnormal value.Also not if any FIR max values are closer than 10 to the Threshold value.
- Problems detected at this step are typically caused by a clogged aspirator or low vacuum pressure. Remove and inspect aspirators and note what kind of substance (if any) is removed from the aspirator.
- Empty check failure will result in a failed prime.
Priming check (command 47) – Process control verifies fluid is properly removed by aspirator after each dispense during prime. Priming fails if liquid is detected.
MW FIR Motor Positions translated to ML2 or ML3 errors
When threshold is valid, FIR motor position:
FIR Motor <= 8475, Detected volume is greater than 1.2ml (ML2)
FIR Motor >= 9170, Detected volume is less than 0.8ml (ML3)
Unknown dropouts that can cause LLS errors, tip pick errors, or other errors. If the issue persists:
-
Replace the Liquid Level Sense PCB.
-
If that does not work, replace the module.

## 000.006.00034 – COP Communication Error with a Device
id="mc-main-content">
000.006.00034 – COP Communication Error with a Device
Error Code
000.006.00034
Complaint Description
-
When looking up device address:
04/27/2023 00:04:17 (26 20:04:17) [E] (Fatal , High ) [COP] COP communication error with a device (Can bus driver [6319,0,1]) (LowLevelEvent) [0x00.0x06.0x0022] bytes: 00 00 03 06 22 13 05 58 01 58 04 58 01 58 01 64 01 01 AF 18 00 00 00 01 0A [000.006.00034]
-
Begin with error code, [000.006.00034] :
000 = use Panther CAN Bus
1000 = use Fusion CAN Bus
-
Identify device, [6319,0,1]:
6319 = This is an air pipettor
0 or 60 = 0: APP, 60: BLDC
1 or 2 = 1: left arm, 2: right arm
-
In block diagrams, Panther CAN Bus, Fusion CAN Bus:
6319,60,1 = BLDC
6319, 0, 1 = APP

## 000.014.00150
id="mc-main-content">
000.014.00150
APPCONFG – COP System Message
Complaint Description
No tips loaded. Reagent Pipettor unable to continue processing.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
-
The operator did not load enough tips for processing all tests loaded.
-
Determine if there were 'tip pick up failure' messages from the Health report or the Message log.
- Follow the steps below to isolate the root cause of the tip pick up failures.
-
Enough tip pick up failures have occurred to cause the pipettors to skip trays and mark them as empty. The system does not have enough tips inventory to complete processing of samples and has halted processing.
- Determine which trays if any have been skipped because of tip pick up failures.
- Follow the steps below to determine if this was an operator error or the pipettors should be re-taught by the FSE Field Service Engineer. .
-
The operator has not replaced the tips and has accidentally set an empty or partially empty tray as full when loading tips through the GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. .
- Check to see if the first tip locations are empty on that tray. Or if the tray is completely empty.
- Replace the tip tray with a tray full of tips.
- The pipettors need to be re-taught to the tip trays.
- If the tip pick failures are intermittent. When looking at the tray some tips will be skipped and some will be picked.
- Pipettor alignment is incorrect, the pipettors will need to be re-taught.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
-
See above for possible operator errors during tip loading.
- Pipettor alignment is incorrect, the pipettors will need to be re-taught.
- Tip pick failures are usually intermittent, some tips may be picked and some will still be present at positions where the failures occurred. Test tip picks at the tray location and observe the alignment of the DiTi to the tips when picking. Ensure that the instrument is on a stable surface and the instrument feet are secure.
- Re-teach the pipettor arms.
- Panther Service Manual
- There may be a physical cause for the tip pick failures.
- Test tip picks at the tray location where the tip pick failures occurred and observe for any obstruction to the DiTi.
- Remove obstruction and re-teach to the tip trays.
- Panther Service Manual

Technical Support / Customer Action

Obstruction.

## 016.000.00006
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00006
016 000 00006, 01600000006
Distributor Z/Theta Drive—COP System Message
Description
Distributor Z/Theta Drive voltage out of range.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- Faulty PCB. Often this error occurs if the PCB is wet or has been dipped in the past.
- Ask the operator to initialize the instrument.
- If able to replicate the error, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- Otherwise, prime the instrument and proceed with a small run.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Faulty PCB. Often this error occurs if the PCB is wet or has been dipped in the past.
- Power down the instrument.
- Open the Service Drawer.
- Look for fluid or fluid residue on all Distributor PCB boards, or burned out components.
- Replace the faulty board.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Z/Theta-Axis PCB Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor X-Axis PCB Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Module Removal and Replacement
- Faulty flex cable (much less likely)
- Inspect all Distributor flex cables for any kinks, worn out and/or broken sections of cable.
- Using the System OQ procedure in Service Software, select all positions to exercise the Distributor flex cables in the X, Theta, and Z directions (8 times). Look for problems with any of the flex cables.
- Replace faulty flex cable.
- Replace the faulty flex cable.
Note: It is difficult to determine a faulty flex cable. Most of the time, Theta and X flex cables are replaced.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Theta Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor X-Axis Flex Cable Removal and Replacement

## 016.000.00014
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00014
016 000 00014, 01600000014
Distributor Z/Theta Drive—COP System Message
Description
Distributor error (Unable to execute command).
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- The Distributor is jammed against another module.
- The operator can attempt to restart the instrument, but this is an error that will most likely reoccur.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE Field Service Engineer. can determine where the error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The Distributor is jammed against another module.
- Power down the instrument.
- Look into the instrument from the left side or open the Service Drawer.
- Check to see if the Distributor is obviously jammed against another module.
- If it is, determine why the Distributor is jammed. Is the teaching bad? Is there a stray tiplet blocking the Distributor?
- Determine the reason for the jam and remedy.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedurre
- Poor connection between the Distributor and the COP.
- Check to see if the Distributor–COP cable is properly plugged in.
- Check to see if all other Distributor cables (flex cables, motor cables, etc.) are properly plugged in.
- Properly plug in all cables.
N/A
- Bad Distributor flex cable.
- Look through the logs and determine the location at which the Distributor error occurred.
- Using Service Software, cycle the Distributor to the faulty location to attempt to recreate the error.
- Replace faulty flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Removal and Replacement Procedures for the Distributor X-Axis Flex Cable and the Distributor Theta Flex Cable

This error will occur again, however frequency between failures is not predictable. Review case history to see if linear distributor errors occurred recently. Dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. sev 2 or sev 3.

Field Service
Bad Distributor Flex Cable
Resolution
Replace faulty flex cable.
Note: If unable to determine which cable is damaged, replace both X and Theta cables.
Test
- Look through the logs and determine the location at which the Distributor error occurred.
- Using Service Software, cycle the Distributor to the faulty location to attempt to recreate the error.
Poor Connection Between Distributor and the COP
Resolution:
Properly plug in all cables.
Test
- Check to see if the Distributor–COP cable is properly plugged in.
- Check to see if all other Distributor cables (flex cables, motor cables, etc.) are properly plugged in.
Distributor Jammed Against Another Module
Resolution
Clear the jam.
Test
- Power down the instrument.
- Look into the instrument from the left side or open the Service Drawer.
- Check to see if the Distributor is obviously jammed against another module.
- If it is, determine why the Distributor is jammed. Is the teaching bad? Is there a stray tiplet blocking the Distributor?
Alignment of Distributor to the MTU Scanner
Resolution
-
Check the alignment of the input queue barcode scanner to the MTU barcode in service software, adjust such that the barcode laser is in the center of the MTU barcode.
or
-
Replace the faulty scanner.
Test
- Look through the logs and determine the location at which the Distributor error occurred.
- If the distributor was moving an MTU from the Input queue to either the sample dispense slot or the transition incubator (Priming MTU). Check for messages related to Input Queue Barcode scanner timeouts, it may be a normal message.
- If the distributor was moving an MTU to the Luminometer, check for Input Queue Barcode scanner timeouts.
- Using service software, repeatedly scan MTUs and visually check the laser alignment to the MTU barcode.

## 016.000.00032
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00032
016 000 00032, 01600000032
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
Teach sensor active before starting teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- Only happens in Service Software during a Distributor auto teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Instrument has not been upgraded to SP4.
- In Service Software, check the Distributor's firmware version. (On the main screen) verify that the Distributor Module firmware version is 19, or higher.
- If the firmware version is not SP4 or higher, upgrade the firmware and re-attempt teaching.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- Linear Distributor hook is dirty.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check for oil/grime on the hook.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol.
N/A
- The initial teaching is off so much that the hook is touching the pin before teaching starts.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is touching the pin before teaching begins.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin and save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Faulty hook flex cable.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check the oscillator value. The value should be ~240,000.
- Touch the hook and again read the oscillator value. The value should be ~38,000.
- If these are not the values, then the hook flex cable is most likely compromised.
- If identified as defective, replace the Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement

## 016.000.00033
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00033
016 000 00033, 01600000033
Distributor Z/Theta Drive—COP System Message
Description
Teach pin not reached within teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Tape has been added to the plates securing the Distributor hook flex cable and the instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- Open the Service Drawer and look at the plates that secure the Distributor hook flex cable.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.(On the main screen, verify that the Distributor Module firmware version is 19 or higher.
- Remove the tape on the Distributor hook flex cable plates
- Upgrade firmware to SP4, or higher.
- Teach the Distributor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Initial teaching is off so much that the hook never reaches the teach pin during the teach procedure.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is either touching the pin before teaching begins, or missing the pin all together.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin, and save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook teaching is too deep. (If the hook is taught too deep, the side of the slot or carriage may prevent the hook sensor from triggering.)
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- Auto-teach the Distributor to the position.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Hook is dirty, preventing the sensor from triggering when touching the pin.
- Inspect the hook and teach pins for oil/grime.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol and DI water.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all positions, observing the hook for proper sensing.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook flex cable ends are not making proper contact.
- Inspect both ends of the hook flex cable for proper seating in connectors. One end is perforated and is held in place with a screw.
- Reseat the hook cable end into the Distributor head board and check the screw in the perforated end for tightness.
N/A
- Hook flex cable is broken.
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- The hook should sense the pin the instant it touches it. If the hook touches the pin and senses after significant force, causing the carriage to move or the theta positioning to loose steps, replace the hook flex cable.
- Replace Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- Missing teach pin.
- Inspect the position pin to determine if it has broken off.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
OR
- Replace the module with the broken teach pin.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure

## 016.000.00055
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00055
016 000 00055, 01600000055
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
Distributor error (After processing a pick MTU command no MTU is present on sledge. Position X.).
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- See Field Service section.
- Ask if the operator can determine the position of the crash.
- Contact an FSE Field Service Engineer. to determine if he/she would like the operator to leave the system in the error state.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Downstream error.
- Through PANTHER Dashboard, launch Event Log and identify message assignment.
- Review the logs, and determine if there is a prior error.
- Review the logs, and determine the location of the Distributor error.
- Fix the upstream error.
- Launching the PANTHER Dashboard
- Error in the module at which the Distributor was attempting to pick the MTU.
- Look at he logs and determine if there was an error preceding the Distributor error. This can often be an Incubator carousel position "retried" error or an MTU Input Queue stacking error.
- Fix the module error.
- If the error was at the MTU Input Queue, make sure the Input Queue teaching is correct and the that Input Queue bolts are tight.
- Linear Distributor - Incubator Interaction Errors
- Linear Distributor Error Modes - White Paper
- GP11-228 FSN Incubator Replacement Belt Tensioning
- Poor Teaching.
This error often occurs at the MTU Input Queue. If the teaching of the Distributor to the MTU Input Queue is not correct, complete the following steps:
- Check the Distributor Theta Positioning at the Input Queue.
- Check the Distributor height relative to the MTU in the Input Queue. Make sure it is not too high (so that the hook is hitting the bottom of the MTU tab when the Distributor rotates to grab the MTU) or too low (so that the MTU is missed).
- Make sure the Distributor hook is extended the correct distance. If the hook is not extended far enough, it will hit the MTU tab when attempting to grab the MTU. If the hook is extended too far, it will hit the MTU when grabbing the MTU.
- In Service Software, exercise the Distributor at the location of step loss.
- Re-teach the Distributor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Distributor Failure Points
- Intermittent or bad MTU presence sensor.
- Using Service Software, make sure the MTU presence sensor is reading properly.
- Clean the MTU presence sensor.
- Replace the MTU presence sensor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Hook PCB with Home Sensor Removal and Replacement

## 016.000.00056
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00056
016 000 00056, 01600000056
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
Distributor error (After processing a place MTU command a MTU is still present on sledge. Position X.).
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
- Can the operator determine the position of the crash.
- Contact FSE to determine if he/she would like for the system to remain in error state.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Downstream error.
- Through PANTHER Dashboard, launch Event Log and identify message assignment.
- Review the logs, and determine if there is a prior error.
- Review the logs, and determine the location of the Distributor error.
- Fix the upstream error.
- Launching the PANTHER Dashboard
- Error in the module at which the Distributor was attempting to pick the MTU.
- Look at he logs and determine if there was an error preceding the Distributor error. This can often be an Incubator step loss error.
- Fix the module error.
- Poor Teaching.
- This error often occurs at the Incubators. If the teaching of the Distributor to the Incubators is not correct, when the Distributor rotates to disengage the hook from the MTU, the hook is positioned so that it is still interacting slightly with the MTU. In this case, when the hook retracts, it can still pull the MTU back into the Distributor head.
- Re-teach the Distributor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching

Reference
- See Field Service section.
- This error does not show up in the GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. . It is hidden, and is not fatal. It does show up in the Health Report. If this error is seen, the FSE Field Service Engineer. in charge of the instrument should be made aware of it so that it can be addressed on teh next service call.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the error occurred.

LD Positions Tested During Prime or MW:

Field Service
Loose Theta Motor
RESOLUTION:
Tighten the Theta motor screws.
TEST:

Loose Theta motor cable or Encoder cable
RESOLUTION:
Properly plug in all cables
TEST:

- Open the Service Drawer.

Foreign object is causing an obstruction
RESOLUTION:
Remove the foreign object.

Sticky Door
Any of the Load Station or Incubators
RESOLUTION:
Clean the Sticky door and door slide
TEST:
The door is not smooth to open, especially when attempting to open with a Theta movement.
Distributer Hook is Unlevel
RESOLUTION:
Level the Distributor hook. Re-teach the Distributor to all locations, starting with the Input Queue.
Teaching
Distributor is taught too high and so clips the MTU tab when grabbing the MTU.
RESOLUTION:
Re-auteach the Distributor to the affected location.
If the auto-teach still teaches the Distributor too high, check the levelness of the hook
TEST:
Observe the Distributor picking/placing MTUs.
Is the Distributor hook hitting the bottom of the MTU tab when the Distributor picks MTUs?
MTU positioning problem to an assigned location.
RESOLUTION:
Re-teach the Distributor.
At the MTU Input Queue, make sure the Input Queue teaching is correct and that the Input Queue bolts are tight.
TEST:
- Using Service Software, place an MTU to the identified location and observe.
- Does the insertion/removal sound loud?
- Is there a lot of movement of the Distributor head?
- Is the hook hitting either the tab or the body of the MTU when it is rotating to grab the MTU?

## Linear Distributor Hook Motor Step Loss or Stall – Position X
id="mc-main-content">
Linear Distributor Hook Motor Step Loss or Stall – Position X
Error Code
Dec
Hex
016.000.00128
0x10.0x00.0x0080
Complaint Description
Linear Distributor Hook motor step loss or stall. Position X.
10/25/2023 09:03:59 Fatal 016.000.00128 Linear Distributor hook motor suffered step loss or stalled. Position 0
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
- Troubleshooting
- References
-
Field Service
- Sticky Door
- Module position mounting screws have loosened
- Loose Theta Motor
- Loose Hook
- Distributor Teaching
- Warped MTU carriage or slot
- LD-Hook step losses at the IQ, SW 5.3
Technical Support
Troubleshooting
- Instruct customer to shutdown/restart, prime, and perform a run of untested samples.
- If the position is tested during a MW clean, instruct customer to perform the MW clean maintenance.
- Reference the “LD Positions Tested During Prime or MW” sheet below.
- Review logs for linear distributor messages, warnings, and critical error messages before the fatal error message.
- NotePad++ Search Terms:
- All LD movements: COP->PC 10
- All LD movements that gave a warning, critical, or fatal error message: COP->PC 10 [0-9][0-9] [0][1-3]
- Review case history to see if linear distributor errors occurred recently. If the same linear distributor error occurred recently, notify the FSEs.
- Instruct customer to monitor. If the issue reoccurs, dispatch FSEs.
References
LD Positions Tested During Prime or MW:
Linear Distributor Movement:
Field Service
Sticky Door
If hook step loss occurs at an Incubator or at a Load Station Door:
Resolution:
- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.
- Perform a System Operational Qualification procedure.
Test:
Check the Incubator and Load Station for sticking doors. Manually move the doors open and closed and observe for sticking.
Module position mounting screws have loosened
Resolution:
- Re-teach the Distributor to the Input Queue.
- Use a straight hex driver (not ball end) to properly torque the Input Queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws do not become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the Input Queue.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Close the Service Drawer, install the injector, start the PANTHER UI, and prime the instrument to test the Distributor MTU picking from the Input Queue.
Test:
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
Loose Theta Motor
Causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or hook not square with Distributor Head.
Resolution:
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
Test:
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
Loose Hook
causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
Resolution:
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
Test:
Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
Distributor Teaching
Resolution:
- Inspect the Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors, or loose belts.
- Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement" or section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Re-test MTU picking and placing at the Load Station through Service Software.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
TEST:
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review te logs using view log for Distributor messages indicating "lost steps" or "lost some steps" at the suspected position and at other positions. "Lost some steps" is not a fatal message.
- Check the Distributor teaching at the affected positions.
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
Warped MTU carriage or slot
All positions
Resolution:
Replace the module with the affected position.
Test:
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough
LD-Hook step losses at the IQ, SW 5.3
If the instrument is still on SW 5.3, make sure TB-01303 is implemented (adjusts the IQ packing).

## 016.000.00129
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00129
016 000 00129, 01600000129
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
Distributor hook motor lost some steps. Position X.
The Distributor hook drive motor lost some steps during a pick or lace of an MTU at position X. This error is non-fatal, so the instrument was able to recover. However, it indicates an issue at position X.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
-
This error does not show up on the GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. . It is hidden, and is not fatal. It does show up in the Health Report. If this error is seen, the FSE in charge of the instrument should be made aware of it, so that it can be addressed on the next service call.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the "lost some steps" error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Sticky door (if hook step loss occurs at an Incubator or at a Load Station).
- Check the Incubator and Load Station for sticking doors. Manually move the doors open and closed and observe for sticking.
- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.
- Perform a System Operational Qualification procedure.
- Module position mounting screws have loosened (especially at the Input Queue).
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
- Re-teach the linear distributor to the input queue following the procedure in the PANTHER Service Manual.
- Use a straight hex driver (not a ball end) to properly torque the input queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws don’t become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the input queue.
- Run a system Operational Qualification.
- Close the service drawer, install the injectior, start the PANTHER UI and prime the instrument to test the Linear Distributor MTU picking from the input queue.
- GP11-243-FSN System Input Queue Detent Mechanism Adjustment
- Loose Theta motor causing poor auto-teaching or excessive Distributor head movement during a pick or place MTU operation.
- Inspect the Theta drive meshing.
- The Distributor head should not have excessive play in the Theta direction due to gear backlash.
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching
- Loose hook causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
- Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Linear Distributor Hook Leveling Instructions
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Distributor teaching.
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review the logs using view log (procedure) for Linear Distributor messages indicating 'lost steps' or 'lost some steps' at the suspected position and at other positions. 'lost some steps' will not be a fatal message.
- Check Linear Distributor teaching at the affected positions. (procedure indicating thorough method of checking teaching, with a marked MTU)
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
- Inspect the Linear Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors or loose belts.
- Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement or section 017.001.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Retest MTU picking and placing at the load station through service software. Run a system operational qualification."
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Warped MTU carriage or slot (all positions).
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough.
- Replace the module with the affected position.
N/A

## 016.000.00137
id="mc-main-content">
016.000.00137
016 000 00137, 01600000137
Distributor Hook – COP System Message
Description
Hook drive teach sensor active before starting teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.
- Verify that the Distributor firmware version is 19 or higher.
- If the firmware version is not SP4 or higher, upgrade the firmware and re-attempt teaching.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Distributor hook is dirty.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check for oil/grime on the hook.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol.
N/A
- The initial teaching is off so much that the hook is touching the pin before teaching starts.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is touching the pin before teaching begins.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin.
- Save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Faulty hook flex cable.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check the oscillator value. The value should be ~240,000.
- Touch the hook and again read the oscillator value. The value should be ~38,000.
- If these are not the values, then the hook flex cable is most likely compromised.
- If identified as defective, replace the Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement

## 016.001.00008
id="mc-main-content">

- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.

Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Faulty PCB. Often this error occurs if the PCB is wet or has been dripped on in the past.
- Power down the instrument.
- Open the Service Drawer.
- Look for fluid or fluid residue on all Distributor PCB boards, or burned out components.
- Replace the faulty board.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor PCB Board Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Module Removal and Replacement
- Faulty flex cable (much less likely).
- Using the PANTHER Dashboard, launch Event Log and identify message assignment.
- In Service Software, use the Output queue procedure and look for rough MTU positioning to stations or slots.
- If identified as defective, replace component.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Module Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Launching the Dashboard

## 016.001.00033
id="mc-main-content">
016.001.00033
016 001 00033, 01600100033
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
X drive teach pin not reached within teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Tape has been added to the plates securing the Distributor hook flex cable and the instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- Open the Service Drawer and look at the plates that secure the Distributor hook flex cable.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.(On the main screen, verify that the Distributor Module firmware version is 19 or higher.
- Remove the tape on the Distributor hook flex cable plates
- Upgrade firmware to SP4, or higher.
- Teach the Distributor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Initial teaching is off so much that the hook never reaches the teach pin during the teach procedure.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is either touching the pin before teaching begins, or missing the pin all together.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin, and save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook teaching is too deep. (If the hook is taught too deep, the side of the slot or carriage may prevent the hook sensor from triggering.)
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- Auto-teach the Distributor to the position.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Hook is dirty, preventing the sensor from triggering when touching the pin.
- Inspect the hook and teach pins for oil/grime.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol and DI water.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all positions, observing the hook for proper sensing.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook flex cable ends are not making proper contact.
- Inspect both ends of the hook flex cable for proper seating in connectors. One end is perforated and is held in place with a screw.
- Reseat the hook cable end into the Distributor head board and check the screw in the perforated end for tightness.
N/A
- Hook flex cable is broken.
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- The hook should sense the pin the instant it touches it. If the hook touches the pin and senses after significant force, causing the carriage to move or the theta positioning to loose steps, replace the hook flex cable.
- Replace Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- Missing teach pin.
- Inspect the position pin to determine if it has broken off.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
OR
- Replace the module with the broken teach pin.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure

- In Service Software, extend the hook and check for oil/grime on the hook.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol.
N/A
- The initial teaching is off so much that the hook is touching the pin before teaching starts.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is touching the pin before teaching begins.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin.
- Save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Faulty hook flex cable.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check the oscillator value. The value should be ~240,000.
- Touch the hook and again read the oscillator value. The value should be ~38,000.
- If these are not the values, then the hook flex cable is most likely compromised.
- If identified as defective, replace the Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement

## 016.003.00096
id="mc-main-content">
016.003.00096
016 003 00096, 01600300096
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
Distributor Theta motor step loss or stall. Position %1.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
- Ask if the operator can determine the position of the crash.
- Contact an FSE to determine if he/she would like the operator to leave the system in the error state.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Loose Theta motor.
- Power down the instrument.
- Open the Service Drawer.
- Confirm that the Theta motor screws are tight.
- Tighten the Theta motor screws.
N/A
- Loose Theta motor cable or encoder cable.
- Power down the instrument.
- Open the Service Drawer.
- Confirm that all Distributor cables are properly seated.
- Properly plug in all cables.
( Trunk Stock Part - Theta Flex Cable )
( Trunk Stock Part - X-Axis Flex Cable )
N/A
- Foreign object is causing an obstruction.
- Power down the instrument.
- Open the Service Drawer.
- Look to see if there is a foreign object causing an obstruction (loose tiplet, tip, MTU, etc.)
- Remove the foreign object.
N/A
- Sticky door (any of the Load Stations or Incubators).
- The door is not smooth to open, especially when attempting to open with a Theta movement.
- Clean the sticky door.
N/A
- Distributor hook is not mounted levelly.
- See Distributor Hook leveling instructions.
- Level the Distributor hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all locations, starting with the Input Queue.
- Linear Distributor leveling instrument
- Distributor is taught too high and so clips the MTU tab when grabbing the MTU.
- Observe the Distributor picking/placing MTUs.
- Is the Distributor hook hitting the bottom of the MTU tab when the Distributor picks MTUs?
- Re-auteach the Distributor to the affected location.
- If the auto-teach still teaches the Distributor too high, check the levelness of the hook (see Distributor Hook leveling instruments).
- PANTHER System Service Manual - Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Linear Distributor leveling instrument
- MTU positioning problem to an assigned location.
- Using Service Software, place an MTU to the identified location and observe.
- Does the insertion/removal sound loud?
- Is there a lot of movement of the Distributor head?
- Is the hook hitting either the tab or the body of the MTU when it is rotating to grab the MTU?
- Is the theta teaching of the Distributor to the Input Queue correct?
- Re-teach the Distributor.
- At the MTU Input Queue, make sure the Input Queue teaching is correct and that the Input Queue bolts are tight.
- PANTHER System Service Manual - Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Linear Distributor leveling instrument

## 016.004.00033
id="mc-main-content">
016.004.00033
016 004 00033, 01600400033
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
Teach pin not reached within teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Tape has been added to the plates securing the Distributor hook flex cable and the instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- Open the Service Drawer and look at the plates that secure the Distributor hook flex cable.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.(On the main screen, verify that the Distributor Module firmware version is 19 or higher.
- Remove the tape on the Distributor hook flex cable plates
- Upgrade firmware to SP4, or higher.
- Teach the Distributor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Initial teaching is off so much that the hook never reaches the teach pin during the teach procedure.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is either touching the pin before teaching begins, or missing the pin all together.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin, and save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook teaching is too deep. (If the hook is taught too deep, the side of the slot or carriage may prevent the hook sensor from triggering.)
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- Auto-teach the Distributor to the position.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Hook is dirty, preventing the sensor from triggering when touching the pin.
- Inspect the hook and teach pins for oil/grime.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol and DI water.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all positions, observing the hook for proper sensing.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook flex cable ends are not making proper contact.
- Inspect both ends of the hook flex cable for proper seating in connectors. One end is perforated and is held in place with a screw.
- Reseat the hook cable end into the Distributor head board and check the screw in the perforated end for tightness.
N/A
- Hook flex cable is broken.
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- The hook should sense the pin the instant it touches it. If the hook touches the pin and senses after significant force, causing the carriage to move or the theta positioning to loose steps, replace the hook flex cable.
- Replace Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- Missing teach pin.
- Inspect the position pin to determine if it has broken off.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
OR
- Replace the module with the broken teach pin.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure

## 016.004.00128
id="mc-main-content">
016.004.00128
016 004 00128, 01600400128
Distributor Z/Theta Drive – COP System Message
Description
Distributor hook motor step loss or stall. Position X.
The Distributor hook drive motor lost steps during a pick or a place of an MTU at Position X.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
- Can the operator determine the position of the crash. Contact FSE to determine if he/she would like for the system to remain in error state.
- Have the vendor collect the MTUs lot number.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Sticky door (if hook step loss occurs at an Incubator or at a Load Station door).
- Check the Incubator and Load Station for sticking doors. Manually move the doors open and closed and observe for sticking.
- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.
- Perform a System Operational Qualification procedure.
N/A
- Module position mounting screws have loosened (especially at the Input Queue).
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the Input Queue.
- Use a straight hex driver (not ball end) to properly torque the Input Queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws do not become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the Input Queue.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Close the Service Drawer, install the injector, start the PANTHER UI, and prime the instrument to test the Distributor MTU picking from the Input Queue.
- GP11-243-FSN System Input Queue Detent Mechanism Adjustment
- Loose Theta motor causing poor auto-teaching or excessive Distributor head movement during a pick or place MTU operation.
- Inspect the Theta drive meshing.
- The Distributor head should not have excessive play in the Theta direction due to gear backlash.
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching
- Loose hook causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
- Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Linear Distributor Hook Leveling Instructions
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Distributor teaching.
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review te logs using view log for Distributor messages indicating "lost steps" or "lost some steps" at the suspected position and at other positions. "Lost some steps" is not a fatal message.
- Check the Distributor teaching at the affected positions.
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
- Inspect the Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors, or loose belts.
-
Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement" or section 017.001.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Re-test MTU picking and placing at the Load Station through Service Software.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Warped MTU carriage or slot (all positions).
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough.
- Replace the module with the affected position.
N/A
