Service Action
Reference
- Sticky door (if hook step loss occurs at an Incubator or at a Load Station).
- Check the Incubator and Load Station for sticking doors. Manually move the doors open and closed and observe for sticking.
- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.
- Perform a System Operational Qualification procedure.
- Module position mounting screws have loosened (especially at the Input Queue).
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
- Re-teach the linear distributor to the input queue following the procedure in the PANTHER Service Manual.
- Use a straight hex driver (not a ball end) to properly torque the input queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws don’t become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the input queue.
- Run a system Operational Qualification.
- Close the service drawer, install the injectior, start the PANTHER UI and prime the instrument to test the Linear Distributor MTU picking from the input queue.
- GP11-243-FSN System Input Queue Detent Mechanism Adjustment
- Loose Theta motor causing poor auto-teaching or excessive Distributor head movement during a pick or place MTU operation.
- Inspect the Theta drive meshing.
- The Distributor head should not have excessive play in the Theta direction due to gear backlash.
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching
- Loose hook causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
- Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Linear Distributor Hook Leveling Instructions
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Distributor teaching.
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review the logs using view log (procedure) for Linear Distributor messages indicating 'lost steps' or 'lost some steps' at the suspected position and at other positions. 'lost some steps' will not be a fatal message.
- Check Linear Distributor teaching at the affected positions. (procedure indicating thorough method of checking teaching, with a marked MTU)
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
- Inspect the Linear Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors or loose belts.
- Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement or section 017.001.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Retest MTU picking and placing at the load station through service software. Run a system operational qualification."
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Warped MTU carriage or slot (all positions).
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough.
- Replace the module with the affected position.
N/A

## 016.004.00137
id="mc-main-content">
016.004.00137
016 004 00137, 01600400137
Distributor Hook – COP System Message
Description
Hook drive teach sensor active before starting teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.
- Verify that the Distributor firmware version is 19 or higher.
- If the firmware version is not SP4 or higher, upgrade the firmware and re-attempt teaching.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Distributor hook is dirty.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check for oil/grime on the hook.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol.
N/A
- The initial teaching is off so much that the hook is touching the pin before teaching starts.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is touching the pin before teaching begins.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin.
- Save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Faulty hook flex cable.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check the oscillator value. The value should be ~240,000.
- Touch the hook and again read the oscillator value. The value should be ~38,000.
- If these are not the values, then the hook flex cable is most likely compromised.
- If identified as defective, replace the Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement

## 017.000.00008
id="mc-main-content">
017.000.00008
Distributor X-Drive – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Distributor X drive thermal or short circuit protection activated.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
- Operator can attempt to restart the instrument, but this is an error that will most likely reoccur.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Faulty PCB. Often this error occurs if the PCB is wet or has been dripped on in the past.
- Power down the instrument.
- Open the Service Drawer.
- Look for fluid or fluid residue on all Distributor PCB boards, or burned out components.
- Replace the faulty board.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor PCB Board Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Module Removal and Replacement
- Faulty flex cable (much less likely).
- Using the PANTHER Dashboard, launch Event Log and identify message assignment.
- In Service Software, use the Output queue procedure and look for rough MTU positioning to stations or slots.
- If identified as defective, replace component.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Module Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Launching the Dashboard

- Verify that the Distributor firmware version is 19 or higher.
- If the firmware version is not SP4 or higher, upgrade the firmware and re-attempt teaching.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Distributor hook is dirty.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check for oil/grime on the hook.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol.
N/A
- The initial teaching is off so much that the hook is touching the pin before teaching starts.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is touching the pin before teaching begins.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin.
- Save the value.

- In Service Software, extend the hook and check the oscillator value. The value should be ~240,000.

## 017.000.00033
id="mc-main-content">
017.000.00033
Distributor X-Drive – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Teach pin not reached within teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Tape has been added to the plates securing the Distributor hook flex cable and the instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- Open the Service Drawer and look at the plates that secure the Distributor hook flex cable.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.(On the main screen, verify that the Distributor Module firmware version is 19 or higher.
- Remove the tape on the Distributor hook flex cable plates
- Upgrade firmware to SP4, or higher.
- Teach the Distributor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Initial teaching is off so much that the hook never reaches the teach pin during the teach procedure.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is either touching the pin before teaching begins, or missing the pin all together.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin, and save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook teaching is too deep. (If the hook is taught too deep, the side of the slot or carriage may prevent the hook sensor from triggering.)
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- Auto-teach the Distributor to the position.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Hook is dirty, preventing the sensor from triggering when touching the pin.
- Inspect the hook and teach pins for oil/grime.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol and DI water.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all positions, observing the hook for proper sensing.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook flex cable ends are not making proper contact.
- Inspect both ends of the hook flex cable for proper seating in connectors. One end is perforated and is held in place with a screw.
- Reseat the hook cable end into the Distributor head board and check the screw in the perforated end for tightness.
N/A
- Hook flex cable is broken.
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- The hook should sense the pin the instant it touches it. If the hook touches the pin and senses after significant force, causing the carriage to move or the theta positioning to loose steps, replace the hook flex cable.
- Replace Distributor hook flex cable.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- Missing teach pin.
- Inspect the position pin to determine if it has broken off.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
OR
- Replace the module with the broken teach pin.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure

## 017.001.00032
id="mc-main-content">
017.001.00032
Distributor X-Drive – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Teach sensor active before starting teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.
- Verify that the Distributor firmware version is 19 or higher.
- If the firmware version is not SP4 or higher, upgrade the firmware and re-attempt teaching.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Distributor hook is dirty.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check for oil/grime on the hook.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol.
N/A
- The initial teaching is off so much that the hook is touching the pin before teaching starts.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is touching the pin before teaching begins.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin.
- Save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Faulty hook flex cable.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check the oscillator value. The value should be ~240,000.
- Touch the hook and again read the oscillator value. The value should be ~38,000.
- If these are not the values, then the hook flex cable is most likely compromised.
- If identified as defective, replace the Distributor hook flex cable.

## 018.000.00128
id="mc-main-content">
018.000.00128
Distributor Hook – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Distributor hook motor step loss or stall. Position X.
The Distributor hook drive motor lost steps during a pick or a place of an MTU at Position X.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
- Can the operator determine the position of the crash. Contact FSE to determine if he/she would like for the system to remain in error state.
- Have the vendor collect the MTUs lot number.
- Please refer to the chart to determine if a Full Prime or MagWash cleaning or nothing needs to be performed in case of a LD position failure.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Sticky door (if hook step loss occurs at an Incubator or at a Load Station door).
- Check the Incubator and Load Station for sticking doors. Manually move the doors open and closed and observe for sticking.
- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.
- Perform a System Operational Qualification procedure.
N/A
- Module position mounting screws have loosened (especially at the Input Queue).
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the Input Queue.
- Use a straight hex driver (not ball end) to properly torque the Input Queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws do not become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the Input Queue.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Close the Service Drawer, install the injector, start the PANTHER UI, and prime the instrument to test the Distributor MTU picking from the Input Queue.
- GP11-243-FSN System Input Queue Detent Mechanism Adjustment
- Loose Theta motor causing poor auto-teaching or excessive Distributor head movement during a pick or place MTU operation.
- Inspect the Theta drive meshing.
- The Distributor head should not have excessive play in the Theta direction due to gear backlash.
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching
- Loose hook causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
- Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Linear Distributor Hook Leveling Instructions
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Distributor teaching.
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review the logs using view log for Distributor messages indicating "lost steps" or "lost some steps" at the suspected position and at other positions. "Lost some steps" is not a fatal message.
- Check the Distributor teaching at the affected positions.
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
- Inspect the Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors, or loose belts.
-
Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement" or section 017.001.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Re-test MTU picking and placing at the Load Station through Service Software.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Warped MTU carriage or slot (all positions).
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough.
- Replace the module with the affected position.
N/A

## 018.000.00129
id="mc-main-content">
018.000.00129
Distributor Hook – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Distributor hook motor lost some steps. Position X.
The Distributor hook drive motor lost some steps during a pick or lace of an MTU at position X. This error is non-fatal, so the instrument was able to recover. However, it indicates an issue at position X.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
-
This error does not show up on the GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. . It is hidden, and is not fatal. It does show up in the Health Report. If this error is seen, the FSE in charge of the instrument should be made aware of it, so that it can be addressed on the next service call.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the "lost some steps" error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Sticky door (if hook step loss occurs at an Incubator or at a Load Station).
- Check the Incubator and Load Station for sticking doors. Manually move the doors open and closed and observe for sticking.
- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.
- Perform a System Operational Qualification procedure.
- Module position mounting screws have loosened (especially at the Input Queue).
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
- Re-teach the linear distributor to the input queue following the procedure in the PANTHER Service Manual.
- Use a straight hex driver (not a ball end) to properly torque the input queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws don’t become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the input queue.
- Run a system Operational Qualification.
- Close the service drawer, install the injectior, start the PANTHER UI and prime the instrument to test the Linear Distributor MTU picking from the input queue.
- GP11-243-FSN System Input Queue Detent Mechanism Adjustment
- Loose Theta motor causing poor auto-teaching or excessive Distributor head movement during a pick or place MTU operation.
- Inspect the Theta drive meshing.
- The Distributor head should not have excessive play in the Theta direction due to gear backlash.
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching
- Loose hook causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
- Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Linear Distributor Hook Leveling Instructions
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Distributor teaching.
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review the logs using view log (procedure) for Linear Distributor messages indicating 'lost steps' or 'lost some steps' at the suspected position and at other positions. 'lost some steps' will not be a fatal message.
- Check Linear Distributor teaching at the affected positions. (procedure indicating thorough method of checking teaching, with a marked MTU)
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
- Inspect the Linear Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors or loose belts.
- Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement or section 017.001.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Retest MTU picking and placing at the load station through service software. Run a system operational qualification."
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Warped MTU carriage or slot (all positions).
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough.
- Replace the module with the affected position.
N/A

- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Module Removal and Replacement
- Faulty flex cable (much less likely).
- Using the PANTHER Dashboard, launch Event Log and identify message assignment.
- In Service Software, use the Output queue procedure and look for rough MTU positioning to stations or slots.
- If identified as defective, replace component ( Trunk Stock Part ).
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Module Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Launching the Dashboard

id="mc-main-content">

Complaint Description

Technical Support
Possible Root Cause

Reference
- Only Happens in Service Software during a Distributor auto teaching sequence
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Instrument has not been upgraded to SP4.
- In Service Software, check the Distributor's firmware version. (On the main screen) verify that the Distributor Module firmware version is 19, or higher.
- If the firmware version is not SP4 or higher, upgrade the firmware and re-attempt teaching.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- Linear Distributor hook is dirty.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check for oil/grime on the hook.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol.
N/A
- The initial teaching is off so much that the hook is touching the pin before teaching starts.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is touching the pin before teaching begins.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin and save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Faulty hook flex cable.
- In Service Software, extend the hook and check the oscillator value. The value should be ~240,000.
- Touch the hook and again read the oscillator value. The value should be ~38,000.
- If these are not the values, then the hook flex cable is most likely compromised.

## 018.004.00033
id="mc-main-content">
018.004.00033
Distributor Hook – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Teach pin not reached within teach movement.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- This error occurs only in Service Software during a Distributor auto-teaching sequence.
N/A
N/A
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Tape has been added to the plates securing the Distributor hook flex cable and the instrument software has not been upgraded to SP4.
- Open the Service Drawer and look at the plates that secure the Distributor hook flex cable.
- On the Service Software main screen, check the Distributor's firmware version.(On the main screen, verify that the Distributor Module firmware version is 19 or higher.
- Remove the tape on the Distributor hook flex cable plates
- Upgrade firmware to SP4, or higher.
- Teach the Distributor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Run PANTHER Instrument Setup (Firmware)
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Initial teaching is off so much that the hook never reaches the teach pin during the teach procedure.
- In Service Software, teach the Distributor.
- Watch the teaching procedure to determine if the hook is either touching the pin before teaching begins, or missing the pin all together.
- On the Teach page, manually change the teach value sufficiently to move the hook away from the pin, and save the value.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the location.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook teaching is too deep. (If the hook is taught too deep, the side of the slot or carriage may prevent the hook sensor from triggering.)
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- Auto-teach the Distributor to the position.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Hook is dirty, preventing the sensor from triggering when touching the pin.
- Inspect the hook and teach pins for oil/grime.
- Clean the hook and all module auto-teach pins with alcohol and DI water.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all positions, observing the hook for proper sensing.
- Run a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Hook flex cable ends are not making proper contact.
- Inspect both ends of the hook flex cable for proper seating in connectors. One end is perforated and is held in place with a screw.
- Reseat the hook cable end into the Distributor head board and check the screw in the perforated end for tightness.
N/A
- Hook flex cable is broken.
- In Service Software, auto-teach the Distributor and observe.
- The hook should sense the pin the instant it touches it. If the hook touches the pin and senses after significant force, causing the carriage to move or the theta positioning to loose steps, replace the hook flex cable.
- Replace Distributor hook flex cable.
( Truck Stuck Part )
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Hook Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- Missing teach pin.
- Inspect the position pin to determine if it has broken off.
- Manually teach the Distributor with a marked MTU to the position.
OR
- Replace the module with the broken teach pin.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure

## 018.004.00128
id="mc-main-content">
018.004.00128
Distributor Hook – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Distributor hook motor step loss or stall. Position X.
The Distributor hook drive motor lost steps during a pick or a place of an MTU at Position X.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
ServiceAction
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
- Can the operator determine the position of the crash. Contact FSE to determine if he/she would like for the system to remain in error state.
- Have the vendor collect the MTUs lot number.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Sticky door (if hook step loss occurs at an Incubator or at a Load Station door).
- Check the Incubator and Load Station for sticking doors. Manually move the doors open and closed and observe for sticking.
- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.
- Perform a System Operational Qualification procedure.
N/A
- Module position mounting screws have loosened (especially at the Input Queue).
- Inspect the mounting screws to determine if any are loose.
- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
- Re-teach the Distributor to the Input Queue.
- Use a straight hex driver (not ball end) to properly torque the Input Queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws do not become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the Input Queue.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Close the Service Drawer, install the injector, start the PANTHER UI, and prime the instrument to test the Distributor MTU picking from the Input Queue.
- GP11-243-FSN System Input Queue Detent Mechanism Adjustment
- Loose Theta motor causing poor auto-teaching or excessive Distributor head movement during a pick or place MTU operation.
- Inspect the Theta drive meshing.
- The Distributor head should not have excessive play in the Theta direction due to gear backlash.
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching
- Loose hook causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
- Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Linear Distributor Hook Leveling Instructions
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Distributor teaching.
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review te logs using view log for Distributor messages indicating "lost steps" or "lost some steps" at the suspected position and at other positions. "Lost some steps" is not a fatal message.
- Check the Distributor teaching at the affected positions.
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
- Inspect the Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors, or loose belts.
-
Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement" or section 017.001.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Re-test MTU picking and placing at the Load Station through Service Software.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Warped MTU carriage or slot (all positions).
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough.
- Replace the module with the affected position.
N/A

id="mc-main-content">

Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. section.
-
This error does not show up on the GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. . It is hidden, and is not fatal. It does show up in the Health Report. If this error is seen, the FSE in charge of the instrument should be made aware of it, so that it can be addressed on the next service call.
- Collect Advanced Sendlogs so that the FSE can determine where the "lost some steps" error occurred.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference

- Clean the door bearings to remove the tendency to stick.
- In Service Software, repeatedly re-teach and test the MTU picking and placing to verify the fix.

- If the Input Queue has moved because of operator use, inspect the ball detent for proper lubrication and adjustment.
- Re-teach the linear distributor to the input queue following the procedure in the PANTHER Service Manual.
- Use a straight hex driver (not a ball end) to properly torque the input queue mounting screws to ensure that the screws don’t become loose.
- Lubricate and adjust the ball detent to reduce the amount of force required to open and close the input queue.
- Run a system Operational Qualification.
- Close the service drawer, install the injectior, start the PANTHER UI and prime the instrument to test the Linear Distributor MTU picking from the input queue.
- GP11-243-FSN System Input Queue Detent Mechanism Adjustment
- Loose Theta motor causing poor auto-teaching or excessive Distributor head movement during a pick or place MTU operation.
- Inspect the Theta drive meshing.
- The Distributor head should not have excessive play in the Theta direction due to gear backlash.
- Adjust the Theta drive meshing.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules after adjusting the Theta drive. Most likely all modules have been taught incorrectly.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching
- Loose hook causing poor auto-teaching and excessive movement during MTU picking and placement. Or, hook not square with Distributor head.
- Inspect the hook for squareness with the Distributor head.
- Re-square the hook.
- Re-teach the Distributor to all modules.
- Perform a System Level Operational Qualification.
- Linear Distributor Hook Leveling Instructions
- PANTHER System Service Manual System Level Operational Qualification
- Distributor teaching.
- Prepare the PANTHER instrument for service.
- Review the logs using view log (procedure) for Linear Distributor messages indicating 'lost steps' or 'lost some steps' at the suspected position and at other positions. 'lost some steps' will not be a fatal message.
- Check Linear Distributor teaching at the affected positions. (procedure indicating thorough method of checking teaching, with a marked MTU)
- Check MTU placements of affected modules in Service Software.
- Inspect the Linear Distributor for a loose hook, loose drive motors or loose belts.
- Re-teach the Linear Distributor to the affected module, paying close attention to how the hook touches the teach pin. (procedure) If there are problems teaching, refer to the Trouble Shooting Guide section 017.000.00032 Teach Sensor Active Before Starting Teach Movement or section 017.001.00032 Teach Sensor Not Reached".
- Retest MTU picking and placing at the load station through service software. Run a system operational qualification."
- PANTHER System Service Manual Distributor Alignment and Teaching Procedure
- Warped MTU carriage or slot (all positions).
- Inspect the position and Distributor head for signs of white dust created by MTU scraping.
- Inspect picking and placing into the position repeatedly to determine if the MTU placement is rough.
- Replace the module with the affected position.
N/A

## Linear Distributor Error 0x89 During Teach Movement
id="mc-main-content">
Linear Distributor Error 0x89 During Teach Movement
Error Code:
10 23 01 00 89
Occurs only during the Auto Teach Movement.
LD Movement Description
After telling the Linear Distributor to teach, the Linear Distributor moves to the Input Queue, rotates, then moves down and throws the error message.
89 is your error code here. From the MDD, that translates to Hook Drive teach sensor active before starting teach movement .
Quick review of how the Linear Distributor teach circuit works
-
Linear Distributor initializes.
-
When the Linear Distributor is in the initialized state, the hook is retracted all the way back in the head, and needs to make good contact with the teach tab at the back of the Linear Distributor head. This grounds out the circuit. If the circuit is not ground out before starting the teach movement, then you get the error you are seeing.
Picture of the teach tab at the back of the Linear Distributor head. Note, in this picture, the tab is not making contact, there is a gap.
If your Linear Distributor looks like the above picture, extend the hook, bend the tab toward the hook, and retry.
Also, make sure the Linear Distributor head is very clean. Clean all debris from inside of the head. Clean the back of the hook, clean the teach tab. Apply a dab of deoxit to the teach tab.
-
If conditions in step 2 above are not your issue, then take a close look at the hook flex cable. This flex cable is only used during teaching, and monitors if the teach circuit is grounded out or not. If there are any breaks - or even big creases - in this cable, then you will see this error.

## Vacuum and Cooling System Error – Liquid Waste Bottle Is Full
id="mc-main-content">
Vacuum and Cooling System Error – Liquid Waste Bottle Is Full
Error Code
Dec
Hex
024.000.00038
0x18.0x00.0x26
Complaint Description
Liquid waste bottle is full.
Technical Support
Possible root causes
- Waste bottle full (possible operator did not empty all the way when changing waste).
- Waste bottle float stuck.
- Waste bottle sensor bad.
- Loose connection from waste drawer to vacuum/cooling.
- Vacuum/cooling module PCB Failure.
Troubleshooting
- Check bottle level, if full, empty waste bottle.
- Check the bottle to make sure floater is not stuck.
- Replace waste and use a different bottle.
- Recommend to monitor, but notify FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Loose Connection
From waste drawer to Vacuum/Cooling Module.
RESOLUTION:
Repair or replace the cable.
TEST:
Visually inspect cable connection.
Laboratory Temperature out of ambient range
Verify the laboratory is within ambient temperature (15–30°C).
RESOLUTION:
Set Laboratory between (15–30°C) and let instrument warm up or cool down.
TEST:
Cooling Module Sub-assembly
From Panther Temperature Screen, make sure that both Reagent (15.5-22.0 ˚C) and Sample Bays (15.5-22.5 ˚C) are within temperature ranges.
Check that cooling module temperature does not drop below 3.5 ˚C.
RESOLUTION:
Re-start instrument and computer.
Monitor bay's temperatures.
TEST:
Field Service
Laboratory Temperature out of ambient range
Verify the laboratory is within ambient temperature (15–30°C).
RESOLUTION:
Set Laboratory between (15–30°C) and let instrument warm up or cool down.
Cooling Module sub-assembly
- From Panther Temperature Screen, make sure that both Reagent(15.5-22.0 ˚C) and Sample Bays (15.5-22.5 ˚C) are within temperature ranges.
- Check that cooling module temperature does not drop below 3.5 ˚C.
RESOLUTION:
- Re-start instrument and computer.
- Monitor bay's temperatures.
Reagent or Sample Bay out of allowed temperature range
Verify both Reagent (15.5-25.5 ˚C) and Sample Bays (15.5-25.5 ˚C) are within temperature ranges.
RESOLUTION:
Reference Event IDs for Reagent and Sample bay troubleshooting.
Not Enough Coolant in Reservoir
- Verify the cooling module reservoir is full.
- Also make sure that there's no loose fittings, leaks or kinks.
RESOLUTION:
- Add Coolant.
- Fix any leaks or kinks.
TEST:
- Cooling Module pump.
- Verify the cooling module pump is running.
RESOLUTION:
Replace coolant pump.
TEST:
Cooling Module Thermistor broken or stuck at high or low temperature
- Verify the thermistor is connected.
- Check for thermistor broken wire.
RESOLUTION:
Replace coolant pump.
Fan
RESOLUTION:
- Slow spinning - Replace fan.
- Not spinning - Replace fan.
- Not connected - Re-connect fan.
Peltiers
Note: A good peltier should feel warm to the touch.
- Using Service Software, compare seebeck voltages, all should read about the same, but the one pair that reads close to 0 volts is most likely the culprit.
- Using a multimeter and set to ohms [(+) lead to red peltier wire and (-) lead to black peltier wire], should display around negative 1.5 ohms on a good peltier (Bad peltier in the Megaohms).
- Then, placing the palm of your hand on the black bracket should cause the resistance reading to go more negative(on a bad peltier, the reading does not change). Once the hand palm is removed, eventually the multimeter should go back to original ohm reading.
RESOLUTION:
Replace peltiers.
PCB
- Check for loose connections.
- Check for burnt components or sign of old spills, dry fluid.
RESOLUTION:
- Re-seat any loose connections.
- Replace PCB.
- If problem persists, replace chiller ramp module.
Check connections on vacuum/cooling module PCB.

## Seebeck Voltage Too Low – Cooling Module Error
id="mc-main-content">
Seebeck Voltage Too Low – Cooling Module Error
This topic covers troubleshooting procedures for low Seebeck voltages numbered 0, 1, 2, and 3. Error codes for these voltages appear in the table below.
Error Codes
Seebeck Voltage
Dec
Hex
0
024.000.00050
0x18.0x00.0x32
1
024.000.00052
0x18.0x00.0x34
2
024.000.00054
0x18.0x00.0x36
3
024.000.00056
0x18.0x00.0x38
Complaint Description
Cooling Module Error, Seebeck voltage too low (%1 C).
Generally caused by a lack of voltage generated during the Seebeck voltage check, such as a broken junction in the Peltier.
Table of Contents
Technical Support
Field Service
Laboratory Temperature
Cooling Module Sub-Assembly
Cooling Fan
Reagent or Sample Bay Out of Temperature
Not Enough Coolant in Reservoir
Cooling Module Pump
Cooling Module Thermistor
Peltiers
Printed Circuit Board
Technical Support
Auto Dispatch all Seebeck Voltage Too Low errors as a Severity 2. Troubleshoot error as normal. Inform customers FSE Field Service Engineer. will contact them to schedule service. Customer can continue to process samples if instrument restart is successful.
Troubleshooting
-
Check lab temperature.
-
Check temperature, and feel temperature of bays.
-
Check cooling module water level.
-
Check for loud noise coming from the right side of the instrument.
-
If cooling module temperature is low – in the single digits – turn instrument off, and await FSE dispatch.
-
This will require FSE dispatch.
Field Service
Laboratory Temperature
Verify the laboratory is within ambient temperature (15 - 30 ˚C).
Resolution
Set laboratory temperature between 15 - 30 ˚C, then allow instrument to warm up or cool down.
Cooling Module Sub-Assembly
From Panther Temperature screen, make sure that both Reagent and Sample bays are within temperature ranges (15.5 - 22.0 ˚C for both bays). Also, check that cooling module temperature does not drop below 3.5 ˚C.
Resolution
Restart instrument and computer. If Reagent or Sample bays do not move within temperature range, dispatch FSE.
Cooling Fan
If cooling fan is defective, replace fan.
Resolution
If cooling fan spins slowly, or does not spin, replace fan.
If cooling fan is not connected, reconnect fan.
Reagent or Sample Bay Out of Temperature
Verify both Reagent and Sample bays are within temperature range (15.5 - 22.0 ˚C for both bays).
Resolution
Reference Event IDs for Reagent and Sample bay troubleshooting.
Not Enough Coolant in Reservoir
Verify the cooling module reservoir is full.
Also, make sure there are no loose fittings, leaks, or kinks.
Resolution
- Add coolant.
- Fix loose fittings, leaks, or kinks.
Cooling Module Pump
Verify the cooling module pump is running.
Resolution
Replace coolant pump.
Cooling Module Thermistor
Note: Cooling module thermistor may be broken, or stuck at high temperature.
- Verify thermistor is connected.
- Check for thermistor broken wire.
Resolution
Replace thermistor.
Peltiers
Note: A good Peltier should feel warm to the touch.
Using Service Software, compare seebeck voltages. All should read about the same, but the one pair that reads close to 0 volts is most likely the culprit.
Use a multimeter set to ohms. Attache plus lead to red Peltier wire, and minus lead to black Peltier wire. A good Peltier displays about negative 1.5 ohms. A bad Peltier displays a reading in the Megaohms range.
Then, place the palm of your hand on the black bracket, to cause resistance reading to indicate more negative. When you remove your palm, multimeter gradually returns to original reading.
For a bad Peltier, the resistance reading does not change.
Resolution
Replace Peltiers.
Printed Circuit Board
Check for loose connections.
Check for burnt components or signs of old spills or dry fluid.
Resolution
- Reseat any loose connections.
- Replace printed circuit board.
- If problem persists, replace chiller ramp module.

## Cooling Module Error - Cooling liquid too cold
id="mc-main-content">
Cooling Module Error - Cooling liquid too cold
Error Code
Dec
Hex
024.000.00063
0x18.0x00.0x3F
Complaint Description
Cooling module error - Cooling liquid too cold.
Technical Support
Laboratory Temperature
Verify the laboratory is within ambient temperature (15-30 ˚C)
Resolution
Set Laboratory temperature between 15 - 30 ˚C, and let instrument warm up or cool down.
Cooling Module Sub-assembly
From Panther Temperature Screen, Make sure that both Reagent(15.5-22.0 ˚C) and Sample Bays (15.5-22.5 ˚C) are within temperature ranges, also check that cooling module temperature does not drop below 3.5 ˚C.
Resolution
Re-start instrument and computer. If Reagent or Sample bay do not get within temperature range, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
Laboratory Temperature
Verify the laboratory is within ambient temperature (15-30 ˚C)
Resolution
Set Laboratory temperature between 15-30 ˚C, and let instrument warm up or cool down.
Cooling Module Sub-assembly
From Panther Temperature Screen, Make sure that both Reagent(15.5-22.0 ˚C) and Sample Bays (15.5-22.5 ˚C) are within temperature ranges, also check that cooling module temperature doesn't drop below 3.5 ˚C
Resolution
Re-start instrument and computer. If Reagent or Sample bay do not get within temperature range, dispatch FSE.
Reagent or Sample Bay Out of Temperature Range
Verify both Reagent (15.5-22.0 ˚C) and Sample Bays (15.5-22.5 ˚C) are within temperature ranges.
Resolution
Reference Event Ids for Reagent and Sample bay troubleshooting.
Not Enough Coolant in Reservoir
- Verify the cooling module reservoir is full
- Make sure that there are no loose fittings, leaks, or kinks
Resolution
- Add Coolant
- Fix any leaks or kinks
Cooling Module pump
Verify the cooling module pump is running
Resolution
Replace coolant pump.
Cooling Module Thermistor (Broken or stuck at high temperature)
-
Verify the thermistor is connected
-
Check for thermistor broken wire
Resolution
Replace thermistor.
Peltiers
Note: A good peltier should feel warm to the touch
- Using Service Software, compare seebeck voltages. All should read about the same, but the one pair that read close to 0 volts is most likely the culprit.
- Using a multimeter and set to ohms [(+) lead to red peltier wire and (-) lead to black peltier wire], should display around negative 1.5 ohms on a good peltier (Bad peltier in the Megaohms). Then, placing the palm of your hand on the black bracket should cause the resistance reading to go more negative (on a bad peltier, the reading does nott change). Once the hand palm is removed, eventually the multimeter should go back to original ohm reading.
Resolution
Replace peltiers.
PCB
- Check for loose connections
- Check for burnt components or sign of old spills, dry fluid.
Resolution
- Re-seat any loose connections.
- Replace PCB.
- If problem persists, replace chiller ramp module.

## 024.003.00039
id="mc-main-content">
024.003.00039
Vacuum/Cooling – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Locking state problems.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The locking mechanism for the waste drawer is blocked by cables in the computer bay
- Open the left instrument side panel and inspect the waste drawer lock.
- Open and close the waste drawer to see if the locking mechanism is blocked by hanging cables.
- Relocate the cables that are obstructing the waste drawer interlock mechanism and ensure that they will not get in the way of the locking mechanism again.
- The clip retainers on the waste drawer rails have fallen off or there is an obstruction behind the waste drawer and the drawer will not remain fully closed.
- Open the left instrument side door and look behind the waste drawer for debris that may be obstructing the waste drawer from closing.
- Open and close the waste drawer to see if anything is in the way or if the drawer will fully close.
- During unloading of the liquid and solid waste the operator should apply pressure to the drawer to ensure that the door is fully closed while locking.
- Contact the FSE Field Service Engineer. to schedule a service visit to correct the issue with the waste drawer.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The locking mechanism for the Waste Drawer is blocked by cables in the computer bay.
- Open the left instrument side panel and inspect the Waste Drawer lock.
- Open and close the Waste drawer to see if the locking mechanism is blocked by hanging cables.
- Relocate the cables that are obstructing the Waste Drawer interlock mechanism.
- Ensure that the cables will not get in the way of the locking mechanism again.
N/A
- The clip retainers on the Waste Drawer rails have fallen off or there is an obstruction behind the Waste drawer and the drawer will not remain fully closed.
- Open the left instrument side door and look behind the Waste Drawer for debris that may be preventing the Waste Drawer from closing.
- Open and close the Waste Drawer to see if anything is in the way or if the drawer will fully close.
- During unloading of the liquid and solid waste, ask the operator to apply pressure to the drawer to ensure that the door is fully closed while locking.
- Contact an FSE to schedule a service visit to correct the issue with the Waste Drawer.
N/A
- Missing or broken spring on the Waste Drawer or the tab that holds tension on the spring when the drawer is closed is bent, preventing the locking mechanism from closing properly.
- Open the left instrument side panel and inspect the locking mechanism.
- Open and close the Waste Drawer to visually inspect the action of the locking mechanism.
- Determine if the mechanism is properly engaging when the drawer is fully closed.
- Replace the spring if it is missing or broken.
- Adjust the tab if it is bent.
N/A
- Missing or broken spring on the locking mechanism, preventing the locking mechanism from closing properly.
- Open the left instrument side panel and inspect the locking mechanism.
- Open and close the Waste Drawer to visually inspect the action of the locking mechanism.
- Determine if the mechanism is properly engaging when the drawer is fully closed.
- Replace the spring if it is missing or broken.
N/A
- The clip that holds the Waste Drawer closed is broken and the drawer does not stay fully closed when the operator closes the drawer.
- Open the left instrument side panel and inspect behind the Waste Drawer for debris.
- Inspect the end of each of the slide rails where the retaining clips are located.
- Open and close the Waste Drawer to visually inspect that the drawer if the drawer fully closes and stays in place when closed.
- If broken rail retaining clips are determined to be the cause of the problem, replace the slide rail(s).
N/A
- The ribbon cable connectors on the Cooling Module or the interlock are improperly seated or the cable is damaged.
- Inspect the connectors at the Cooling Module and at the interlock for proper seating.
- Inspect the ribbon cable for damage.
- Using Service Software, test interlock reading and function.
Note—If the connector is upside down, the Cooling Module will not initialize and the green light on the Cooling Module will not be lit.
- Reseat the connectors at the interlock and the Cooling Module PCB.
- Inspect the ribbon cable that runs from the Cooling Module PCB to the interlock for nicks, especially if the ribbon cable is not contained in the cable race at the back wall of the instrument.
- Replace the cable if it is damaged.
N/A
- Sensor on interlock or interlock pin is obstructed by fluid or debris.
- Inspect the interlock and locking mechanism for debris or evidence of fluid leakage.
- Remove the locking mechanism and clean with 70% EtOH.
- Inspect the action of the solenoid pin and locking mechanism by hand.
- If dried fluid was the cause of the failure, stickiness of the mechanism and the interlock pin movement will be improved by cleaning.
- Allow the mechanism and the interlock to dry and reinstall.
- Using Service Software, verify that the interlock functions properly, and the drawer closes and locks properly
N/A
- Interlock damaged or failed.
After all other options have been attempted and the interlock problem persists, test with a new interlock.
- Remove the locking mechanism and replace the interlock.
- Using Service Software, test the new interlock.
- If the problem does not recur with the new interlock, the part may have failed and a replacement was required.
N/A

id="mc-main-content">

AMP (Inc. 3)
Complaint Description
-
High Temp (Incubator 1) Temperature Out of Range.
-
Transition (Incubator 2) Temperature Out of Range.
-
AMP (Incubator 3) Temperature Out of Range.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Troubleshooting
-
Possible Root Cause
-
Field Service
-
Laboratory Temperature
-
Incubator Main PCB
-
Incubator Heater Foils and Connections
-
Faulty Incubator Fan
Technical Support
Troubleshooting
- Check lab temperature.
- Check the time since exited power save. Incubator temperature should lock after thirty minutes of warm-up.
- Make sure the instrument is not in direct sunlight.
- Make sure there are no objects blocking vents.
- Restart the instrument.
- If the incubator temperature doesn’t come back into range, notify FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- If Incubator 1 temperature is out of range (too low) during MW cleaning: could be due to cold endozyme. Recommend to monitor.
Possible Root Cause
- Lab temperature outside range
- Failed PCB
- Failed incubator
- For Incubator 1 only: cold endozyme (= Magwash cleaning solution)
Field Service
Laboratory Temperature
- Ensure laboratory room temperature is 15 – 30˚ Celsius.
- Verify instrument is not in direct sunlight - close window blinds, if applicable.
- Verify instrument has proper service clearance on the left and right, with no foreign objects blocking the air vents on either side.
Resolution
- Ask operator to set laboratory temp to 15 – 30˚ Celsius.
- Close blinds (if applicable).
- Remove foreign objects that may impede airflow from either side of instrument.
Test
- Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
- Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1) 64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2) 43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3) 42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
Incubator Main PCB
- Remove Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Inspect the PCB for signs of electronic damage.
Resolution
If damage is observed, replace the Incubator Main PCB.
TEST:
- Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
- Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
See Panther Service Manual for required replacement verifications.
Incubator Heater Foils and Connections
Troubleshooting:
-
Remove the Mid Bay Cover to inspect Incubator PCB connections.
-
Inspect the following:
Note: The labeling on the Incubator PCB is counterintuitive. The left connector is labeled Heat Housing , and is connected to the Bottom Heater. The right connector is labeled Heat Bottom , and is connected to the Side Heater.
- Connect Bottom Heater foil (x1), and Switch A to Heat Housing .
- Connect Side Heater foils (x2), and Switch B to Heat Bottom .
-
If all connectors are correctly and securely seated, then move to step 4.
-
Test the resistance for both Heaters by following these steps:
-
Turn the power off to the instrument.
-
Unplug the Bottom Heater connector.
-
On the connector, using a multimeter, test the resistance for each of the following combinations:
Test
Lead Combination
Expected Resistance (Ohms)
A
Blue to Orange 1
10-20
B
Blue to Orange 2
10-20
C
Orange 1 to Orange 2
20-30*
* This expected value will be additive of tests A and B. So, for example, if Test A was 13 Ohms, and Test B was 14 Ohms, the expected resistance for Test C would be ~27 Ohms.
Note: On all heater foils, the Blue wire is (-) and Orange wire is (+).
- Plug the connector back in.
- Repeat steps A-D for the Side Heater.
-
Diagnosis:
a. Bottom Heater: Low ohm reading for Tests A and / or B indicates Bad Bottom Heater.
This will also often show up in the logs or error messages as an IC Failure.
b. Side Heater: High ohm reading for Tests A and / or B indicates Bad Side Heater.
This will also often manifest as the Incubator being able to initialize but will never reach thermal lock. The Incubator temperature will be ~1-2 degree below the set temperature for the incubator.
Example: HT incubator settles in at about 62 - 63 degrees C.
Resolution
-
Correct any incorrect connections as required.
-
If either of the heater foils fail the resistance test in step 4 above, replace entire incubator.
Test
-
Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
-
Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
See Panther Service Manual for required replacement verifications.
Faulty Incubator Fan
Using Service Software, initialize the Incubator. To replicate the issue, turn the fan on.
Replace the fan.

## Incubator Temperature Fails Plausibility Check
id="mc-main-content">
Incubator Temperature Fails Plausibility Check
Error Codes
Dec
Hex
Module
032.001.00114
20.01.72
High Temp (Inc. 1)
033.001.00114
21.01.72
Transition (Inc. 2)
034.001.00114
22.01.72
AMP (Inc. 3)
Complaint Description
- High Temp Incubator temperature fails plausibility check
- Transition Incubator temperature fails plausibility check
- Amplification Incubator temperature fails plausibility check
Every 1600ms temperature readings from redundant sensors on the Axis PCB are checked to ensure they are in range of 5°C to 75°C. If one temperature is out of range the heater is stopped and an error “ 72 ” is sent. The error message contains both temperature readings:
20 00 03 01 72 3E 11 00 00 Temperature 1 : 44.14°C Temperature 2 : 0°C
In v7.1 software and lower, a condition exists in which there could be a delay in the reporting between these two temperatures from the sensors responsible, creating a false fault condition. This was resolved in v7.2 software and higher. See TSE Technical Service Engineer. Review below for more details.
Technical Support
Troubleshooting
- Restart the instrument
- If the incubator temperature fails again, notify FSE Field Service Engineer.
Possible Root Causes
- Failed PCB
- Failed Incubator
Field Service
Incubator Main PCB
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Inspect for the PCB for signs of electronic damage.
Resolution
-
See TSE Review below for more details.
-
Replace faulty Main PCB
Test
-
Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
-
Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
Heater Foils and PCB Connections
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to inspect Incubator PCB connections.
- Inspect the following:
- Bottom Heater foil (x1) and Switch A should be connected to “Heat Housing”.
- Side Heater foils (x2) and Switch B should be connected to "Heat Bottom".
Note: Problems with side heater foils will allow the Incubator to initialize but will never reach thermal lock.
- Using voltmeter, verify that bottom (x1) and side heater foils (x2) each has correct resistance (~14 Ohms).
Note: On all heater foils, the Blue wire is (-) & Orange wire is (+).
Resolution
- See TSE Review below for more details.
- Correct any wrong connections as required.
- If heater foils resistance is open and irreparable, replace entire incubator.
Test
-
Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
-
Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
Axis Board PCB
- Inspect cable connections at internal Axis Board PCB and external Main PCB.
- Using Service Software, make sure Axis Board PCB is properly working.
Resolution
- See TSE Review Below for more details.
- Replace faulty component: Internal Axis Board PCB (#902789), ribbon cable (#902868), and/or Main PCB (#902923).
Test
-
Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
-
Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
TSE Review
Axis PCBs have had firmware upgraded to mitigate timing delay between temperature readings from on-board redundant sensors. Part # (902789) did not change. Updated Axis PCBs will be recognized by the black “dot” visible in the indicated location illustrated below.
Note: If your system is on v7.2 or higher, older Axis PCBs (no black “dot”) can still be used, as the timing issue with those boards was resolved in v7.2 software and higher.

id="mc-main-content">

- Ambient sensor of instrument

Field Service

Technical Support
Troubleshooting
Restart Instrument to verify problem persists.
Review logs and identify faulty component:
20 00 03 01 74 00 : Bottom Heater_1 IC Drive (check bottom heater/replace incubator)
20 00 03 01 74 01: Bottom Heater _2 IC Drive (check bottom heater/replace incubator)
20 00 03 01 74 02: Wall Heater_1 IC Drive (check side heater/replace incubator)
20 00 03 01 74 03: Wall Heater_2 IC Drive (check side heater/replace incubator)
20 00 03 01 74 04: FAN IC Drive (check fan/replace fan)
Possible Root Causes
If problem persists, it usually requires FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch.
Field Service
Fan Cable and Connections
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Inspect fan cable connection at PCB.
- Remove the Incubator cover and inspect fan cable for damage or defects.
Resolution
- Ensure the fan is connected to the “PWR fan” port on the PCB.
- Replace fan if cable or connectors found to be damaged or defective.
Test
-
Perform an error-free System Level Operational Qualification (OQ).
-
In System Software GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. , verify Incubator temps are within specification.
Module
Temp (Range)

64°C (+/- 0.5°C)

AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
Incorrect Fan Installed
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Remove the Incubator cover to inspect the fan part number label:
- High Temp (Incubator 1) should read PMD2412PTB1-A (11.8W) (#902924 or #903627)
- Transition (Incubator 2) should read PMD2412PTB3-A (6.7W) (#902925)
- AMP (Incubator 3) should read PMD2412PTB3-A (6.7W) (#902925)
Resolution
Remove and replace with correct fan for appropriate Incubator.
Test
-
Perform an error-free System Level Operational Qualification (OQ).
-
In System Software GUI, verify Incubator temps are within specification.
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)

42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
Fan Bearings
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Remove the Incubator cover to manually inspect the fan impeller movement for friction due to corroded bearings:
Resolution
- If friction is observed during impeller movement, bearings may be corroded and fan should be replaced.
- Replace with correct fan for associated incubator:
- High Temp (Incubator 1) - PMD2412PTB1-A (11.8W) (#902924 or #903627)
- Transition (Incubator 2) - PMD2412PTB3-A (6.7W) (#902925)
- AMP (Incubator 3) - PMD2412PTB3-A (6.7W) (#902925)
Test
-
Perform an error-free System Level Operational Qualification (OQ).
-
In System Software GUI, verify Incubator temps are within specification.
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
Incubator Heater Foils and Connections
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to inspect Incubator PCB connections.
- Inspect the following:
- Bottom Heater foil (x2) and Switch A should be connected to “Heat Housing”.
-
Side Heater foils (x2) and Switch B should be connected to "Heat Bottom". (Side heater connects to “Heat Bottom” is not an error.)
Note— Problems with side heater foils will allow the Incubator to initialize, but will never reach thermal lock (usually 1 degree below target temperature).
-
Using voltmeter, power down instrument – unplug heater connection. Verify bottom (x2) and side heater foils (x2) each has correct resistance (~14 ohms: 12-16 ohms).
Note— On all heater foils, the  Blue  wire is (-), and Orange  wire is (+):
Blue: Orange expect 12-16 ohms
Orange: Orange expect: 24-32 ohms
Resolution
- Correct any wrong connections as required.
- If heater foils resistance is open and irreparable, replace entire incubator.
Test
-
Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
-
Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
Incubator Main PCB
- Remove Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Inspect the PCB for signs of electronic damage.
Resolution
If damage is observed, replace the Incubator Main PCB.
Test
-
Ensure the system resets without error in System Software.
-
Ensure Incubator temperatures eventually stabilize and lock:
Module
Temp (Range)
High Temp (Inc. 1)
64°C (+/- 0.5°C)
Transition (Inc. 2)
43.7°C (+1.0° / -0.5°C)
AMP (Inc. 3)
42.7°C (+/- 0.3°C)
TSE Review
For this error, the error number/6th byte refers to the damaged component.
Error number/6th byte value:
0: Bottom Heater_1 IC Drive
1: Bottom Heater _2 IC Drive
2: Wall Heater_1 IC Drive
3: Wall Heater_2 IC Drive
4: FAN IC Drive
Example 1 - Operator level message:
11/04/2021 12:12:22 Fatal 032.001.00116 High Temp Incubator status fail of the power drive IC of the heater or of the FAN (error 1)
Error indicates bottom heater foil 2.
FSE measured the heater foil resistance for HT, and compared against Amp and Transition incubators.
HT
Amp
Transition
Bottom_1
16.7
16.7
14.4
Bottom_2
22.3
15.7
14.4
Wall_1
16.9
14.9
15.1
Wall_2
16.8
14.9
15.0
FSE swapped the bottom and wall heater connections for HT and was unable to replicate error in service software.
FSE launched PantherMain:
Example 2 - Log level:
11/04/2021 22:00:42 (04 18:00:42) [E] (Fatal , High ) [Incubator1] High Temp Incubator status fail of the power drive IC of the heater or of the FAN (error 3) (AutomaticModuleEvent) [0x20.0x01.0x0074] bytes: 20 00 03 01 74 03 [032.001.00116]
Note the error followed the heating element.
Resolution: Heating foils are not replaceable, replace HT incubator.

Technical Support
Auto Dispatch Fan Speed Errors as a Severity 2. Troubleshoot error as normal. Inform customers FSE Field Service Engineer. will contact them to schedule service. Customer can continue to process samples if instrument restart in successful.
Troubleshooting
- Restart the instrument.
- Wait for about an hour to see if the error repeats during start-up.
Possible Root Causes
- Faulty or misconnected fan.
Field Service
Fan Cable and Connections
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Inspect internal fan cable connection at Main PCB.
- Remove the Incubator cover and inspect internal fan cable for damage or defects.
Resolution
-
Ensure the internal fan is connected to the “ PWR fan ” port on the Main PCB.
**If affecting the AMP Incubator, ensure External Fan is NOT connected to “PWR fan” on Main PCB.
-
Replace fan if cable or connectors found to be damaged or defective.

- AMP (Incubator 3) should read PMD2412PTB3-A (6.7W) (#902925)

## Incubator Door Failure – IDFx
id="mc-main-content">
Incubator Door Failure – IDFx
Error Codes
DEC
HEX
Module
032.001.00121
20.01.79
High Temp (Inc. 1) (IDF1)
033.001.00121
21.01.79
Transition (Inc. 2) (IDF2)
034.001.00121
22.01.79
AMP (Inc. 3) (IDF3)
Complaint Description
-
High Temperature (Incubator 1) Door Failure (IDF1).
-
Transition (Incubator 2) Door Failure (IDF2).
-
Amplification (Incubator 3) Door Failure (IDF3).
Technical Support
Troubleshooting
-
Restart the instrument.
-
If reset passes, customer can run. However, door may be sticky so issue may recur. Always notify FSE Field Service Engineer. .
-
If reset fails, dispatch FSE.
Field Service
Obstructions or Impeded Door Movement
-
Perform visual inspection for any mechanical or physical obstructions.
-
Manually actuate door by hand to feel for binding in door open/close movements.
Resolution
-
Address and remove any visually observed mechanical or physical obstructions.
-
Clean and relubricate door slide guides.
Test
Using Service Software, repeat testing by verifying the sensor properly reports output as “Open” and “Closed” accordingly.
Warped Door Due to Over-Torqued Mounting Screws
-
Manually actuate door by hand to feel for binding in door open/close movements.
-
Perform visual inspection to ensure door is not warped.
Note— Over-torqueing screw can warp the screw hole and push the door open, see pictures. It may be intermittent or permanently read "Open".
Resolution
-
Reduce torque on mounting screws to see if door comes back into alignment.
-
Replace Incubator Door if warped beyond repair.
Test
Using Service Software, repeat testing by verifying the sensor properly reports output as “Open” and “Closed” accordingly.
Door PCB, Sensor, Pin, and Cable Connection
-
Visually inspect Door PCB for:
-
Cable Connections between Incubator Door PCB and Incubator Main PCB.
-
Door Pin alignment and clearance within Door Sensor.
-
Using Service Software, verify the sensor properly reports output as “Open” and “Closed” accordingly.
Resolution
-
Re-seat both ends of cable at Incubator Door PCB & Incubator Main PCB.
-
Using a swab and alcohol, clean the door sensor and door pin to remove any residue that may affect functionality of the optical door sensor.
-
Replace door home sensor/PCB if faulty.
Test
Using Service Software, repeat testing by verifying the sensor properly reports output as “Open” and “Closed” accordingly.
Linear Distributor Alignment to Incubator (Poor MTU Placement)
-
In Service Software, utilize Linear Distributor to place an MTU at the affected Incubator.
-
Ensure the transition of MTU into & out of the incubator slot is “clean” and unobstructed, with little to no “jitter” or “bounce” during transition.
-
Ensure the MTU placement does not obstruct door from closing.
Resolution
-
Perform Linear Distributor Teaching to Affected Incubator.
-
Perform Incubator Slot Alignment to Door at affected Incubator.
Test
Using Service Software, repeat testing by verifying the sensor properly reports output as “Open” and “Closed” accordingly.

## Incubator Thermistor Failure – ITFx
id="mc-main-content">
Incubator Thermistor Failure – ITFx
Difference Between Temperature Sensor Values Exceeds Allowable Limit
Error Codes
Dec
Hex
Module
032.001.00122
20.01.7A
High Temp (Inc. 1) (ITF1)
033.001.00122
21.01.7A
Transition (Inc. 2) (ITF2)
034.001.00122
22.01.7A
AMP (Inc. 3) (ITF3)
Complaint Description
- Incubator 1 (HT) Thermistor Failure… (ITF1).
- Incubator 2 (Transition) Thermistor Failure… (ITF2).
- Incubator 3 (AMP) Thermistor Failure… (ITF3).
Every 1600ms temperature readings from redundant sensors on the Incubator Axis PCB are checked to ensure the averaged difference between sensors is < 0.5°C. If found >0.5°C, the heater is stopped and error “ 7A ” is generated. The error message contains both temperatures:
22 00 03 01 7A 00 00 A4 10 Temperature 1 : 0°C Temperature 2 : 42.60°C
In v7.1 software and lower, a condition exists in which there could be a delay in the reporting between these two temperatures from the sensors responsible, creating a false fault condition. This was resolved in v7.2 software and higher. See TSE Technical Service Engineer. Review below for more details.
Technical Support
Troubleshooting
- Check lab temperature
- Check the time since exited power save (incubator temperature should lock after 30 minute of warm-up)
- Make sure the instrument isn’t in direct sunlight
- Make sure there are no objects blocking vents
- Restart the instrument
- If the incubator temperature doesn’t come back into range, notify FSE Field Service Engineer.
- If Incubator 1 temperature is out of range (too low) during MW cleaning: could be due to cold endozyme. Recommend to monitor.
Possible Root Cause
- Lab temperature outside range
- Failed PCB
- Failed incubator
- For Incubator 1 only: cold endozyme (=Magwash cleaning solution)
Field Service
Firmware
- Ensure firmware has been upgrades to v3.2.2.18 (SP2) or later.
Resolution
Run Instrument Setup to ensure latest Firmware is correctly pushed to the affected incubator.
Test
In system software, ensure the system resets without error, and temperatures eventually stabilize and lock.
Incubator Main PCB
- Remove the Mid Bay Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB(s).
- Inspect for the PCB for signs of electronic damage.
Resolution
- See TSE Review below for more details.
- Replace faulty Main PCB
Test
In system software, ensure the system resets without error, and temperatures eventually stabilize and lock.
Axis Board PCB
- Inspect cable connections at internal Axis Board PCB and external Main PCB.
- Using Service Software, make sure Axis Board PCB is properly working.
Resolution
- See TSE Review Below for more details.
- Replace faulty component: Internal Axis Board PCB (#902789), ribbon cable (#902868), and/or Main PCB (#902923).
Test
In system software, ensure the system resets without error, and temperatures eventually stabilize and lock.
TSE Review
Axis PCBs have had firmware upgraded to mitigate timing delay between temperature readings from on-board redundant sensors. Part # (902789) did not change. Updated Axis PCBs will be recognized by the black “dot” visible in the indicated location illustrated below.
Note— If your system is on v7.2 or higher, older Axis PCBs (no black “dot”) can still be used, as the timing issue with those boards was resolved in v7.2 software and higher.

## 032.002.00001
id="mc-main-content">
032.002.00001
High Temperature Incubator – COP System Message
Error Codes
This topic consolidates information for three error codes, one for each Incubator Carousel Drive.
Drive

034.002.00001
0x20.0x02.0x01
0x21.0x02.0x01
0x22.0x02.0x01
Complaint Description
Incubator Carousel Drive 1, 2, or 3 failed to initialize:
- Incubator 1 = High Temperature Incubator.
- Incubator 2 = Transition Incubator.
- Incubator 3 = AMP Incubator.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Dip Switch
- Door Home Sensor or Pin
- Over Torque of Door Fastener
- Carousel Home Sensor or Pin
- Door Assembly
- Faulty COP Cable or Connection
Technical Support
Restart the instrument to verify problem persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem and will require an FSE Field Service Engineer. service call.
Field Service
Dip Switch
Make sure dip switches on the Incubator main PCB are correctly set.
Dip Switch
Transition Incubator
HT Incubator
Amplification Incubator
1
ON
OFF
OFF
2
OFF
OFF
OFF
3
OFF
OFF
OFF
4
OFF
OFF
OFF
RESOLUTION:
Set the dip switch correctly.
TEST:
Initialize the Incubator.
Door Home Sensor or Pin
Using Service Software, verify that the sensor outputs “Open/Close”.
RESOLUTION:
- Using a swab and alcohol, clean the door sensor and door pin of any residue that may affect the optical door sensor.
- Replace the door sensor if faulty.
TEST:
Initialize the Incubator.
Over Torque of Door Fastener
Over-torquing the screw can warp the screw hole and push the door open. Fault may be intermittent, or door status may permanently read “Open”.
Make sure that the door is not warped, and use Service Software to determine if door sensor is properly reading.
RESOLUTION:
Reduce torque on the door fastener – replace door if warped beyond repair.
TEST:
Initialize the Incubator.
Carousel Home Sensor or Pin
Using Service Software, verify that the sensor outputs “In/Out”.
RESOLUTION:
- Using a swab and alcohol, clean the carousel home sensor and door pin of any residue that may affect the optical home sensor.
- Replace the carousel home sensor if faulty.
TEST:
Initialize the Incubator.
Door Assembly
The Incubator cover, wiring, or over torqued door screw can skew the door away from the carousel home pin.
Verify the door seats as flush as possible.
Verify the carousel home sensor correctly interacts with the carousel home pin.
RESOLUTION:
Re-seat the door ensuring the Incubator cover, wiring, and screws do not cause the door to skew away from the carousel home pin.
TEST:
Initialize the Incubator.
Faulty COP Cable or Connection
Isolate faulty connection or connections. The Panther modules are on a CAN-bus – the faulty connections may be upstream and caused by a preceding module. Use the jumpers to assist in isolating the faulty cable cable connection.
RESOLUTION:
Replace the faulty cable or cable connection.
TEST:
Initialize the Incubator.

TABLE OF CONTENTS

-
Incubator Target Not Reached Since Motor Is Not Moving
- Poor Home Pin or Door Interaction
- Home Pin Sensor Faulty or Dirty
- Faulty Pulley or Belt
