Technical Support
Mandatory Dispatch: Classify all Incubator Target Not Reached errors as Severity 2. Troubleshoot error as normal. Inform customers FSE Field Service Engineer. will contact them to set up service. Customer can continue to process samples if instrument restart is successful.
Restart the instrument to verify problem persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem, and will require an FSE service call.
Field Service
Poor Home Pin or Door Interaction
Using Service Software verify the interaction between the home sensor and the home pin – the sensor output should correctly read “Open” or “Close”.
Resolution
-
Install door clip per Panther System Service Manual.
Note: Screws were cut into all Panthers above Serial #00919 – Incubators with a screw do not require installation of door clips. If Panther SN is above #00919, ensure screw is present and secure.
-
Verify that the interaction between the home pin and the home sensor is optimal; the home pin should be reasonably centered in the home sensor; the home pin should not contact the home sensor during carousel movement.
Test
-
Initialize the Incubator.
-
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Home Pin Sensor Faulty or Dirty
Resolution
Using a swab and alcohol, clean the door sensor of any residue that may affect the optical door sensor.
Test
-
Using Service software, verify the sensor output as “Open” and “Close”.
-
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Faulty Pulley or Belt
Check pulley and belt for damage.
Check belt tension.
Resolution
-
Replace pulley and/or belt.
-
Re-tension the belt.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Motor Faulty
Resolution
Replace Carousel motor.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Encoder Cable or Connection Faulty
Check the motor encoder cable and connection at the Incubator Carousel Drive main PCB for damage.
Resolution
-
Replace the encoder cable.
-
Replace the Incubator main PCB.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Motor Cable or Connection Faulty
Check the cable and connection at the Incubator main PCB for damage.
RESOLUTION:
-
Replace the motor cable.
-
Replace the Incubator main PCB.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.

id="mc-main-content">
033.001.00115
Transition Incubator – COP System Message
Complaint Description
Ambient temperature fails plausibility check.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- See FSE Field Service Engineer. Root Cause
N/A
Restart Instrument to verify problems persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem and will require an FSE service call.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Ambient sensor of instrument
- Use Service Software to determine if ambient temperature sensor is faulty (loose connection, faulty sensor, shorted 5 volt supply to Ambient).
- Replace ambient sensor (found on Cooling Unit)
( Trunk Stock Part )
- Cooling Module PCB Removal and Replacement.
- 5 volt supply
- Make sure that 5V supply going to ambient sensor is not shorted. Possibly wire pinched in the Input Queue.

- Possibly faulty Main PCB

## 033.001.00117
id="mc-main-content">
033.001.00117
Transition Incubator – COP System Message
Complaint Description
FAN speed is out of range.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
Faulty Incubator fan system
Instruct the customer to complete the following steps:
- Restart the instrument and allow the system to unload MTUs.
- Wait an hour to see if the error quickly recurs during start-up.
If the error recurs during start-up, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
PANTHER System Operator's Manual
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Fan is connected to the wrong port on the Incubator Main PCB.
- Remove the Upper Bay Front Cover to expose the Incubator Main PCB.
- Connect the fan to the correct port on the PCB, labeled PWR fan .
- PANTHER System Service Manual Upper Bay Front Cover Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual Incubator Main PCB Removal and Replacement
- Faulty cable/cable to fan
- Remove the Incubator cover.
- Inspect the fan connections.
- Diagnose the integrity of the connections and resolve accordingly.
N/A
- Wrong Incubator fan is installed
- Remove the Incubator cover to expose the fan Part Number.
- The the P/N for the correct fan for Incubator 2 (Transition) is PMD2412PTB3-A(6.7W) .
- If the wrong fan is installed, remove and replace with the correct fan.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Incubator Fan Removal and Replacement
- Fan RPM is outside specified range/fan RPM failure
- Remove the Incubator cover.
- Verify the fan impeller moves smoothly.
- If there is undue friction, the fan is faulty.
- Replace the Incubator fan.
- PANTHER System Service Manual Incubator Fan Removal and Replacement
- See: Corroded Fan Bearings
- See: New Fan Bearings

## 033.002.00001
id="mc-main-content">
033.002.00001
Transition Temperature Incubator – COP System Message
Error Codes
This topic consolidates information for three error codes, one for each Incubator Carousel Drive.
Drive
Dec
Hex
1
2
3
032.002.00001
033.002.00001
034.002.00001
0x20.0x02.0x01
0x21.0x02.0x01
0x22.0x02.0x01
Complaint Description
Incubator Carousel Drive 1, 2, or 3 failed to initialize:
- Incubator 1 = High Temperature Incubator
- Incubator 2 = Transition Incubator
- Incubator 3 = AMP Incubator
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Dip Switch
- Door Home Sensor or Pin
- Over Torque of Door Fastener
- Carousel Home Sensor or Pin
- Door Assembly
- Faulty COP Cable or Connection
Technical Support
Restart the instrument to verify problem persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem and will require an FSE Field Service Engineer. service call.
Field Service
Dip Switch
Make sure dip switches on the Incubator main PCB are correctly set.
Dip Switch
Transition Incubator
HT Incubator
Amplification Incubator
1
ON
OFF
OFF
2
OFF
OFF
OFF
3
OFF
OFF
OFF
4
OFF
OFF
OFF
Resolution
Set the dip switch correctly.
Test
Initialize the Incubator.
Door Home Sensor or Pin
Using Service Software, verify that the sensor outputs “Open/Close”.
Resolution
- Using a swab and alcohol, clean the door sensor and door pin of any residue that may affect the optical door sensor.
- Replace the door sensor if faulty.
Test
Initialize the Incubator.
Over Torque of Door Fastener
Over-torquing the screw can warp the screw hole and push the door open. Fault may be intermittent, or door status may permanently read “Open”.
Make sure that the door is not warped, and use Service Software to determine if door sensor is properly reading.
Resolution
Reduce torque on the door fastener – replace door if warped beyond repair.
Test
Initialize the Incubator.
Carousel Home Sensor or Pin
Using Service Software, verify that the sensor outputs “In/Out”.
Resolution
- Using a swab and alcohol, clean the carousel home sensor and door pin of any residue that may affect the optical home sensor.
- Replace the carousel home sensor if faulty.
Test
Initialize the Incubator.
Door Assembly
The Incubator cover, wiring, or over torqued door screw can skew the door away from the carousel home pin.
Verify the door seats as flush as possible.
Verify the carousel home sensor correctly interacts with the carousel home pin.
Resolution
Re-seat the door ensuring the Incubator cover, wiring, and screws do not cause the door to skew away from the carousel home pin.
Test
Initialize the Incubator.
Faulty COP Cable or Connection
Isolate faulty connection or connections. The Panther modules are on a CAN-bus – the faulty connections may be upstream and caused by a preceding module. Use the jumpers to assist in isolating the faulty cable cable connection.
Resolution
Replace the faulty cable or cable connection.
Test
Initialize the Incubator.

Technical Support

033.002.00009

Technical Support
Restart the instrument to verify problem persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem, and will require an FSE Field Service Engineer. service call.
Field Service
Pulley or Belt Tension Not Correct
Resolution
- Replace pulley and/or re-tension belt.
- Perform Carousel Slot alignment.
- Perform Linear Distributor teaching to the Incubator.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Faulty Carousel Components
Check integrity of motor, belt, pulley and bearings.
Refer to Incubator Troubleshooting Best Practices .
Resolution
Replace defective component. If bearings are determined to be defective, replace the Incubator.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.

Complaint Description
Target for Incubator Carousel Drive not reached, since motor is not moving.
- Incubator 1 = High Temperature Incubator
- Incubator 2 = Transition Temperature Incubator
- Incubator 3 = Amplification Incubator
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Poor Home Pin or Door Interaction
- Home Pin Sensor Faulty or Dirty
- Faulty Pulley or Belt
- Carousel Motor Faulty
- Encoder Cable or Connection Faulty
- Motor Cable or Connection Faulty
Technical Support
Mandatory Dispatch: Classify all Incubator Target Not Reached errors as Severity 2. Troubleshoot error as normal. Inform customers FSE Field Service Engineer. will contact them to set up service. Customer can continue to process samples if instrument restart is successful.
Restart the instrument to verify problem persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem, and will require an FSE service call.
Field Service
Poor Home Pin or Door Interaction
Using Service Software verify the interaction between the home sensor and the home pin – the sensor output should correctly read “Open” or “Close”.
Resolution
-
Install door clip per Panther System Service Manual.
Note: Screws were cut into all Panthers above Serial #00919 – Incubators with a screw do not require installation of door clips. If Panther SN is above #00919, ensure screw is present and secure.
-
Verify that the interaction between the home pin and the home sensor is optimal; the home pin should be reasonably centered in the home sensor; the home pin should not contact the home sensor during carousel movement.
Test
-
Initialize the Incubator.
-
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Home Pin Sensor Faulty or Dirty
Resolution
Using a swab and alcohol, clean the door sensor of any residue that may affect the optical door sensor.
Test
-
Using Service software, verify the sensor output as “Open” and “Close”.
-
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Faulty Pulley or Belt
Check pulley and belt for damage.
Check belt tension.
Resolution
-
Replace pulley and/or belt.
-
Re-tension the belt.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Motor Faulty
Resolution
Replace Carousel motor.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Encoder Cable or Connection Faulty
Check the motor encoder cable and connection at the Incubator Carousel Drive main PCB for damage.
Resolution
-
Replace the encoder cable.
-
Replace the Incubator main PCB.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ
Motor Cable or Connection Faulty
Check the cable and connection at the Incubator main PCB for damage.
Resolution
-
Replace the motor cable.
-
Replace the Incubator main PCB.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.

Faulty Incubator fan system.

Isolation Procedure

Resolution
-
Install door clip per Panther System Service Manual.
Note: Screws were cut into all Panthers above Serial #00919 – Incubators with a screw do not require installation of door clips. If Panther SN is above #00919, ensure screw is present and secure.
-
Verify that the interaction between the home pin and the home sensor is optimal; the home pin should be reasonably centered in the home sensor; the home pin should not contact the home sensor during carousel movement.
Test
-
Initialize the Incubator.
-
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Home Pin Sensor Faulty or Dirty
Resolution
Using a swab and alcohol, clean the door sensor of any residue that may affect the optical door sensor.
Test
-
Using Service software, verify the sensor output as “Open” and “Close”.
-
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Faulty Pulley or Belt
Check pulley and belt for damage.
Check belt tension.
Resolution
-
Replace pulley and/or belt.
-
Re-tension the belt.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Motor Faulty
Resolution
Replace Carousel motor.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Encoder Cable or Connection Faulty
Check the motor encoder cable and connection at the Incubator Carousel Drive main PCB for damage.
Resolution
-
Replace the encoder cable.
-
Replace the Incubator main PCB.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Motor Cable or Connection Faulty
Check the cable and connection at the Incubator main PCB for damage.
Resolution
-
Replace the motor cable.
-
Replace the Incubator main PCB.
Test
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.

## Out of Service Due to Incorrect Level Detection  –  Magnetic Wash 1 and 2
id="mc-main-content">
Out of Service Due to Incorrect Level Detection – Magnetic Wash 1 and 2
Error Codes
Magnetic Wash 1
Magnetic Wash 2
Dec
Hex
Dec
Hex
048.000.00044
0x18.0x00.0x030
049.000.00044
0x18.0x00.0x031
Complaint Description
Out of service due to incorrect level detection.
Technical Support
Data pending.
Field Service
VAC-PRESS Level Out of Range Low
-
From PANTHER Dashboard launch Event Log and identify message assignment.
-
Using Service Software to identify possible pressure leak on Liquid Waste Bottle.
-
Check if VAC Filter got soaked. Tighten bottle cap and connectors
-
Check in Service Software if residual fluid was left in MTU tube position during Wash Fluid Prime.
Resolution
-
If VAC Filter got soaked, tighten bottle cap and connectors.
-
Replace vacuum filter if wet.
Test
In Service Software verify vacuum pressure is within range.
Aspirator Clogged
Resolution
-
Clean/replace faulty MW aspirator.
-
Possibly unclog MW aspirator tubing and/or VAC manifold.

Technical Support
N/A

Magnetic Wash Mixer Error
Mixer started
2020-10-13 11:56:04,612|[ProcessEvent]|PantherEventLogCreator|EventLogEntry|Info|Normal| <>(Message) 16:55:44.546: No error. Event [0x31.0x02.0x0000] bytes: 31 20 00 02 00
Unable to execute the stop mix command
2020-10-13 11:56:04,612|[ProcessEvent]|PantherEventLogCreator|EventLogEntry|Info|Error| <>(Fatal) 16:55:54.646: Magnetic Wash 2 mixer error (Unable to execute command). Event [0x31.0x02.0x000E] bytes: 31 18 03 02 0E
2020-10-13 11:56:04,612|[ProcessEvent]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error|10/13/2020 16:56:04 (13 11:56:04) [E] (Fatal , High ) [MagWash2] Magnetic Wash 2 mixer error (Unable to execute command) ID=59911 MagneticWashResponse: , start=16:50:21.746 end=16:56:04.046. Event [0x31.0x02.0x000E] at 16:55:54.646 bytes: 31 18 03 02 0E [049.002.00014]
Resolution
Check the mixing sensor, in SSW first – the sensor state can be read without initializing the MW. This sensor may have grease or is unplugged.

## 064.001.00001
id="mc-main-content">
064.001.00001
Luminometer – COP System Message
Description
Luminometer shutter, door and isolator drive failed to initialize.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Luminometer sub-assemblies
- Re-start instrument. Let it initialize and unload. If able to unload, prime instrument twice trying to replicate error.
- If error persists, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Data pending
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Luminometer sub-assemblies
- Re-start instrument. Let it initialize and unload. If able to unload, prime instrument twice trying to replicate error.
- If error persists, dispatch FSE.
- Debris or foreign object preventing mechanical motion of door/isolator/shutter drive.
- Failure may (or may not) be replicated using Service Software.
- Inspect internal mechanical components for debris such as dried over-spray or a foreign object.
- Clean internal mechanical components or remove foreign object.
- Transporter positions incorrectly taught.
- Using Service Software, Make sure that MTU is not blocking the isolator motion.
- Re-teach Transporter Position.
- Door/isolator/shutter mechanical drive failure due to binding or failed components.
- Failure may (or may not) be replicated using Service Software. Check operation of mechanical drives.
- Replace Luminometer.
- Luminometer Module Removal and Replacement.

## 064.001.00010
id="mc-main-content">
064.001.00010
Luminometer – COP System Message
Description
Luminometer shutter, door and isolator drive step loss or stall.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
The luminometer shutter door and isolator drive is loose causing it to jam.
Shut down and restart, the problem may be intermittent and the FSE Field Service Engineer. will need to be dispatched if it occurs again or at the next service visit.
The luminometer MTU positions to the PMT isolator are incorrect and the MTU is jamming the isolator.
Shut down and restart, the problem may be intermittent and the FSE will need to be dispatched if it occurs again or at the next service visit.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
The luminometer shutter door and isolator drive is loose, causing it to jam
Unload the instrument. Go into service software and initialize the luminometer multiple times in an attempt to recreate. Use the linear distributor to place an MTU into the luminometer and move each of the MTU tubes to the isolator and click measure; this moves the isolator over the MTU tube.
- Unload the instrument and turn the power off. Unplug the PMT cable.
- Open the luminometer lid and locate the door and shutter isolator drive.
- Use a long tool to carefully apply pressure to the luminometer door actuator to open and close the door and the shutter isolator.
- The actuator should move freely, without having to apply excessive force.
- Pay close attention to how much force is required to rotate the actuator and note any positions where more force is required, make sure the shutter isolator is not stuck in the measure position.
- This test can also be done through service software to observe the actuator for any points along the range of motion where the motor may be loosing steps.
- The actuator motor mount screws may need to be loosened to reposition the drive such that it moves freely when moving the door and the isolator (two screws on the MTU side of the wall and one screw on the bottom of the luminometer).
- Close and secure the lid, turn off power, plug in the PMT, run a 10 cycle operational qualification on the Luminometer.
Incorrect MTU tube position teaching.
Unload the instrument. Go into service software and initialize the luminometer multiple times in an attempt to recreate. Use the linear distributor to place an MTU into the luminometer and move each of the MTU tubes to the isolator and click measure. If a step loss or stall is observed, there is a problem.
- Turn the instrument off and unplug the PMT cable.
- Power on the instrument and open the luminometer lid.
- Use the distributor to place an MTU into the luminometer.
- Move each of the MTU tubes to the isolator in service software and click measure; The MTU should not move at all when the isolator moves over the tube.
- Re-teach the Luminometer tube positions if needed. Close and secure the lid, turn off power, plug in the PMT, run a 10 cycle operational qualification on the Luminometer.
- See PANTHER Service Manual, Luminometer Teaching

## 064.001.00016
id="mc-main-content">
064.001.00016
Luminometer – COP System Message
Description
Luminometer shutter, door and isolator drive error (Command execution timeout).
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Luminometer sub-assemblies
- Re-start instrument. Let it initialize and unload. If able to unload, prime instrument twice trying to replicate error.
- If error persists, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Luminometer sub-assemblies
- Re-start instrument. Let it initialize and unload. If able to unload, prime instrument twice trying to replicate error.
- If error persists, dispatch FSE.
- Debris or foreign object preventing mechanical motion of door/isolator/shutter drive.
- Failure may (or may not) be replicated using Service Software. Inspect internal mechanical components for debris such as dried over-spray or a foreign object.
- Clean internal mechanical components or remove foreign object.
- Loose Connections
- Make sure all connections are snug ,and no loose or broken pin from connectors (Check from COP to module, and module connections)
- Replace faulty cables.
- Failed PCB causing communications errors.
- Difficult to diagnose.
- Replace Luminometer PCB or Replace Luminometer.
- Luminometer PCB Control Removal and Replacement.
- Luminometer Module Removal and Replacement.
- Door/isolator/shutter mechanical drive failure due to binding or failed components.
- Failure may (or may not) be replicated using Service Software. Check operation of mechanical drives.
- Replace Luminometer.

## 080.000.00001
id="mc-main-content">
080.000.00001
MTU Input Queue – COP System Message
Description
Input Queue failed to initialize.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Communications error.
- Re-start the instrument and software.
- Shut down instrument power.
- Re-boot the PC.
- Turn on instrument power, wait 20 seconds, and start the PANTHER Main software.
- Prime the instrument.
- Dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. if the problem persists.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Starting the System
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —System Prime
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Communications error.
- Re-start the instrument and software.
- Shut down instrument power.
- Re-boot the PC.
- Turn on instrument power, wait 20 seconds, and start the PANTHER Main software.
- Prime the instrument.
- Dispatch an FSE if the problem persists.
N/A
- Stray tiplet fell in between the rails, preventing pusher mechanism from fully retracting.
- Open the Input Queue.  Look in between the rails for any stray tiplets that may be preventing the pusher mechanism from fully actuating.
- Remove the stray tiplet(s).
N/A
- Loose connection.
- Initialize module using Service Software and if it still fails: make sure all connections are tight (COP to Input Q module and all Input Q module connections).
- Check for broken wires, loose pins or bad flex cables.
- Re-seat connections.
- Replace any broken or worn-out cables.
N/A
- Misaligned rails
- Open the Input Queue. Slide several MTUs back and forth across the rails, the MTUs should slide smoothly. Also, use the Rail Alignment Tool to check the rail alingment.
- Align the rails with the Rail Alignment Tool.
N/A
- Dirty packing sensor, Mis-aligned or Bad packing sensor.
- Open the Input Queue and inspect the optical sensor behind the white packing button. Note whether it is dirty. In Service Software push the packing button and see if the state changes.
- Open the Input Queue and inspect the 3 posts that hold the PCB which contains the packing optical sensor. The posts should be screwed on tight, the screws that hold the PCB should be tight.
- Use Service Software to pack some MTUs. If the module packs MTUs perfectly, yet the system still reports a packing error, it is likely due to a bad packing sensor.
- Clean the packing optical sensor.
- Tighten the 3 posts and screws that secure the PCB.
- Replace the Slave PCB.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —MTU Input Queue Slave PCB Removal and Replacement
- Faulty PCBs.
- Check for burnt components on PCBs or signs of old spills.
- Replace any faulty PCBs.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —MTU Input Queue Slave PCB Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —MTU Input Queue Main PCB Removal and Replacement
- Bad encoder
- Use Service Software to pack some MTUs. If the motor does not stop and keeps pushing for an excessive amount of time, it is likely due to a bad encoder.
- Replace the encoder or module.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —MTU Input Queue Module Removal and Replacement
- Bad motor or drive mechanism
- In Service Software initialize the module. Note whether the MTU pusher moves, if it does not move it is likely a bad motor or drive belt. Also check for debris, like tiplets.
- Replace the motor, belt, or module.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —MTU Input Queue Module Removal and Replacement
- Faulty module.
- If the module fails to initialize after attempting all other fixes listed above, replace the module.
- Replace the MTU Input Queue module.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —MTU Input Queue Module Removal and Replacement

## Input Queue Pack Drive Motor Suffered Step Loss
id="mc-main-content">
Input Queue Pack Drive Motor Suffered Step Loss
Error Code
Dec
Hex
080.000.00010
Complaint Description
Input Queue pack drive motor suffered step loss or stalled
Technical Support
Check Input Queue
- Check if MTUs are placed in front of the pusher.
- Check for jammed MTUs or obstructions in the queue.
- Make sure only 25 MTUs are loaded in the queue.
- Remove incorrectly seated MTUs or obstructions.
Next Steps
- Restart the instrument.
- Perform a prime and/or MW clean to test the Input Queue.
- Review case history for previous Input Queue errors. Notify FSE Field Service Engineer. if there were recent cases.
- Instruct customer to monitor.
Field Service
Bad MTUs
Resolution
- If possible, take a photograph of the state of the MTUs.
- Remove the MTUs by hand, taking care not to spill tiplets.
- Inspect MTUs for any abnormalities.
- If the MTU is suspect as defective note the LOT number of the MTU’s contact Tech Support to open a complaint and return the suspect bad MTU’s for further investigation.
Test
Make sure other MTU Lot numbers are able to process thru the input queue successfully
Stray Tiplet
A stray tiplet fell between the rails, preventing the pusher mechanism from fully retracting.
Resolution
Remove the stray tiplet.
Test
- Open the MTU Input Queue.
- Look between the rails for any stray tiplets that may be preventing the pusher mechanism from fully actuating.
Misaligned MTU Input Queue Rails
RESOLUTION:
Use the alignment tool to properly align the rails per the Panther Service Manual.
TEST:
- Open the MTU Input Queue.
- Slide several MTUs back and forth across the rails. The MTUs should slide smoothly.
- Also, use the Rail Alignment Tool to check the rail alignment.
Damaged Cable
A stray tiplet fell between the rails, preventing the pusher mechanism from fully retracting
RESOLUTION:
Repair or replace damaged cable
TEST:
Visually inspect for damaged cable. Insure the cable is not pinched in the service drawer.
Dirty packing sensor, misaligned, or faulty packing sensor
RESOLUTION:
- Clean the packing optical sensor.
- Tighten the 3 posts and screws that secure the PCB.
- Replace the Slave PCB.
TEST:
- Open the MTU Input Queue and inspect the optical sensor behind the white packing button. Note whether it is dirty. Using Service Software, push the packing button and see if the state changes.
- Open the MTU Input Queue and inspect the 3 posts that hold the PCB which contains the packing optical sensor. The posts should be screwed on tight. The screws that secure the PCB should be tight.
- Using Service Software, pack some MTUs. If the module packs MTUs correctly, yet the system still reports a packing error, it is likely due to a faulty packing sensor.
Faulty Encoder
RESOLUTION:
Replace the Encoder or the Module
TEST:
Using Service Software, pack some MTUs.
If the motor does not stop and keeps pushing for an excessive amount of time, it is likely due to a faulty encoder
Faulty Motor or Drive Mechanism
RESOLUTION:
Replace the Motor, Belt, or the Module
TEST:
Using Service Software, initialize the module.
Note whether the MTU pusher moves. If it does not move, it is likely due to a faulty motor or drive belt.
Also check for debris, such as tiplets.

## 081.000.00016
id="mc-main-content">
081.000.00016
Output Queue – COP System Message
Description
Output Queue error (Command execution timeout).
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
This is a Firmware bug, in that error reporting needs improvement. Generally there is an upstream error during a mini-prime that causes a timing conflict. This leads to a command execution timeout as the Output Queue waits for the delayed MTU.
- Ask the customer what was happening when the error occurred (for example, was it during a prime, mini-prime, instrument unload, or Assay Processing)?
- Retrieve the logs and curve files. Review the logs to determine if there was an error with a different module prior to the Output Queue timeout.
- If the error occurred during a mini-prime, the customer can attempt to force a full prime and see if the instrument will pass a full prime. It is important to first review the Luminometer OLV curve files to make sure the instrument does not have bad Luminometer injectors.
- Reviewing Luminometer OLV Curve Files
Software Anomaly
If occurred during Assay Processing
- Re-start the instrument.
- If the same error occurs during re-start, it is most likely a true OQ module error. Get logs and determine problem.
- Verify the PC is online.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- This is a Firmware bug, in that error reporting needs improvement. Generally there is an upstream error during a mini-prime that causes a timing conflict. This leads to a command execution timeout as the Output Queue waits for the delayed MTU. Possible errors are listed below.
- Review the logs and determine when the error occurred. If it happened during mini-prime, look for an error preceding the Output Queue Command Execution Timeout.
- Replace/fix the faulty part (see below).
Reviewing Luminometer OLV Curve Files
- Bad Luminometer injector. (Software Bug: Luminometer injector calibration is taking too log to complete. This causes the Output Queue module to experience execution timeouts.)
- Lumo injectors-check for any kinks or damage to injector.
- Replace the injectors.
PANTHER System Service Manual —Luminometer Module Removal and Replacement
Bad Lumo Injector causing OQ execution time out during Instrument Priming
- Input Queue stacking error
- See System Message 080.000.00052—MTU Packing Error.
- Adjust the Input Queue Rails.
Adjust Input Queue rails
- Linear Distributor step loss
- See the following System Messages:
- 016.000.00080—Distributor Z motor step loss or stall. Position X
- 016.000.00096—Distributor Theta motor step loss or stall. Position X
- 016.000.00112—Distributor X motor step loss or stall. Position X
- 016.000.00128—Distributor Hook motor step losss or stall. Position X
- Re-teach the Distributor.
Install SP4 or greater and Teach Linear Distributor

## 081.000.00035
id="mc-main-content">
081.000.00035
Output Queue – COP System Message
Description
Output loader drive failed to initialize.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Jammed Output Queue loader drive.
- Request the Logs from the customer.
- Determine if this error has happened in recent history on the instrument. If it has, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- Ask the customer to attempt to restart the instrument. Usually this error requires an FSE to clear the jam, but a restart may work.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —System Startup
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- An MTU jammed on the Output Queue rails as the Output Queue loader drive attempted to move the MTU to the handoff position.
- Look at the Output Queue and observe the jam.
- Look for stray tubing which could be blocking the MTU or drive movement.
- If the load drive stall is due to an MTU jamming at the handoff position, clean the Output Queue surfaces and install the Output Queue Guided Cover.
- If the Guided Cover is already installed, and an MTU is still jammed against the rails, replace the Output Queue.
- GP11-253-FSN Output Queue Guided Cover
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue Module Removal and Replacement
- Broken Output Queue loader drive home sensor.
- Using a flashlight, look into the instrument at the Output Queue load drive home sensor. Check to see if it appears broken.
- Using Service Software, check the state of the sensor on the Output Queue main page. If the sensor reads In when the drive is not home, the sensor is probably broken or dirty.
- Replace the load drive home sensor if it is broken.
( Trunk Stock Part )
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue Load Drive Home Sensor Removal and Replacement

id="mc-main-content">
081.000.00040
Output Queue – COP System Message
Description
Output Queue did not detect a MTU.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
This is due to a Firmware bug in pre-4.2 software versions. It occurs during prime, when an MTU from the Luminometer is placed in the Output Queue.
During prime, the MTUs from the Luminometer are very full. The fluid inside the MTU tube is above the MTU presence sensor, and acts as a "magnifying glass." So, instead of the light beam from the MTU presence sensor being obstructed by the MTU, the light is magnified to the receiving end of the MTU presence sensor, and the MTU is not detected.
Request the Logs and determine if the error occurred during a prime.
- Ask the customer to restart the instrument and re-prime.
- If the error recurs, dispatch and FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual — System Startup and Prime Instrument
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- This is due to a Firmware bug in pre-4.2 SP5 software versions. It occurs during prime, when an MTU from the Luminometer is placed in the Output Queue. During prime, the MTUs from the Luminometer are very full. The fluid inside the MTU tube is above the MTU presence sensor, and acts as a "magnifying glass." So, instead of the light beam from the MTU presence sensor being obstructed by the MTU, the light is magnified to the receiving end of the MTU presence sensor, and the MTU is not detected.
- Check to see if the error occurred during a prime, on an MTU coming out of the Luminometer.
- Check the MTU position relative to the Output Queue MTU presence sensor.
- Manually teach the Distributor hook position up to ± 50 steps at the Output Queue from the current auto-taught position.
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Adjusting the MTU at Output Queue Hand Off Position
- PANTHER System Service Manual — GP12-220-FSN Adjust the Linear Distributor MTU Handoff Position
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Distributor Teaching
- MTU produced by Helix with the "D" mold are clearer than MTUs produced by an "A" mold; Therefore, the MTU present sensor has a more difficult time detecting the MTUs.
- Check that the MTU LOT is not 418247, This is one of the lots produced by the "D" mold.
- Either teach the linear distributor hand off position at the OQ until the MTU is consistently detected by the MTU present sensor (GP12-220-FSN)
OR
- Use a MTU lot produced by an ""A, B, or C"" mold
- PANTHER System Service Manual —GP12-220-FSN Adjust the Linear Distributor MTU Handoff Position.
- See document: MTU Mold Stamp
- Distributor teaching is off and the Distributor incorrectly placed the MTU.
- Check to be sure the Service Drawer if fully closed and latched.
- Check the MTU position relative to the Output Que MTU presence sensor.
- If the Service Drawer is open, close the drawer and fully re-teach the Distributor to the Output Queue, and Magnetic Wash Stations 1 and 2.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Teaching
- PANTHER System Service Manual —GP12-220-FSN Adjust the Linear Distributor MTU Handoff Position"
- Build-up on the Output Queue injectors.
- Check the Output Queue injectors for dry fluid build-up.
- Clean the Output Queuje dispense injectors. (Build-up may cause injectors to spray fluid that eventually might get into the MTU.
- Clean the MTU presence sensor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Output Queue Injector Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue Injectors Cleaning Procedure
- Dirty MTU presence sensor.
- Using Service Software, check to see if the MTU sensor is reading properly.
- Clean the MTU presence sensor.
- Clean the Output Queue injector.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue MTU Presence Sensor Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Cleaning and Applying Grease to the Output Queue Injector
- Faulty MTU presence sensor.
- Using Service Software, check to see if the MTU sensor is reading properly.
- Replace the MTU presence sensor
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Output Queue MTU Presence Sensor Removal and Replacement
- Output Queue MTU Presence Sensor Calibration and Verification

## 081.000.00049
id="mc-main-content">
081.000.00049
Output Queue – COP System Message
Description
Aspirator reinitialized; waste slot possibly blocked.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Jammed Output Queue
- Open the Waste Drawer and listen for dropped MTUs.
- If the jam cannot be isolated to the Solid Waste bin, and the instrument cannot be restarted, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- Did MTUs fall when the waste drawer was opened? if yes,
- It most likely a jam due to improper placement of the Solid Waste Bag or Solid Waste Cover.
- Have the customer look at the Solid Waste Bin:
- Does it appear that there was a build up of MTUs either from waste bag or the waste cover? if yes,
- Was the waste cover installed correctly?
- Was the waste bag installed correctly?
Output Queue Waste Chute Jam Locations (PPT)
Jammed Output Queue
Look at the Output Queue cover, is it crooked and/or not fully seated (pushed down)?
Properly seat the cover.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
Waste Cover improperly installed, causing a backup of MTUs into the Output Queue
Look at the Waste Cover. Is it installed correctly (pushed back and down fully)?
If the Waste Cover is not installed correctly, instruct the PANTHER users how to properly install the Waste Cover
- Panther User Manual
- Output Queue Waste Chute Jam Locations (PPT)
Waste Bag improperly installed, causing a backup of MTUs into the Output Queue
Look at the Waste Bag. Is it installed flush against the walls of the Waste Bin, so there are no folds for MTUs to get caught on and back up
If the Waste Bag is not installed correctly, instruct the PANTHER user how to properly install the Waste Cover
- Panther User Manual
- Output Queue Waste Chute Jam Locations (PPT)
Output Queue cover on crooked or loose
Look at the cover, is it crooked and/or not fully pushed down?
Properly seat the cover
MTU caught on drooping COP-LD cable (or other cable)
Look under the service drawer. Are there any drooping cables that the MTUs could get caught on?
Properly secure any loose cables
Output Queue Waste Chute Jam Locations (PPT)
MTU is caught on the MTU eject chute
Is the jam in the waste chute? This is easiest to see from the left service drawer, with the waste drawer pulled out, look up underneath the Output Queue Is the Service drawer fully closed?
- If NO, close and latch it.
- If Yes, Is there a lip from the MTU chute that the MTUs can get caught on?
- If Yes, see GP11-236-FSN Output Queue Chute Modification.
Ensure Service Drawer is fully closed and latched.
Refer to GP11-236-FSN document.
GP11-236-FSN Output Queue Chute Modification
Output Queue Waste Chute Jam Locations (PPT)
MTU is crooked on the Output Queue Rails
Look at the Output Queue Is there a crooked MTU under the Output Queue Aspirators?
Is the instrument level?
Is the vacuum excessively noisy/ vibrating?
Rails too close together.
Instrument Leveling procedure
Vacuum section
Adjust rail so MTUs slide freely, without any dragging.
Movement of drive blocked or stalled by: stray tubing, loose screws, loose belts, or worn out motors
If there is no MTU jam, then look for any loose screws, belts, or worn out motors.
Replace faulty part

## 081.000.00051
id="mc-main-content">
081.000.00051
Output Queue – COP System Message
Description
Load reinitialized.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Jammed Output Queue loader drive.
- Request the Logs from the customer.
- Determine if this error has happened in recent history on the instrument. If it has, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Ask the customer to attempt to restart the instrument. Usually this error requires an FSE to clear the jam, but a restart may work.
PANTHER System Operator's Manual —System Startup
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- An MTU jammed on the Output Queue rails as the Output Queue loader drive attempted to move the MTU to the handoff position.
- Look at the Output Queue and observe the jam.
- Look for stray tubing which could be blocking the MTU or drive movement.
- If the load drive stall is due to an MTU jamming at the handoff position, clean the Output Queue surfaces and install the Output Queue Guided Cover.
- If the Guided Cover is already installed, and an MTU is still jammed against the rails, replace the Output Queue.
- GP11-253-FSN Output Queue Guided Cover
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue Module Removal and Replacement
- Broken Output Queue loader drive home sensor.
- Using a flashlight, look into the instrument at the Output Queue load drive home sensor. Check to see if it appears broken.
- Using Service Software, check the state of the sensor on the Output Queue main page. If the sensor reads In when the drive is not home, the sensor is probably broken or dirty.
- Replace the load drive home sensor if it is broken.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue Load Drive Home Sensor Removal and Replacement

## Output Queue Failed to Initialize
id="mc-main-content">
Output Queue Failed to Initialize
Error Code
Dec
Hex
081.000.00052
Complaint Description
Output Queue Failed to initialize
Technical Support
TS Troubleshooting
- Shutdown and restart.
- Check the waste bin to make sure cover/bag is in place-MTUs are not stacking.
- Perform a prime and MW cleaning to test the output queue.
- If reset/prime or MW cleaning fail or the error persists, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
OQ Cover
Output Queue cover on crooked or loose
Resolution
Properly install the OQ Cover
Test
Look at the cover, is it crooked and/or not fully pushed down?
Cable Interference
MTU caught on drooping COP-LD cable (or other cable)
Resolution
Properly secure any loose cables.
Test
Look under the service drawer. Are there any drooping cables that the MTUs could get caught on?
Eject Chute
MTU is caught on the MTU eject chute.
Resolution
Ensure Service Drawer is fully closed and latched.
Test
Is the jam in the waste chute? This is easiest to see from the left service drawer, with the waste drawer pulled out, look up underneath the Output Queue Is the Service drawer fully closed?
If NO, close and latch it.
OQ Rails
MTU caught on drooping COP-LD cable (or other cable).
Resolution
Check for bent rails and make sure the instrument is level.
Test
Look at the Output Queue Is there a crooked MTU under the Output Queue Aspirators?
Aspirator Drive
Movement of drive blocked or stalled by: stray tubing, loose screws, loose belts, or worn out motors.
Resolution
Remove obstruction.
Test
If there is no MTU jam, then look for any loose screws, belts, or worn out motors.

## Output Queue Load Drive Suffered Step Loss or Stalled
id="mc-main-content">
Output Queue Load Drive Suffered Step Loss or Stalled
Error Code
Dec
Hex
081.000.00068
Complaint Description
Output Queue load drive suffered step loss or stalled.
Technical Support
TS Troubleshooting
- Shutdown/Restart.
- While instrument is off, check the waste bin to make sure cover/bag is in place-MTUs are not stacking.
- Check Output Cover make sure it is seated properly.
- Run/monitor if unload and prime and MW cleaning complete successfully. Do a small run of untested samples.
- If the error persists, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
MTU Jam
An MTU jammed in the Output Queue rails as the Output Queue Load Drive attempted to move the MTU to the handoff position.
Resolution
- If the load drive stall is due to the MTU jamming at the handoff position, clean the output Queue surfaces and install the Output Queue Guided Cover.
- If the Guided Cover is already installed, and the MTU still jams against the rails, replace the Output Queue.
Test
- Examine the jam in the Output Queue.
- Look for stray tubing that could be blocking MTU or drive movement.
Load Drive Home Sensor
Broken Output Queue Load Drive Home Sensor.
Resolution
If the Load Drive Home Sensor is broken, replace it.
Test
- Using a flashlight, check to see if the Output Queue appears to be broken.
- Using Service Software, check the state of the sensor. If the sensor reads In when the drive is not home, the sensor is broken or dirty.

## Output Queue Actuator Suffered Step Loss or Stalled
id="mc-main-content">
Output Queue Actuator Suffered Step Loss or Stalled
Error Code
Dec
Hex
081.000.00071
0x51.0.00.0x0047
Complaint Description
Output queue actuator suffered step loss or stalled.
MDD recognizes the error h47 as
Waste slot blocked (Steploss stacker > MTU width)
Technical Support
Possible root cause
Jammed MTU.
TS troubleshooting
-
Reset instrument.
-
While instrument is off, have customer open the right panel and look at the output queue for any jammed or crooked MTU. It is not recommended for TS to advise customer to correct the jam. Always contact FSE Field Service Engineer. first.
-
Open the Waste Drawer and listen for dropped MTUs.
-
Ask the customer to look at the Solid Waste and check the bag is flush against the walls and cover is seated properly. Correct if needed.
-
If instrument reset passes, perform a prime and MW cleaning to test the output queue. If all passes, recommend to run.
-
If the instrument doesn't pass initialization, dispatch FSE.
Field Service
MTU Jam
Possible Cause of Jam due to misrouted COP cable.
RESOLUTION:
Properly secure any loose cables.
TEST:
Look under the Service Drawer.
Check for any drooping cables on which MTUs could be caught.
MTU is stuck on the rails
MTU is stuck on the output queue rails as they may be dirty bent or have sharp edges.
Resolution
- Verify that the instrument is level.
- Verify that the vacuum is not excessively noisy or vibrating.
- Check to see if the rails are too close.
- Clean the rails.
Test
Check to see if there is a crooked MTU under the Output Queue aspirators.
MTU caught on the MTU eject chute
Resolution
Ensure the Service Drawer is fully closed and latched.
Test
- Check to see if the jam is in the waste chute. This is easiest ot see from the left Service Drawer, with the Waste Drawer pulled out. Look up underneath the Output Queue.
- Using Service Software, check to see if the drawer reads as fully closed.
- If No, close and latch the drawer.
- If Yes, check to see if there is a lip from the MTU chute on which MTUs can get caught.
Faulty Motor Drive
Movement of the drive is blocked or stalled by stray tubing, loose screws, loose belts, or worn out motors.
Resolution
Replace any faulty parts.
Test
If there is no MTU jam, look for any loose screws, belts, or worn out motors.

## 081.001.00040
id="mc-main-content">
081.001.00040
Output Queue – COP System Message
Description
Output Queue did not detect a MTU.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
This is due to a Firmware bug in pre-4.2 software versions. It occurs during prime, when an MTU from the Luminometer is placed in the Output Queue.
During prime, the MTUs from the Luminometer are very full. The fluid inside the MTU tube is above the MTU presence sensor, and acts as a "magnifying glass." So, instead of the light beam from the MTU presence sensor being obstructed by the MTU, the light is magnified to the receiving end of the MTU presence sensor, and the MTU is not detected.
Request the Logs and determine if the error occurred during a prime.
- Ask the customer to restart the instrument and re-prime.
- If the error recurs, dispatch and FSE Field Service Engineer. .
PANTHER System Operator's Manual — System Startup and Prime Instrument
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- This is due to a Firmware bug in pre-4.2 SP5 software versions. It occurs during prime, when an MTU from the Luminometer is placed in the Output Queue. During prime, the MTUs from the Luminometer are very full. The fluid inside the MTU tube is above the MTU presence sensor, and acts as a "magnifying glass." So, instead of the light beam from the MTU presence sensor being obstructed by the MTU, the light is magnified to the receiving end of the MTU presence sensor, and the MTU is not detected.
- Check to see if the error occurred during a prime, on an MTU coming out of the Luminometer.
- Check the MTU position relative to the Output Queue MTU presence sensor.
- Manually teach the Distributor hook position up to ± 50 steps at the Output Queue from the current auto-taught position.
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Adjusting the MTU at Output Queue Hand Off Position
- PANTHER System Service Manual — GP12-220-FSN Adjust the Linear Distributor MTU Handoff Position
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Distributor Teaching
- MTU produced by Helix with the "D" mold are clearer than MTUs produced by an "A" mold; Therefore, the MTU present sensor has a more difficult time detecting the MTUs.
- Check that the MTU LOT is not 418247, This is one of the lots produced by the "D" mold.
- Either teach the linear distributor hand off position at the OQ until the MTU is consistently detected by the MTU present sensor (GP12-220-FSN)
OR
- Use a MTU lot produced by an ""A, B, or C"" mold
- PANTHER System Service Manual —GP12-220-FSN Adjust the Linear Distributor MTU Handoff Position.
- See document: MTU Mold Stamp
- Distributor teaching is off and the Distributor incorrectly placed the MTU.
- Check to be sure the Service Drawer if fully closed and latched.
- Check the MTU position relative to the Output Que MTU presence sensor.
- If the Service Drawer is open, close the drawer and fully re-teach the Distributor to the Output Queue, and Magnetic Wash Stations 1 and 2.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Distributor Teaching
- PANTHER System Service Manual —GP12-220-FSN Adjust the Linear Distributor MTU Handoff Position"
- Build-up on the Output Queue injectors.
- Check the Output Queue injectors for dry fluid build-up.
- Clean the Output Queuje dispense injectors. (Build-up may cause injectors to spray fluid that eventually might get into the MTU.
- Clean the MTU presence sensor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Output Queue Injector Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue Injectors Cleaning Procedure
- Dirty MTU presence sensor.
- Using Service Software, check to see if the MTU sensor is reading properly.
- Clean the MTU presence sensor.
- Clean the Output Queue injector.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Output Queue MTU Presence Sensor Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Cleaning and Applying Grease to the Output Queue Injector
- Faulty MTU presence sensor.
- Using Service Software, check to see if the MTU sensor is reading properly.
- Replace the MTU presence sensor
- PANTHER System Service Manual — Output Queue MTU Presence Sensor Removal and Replacement
- Output Queue MTU Presence Sensor Calibration and Verification

## Sample or Reagent Bay Temperature Is Out of Range
id="mc-main-content">
Sample or Reagent Bay Temperature Is Out of Range
Error Codes
Dec
Hex
096.000.00080
112.000.00080
024.000.00048
Sample Bay
Reagent Bay
Reagent Bay
Complaint Description
Sample or Reagent Bay temperature is out of range.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
-
Faulty Thermistor
-
Reagent Bay PCB
-
Cooling Module
-
TSE Fault Mode Example
Technical Support
Possible root cause:
-
Room temperature too high
-
Water in Cooling Module is too low. Water level should be about an inch above the top notch.
-
Failed Cooling Pump
-
Cooling Module Peltier failure
-
Reagent Bay Thermistor failure
Technical Support troubleshooting:
-
Check lab temperature. Temperature should be 15 - 30C.
-
Check temperature of reagent and sample bays by feel.
-
Sample bay temperature range: 15.5-22.5C. Reagent bay temperature range: 16.5-19.5C.
-
Check Cooling Module water level. Level should be about an inch above the top notch.
-
Check for loud noise coming from the right side of the instrument.
-
Refer to troubleshooting table below:
Field Service
Faulty Thermistor
-
In Service Software, make sure the temperature read from Reagent Bay module, normal range from 15.5 to 22˚C, matches the calibrated thermometer reading from Reagent Bay.
-
Make sure thermistor is connected.
-
Check for thermistor broken wire.
Resolution
Replace Thermistor as needed, per the removal and replacement procedure in the Panther Service Manual.
Reagent Bay PCB
Check for burnt components or signs of spills on the Reagent Bay PCB.
Resolution
Replace the Reagent Bay or its PCB as needed, per the Panther Service Manual.
Cooling Module
-
Insure the cooling module is working properly and fluid is flowing.
-
Make sure there are no clogs in the cooling lines.
Resolution
If it is determined to be a cooling system issue, refer to the Cooling module troubleshooting section.
TSE Fault Mode Example
08/11/2023 01:46:48 (10 20:46:48) [E] (Critical , High ) [SampleLoadingBay] Sample Bay temperature is out of range (TemperatureEvent) [0x60.0x00.0x0050] bytes: 60 00 03 00 50 DD 05 [ 096.000.00080 ]
The thermistor in the Sample Bay only reports temperature.
The cooling system does not use that information to drive cooling.
The Reagent Bay’s thermistor drives cooling.
Either the Reagent Bay has a bad thermistor, or there is a blockage in the lower tubing of the Reagent Bay. When that happens, the coolant flows through the back radiator and does not cool the bottom of the bay, where the thermistor resides. Since the Reagent Bay is not making temperature, the Liquid Cooling keeps driving its temperature down.
The Liquid Cooling minimum temperature thermistor should protect the module from freezing, but not if it is low on fluid. Also, remember when the Liquid Cooling module suction hose and return hoses were reversed? That could cause a similar problem. Also, at one-point Stratec was cutting the suction tubing in the Liquid Cooling module at 90 degrees. The tubing would, sometimes, suction to the bottom of the reservoir and no coolant would flow. It would be intermittent.
Notice in the image below, the temperature in the cooling module is going lower and lower, while the Reagent Bay is going higher. That indicates that the physical flow is not happening. The Cooling module continues to try and fight to cool the bays per the feedback control loop. This is most likely due to a blockage.

id="mc-main-content">

Error Codes
Sample Bay
Reagent Bay
Dec
Hex
Dec
Hex

258.000.00009
Complaint Description
- Sample Bay barcode scanner is not communicating.
- Reagent Bay barcode scanner is not communicating.
Usually the following error message also appears:
Rack loading error: Barcode Scanner failed to focus on lane x in the Sample Loading Bay.
Technical Support
Possible root causes
- Communication failure
- Loose connection
- A known scanner firmware issue with slim scanner:
- MME-04065 (see Panther Service Manual AW-11136)
- Failing barcode scanner
- Sample or Reagent bay PCB
Troubleshooting
- Close sample bay door and wait for half hour or longer to reload sample rack,
- Shutdown/restart of the instrument
- Notify FSE Field Service Engineer. if issue is not resolved or recurring.
Field Service
Communications Error
Resolution
Shut down instrument power. Re-boot the PC. Turn on instrument power, wait 20 seconds, start the Panther Main software.
Test
Restart Instrument and software
Loose Connection
Resolution
Tighten or replace any bad cables
TEST:
Make sure all cables are tight from COP to module and within module.
Faulty Scanner
Resolution
- Re-start the computer and instrument.
- Make sure the scanner is tightly plugged in.
- Check to be sure that no foam is interfering with the path of the scanner beam.
- Re-align the scanner.
- Properly configure the scanner.
- Replace the scanner.
Test
- Make sure the instrument is able to scan other sample tube barcodes.
- Make sure the scanner is plugged in.
- Make sure the scanner has no physical interference.
- Make sure the scanner is properly aligned.
- Make sure the scanner has been properly configured.
- Make sure the scanner is focusing properly.
Faulty PCB
Resolution
Replace the damaged PCB as needed
Test
Check for burnt components or sighs of old spills
Wide Focus Beam
Causes Barcode reader lane 1 and 2 errors
Example of wide beam at an angle causing poor lane 1 and 2 scanning
Resolution
Replace the scanner.
Firmware Version
Check firmware version - v82.18 is the most current.
Leuze is investigating wide scan beam which causes poor reads farther away from scanner.

Description
Sample Bay barcode scanner unable to focus on scan lane.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Rack inserted too fast.
Make sure to insert rack at a normal speed.
- Remove any Sample Racks from the lane.
- Close the Sample Bay door.
- Open the Sample Bay door, wait until the lane highlights purple, and insert the Sample Rack.
- If this does not work, restart the instrument.
- If the problem persists, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Load Samples

Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action

- Make sure the scanner is focusing properly.

## 096.002.00053
id="mc-main-content">
096.002.00053
Sample Bay – COP System Message
Description
Tip Drawer 1 not able to lock. The Sample Tip Drawer locks intermittently—sometimes, the instrument does not lock the Sample Tip Tray.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Tip Drawer may have been pulled out, preventing the locking pin from locking properly.
- Open Tip Drawer 1 (left Tip Drawer).
- Apply pressure to the affected door to engage the locking pin.
N/A
Tip Drawer is not properly closed.
- Check to see if the Tip Drawer is flush (at the same level as the rest of the door).
- Push the Tip Drawer flush with the adjacent door.
- Open the drawer, remove any loose objects preventing the door from closing properly.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Tip Drawer may have been pulled out, preventing the locking pin from locking properly.
- Open Tip Drawer 1 (left Tip Drawer).
- Apply pressure to the affected door to engage the locking pin.
N/A
- Tip Drawer is not properly closed.
- Check to see if the Tip Drawer is flush (at the same level as the rest of the door).
- Push the Tip Drawer flush with the adjacent door.
- Open the drawer, remove any loose objects preventing the door from closing properly.
N/A
- Tip Drawer is not adjusted correctly and the interlock locking pin is rubbing against the hole, preventing the pin from extending properly.
- Inspect the locking pin for interference with the locking pin hole.
- Loosen the affected interlock module's three screws and adjust the screws so that the pin is centered in the pin hole.
- Adjust the affected Tip Drawer rail to better align the pin hole.
- GP11-215 FSN—Additional Items for PANTHER Installation and Verification
- Tip Drawer glide is not parallel.
- Check to see if the Tip Drawer cannot completely close and if resistance gradually increases as you slide the drawer into the instrument.
- Replace the defective component.
N/A
- The Tip Drawer panel was installed too far in.
- Check to see if the Tip Drawer panel hits the frame and prevents the drawer from sliding in fully.
- Loosen the screw that secures the Tip Drawer panel.
- Slide the drawer in completely by moving the drawer (not pushing the panel).
- Slide the drawer out and do not touch the panel.
- Tighten the screw that secures the panel.
N/A

## 096.002.00054
id="mc-main-content">
096.002.00054
Sample Bay – COP System Message
Description
Tip Drawer 1 not able to unlock.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
It is possible the Tip Drawer was pulled out causing the locking pin to lock properly.
- Open Tip Drawer 1 (left Tip Drawer).
- Apply pressure to the affected door to unlock the pin. Retry a drawer unlock through the PANTHER Software .
Tip Drawer is not properly closed.
- Tip Drawer is not flush (the same level as the rest of the door).
- Push the Tip Drawer flush to the rest of the door next to it.
- Pull out the drawer, remove any loose object preventing the drawer to close.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- It is possible the drawer was pulled causing the locking pin to not lock properly.
- Open Tip Drawer 1 (left tip drawer).
- Apply pressure to the affected door to lock the pin.
- Tip Drawer is not properly closed.
- Tip Drawer is not flush (the same level as the rest of the door).
- Push the Tip Drawer flush to the rest of the door next to it.
- Pull out the drawer, remove any loose object preventing the drawer to close.
- The Tip Drawer is not adjusted correctly and the locking pin of the interlock module is rubbing against the hole preventing the pin from extending properly.
- Inspect the locking pin for interference with the locking pin hole.
- Loosen the affected interlock module's three screws and adjust the scres so that the pin is more centered in the pin hole.
- Adjust the affected tip drawer rail to better align the pin hole.
- GP11-215 FSN Additional Items for Panther Installation and Verification
- Tip Drawer Glide is not parallel.
- Check if the tip drawer can not completely close and the resistance is gradually larger to slide in the drawer.
- Replace the defective component.
- The installed Tip Drawer Panel too far in.
- Check if the Tip Drawer Panel hits the frame and prevents the drawer from sliding in fully.
- Loosen the screw holding the Tip Door Panel. Slide the drawer in completely by moving the drawer (not by pushing the panel). Slide the drawer out, do not touch the panel. Tighten the screw holding the panel.

## 096.003.00053
id="mc-main-content">
096.003.00053
Sample Bay – COP System Message
Description
Tip Drawer 2 not able to lock. Sample Tip Drawer intermittently locking – Instrument sometimes wouldn't lock the sample tip tray.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
It is possible the Tip Drawer was pulled out causing the locking pin to lock properly.
Open Tip Drawer 2 (right Tip Drawer)
Apply pressure to the affected door to lock the pin.
Tip Drawer is not properly closed.
Tip Drawer is not flush (the same level as the rest of the door).
- Push the Tip Drawer flush to the rest of the door next to it.
- Pull out the drawer, remove any loose object preventing the drawer to close.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- It is possible the drawer was pulled causing the locking pin not able to lock.
- Able to open Tip Drawer 2 (the left tip drawer)
- Apply pressure to the affected door to lock the pin.
- Drawer not properly closed.
- Drawer not flush/same level as the rest of the door.
- Push the Tip Drawer flush to the rest of the door next to it.
- Pull out the drawer, remove any loose object preventing the drawer to close.
- The Tip Drawer is not adjusted correctly and the locking pin of the interlock module is rubbing against the hole preventing the pin from extending properly.
- Inspect the locking pin from interference with the locking pin hole.
- Loosen the affected interlock module's 3 screws and adjust so that the pin is more centered in the pin hole.
- Adjust the affected tip drawer rail to better align the pin hole.
- GP11-215 FSN Additional Items for Panther Installation and Verification
- Tip Drawer Panel installed too far in.
- Check if the Tip Drawer Panel hit the frame and preventing the drawer to slide in fully.
- Loosen up the screw holding the Tip Door Panel. Slide drawer in completely by moving the drawer it self, not by pushing the panel.
- Slide the drawer out, do not touch the panel.
- Tighten screw holding the panel.
- Drawer Glide is not parallel
- Check if the drawer can not completely be closed and resistance is gradually larger to slide in the drawer.
- Replace defective component.

## Chiller Ramp Seebeck voltage is too low, too high or the difference of Seebeck voltage is too high.
id="mc-main-content">
Chiller Ramp Seebeck voltage is too low, too high or the difference of Seebeck voltage is too high.
Error Code
Dec
Hex
098.000.00033
098.000.00034
098.000.00035
Complaint Description
Chiller ramp Seebeck voltage is too low
Chiller ramp Seebeck voltage is too high
Chiller ramp difference of Seebeck voltage is too high
Technical Support
Troubleshooting
- Check lab temperature
- Check if chiller ramp fan is blowing
- If the lab temperature is within range, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer.
Possible Root Causes
- Lab temperature outside the range
- Faulty/failed fan
- Chiller Ramp Peltier failure
- Faulty PCB
Field Service
Inspect chiller ramp fan is installed and working correctly. Remove lumo injectors and pull-out service drawer. Activate = starts the fan, Deactivate = stops the fan. Pay attention to fan blades. They should start easily and slowly spin down when de-activate is pressed.
RESOLUTION:
Replace chiller fan (select correct fan depending on configuration) 6 slot chiller ramp has a 260mm or 295mm cable. 5 slot (MRSA chiller) cable length is 360mm
TEST:
Check in service software or allow temp to lock in Panther GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. .
Fan is working but Peltier does not cool.
RESOLUTION:
Rreplace chiller ramp Peltier module
TEST:
Check in service software or allow temp to lock in Panther GUI.
Faulty Thermistor
RESOLUTION:
Replace the Thermistor
Faulty Peltier
RESOLUTION:
Replace the Peltier
Faulty PCB
RESOLUTION:
Replace the PCB
Improperly Installed Fan
RESOLUTION:
Replace the Fan as needed and make sure it is properly installed.

## 098.000.00037
id="mc-main-content">
098.000.00037
Chiller Ramp – COP System Message
Description
All Chiller Ramp peltiers are off.
Tier 1
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support/Customer Action
Reference
Laboratory Temperature.
- Verify laboratory is within ambient temperature (15-30 ˚C).
- Set Laboratory temperature between 15-30 ˚C, and let instrument to warm up or cool down.
Chiller Ramp sub-assembly.
- From Panther Temperature Screen, Make sure chiller ramp temperature is within 17-19 ˚C.
- If not, re-start instrument.
if problem persists, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
FSE
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Laboratory Temperature
- Verify laboratory is within ambient temperature (15-30 ˚C).
- Set Laboratory temperature between 15-30 ˚C, and let instrument to warm up or cool down
- Chiller Ramp sub-assembly
- From Panther Temperature Screen, Make sure chiller ramp temperature is within 17-19 ˚C.
- If not, re-start instrument.
- Fan
- Slow spinning.
- Not spinning.
- Up side Down ( Fan should be blowing toward peltiers).
- Replace Fan.
- Replace Fan.
- Properly install fan.
- Chiller Ramp Fan Removal and Replacement.
- Chiller Ramp Removal and Replacement.
- Thermistor
- In Service Software, Make sure the temperature read from chiller module matches the calibrated thermometer reading from chiller.
- Make sure thermistor is connected.
- Check for thermistor broken wire.
- Replace thermistor.
( Trunk Stock Part )
- Chiller Ramp Temperature Sensor Removal and Replacement.
- Peltiers
- Using a calibrated thermometer, make sure chiller is reading between 17-19 ˚C.
- A good peltier should feel warm to the touch.
- Using Service Software, if seebeck voltage reads close to 0 volts (i.e. 0.003V), it's most likely a bad peltier.
- Using a multimeter and set to ohms [(+) lead to red peltier wire and (-) lead to black peltier wire], should display around negative 1.5 ohms on a good peltier (Bad peltier in the Megaohms). Then, placing the palm of your hand on the black bracket should cause the resistance reading to go more negative(on a bad peltier, the reading doesn't change). Once the hand palm is removed, eventually the multimeter should go back to original ohm reading.
- Replace peltiers.
( Trunk Stock Part )
- Chiller Ramp Peltier Module Removal and Replacement.
- PCB
- Using a calibrated thermometer, make sure chiller is reading between 17-19 ˚C.
- Check for burnt components or sign of old spills, dry fluid.
- Check for loose connections.
- Replace PCB.
- Re-seat any loose connections
If problem persists, replace chiller ramp module.
- Chiller Ramp PCB Removal and Replacement.
- Chiller Ramp Removal and Replacement.

## Pipettor Shutter Close Error
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor Shutter Close Error
Error Code
Dec
Hex
112.000.00097
Complaint Description
Pipettor Shutter Close Error, Shutter is Blocked or Sensor defect.
Field Service
-
Shutters properly seated and secured.
-
Check for debris between shutters.
-
Check pin and gear that move shutter are secure.
-
Check sensor flag is secure.
-
Check sensor using service software.
-
Device drop down can select reagent bay, or just shutter drive.
-
Also check controls to open and close.
Reagent bay shutter and Reagent bay PCB are only spare parts available.
Sensor or motor damage that is not resolved by reseating cables, or with Loctite, requires new reagent bay.

System believes there is still a rack in the reagent lane.
Re-start instrument and software.
- Remove any sample racks from the lane.
- Close the Reagent Bay Door.

- Re-start instrument if this does not work.

FSE
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- System believes there is still a rack in the reagent lane.
- Remove any sample racks from the lane.
- Close the Reagent Bay Door.
- Open Reagent Door, wait until lane highlights purple, insert the Reagent rack.
- Re-start instrument if this does not work.

- Adjust the TCR door lock mechanism or replaced TCR door OPEN/CLOSE sensor.

## Reagent or Sample Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner takes too long to reach the correct polygon speed)
id="mc-main-content">
Reagent or Sample Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner takes too long to reach the correct polygon speed)
Error Codes
Reagent Bay
Sample Bay
Dev
Hex
Dec
Hex
112.001.00043
096.001.00043
112.001.00016
096.001.00016
258.000.00009
258.000.00009
Complaint Description
Reagent/Sample Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner takes too long to reach the correct polygon speed)
Might be associated with the following error messages:
- Reagent/Sample Bay barcode scanner error (Command execution timeout)
- Rack loading error. Barcode Scanner failed to focus on lane x in the Reagent Loading Bay
Technical Support
Possible root causes
- Failing barcode scanner
- TB-01480: Sample Bay and Reagent Bay barcode scanners MUST be replaced if a Polygon Speed Error is reported, 4/17/2019.
Troubleshooting
- Shutdown/restart instrument (short term fix)
- Notify FSE Field Service Engineer. to replace the barcode scanner.
Barcode Scanner
RESOLUTION:
- Re-start the computer and instrument.
- Make sure the scanner is tightly plugged in.
- Check to be sure that no foam is interfering with the path of the scanner beam.
- Re-align the scanner.
- Properly configure the scanner.
- Replace the scanner.
TEST:
- Make sure the instrument is able to scan other sample tube barcodes.
- Make sure the scanner is plugged in.
- Make sure the scanner has no physical interference.
- Make sure the scanner is properly aligned.
- Make sure the scanner has been properly configured.
- Make sure the scanner is focusing properly.
Sample Bay PCB
RESOLUTION:
Replace Damaged PCB.
TEST:
Check for burnt components or signs of old spills.

## 112.001.00048
id="mc-main-content">
112.001.00048
Reagent Bay – COP System Message
Description
Reagent Bay barcode scanner unable to focus on scan lane.
Tier 1
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support/Customer Action
Reference
Rack inserted too fast.
Make sure to insert rack at a normal speed.
- Remove any reagent racks from the lanes.
- Close the Reagent Bay Door.
- Open Reagent Door, wait until lane highlights purple, insert the reagent rack. if this does not work, Re-start instrument.

id="mc-main-content">
COP 112 – Reagent Bay Module
COP System Messages
112.000 – Default for Reagent/Disposable Tip Unit
Event ID
Description
112.000.00000
No error.
112.000.00001
Reagent Bay failed to initialize.
112.000.00002
Reagent Bay error (Unknown Command).
112.000.00003
Reagent Bay error (Parameter value out of range).
112.000.00004
Reagent Bay error (Write failure of permanent parameter).
112.000.00005
Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (Write failure of permanent parameter).
112.000.00006
Reagent Bay supply voltage out of range (%1 V)
.
112.000.00007
Supply voltage CHN 1 back in range (%1 V).
112.000.00010
Reagent Bay shutter error.

Reagent Bay error (Command parameter value out of range).
112.000.00014
Reagent Bay error (Unable to execute command).
112.000.00015
Reagent Bay error (Command not implemented).
112.000.00016
Reagent Bay error (Command execution timeout).
112.000.00017
Reagent Bay error (Illegal parameter type definition).
112.000.00018
Reagent Bay error (Invalid parameter index).
112.000.00019
Reagent Bay error (Access to parameter not allowed).
112.000.00020
Reagent Bay error (Wrong parameter unlock code).
112.000.00021
Reagent Bay error (Illegal parameter type in command).
112.000.00022
Reagent Bay error (Illegal parameter type definition).
112.000.00032
Rack state of position %1 has changed.
112.000.00033
Reagent Bay scanning error lane %1 rack lane occupied.
112.000.00037
Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (Wrong barcode communication format).
112.000.00038
Reagent Bay scanning error data not transmitted to the PC because the scanner switched lanes too soon.
112.000.00039
Reagent Bay barcode scanner is not communicating.
112.000.00041

112.000.00042
Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (barcode scanner temperature too high).
112.000.00043
Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner takes too long to reach the correct polygon speed).
112.000.00044
Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner takes too long to focus).
112.000.00045
Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner takes too long to switch on laser diode).

Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner takes too long to switch off laser diode).

Reagent Bay barcode scanner error (Scanner polygon speed not ok).
112.000.00048
Reagent Bay barcode scanner unable to focus on scan lane.
112.000.00049
Reagent Bay barcode scanner rest delay error.
112.000.00050
Reagent Bay barcode scanner still on.
112.000.00051
Reagent Bay barcode scanner timeout while waiting for a rack to scan.
112.000.00065
First tube position barcode is missing on the rack inserted in the Reagent Bay.
112.000.00066
Rack ID barcode not read for the rack inserted in the Reagent Bay.
112.000.00067
Position barcode missing for the rack inserted in the Reagent Bay.

112.000.00080

112.000.00081

## 113.000.00001
id="mc-main-content">
113.000.00001
TCR Carousel – COP System Message
Description
TCR Carousel failed to initialize.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Obstructions that would prevent the TCR Carousel from moving properly.
- Is there a stray object preventing the Mixer from turning? Look for tips, loose spring, etc.
- Is the TCR mixer coming in contact with the incubator lid?
- Any other obstructions below the TCR mixer?
- Any obstructions on the top?
Remove the obstruction if one is found.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Obstructions that would prevent the TCR Mixer from moving properly.
- Is there a stray object preventing the Mixer from turning? Look for tips, loose spring, etc.
- Is the TCR mixer coming in contact with the incubator lid?
- Is there a loose cable that is preventing the TCR Mixer movement?
- Any other obstructions below the TCR mixer?
- Any obstructions on the top?
- Remove obstruction.
- Loose/Broken TCR Mixer Home Sensor and/or missing TCR Mixer Home Flag.
- Look at the TCR Mixer Home sensor and TCR Mixer Home Flag, ensure they are intact and functioning.
- Fix, replace, tigten the broken/missing partk.
- TCR Carousel Home Sensor Removal and Replacement.
- TCR Belt is tensioned incorrectly.
- Feel the TCR belt- is it too loose/tight.
- Retension the TCR Belt.
- TCR Carousel Belt Removal and Replacement.
- TCR has been spilled on the mixer, most notably into one (or all) of the bearings.
- Are there any noticeable spills in or around the bearings?
- Attempt to clean the spilled TCR with water.
- If this does not work, replace the mixer. Do not take the mixer apart - a jig is needed to correctly assemble it.
- TCR Carousel Module Removal and Replacement.
- TCR mixer motor burned out.
- With the power to the instrument off, attempt to move the TCR mixer.
- If it is difficult to move the mixer, the motor needs to be replaced.
- Replace TCR Mixer Motor.
- If this does not work, replace the mixer. Do not take the mixer apart- a jig is needed to correctly assemble it.
- TCR Carousel Motor Removal and Replacement.
