## TCR Carousel barcode scanner does not read a bottle barcode
id="mc-main-content">
TCR Carousel barcode scanner does not read a bottle barcode
Error Code
Dec
Hex
113.000.00051
0x71.0x00.0x0033
Complaint Description
TCR Carousel barcode scanner does not read a bottle barcode.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Incorrectly Positioned
- Faulty Reader
- TSE Example
Technical Support
Troubleshooting
-
Inspect the barcode and confirm it is not damaged are scratched up.
Replace the barcode or bottle as needed.
-
Inspect the TCR cup insert. Confirm that it is installed correctly, and is not blocking the TCR bottle barcode reader.
-
Correctly install the TCR cup insert.
-
Confirm that to correct, insert 100 or 250 test kit.
-
To correct dirty barcode reader lens, clean the barcode reader lens with ethanol.
Field Service
Incorrectly Positioned
Resolution
-
Use the bottle that the TCR Carousel has trouble reading. Use Service Software to recreate the error.
-
Change the position of the TCR Carousel barcode reader, to adjust the focal length of the scanner.
Faulty Reader
Resolution
If position for the barcode reader does not correct the problem, replace the reader.
TSE Example
The new twenty-one-position TCR Carousel has trouble scanning TCR barcodes.
Both instances appear to have been resolved after FSEs adjusted scanning angle to the empty slot barcode at the back of an empty slot on the carousel. See attached workaround.
Prior to this adjustment, customers would already have a valid kit scanned into sectors 1 and 2.
They would later add another kit to sector 3. When the system rescanned TCR to add kit at 3, it would then have trouble rescanning 1 or 2, and not recognize the TCR bottle that had already been loaded, scanned, or accepted.
The system then thinks those kits had been removed, and invalidates any samples already queued up against the kit now not seen.
-
2090002969 – upgraded with Fusion (21 pos TCR Carousel) on 6/29/23 (WO# 02122977).
-
6/30 – Case# 01313671 – TCR barcode Reader Not Working – FSE Field Service Engineer. Replaced TCR barcode Scanner (WO# 02186846).
-
7/12 – Case# 01320064 – TCR barcode Reader – FSE adjusted scanning angle (WO# 02252551).
-
1010910389 – Upgraded with Fusion (21-pos TCR Carousel) on 7/12/23 (WO# 02173702)
-
7/14 – Case# 01321100 – TCR Carousel Barcode Reader Failures – FSE adjusted with attached workaround (WO# 02255155).

- If it is difficult to move the mixer, the motor needs to be replaced.
- Replace TCR Mixer Motor.
- TCR Carousel Motor Removal and Replacement.

## 113.001.00050
id="mc-main-content">
113.001.00050
TCR Carousel – COP System Message
Description
TCR Carousel barcode scanner timeout error.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Barcode is not lined up with slot, or scratched or gravelly barcode.
Inspect the barcode and confirm that it is not scratched, gravelly, or otherwise compromised.
- Line up barcode properly or replace with a new bottle.
- Instruct the customer how to correctly install the TCR bottle, if necessary.
- The TCR cup insert (250 or 100 test kit) is not installed correctly.
- Inspect the TCR cup insert.
- Confirm that it is installed correctly and is not blocking the TCR bottle barcode reader.
- Correctly install the TCR cup insert.
- Instruct the customer how to correctly install the TCR bottle, if necessary.
- Dirty barcode reader lens.
- Check to see if the barcode reader lens is dirty.
- Clean the barcode reader lens with ethanol.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Barcode is not lined up with slot, or it is scratched or gravelly barcode.
- Inspect the barcode and confirm that it is not scratched, gravelly, or otherwise compromised.
- Line up the barcode properly or replace with a new bottle.
- Instruct the customer how to correctly install the TCR bottle, if necessary.
- The TCR cup insert (250 or 100 test kit) is not installed correctly.
- Inspect the TCR cup insert.
- Confirm that it is installed correctly and is not blocking the TCR bottle barcode reader.
- Correctly install the TCR cup insert.
- Instruct the customer how to correctly install the TCR bottle, if necessary.
- Dirty barcode reader lens.
- Check to see if the barcode reader lens is dirty.
- Clean the barcode reader lens with ethanol.
N/A
- The barcode reader needs to be repositioned.
- Using the bottle that the TCR Carousel was having trouble reading, use Service Software to recreate the error.
- Change the positioning of the TCR Carousel barcode reader to adjust the focal length of the scanner.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —TCR Carousel Barcode Reader Removal and Replacement
- The barcode reader is faulty.
- Using Service Software, try to repeat the error.
- If adjusting the positioning barcode and it does not fix the problem, replace the reader.
- Replace the TCR Carousel barcode reader.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —TCR Carousel Barcode Reader Removal and Replacement

## 113 002 00001
id="mc-main-content">
113 002 00001
TCR Carousel – COP System Message
Description
TCR Carousel mixer failed to initialize.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Obstructions that would prevent the TCR Mixer from moving properly.
- Is there a stray object preventing the Mixer from turning? Look for tips, loose spring, etc.
- Is the TCR mixer coming in contact with the incubator lid?
- Any other obstructions below the TCR mixer?
- Any obstructions on the top?
Remove obstruction.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Obstructions that would prevent the TCR Carousel from moving properly.
- If there a stray object preventing te mixer from turning? look for tips, loose, spring, etc.
- Is the TCR mixer coming in contact with the incubator lid?
- Is there a loose cable that is preventing the TCR mixer movement?
- Any other obstructions below the TCR mixer?
- Any obstructions on the top
- Remove the obstruction if one is found.
N/A
- Loose/broken TCR mixer home sensor, and/or missing TCR mixer home flag.
- Look at the TCR mixer home sensor and TCR mixer home flag, ensure they are intact and funstioning.
- Fix, replace, or tighten the broken or missing part.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —TCR Carousel Home Sensor Removal and Replacement
- The TCR Carousel belt is tensioned incorrectly.
- Feel the TCR belt is it too loose/tight
- Retension the TCR Carousel belt.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —TCR Carousel Motor Removal and Replacement
- TCR has been spilled on the mixer, most notably into one (or all) of the bearings.
- Are there any noticeable spills or around the bearings?
- Attempt to clean spilled TCR with water.
- If this does not work, replace the mixer. Do not take the mixer apart—a jig is needed to correctly assemble it.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —TCR Carousel Module Removal and Replacement
- The TCR Carousel motor is burned out.
- With the power to the instrument off, attempt to move the TCR mixer.
- If it is difficult to move the mixer, the motor needs to be replaced..
- Replace the TCR Carousel Motor.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —TCR Carousel Motor Removal and Replacement

## 253.000.00042
id="mc-main-content">
253.000.00042
Pipettor – COP System Message
Description
Reagent Pipettor error (Pump response timeout).
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Flex Cables, connections, PCBs
Initialize Instrument 3 times.
If able to replicate error, contact FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- Wet Pipettor Head
- Make sure Reagent bottle is not completely full (Up to the bottle neck).
- Initialize Instrument 3 times.
- Look for repeat errors in the log files.
- Use different Reagent Kit.
If able to replicate error, contact FSE.
If able to find repeat errors, contact FSE.
PANTHER System Operator's Manual
- Bad Pump, Piston or Lead Screw (Stiff Plunger)
- Initialize Instrument 3 times.
- Look for repeat errors in the log files.
- If able to replicate error, contact FSE.
-
If able to find repeat errors, contact FSE.
Field Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Flex Cables, connections, PCBs
- Inspect for any loose connections, worn out or damaged flex cables, burnt components on any of the Pipettor PCBs.
-
Re-connect loose connections, replace any bad flex cables or PCBs.
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Main PCB Removal
"
- Wet Pipettor Head
- Make sure Reagent bottle is not completely full (Up to the bottle neck).
- Remove Diti and Inspect for any fluid.
- Use different Reagent Kit.
- If able to see fluid inside the DiTi, most likely fluid got inside pipettor head, and pipettor needs replacement.
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Arm Removal and Replacement
- Bad Pump, Piston or Lead Screw (Stiff Plunger)
- Intitialize Pipettor 30 times to exercise pump.
or/and
- Perform Pressure Integrity Test 10 times to exercise pump
or/and
- Using Service Software cycle pipettor using BLLD 100 Times to exercise pump.
- If able to replicate error, replace pipettor.
or
-
If able to hear a squeak or see stuttering from plunger, or pipettor fails during the testing, replace pipettor. Otherwise, return instrument to customer.
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Arm Removal and Replacement

## Pipettor Error (Pump error nonstr-type x)
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor Error (Pump error nonstr-type x)
Error Codes
Dec
Hex
Arm

Reagent (Left)

Sample (Right)
Complaint Description
Pipettor error (Pump error nonstr-type x)
Nonstr-type [non-str; non-string; nonstr; nonstring; non str; non string] error codes are standard APP or APE module level message codes.
These are reported in decimal values, refer to appropriate MDD or CDD for detailed messages. (APP: MDD FW APP 6319, APE or BLDC: CDD FW 6319 APE ZSPip EC.)
Reagent pipettor (Left arm), Pump error (nonstr-type)
Sample pipettor (Right arm), Pump error (nonstr-type)
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Flex Cables Connections, PCBs
- Wet Pipettor Head
- Bad Pump, Piston or Lead Screw (Stiff Plunger)
-
Specific Examples
- Non-str type 10 errors
- Non-str type 33 errors
- Non-str type 36 errors
- Non-str type 3 errors (associated with CLT or PFS)
Technical Support
Auto Dispatch all nonstr-type x errors as a Severity 2. Troubleshoot error as normal. Inform customers FSE Field Service Engineer. will contact them to set up service. Customer can continue to process samples if instrument restart is successful.
Troubleshooting:
- Reset instrument.
- Perform MW cleaning to test sample pipettor.
- For Sample pipettor error (Pump error nonstr-type 3, associated with PFS or CLT): no service is needed. See below .
- For all other Sample pipettor error (Pump error nonstr-type x): always contact FSE as likely pipettor will need service. However, it is still possible the instrument will run without recurrences for a while so if FSE is not available, advise customer to run untested samples.
- Specific error codes related to software anomalies
- Nonstr-type 3: should be fixed in 7.2.3 patch, look for overpressure or CLT flag prior to error.
- Nonstr-type 11: downstream anomaly due to 080.000.00066 MTU barcode scanner is not responding. While not a pipettor error, underlying error should be investigated: - MTU lot #, -MTU scanner/LD teach, -MTU scanner
- Nonstr-type 53: common error in prior to sw version 5.3. Fixed with v5.3 instrument setup.
-
Aside from special cases above, this usually requires dispatch.
- 1-9: z-flex cable replacement will usually resolve issue
- 10+: usually requires pipettor replacement.
- FSEs should follow isolation procedures in Field Service section.
- Check reagent bottles are not completely full (up to the bottle neck).
- Reset instrument, will perform simple self test on initialization.
- Prime does not test either pipettor.
- MW cleaning only checks sample pipettor and does NOT test the reagent pipettor.
- Customer can keep running but there is a risk the issue will recur.
Always notify FSE.
Field Service
Flex Cables Connections, PCBs
- Inspect for any loose connections, worn out or damaged flex cables, burnt components on any of the Pipettor PCBs.
- Re-connect loose connections, replace any bad flex cables or PCBs.
Wet Pipettor Head
- Make sure Reagent bottle is not completely full (up to the bottle neck).
- Remove DiTi and inspect for any fluid.
- Use different Reagent Kit.
- If able to see fluid inside the DiTi, most likely fluid got inside pipettor head, and pipettor needs replacement.
Bad Pump, Piston or Lead Screw (Stiff Plunger)
Initialize Pipettor thirty times to exercise pump.
or/and Perform Pressure Integrity Test ten times to exercise pump.
or/and Using Service Software, cycle pipettor using BLLD one hundred times to exercise pump.
-
If able to replicate error, replace pipettor.
or
-
If able to hear a squeak, or see stuttering from plunger, or pipettor fails during the testing, replace pipettor. Otherwise, return instrument to customer.
Specific Examples
Non-str type 10 errors
NonStr-type 10 is “Motor overload detected: Motor defect or blocked or not connected”. Replace the Pipettor.
Panther 00970-sample pipette error OUR LADY OF THE LAKE REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER SR 3477300: Using pipettor graphing to root cause nonstr-type 10
Background:
Customer encountered sample pipette error type 10, upon shutdown and restart the error recurred. FSE arrived on site and processed several samples unable to replicate issue directly as no error messages during sample pipetting. By graphing the pressure curves for the processed samples showed the underlying problem was still there.
What event caused Fatal error?
Using the health report to work backwards, the fatal error is caused by sample pipettor critical error. More specifically, pump error nonstr-type10. Health report also captured second occurrence after restart, which occurred on 09/02/2014 07:35:12.677 253.015.00047.
What is a nonstr-10 error?
From the troubleshooting guide, white paper section for pipettors:
Nonstr-type 10 = Motor overload detected: motor defective, blocked, or not connected.
Characterizing problem using pressure graphs:
-
Logs confirm error occurs during dispensing : 9/2/2014 12:35:13 PM (02 07:35:13) [E] (Critical , High ) [PipettorSystem] Sample Pipettor error ( Pump error nonstr-type 10 ) ID=6238 PipettorDispense 'Add Sample' (Sample) PlannedStart=12:32:20.857 worst event at 12:35:12.157, start=12:35:05.657 end=12:35:12.257 (MTU=1 BarcodeID=1338293471, samples=8014/1424406218 CompletionTime=2014-09-02T15:54:24, , cmd params: Sample (SP) Index=27 finalZ=4611, vol=1299, track=70, fluid=33031 ) [0xFD.0x0F.0x002F] [253.015.00047]
-
Sometimes using aspiration or shearing curves is better for analysis because at slower pipetting velocity, less momentum is available to overcome problems that cause motor overload issues. In addition, the pipetting parameters for aspiration and shearing allow for maximum sampling rate.
-
Graph control tubes instead of actual samples, as the fluid properties are relatively constant as opposed to actual sample which can vary widely. a. Graphing from send logs: (More detailed directions can be found in Panther Troubleshooting Guide) i. Rename *.gpz as *.zip and unpackage.
I. Open the send logs file and choose the “\Curves” folder.
II. Folders are arranged by timestamp of when instrument was last restarted and primed. e.g. YYYY_MM_DD_HH-mm-ss
1. AspirationPressureCurve_2014_09_02_07-17-51.curve
2. ShearingPressure_2014_09_02_07-17-51.curve
Pressure curves from send logs uploaded by customer:
Figure 1 – Dispense curve (1st control tube) shows resolving pressure issues can be difficult. (x-axis: time, y-axis: pressure)
Figure 2 - Shearing pressure (first control tube). Shearing is 3 cycles of aspiration/dispense used to help break mucoidal strands. Blue vertical show pressure spikes are periodic.
Figure 3 - Aspiration Curve: The Controls show an interference with the syringe. They are not mucoidal and a known value of fluid. The curves show a problem even on the Controls. It could be the syringe or the motor driving the syringe on the specimen pipettor.
Confirming the issue:
FSE arrived on site and performed a small run with no errors. Checking the pressure curves showed the underlying problem was still present (Figure 4). FSE replaced pipettor and graphed pressure curves from resulting PQ showing problem resolved as pressure spikes are now gone (Figure 5.) improvement.
Figure 4 – Shearing graph from error free run prior to pipettor replacement shows underlying issue still present.
Figure 5 – Shearing graph after replacement of sample pipettor shows smooth curves.
Non-str type 33 errors
Take a look at the aspiration/ dispense curves. This example had a sticky plunger:
Amplification Aspiration LLD=867 for SIDs 306423/132216613803 [CT/GC] , 306422/132291023803 [CT/GC] , 306426/132443231203 [CT/GC] , 306419/132216599603 [CT/GC] , 306428/132291020303 [CT/GC] . [259.000.00058]
Reagent Pipettor error (Pump error nonstr-type 33) ID=13681 EjectDiTi 'AmpReagentPipettingStep' (Amplification) PlannedStart=12:53:54.191: , start=12:54:20.691 end=12:54:23.591 (MTU=22 BarcodeID=2185465443, samples=306423/132216613803/Normal, 306422/132291023803/Normal, 306426/132443231203/Normal, 306419/132216599603/Normal, 306428/132291020303/Normal, , cmd params: Amplification (RP) [coo=2,fZ=0] ). Event [0xFD.0x0E.0x002E] at 12:54:23.491 bytes: FD 7E 03 0E 2E 01 21 00 [253.014.00046]
Non-str type 36 errors
Non-String Type 36 = Valve Test Failure -> New Pipettor.
Non-str type 3 errors (associated with CLT or PFS)
If there is a CLT error followed by a Pipettor NonStr-3 error, this does not require an immediate dispatch, but can be fixed with a FW upgrade.
This was a big problem in the summer/ fall of 2021. And was fixed with new FW. See TB-01772.
The problem is caused by improper error handling of an overpressure event - It happens on both types of pipettors and previous versions of software as well (5.3, 6.2, etc.). But, was most prevalent with APP pipettors and SW 7.2.1.
Current mitigation is to have the FSE go in and upgrade the FW. This is fixed in the latest version of 7.2.1 Software, and above (Pipettor FW version 01.0310APP or 01.0109.1 BLDC, or Higher).
Pretty sure all nonstr-type and rdv errors will generate a PFS or PFR
Aspiration = CLT
<>(Warning) 08:46:55.414: Sample Pipettor clot detected (Ev=C3) [00.0F.C3] bytes: 00 00 02 0F C3 01 00
<>(Critical) 08:46:56.314: Sample Pipettor error (Pump error nonstr-type 3) (Ev=2F) [FD.0F.2F] bytes: FD DF 03 0F 2F 02 03 00
12/29/2020 08:46:56 (29 17:46:56) [E] (Critical , High ) [PipettorSystem] Sample Pipettor error (Pump error nonstr-type 3) ID=27358 PipettorAspirate 'Add Sample' (Sample) PlannedStart=08:44:18.514 worst event at 08:46:56.314, start=08:46:36.014 end=08:46:56.814 (MTU=76 BarcodeID=2092241080, samples=[0] , [1] , [2] , [3] 6034/12290015601, [4] , , cmd params: Sample (SP) Index=237 finalZ=158, vol=381, track=64, fluid=32779 ) [0xFD.0x0F.0x002F] [253.015.00047]
Dispense: usually don’t always see a pressure trace, but asp curve will look bad (like the graph above shows).
Overpressure (during dispense, if there is a pressure trace)
2021-03-03 11:20:00,186|[ProcessEvent]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error|03/03/2021 17:20:00 (03 11:20:00) [E] (Critical , High ) [PipettorSystem] Sample Pipettor error (Pump error nonstr-type 3) ID=46504 PipettorDispense 'Add Sample' (Sample) PlannedStart=17:19:47.855: , start=17:19:49.255 end=17:19:59.855 (MTU=125 BarcodeID=2079464482, samples=6282/A21458409001/Normal, , cmd params: Sample (SP) [coo=28,fZ=4607] , vol=396, track=70, fluid=33028 ). Event [0xFD.0x0F.0x002F] at 17:19:59.755 bytes: FD DF 03 0F 2F 02 03 00 [253.015.00047]
This is not a fully fatal error- MTUs that have passed through sample dispense with no errors will finish.
Another Example, 03765 Case 00818840 2021.03.03 Sample Pipettor non str type 3 error
It looks to me like a sample quality issue, the PFS samples are highlighted from 3/2 on left and and 3/3 on right:
I would not recommend a replacement at this point. Other process steps appear normal for that arm.
There are three types of nonstr-type 3 errors we’ve seen.
-
Older FW version pre system sw 5.3 – overpressure after aspiration triggered when pulling traveling airgap.
-
Flex cable issue.
-
FW/SW related error handling of an overpressure event (aspirate/dispense). This error can be exacerbated by tips.
In this case - sample pipettor (pump move canceled due to overpressure detection)
If this occurs to a customer, they should allow assay processing to complete. Then they can and restart the instrument and continue to run, but a FSE should be dispatched to upgrade the FW.
There does exist a vortexing protocol that can help mitigate this issue by breaking up the clots and reducing the maximum pressure during aspiration. It is recommended for the SARS-CoV-2 samples, but obviously we cannot force this to be implemented at every site.

Complaint Description
Either Reagent or Sample Panther Pipettor X-axis motor overload detected.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
-
Physical Obstruction
-
Dirty Rails
-
Cables and Connections
-
Belts: Loose, Worn Out, or Wrong Pitch
-
Motor Encoder
Technical Support
-
While instrument is off, open canopy. Check for and remove any obstructions.
-
Inspect sample bay shield.
-
Remove and replace.
-
Reset instrument.
-
Make sure sample bay shield and blue partition wall are properly seated.
-
Perform a MW cleaning to test sample pipettor.
Field Service
Physical Obstruction
Make sure there are no obstructions present along the travel path ie hoses, cables, tubing, covers, shield etc..
Resolution: Remove obstruction (blue partition wall and sample bay shield), inspect mounting bracket is not cracked or broken.
Dirty Rails
Turn off instrument and slide the pipettor in the X-direction to detect any binding
Resolution: Using a towel, wipe down X-axis bearing rods to remove any dirt, or grime.
Cables and Connections
Make sure all cables are properly connected.
Resolution: Re-seat encoder and motor cables and connectors.
Check for any worn out or damaged cables.
Resolution: Replace worn out or damaged Cables. Verify cables are properly secured with cable clamps.
Belts: Loose, Worn Out, or Wrong Pitch
Using Service Software, cycle pipettor to different positions or randomly move pipettor trying to replicate error
Resolution: Re-tension or replace the belts.
Motor Encoder
Dirty Motor Encoder
Resolution: Clean or replace encoder refer to TB-01691.
Listen for Chattering from inside the motor/encoder, signs that its struggling to keep its current position.
Resolution: Replace the X-motor, procedure is in the Panther Service Manual.

Panther Sample or Reagent Pipettor Z-axis motor overload detected.
Log sample
3/25/2021 21:41:29 (25 14:41:29) [E] (Fatal , High ) [PipettorSystem] Reagent Pipettor Z-axis motor overload detected ID=26295 PickupDiTi 'Select ReagentPipettingStep' (Select) PlannedStart=21:41:23.319 worst event at 21:41:29.619, start=21:41:24.219 end=21:41:29.819 (MTU=73 BarcodeID=1933543784, samples=[0] 430/2103252108524, [1] 431/2103252108525, [2] 432/2103252108526, [3] 433/2103252108527, [4] 434/2103252108528, , cmd params: Select (RP) Index=0 finalZ=0 ) [0xFD.0x0E.0x007A] [253.014.00122]
Technical Support
Z-axis = up and down movement.
Sample pipettor z-axis motor overload
- Check for any obstructions: TCR bottle cap left on, cap left on sample or control (if running SarsCov2 uncapped WF), sample shield not seated properly, tip stuck (out of place), etc.
- If sample shield was not seated properly, replace shield (as it will be contaminated).
- Reset instrument.
- If no cause was identified, perform MW cleaning to test sample pipettor and notify FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Reagent pipettor z-axis motor overload
- Check if any reagent bottle cap was left on.
- Reset instrument.
- If no cause was identified, notify FSE.
Field Service
Physical Obstruction
Make sure there are no obstructions present along the travel path: hoses, cables, tubing, covers, bottle caps, sample shield, reagent bay cover, sample tips stuck in tip eject chute, etc.
Remove any obstruction.
Cables/Connections
- Make sure all cables are properly connected.
- Check for any worn out or damaged Cables.
- Re-seat Loose Cables/connectors.
- Replace worn out or damaged cables such as flex cable.
Dirty Pipettor (where L-Shaped bearing slides)
Turn Off instrument and slide the pipettor in the Z-direction to detect any binding.
Using dry lint free cloth, wipe down the pipettor Z-rod to get rid of any grime.
Pipettor Teaching
Make sure pipettor is properly taught and not binding against a module.
Re-Teach pipettor.
L-Shaped Bearing
Make sure L-Shaped bearing are not worn out or damaged.
Replace L-shaped bearing
Z-Motor/Pipettor Meshing
Turn Off instrument and Slide the pipettor in the Z-direction to detect any binding.
Using Service Software, Cycle Pipettor to different positions with sample tip eject option, or randomly move pipettor with sample tip eject option trying to duplicate error (Sample Tip Tray, Reagent Bay Probe, HPA load Station as an example).
Properly Mesh the Z-motor and the Pipettor.
Motor/Encoder Issue
Dirty Motor Encoder
Listen for Chattering from inside the motor/encoder, signs that it's struggling to keep its current position.
Bad Motor and/or Bad Encoder
Replace the motor as needed
TSE Review
First, Check for a bad Z-Motor
If the motor has already been replaced (or isn't bad), check the following (this one occurred at the tip drawer):
- Has the instrument been moved? Is the instrument level?
- The Tip drawers- do you know if it is always happening on the same drawer?
- Check the tip drawers, is there any play, once the drawer is closed and locked? Allowing movement so the tips aren’t where they should be?
- Teaching to the Tip Drawers.
- Watch the arm pick a few tips from both drawers, does the diti seem to be centered in the tips when they are picked?
- The Pipettor, have you replaced the tip eject sleeves (TB-01627), if so, maybe replace the one on the Reagent arm again.
- Check the meshing of the Z-Motor gear to the pipettor is the meshing too tight? The service manual has some good instructions and pictures, search for “Pipettor / Z-Motor Meshing”.
- Check the routing of the home sensor cable, as shown. Is the routing such that it is pushing the motor gear against the pipettor?
- Remove the Pipettor and clean the bearing surfaces, shown below. Clean both the white plastic pieces and the pipettor surfaces.
- Check to make sure there isn’t any plastic or glue impeding the movement of the pipettor, as shown below.
More things to check (especially if errors are random, and continuing to exist after all other options have been checked):
- X-Axis encoder.
- X-Axis Belts- look for debris around the gear. Move the pipettor quickly by hand, and see if the belt "pops". These are indicative of the belt skipping a tooth. The belt needs to be changed.
Checklist
- Reagent Pipettor replaced.
- Reagent pipettor Z motor replaced at least twice.
- TB-01627 new DiTi Sleeve has been performed.
- TB-01691 Encoder and Cap installation has been performed.
- Tip Drawers are properly seated no play or movement.
- No damage or misalignment with the teach positions either reference position or tip drawer teach points.
- Teaching is smooth and accurate to all modules. The Pipettor does not attempt to overexert on the teach point but rather just taps each position. Refer to the Alignment/Calibration section in the Service Manual.
- Tips are the Tecan 513 tips.
- Reagent Pipettor Y-sledge board has been replaced per service manual.
- All replacements have included a successful Firmware reflash.
- All Cable connections around the pipettor are secure and undamaged.
- There are no obstructions causing limited motion of the pipettor in any axis.
- Picking tips seems to me smooth and consistent.
- The Meshing has been performed per the service manual Note: the photo you provided looks like meshing may be a little too tight.
- Routing of the home sensor cable does not interfere with the motor gears.
- The gantry is square. See manual under Parallel check.
- Perform “Pipettor Gantry Rail Maintenance procedure” per the service manual.
- Check and replace X belts, see Pipettor X-Axis Rack Belts Removal and Replacement procedure in the service manual.
- The blue divider is fully seated.
- The sample bay cover and pipettor interference check has been performed see service manual.
- A pipettor main PCB has been replaced per the service manual.
- L shaped Bearings are not worn or damaged, replace as needed.
- Any other Damage or obstruction around the Z motor in the Gantry?
- All bearing and surfaces are clean free of dirt and debris
- The pipettor X-Flex cable and Y-Flex Cable had been replaced.

Technical Support
Possible Root Cause

Flex Cables, connections, PCBs
Initialize Instrument 3 times.
If able to replicate error, contact FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- Wet Pipettor Head

If able to replicate error, contact FSE.
If able to find repeat errors, contact FSE.

- Initialize Instrument 3 times.
- Look for repeat errors in the log files.
- If able to replicate error, contact FSE.
-
If able to find repeat errors, contact FSE.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Flex Cables, connections, PCBs
- Inspect for any loose connections, worn out or damaged flex cables, burnt components on any of the Pipettor PCBs.
-
Re-connect loose connections, replace any bad flex cables or PCBs.
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Flex Cable Removal and Replacement
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Main PCB Removal
"
- Wet Pipettor Head
- Make sure Reagent bottle is not completely full (Up to the bottle neck).
- Remove Diti and Inspect for any fluid.
- Use different Reagent Kit.
- If able to see fluid inside the DiTi, most likely fluid got inside pipettor head, and pipettor needs replacement.
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Arm Removal and Replacement
- Bad Pump, Piston or Lead Screw (Stiff Plunger)
- Intitialize Pipettor 30 times to exercise pump.
or/and
- Perform Pressure Integrity Test 10 times to exercise pump
or/and
- Using Service Software cycle pipettor using BLLD 100 Times to exercise pump.
- If able to replicate error, replace pipettor.
or
-
If able to hear a squeak or see stuttering from plunger, or pipettor fails during the testing, replace pipettor. Otherwise, return instrument to customer.
- PANTHER System Service Manual-Pipettor Arm Removal and Replacement

## Pipettor X-axis Suffered Step Loss or Stalled
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor X-axis Suffered Step Loss or Stalled
Error Codes
Dec
Hex
Arm
253.000.00140
0xFD.0x00.0x008C
Reagent
253.014.00140
0xFD.0x0E.0x008C
Reagent
253.015.00143
0xFD.0x0F.0x008F
Sample
Complaint Description
Either Reagent or Sample Pipettor x-axis suffered step loss or stalled (Position is out of tolerance. Coordinate: xx)
Log Sample
11/05/2020 1:51:10 PM Fatal 253.015.00143 Sample Pipettor X-axis suffered step loss or stalled (Position is out of tolerance. Coordinate: 54)
Table of Contents
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Obstruction
- Pipettor X Belts
- Rust
- TSE Review
Technical Support
-
For reagent pipettor:
- Check reagent bay cover is seated properly, no loose screws or debris on top, and check tip trays are correctly seated.
-
For sample pipettor:
- Depending on the coordinate: verify sample bay cover, tip trays, partition wall etc. are properly seated.
-
Review "Pipettor coordinates" document below for coordinate position of failure. This will give you an idea of the location of the obstruction.
-
Reset instrument.
-
If reset fails, instruct customer to check for stuck or jammed tip on pipettor. If present, customer can gently remove the tip by wrapping the tip in a towel/wipe, and releasing it from the pipettor using the tip eject lever. See photograph below.
-
If reset passes, and error is on sample pipettor: perform a MW cleaning to test. If error is on the reagent pipettor, customer can try a small run of new samples, or just calibrators/controls to test.
-
If no obvious cause can be found, notify FSE Field Service Engineer. .
-
If this is a repeating error, dispatch FSE.
Note— Table below has pipettor coordinates for both sample and reagent pipettors
Picture shows example partition wall not seated properly causing sample pipettor x-axis step loss or stalled. Position out of tolerance. Coordinate 53.
Field Service
Obstruction
Check for obstructions or anything blocking the movement of the pipettor. Sample and reagent bay lids are properly installed, sample bay divider is properly installed, etc.
Pipettor X Belts
Inspect the X Belts.
Make sure there is smooth movement left to right with the power off.
Replace Belts as needed .
Rust
Inspect the instrument for rust.
Replace the GAC filter as needed. Old GAC filters can introduce bleach fumes into the instrument and damage the X motors and encodors. See the photo below.
Replace the encoders and caps Per TB-01691.
TSE Review
X-Axis Step Loss Pipettor
Tips left on pip or dropped tips on system indicates tip eject issue.
Normally we check if error occurred after tip eject on the way to pick tip…
Resolution:
- Verify new eject sleeve.
- Take picture of zmax at tip eject block, reteach if necessary.
- Inspect diti cone carefully, we found one recently with a slight burr on the end.
- What tips are they using?
- Pip/z-motor meshing.
- Check bearing surfaces of pipettor.
- Check z-motor for excessive friction.

## 257.000.00003
id="mc-main-content">
257.000.00003
Manual Action – PC System Message
Description
Requested operation %1 is currently blocked by executing another command.
Remove all racks and close all drawers and doors in order to continue initialization.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- Reagent or Sample Racks have been left in the instrument after a system reboot.
- Check the Reagent and Sample Bays for racks.
- Ask the operator to remove any racks left on the instrument.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Missing or broken spring on the Waste Drawer locking mechanism, preventing the locking mechanism from closing properly.
- Open the left instrument side panel and inspect the locking mechanism.
- Open and close the Waste Drawer to visually inspect the action of the locking mechanism.
- Determine if the mechanism is properly engaging when the drawer is fully closed.
- Replace the spring if it is missing or broken.
N/A
- The clip that holds the Waste Drawer closed is broken and the drawer does not stay fully closed when the operator closes the drawer.
- Open the left instrument side panel and inspect behind the Waste Drawer for debris.
- Inspect the end of each of the slide rails where the retaining clips are located.
- Open and close the Waste Drawer to visually inspect that the drawer if the drawer fully closes and stays in place when closed.
- If broken rail retaining clips are determined to be the cause of the problem, replace the slide rail(s).
N/A
- The ribbon cable connectors on the Cooling Module or the interlock are improperly seated or the cable is damaged.
- Inspect the connectors at the Cooling Module and at the interlock for proper seating.
- Inspect the ribbon cable for damage.
- Using Service Software, test interlock reading and function.
Note—If the connector is upside down, the Cooling Module will not initialize and the green light on the Cooling Module will not be lit.
- Reseat the connectors at the interlock and the Cooling Module PCB.
- Inspect the ribbon cable that runs from the Cooling Module PCB to the interlock for nicks, especially if the ribbon cable is not contained in the cable race at the back wall of the instrument.
- Replace the cable if it is damaged.
N/A
- Sensor on interlock or interlock pin is obstructed by fluid or debris.
- Inspect the interlock and locking mechanism for debris or evidence of fluid leakage.
- Remove the locking mechanism and clean with 70% EtOH.
- Inspect the action of the solenoid pin and locking mechanism by hand.
- If dried fluid was the cause of the failure, stickiness of the mechanism and the interlock pin movement will be improved by cleaning.
- Allow the mechanism and the interlock to dry and reinstall.
- Using Service Software, verify that the interlock functions properly, and the drawer closes and locks properly
N/A
- Interlock damaged or failed.
- After all other options have been attempted to fix the interlock problem and there is no response from the interlock and the problem isn't due to a damaged ribbon cable. Test with a new interlock.
- Remove the locking mechanism and replace the interlock.
- Using Service Software, test the new interlock.
- If the problem does not recur with the new interlock, the part may have failed and a replacement was required.
N/A

## 257.000.00014
id="mc-main-content">
257.000.00014
Manual Action – PC System Message
Description
MTU unload not started. Liquid Waste full. Check waste bottle.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Waste bottle.
- Verify that the waste bottle is completely empty.
- Check to see if the waste bottle floater is stuck.
- Check to see if the waste bottle is collapsed, causing the floater to be stuck.
- Empty the waste bottle.
- Replace the waste bottle.
- Restart the instrument.
- If the problem persists, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Empty Waste and System Startup
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Waste bottle.
- Verify that the waste bottle is completely empty.
- Check to see if the waste bottle floater is stuck.
- Check to see if the waste bottle is collapsed, causing the floater to be stuck.
- Empty the waste bottle.
- Replace the waste bottle.
- Restart the instrument.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Empty Waste and System Startup
- Waste bottle empty/full sensor.
- Verify that the waste bottle empty/full sensor is connected.
- Using Service Software, verify that the sensor reads properly.
- Check for a faulty sensor or broken wires.
- Properly connect the sensor.
- Clean the sensor.
- Adjust the sensor to get it closer to the waste bottle floater.
- If the sensor is faulty, replace.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Waste Bottle Empty/Full Sensor Assembly Removal and Replacement

## 257.000.00015
id="mc-main-content">
257.000.00015
Manual Action – PC System Message
Description
MTU unload not started. MTU waste bag not present.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
Waste bag.
Verify the waste bag is properly installed.
- Properly install the waste bag.
- Restart the instrument.
- If the error persists, dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. .
PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Empty Waste and System Startup
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Waste bag.
- Verify the waste bag is properly installed.
- Properly install the waste bag.
- Restart the instrument.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Empty Waste and System Startup
- Waste bag presence sensor.
- Verify that the waste bag presence sensor is connected.
- Using Service Software, verify that the sensor reads properly.
- Check for a faulty sensor or broken wires.
- Properly connect the sensor.
- Clean the sensor.
- Calibrate the Sensor.
- Adjust the sensor.
- If the sensor is faulty, replace.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Waste Drawer Bag Sensor Removal and Replacement

Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure

Make sure the Tips Drawers are fully closed.
Ask the operator to push the Tips Drawers closed.
N/A

Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Commonly occurs when the operator pulls on the Tips Drawer when it is locked.
- Make sure the Tips Drawers are fully closed.
- Ask the operator to push the Tips Drawers closed.
N/A

- Adjust the position of the Tips Drawer flag so that it remains in the sensor light barrier when the Tips Drawer is pulled on while locked.

## 258.000.00007
id="mc-main-content">
258.000.00007
Loading Management – PC System Message
Description
Multiple pipettor tip pickup failures detected. {Bottom, Middle, Top} tray on {Left or Right} drawer marked empty.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- Loading Tips
-
Check to see if the first tip locations are empty on that tray. Or if the tray is completely empty.
-
Replace the tip tray with a tray full of tips.
-
The pipettors need to be re-taught to the tip trays because the pipettor is misaligned when attempting to pick a tip.
- Tip pick failures will be intermittent. When looking at the tray some tips will be skipped and some will be picked. The tips are picked from back to front and from left to right as observed when facing the instrument.
-
FSE Field Service Engineer. will need to re-teach the pipettors.
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
-
See above for possible operator errors during tip loading.
-
Pipettor alignment is incorrect, the pipettors will need to be re-taught.
-
Tip pick failures are usually intermittent, some tips may be picked and some will still be present at positions where the failures occurred. Ensure that the instrument is on a stable surface and the instrument feet are secure.
- Re-teach the pipettor arms.
-
Panther Service Manual
-
There may be a physical cause for the tip pick failures.
-
Test tip picks at the tray location where the tip pick failures occurred and observe for any obstruction to the DiTi.
- Remove obstruction and re-teach to the tip trays.
-
Panther Service Manual

- Using Service Software, test the Sample and Reagent flap function.

N/A
- If the problem persists and the message still occurs after the customer closes the door, one or more of the Front Cover break out boards may be disconnected from the main board (Reagent Bay).

## Locking or Stacking of MTUs in the Input Queue Failed / Push MTU Failure
id="mc-main-content">
Locking or Stacking of MTUs in the Input Queue Failed / Push MTU Failure
Error Code
Dec
Hex
258.000.00013
0x102.0x00.0x0D
Complaint Description
Input or MTU Queue Stacking Issue
05/15/2023 12:32:13 (15 08:32:13) [E] (Critical , High ) [LoadingManagement] Locking or stacking of the MTUs in the Input Queue failed. [258.000.00013]
05/15/2023 16:38:04 (15 12:38:04) [E] (Critical , High ) [InputQueue] Input Queue pack drive motor suffered step loss ID=49 InitializeInstrumentResponse: , start=16:36:53.926 end=16:38:04.626. Event [0x50.0x00.0x000A] at 16:37:55.626 bytes: 50 02 03 00 0A [080.000.00010]
Push MTU failure in service software. “50 20 02 00 34 00”
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
-
Check Input Queue
-
Next Steps
Field Service
-
Bad MTUs
-
Loose Connection
-
Misaligned MTU Input Queue Rails
-
Dirty, Misaligned, or Faulty MTU Pusher Sensor
-
Faulty Encoder
-
Faulty Motor or Drive Mechanism
-
Spring and Pusher
-
Ball Detent Latch
-
Drawer Latch Adjustment
Technical Support
Check Input Queue
-
Check if MTUs are placed in front of the pusher.
-
Check for jammed MTUs or obstructions in the queue.
-
Make sure only 25 MTUs are loaded in the queue.
-
Remove incorrectly seated MTUs or obstructions.
-
Try opening and closing the Input Queue to make sure it will lock correctly.
-
If the pusher is staying in front and is not touching MTU, push it back manually until it meets the MTU. The drawer should now lock.
Next Steps
-
Restart the instrument.
-
Perform a prime and/or MW clean to test the Input Queue.
-
Review case history for previous Input Queue errors.
-
Notify FSE Field Service Engineer. if there were recent cases.
-
Instruct customer to monitor instrument.
Field Service
Bad MTUs
Resolution
-
If possible, take a photograph of the state of the MTUs.
-
Remove the MTUs by hand, taking care not to spill tiplets.
-
Inspect MTUs for any abnormalities.
-
If the MTU is suspect as defective note the lot number of the MTUs contact Tech Support to open a complaint and return the suspect bad MTUs for further investigation.
Test
Make sure other MTU lot numbers are able to process through the Input Queue successfully.
Loose Connection
Resolution
Reseat loose connection.
Test
Inspect to make sure all connections are secure.
Misaligned MTU Input Queue Rails
Resolution
Use the alignment tool to properly align the rails per the Panther Service Manual.
Test
-
Open the MTU Input Queue.
-
Slide several MTUs back and forth across the rails. The MTUs should slide smoothly.
-
Also, use the Rail Alignment Tool to check the rail alignment.
Note: See diagrams and images below to help identify sensors and flags accordingly.
Dirty, Misaligned, or Faulty MTU Pusher Sensor
Resolution
-
Clean the packing optical sensor.
-
Verify the white plastic packing button easily moves into the sensor when pressed, and springs forward again when released. If not, inspect for cleanliness, or broken or damaged spring.
-
Tighten the three posts and screws that secure the slave PCB.
-
Replace the auxiliary PCB.
Test
-
Unlock and open the MTU Input Queue, and inspect the MTU Pusher optical sensor behind the white packing button. Note whether the sensor or white plastic packing button are dirty. Clean as necessary.
-
Using Service Software, read sensor status. With no MTU at the pick position, the MTU Pusher Sensor should read “OUT”.
-
Push the white packing button into the MTU Pusher sensor and re-read sensor status. When the white plastic packing button interrupts the MTU Pusher, sensor status should change to read “IN”.
-
Open the MTU Input Queue and inspect the three posts holding the Slave PCB. The posts should be secure, and the screws securing the PCB should be tight.
Note: Some IQs used small washers between posts, and Slave PCB to space the sensor/Slave PCB further away from the white packing button for more accurate changes in state. Consider removing these washers if present, reassemble, and re-test to see if washer thickness makes a difference in MTU Pusher Sensor States (In vs. Out in Service Software GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. ).
-
Using Service Software, pack some MTUs. If the module packs MTUs correctly, yet the system still reports a packing error, it is likely due to a faulty MTU Pusher sensor.
Faulty Encoder
Resolution
Replace the Encoder or the Module.
Test
Using Service Software, pack some MTUs.
If the motor does not stop and keeps pushing for an excessive amount of time, it is likely due to a faulty encoder.
Faulty Motor or Drive Mechanism
Resolution
Replace the motor, belt, or the module.
Test
Using Service Software, initialize the module.
Note whether the MTU pusher moves. If it does not move, it is likely due to a faulty motor or drive belt.
Also check for debris, such as tiplets.
Spring and Pusher
The issue in the MTU queue causing the problem is the plastic pusher at the end of the queue, by where the LD picks the MTU. I found the carrier fallen over when trying to pick the empty one from the queue.
Basically, the springs in the pusher are too strong. Therefore the pusher pushes the MTU down too hard, causing the MTU to be at an angle when it is the last one on the carrier. Because the MTU does not sit perfectly in the slot, the carrier hits into it when being taken out of the queue, or when being put back in. A photograph of the MTU appears below. Since the pusher/springs are not orderable, the entire module needs to be swapped.
I have run into an issue caused by these springs being too strong in the past. This error came in the form of an MTU stacking error in the queue. I have tried shaving down the plastic part, but the issue came back, so the entire module was replaced. Would it be possible for these springs/pushers to be orderable in the future?
Resolution
There are two springs up top. In the past, sometimes an extra spring would coil together doubling the force. It is worthwhile to check.
The pusher force can be adjusted by bending the forked pusher spring slightly.
An obstruction may prevent the input drawer from closing completely. This prevents the latch from falling, which obstructs the pusher movement.
Test
Using Service Software, pack some MTUs.
If the motor does not stop and keeps pushing for an excessive amount of time, it is likely due to a faulty encoder.
Ball Detent Latch
Drawer Latch Adjustment
Input queue step loss errors, or unable to initialize due to input queue drawer not pushed in all the way.
The drawer latch cannot drop, which prevents the pusher from moving into initial position, or away.
-
Drawer latch and latch block cannot drop into place correctly.
-
Pin on pusher cannot move if latch does not drop down.
-
Loose detent foot, I do not recall the machined IQ having the same issue.
New foot, which comes with casted IQ. This design seems problematic, as it often gets loose. Clamped down with screw, but force is front to back.
-
Drawer flag / home sensor positioning, protruding too far forward during assembly, or FSE adjusted because detent foot fell off before?

## 258.000.00014
id="mc-main-content">
258.000.00014
Loading Management – PC System Message
Description
TCR door failed to lock. Open and close the door to retry locking the door.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- It is possible the TCR door was pulled on while it was locked causing the locking pin to become stuck. This is a warning message only and should not cause a failure.
- Verify the TCR door is fully closed
- Apply pressure to the affected door to unlock the pin.
- TCR door is out of alignment or lock malfunction
- Message occurs during reagent loading or no message occurs because closing the door has no effect.
- During TCR/TER reagent loading the operator should apply pressure to the door to ensure that the door is fully closed while locking. Contact the FSE Field Service Engineer. to schedule a service visit to properly align the TCR door.
- GP11-250 FSN TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment'
FSE
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- It is possible the TCR door was pulled on while it was locked causing the locking pin to become stuck. This is a warning message only and should not cause a failure.
- Verify the TCR door is fully closed
- Apply pressure to the affected door to unlock the pin.
- TCR door misaligned
- Determine the cause of misalignment: Refer to 'TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment' FSN. If the door lock works properly if there is inward pressure applied on the door the lock is misaligned.
- Follow guidelines to ensure correct alignment. Correct the alignment issues and test door function in Service Software. Observe the operator load the reagent kits to verify correct operation. Refer to 'TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment' FSN.
- GP11-250 FSN TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment'
- Damaged or mis-seated cables
- Initialize the module in service software and check front cover and TCR door function. This is assuming that the cause of the problem is not TCR door alignment.
- Inspect all cables attached to the front cover PCB. Look for pinched/damaged cables or mis seated connectors. The ribbon cable running from the front cover PCB to the left side canopy LED indicator is commonly damaged when removing and replacing the front cover.
- TCR door interlock module is faulty
- After following the procedure in 'TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment' FSN and inspecting the electrical cables/connectors and the lock has shown to be defective still in service software testing.
- Replace the TCR door interlock.
- GP11-250 FSN TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment
- Front Cover Removal and Replacement Procedure

## Samples in MTU Were Invalidated
id="mc-main-content">
Samples in MTU Were Invalidated
Error Code
Dec
Location
259.000.00111
Complaint Description
Samples in MTU were invalidated.
Sample IDs: X, Y, Z...not processed by Fusion sidecar, as MTU had to be disposed due to unavailable storage.
Technical Support
-
Thermocycler bank went out of operations earlier.
-
Software bug.
-
MTUs are scheduled to a specific bank from the moment the samples are pipetted, if a bank goes out of operations, the instrument will not be able to change the scheduling halfway through processing and the MTU will have to be discarded.
-
If there are no previous errors it could be related to a SW bug under MKS 2062387, resolved in software 7.2.
Either case provide lost test count if applicable. Address the reason for the bank to go out of operation (background, thermal error, unhandled tube loss etc.).
Field Service
MKS
2062387
Root Cause
Dumping tests due to sidecar storage conflicts is usually tied to disabling TC banks, or manually adding or deleting tests, and thereby messing with backend scheduling.
Workaround
A workflow change could help to mitigate this issue.
2020-06-03 21:17:25,560|[ProcessEvent]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error|06/04/2020 04:17:25 (03 21:17:25) [E] (Warning , Low ) [ProcessManagement] Sample Ids: 2015504228A, 2015506106A, 2015505511A, 2015504888A, 2015506415A were not processed by Fusion sidecar as MTU had to be disposed due to unavailable storage. [259.000.00111]

## 262.000.00028
id="mc-main-content">
262.000.00028
Inventory Management – PC System Message
Description
Auto Detect 1A bottle is empty or not connected. Please check bottle connection.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- Empty bottle.
- Verify that the Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle contains fluid.
- Install a new Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Load Universal Fluids
- Disconnected bottle.
- Verify that the quick-connect fitting is connected to the Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle.
- Connect the Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle fitting.
- Dispense Curve showing Auto Detect 1 Bottle Empty
- Bottle cap connectors crusty or crystallized.
- Check for crust or crystal formation on bottle cap connectors.
- Clean cap connectors with DI water or replace.
- Prime the instrument and check for air bubbles in the detect line after the prime.
N/A
- Missing, disconnected, or cracked aspirator tube (straw) inside bottle.
- Verify that the aspirator tube is present in the bottle cap/fitting assembly and is not cracked.
- Replace the aspirator tube in the cap assembly or order a new cap assembly.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- Empty bottle.
- Verify that the Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle contains fluid.
- Install a new Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle.
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual —Load Universal Fluids
- Disconnected bottle.
- Verify that the quick-connect fitting is connected to the Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle.
- Connect the Auto Detect 1 fluid bottle fitting.
- Dispense Curve showing Auto Detect 1 Bottle Empty
- Bottle cap connectors crusty or crystallized.
- Check for crust or crystal formation on bottle cap connectors.
- Clean cap connectors with DI water or replace.
- Prime the instrument and check for air bubbles in the detect line after the prime.
N/A
- Missing, disconnected, or cracked aspirator tube (straw) inside bottle.
- Verify that the aspirator tube is present in the bottle cap/fitting assembly and is not cracked.
- Replace the aspirator tube in the cap assembly or order a new cap assembly.
N/A
- Leaky fitting, fluid line, pump, or valve.
- Check for leaks at all fittings, fluid lines, the pump, and the solenoid valve in the fluid path (from the Auto Detect bottle to the injector).
- Correct the leak.
N/A
- Kinked fluid line.
- Inspect all Detect fluid lines for a kink.
- Remove any kinks.
- Verify that the fluid line is not leaking at the kink location.
N/A
- Faulty OLV Sensor circuit board
- Plot the OLV snesor traces.
- If the trace has a near zero signal, then the PCB may be faulty.
- Also, inspect the PCB for moisture and/or dried fluid deposits.
- Replace the PCB.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Luminometer OLV Sensor Removal and Replacement
- Auto Detect 1 Injector
- Check for kinks in the Auto Detect 1 injector fluid lines.
- Inspect the injector housing for leaks.
- Verify that the OLV sight holes in the injector are clear and free of debris.
- Replace the injector.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Luminometer Injector Removal and Replacement
- Faulty solenoid valve.
- Verify that the solenoid valve is properly switching between bottle A and B.
- Ensure that the solenoid wiring is securely attached to the PCB connector.
- Replace the solenoid.
- PANTHER System Service Manual —Solenoid Valve Removal and Replacement

## Bleach bottle is empty or not connected
id="mc-main-content">
Bleach bottle is empty or not connected
Error Code
Dec
Hex
262.000.00036
Complaint Description
Bleach bottle is empty or not connected.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
-
Aged or Worn Peristaltic Pump Tubing
-
Improperly Installed Peristaltic Pump Back Plate or Tubing Mount Clips
-
Leaky Fitting, Fluid Line, Pump, or Valve
-
Kinked Fluid Line
-
Faulty OLV Sensor Circuit Board
-
Output Queue Injector
-
Bleach Bottle full Sensor
-
Faulty Peristaltic Pump
Technical Support
Possible root cause
-
Empty bottle or disconnected
-
Missing or worn connector (O-ring is not a standalone part)
-
Stuck float
-
PCB
-
Worn or old Peri-pump tubing
-
Peri-pump tubing clamp missing or not secured
Troubleshooting
-
Verify bleach bottle has enough fluids
-
Verify the connector snaps in and is intact
-
Check the tubings for any bubbles- if the answer is yes, how far do the bubbles go
-
Verify the floaty is not stuck-by adding DI water to the bottle and see if it moves at all
-
If bleach is not dispensing and there are undeactivated waste errors, remind the customer to double bag solid waste and add equal volume of undiluted bleach to liquid waste, let sit for at least 30 min before discarding.
-
Verify the bottle status panel light is green. If is not, reset instrument. If this doesn't help, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
-
Find out when the last PM or CCC was done to replace the peri-pump tubing. If it was recent, ask customer to check peri-pump tubing housing is properly seated.
Field Service
Aged or Worn Peristaltic Pump Tubing
Resolution
Replace the Peristaltic Pump Tubing
Test
Plot the OLV sensor traces. If the trace shows that no fluid is being dispensed, then replace the tubing. Also, inspect the fluid line that routes from the Universal Fluid drawer to the Peristaltic pump. If the fluid line is not primed from the drawer to the pump, then fluid may be leaking past the pump due to worn tubing.
Improperly Installed Peristaltic Pump Back Plate or Tubing Mount Clips
Resolution
Install the components correctly.
Test
Verify that peristaltic pump back plates are properly installed. Verify that the tubing mount clips are properly installed in the peristaltic pump
Leaky Fitting, Fluid Line, Pump, or Valve
Resolution
Correct the Leak
Test
Check for leaks at all fittings, fluid lines, the pump, and the solenoid valve in the fluid path (from the bleach bottle to the injector)
Kinked Fluid Line
Resolution
Remove the kink. Verify that the fluid line is not leaking at the kink location.
Test
Check for leaks at all fittings, fluid lines, the pump, and the solenoid valve in the fluid path (from the bleach bottle to the injector)
Faulty OLV Sensor Circuit Board
Resolution
Replace the OLV
Test
Plot the OLV sensor traces. If the trace has a near zero signal, then the PCB may be faulty. Also, inspect the PCB for moisture and/or dried fluid deposits
Output Queue Injector
Resolution
Replace the Injector
Test
Check for kinks in Detect injector fluid lines. Inspect the injector housing for leaks. Verify that the OLV sight holes in the injector are clear and free of debris.
Bleach Bottle full Sensor
Resolution
- Connect sensor
- Clean sensor
- Adjust sensor to get it closer to bleach bottle floater
- Replace Faulty sensor
Test
- Verify the sensor is connected
- Using Service Software, verify the sensor properly reads
- Faulty Sensor or broken wires
Faulty Peristaltic Pump
Resolution
Replace the pump as needed
Test
Check for proper operation of the Peristaltic Pump in SSW.

## TCR Too High
id="mc-main-content">
TCR Too High
The Error in the log states:
Target Capture Volume in Quadrant 1 is higher than expected. Ensure bottle is seated properly and no bubbles are present. [262.000.00043]
Rescheduling tests due to error. Reagents already added to the invalidated MTU have been deducted from the available inventory. Test orders will be pipetted with the next MTU. [261.000.00012]
Looking at the TCR Level sense data, initial level sense is at 600 for HPV 100 TK (It should be more like 400).
Also, the TCR cLLD data: The reason there are two sets of curves: the curves to the right are the initial level senses. The curves to the left are the two retries. The difference is the Z-Height start. For the initial level sense, the trigger is armed around the top of the bottle. For the two retries, the SP does not move fully back up. Instead, it just retracts a few steps, then tries again.
For this case, there was probably foam, as this curve shows the bubble pop, where the capacitive path is broken:

## Undeactivated Waste May Be Present in Liquid or Solid Waste
id="mc-main-content">
Undeactivated Waste May Be Present in Liquid or Solid Waste
Error Code
Dec
Hex
262.000.00054
Complaint Description
Undeactivated Waste Maybe Present in liquid or solid waste
Table of Contents
-
Technical Support
- Possible Root Cause:
- TS Troubleshooting:
-
Field Service
- Peri Pump Tubing
- Peri Pump Tubing Clips
- Leak
- Kinked Fluid Line
- Faulty OLV Sensor Circuit Board
- Output Queue Injector
- Faulty Peri Pump
- Continuous Access Waste
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause:
- Empty bleach or deactivation bottle
- Loose fitting and/or straw
- Kinked tubing (not very common)
- Missing or worn O-ring
- Cracked Deactivation fluid cap/fitting
- Old, worn or incorrectly installed peristalitic pump tubing
- Peristaltic pump, A/B Solenoid valve
TS Troubleshooting:
While receiving these messages, when you empty undeactivated waste, dispose of waste as follows:
Double bag solid waste.
Add an equal volume of bleach to removable liquid waste bottle, and let it sit for one hour prior to discarding.
- Verify bleach and both deactivation bottles have enough fluid
- Verify quick-disconnect is securely connected ( inspect the O-ring)
- Verify the straw inside deactivation buffer bottles is snug
- Check the tubing for any air bubbles (near bottle or near peripump?)
- Obtain logs to review
- Analyze OLV dispense curves (see https://teams.hologic.com/sites/MolecularTSDx/KnowledgeBase/Panther/Topics.aspx)
Field Service
Note: Please refer to Output Queue Curves for Process Control Analysis.
Peri Pump Tubing
Aged or worn peristaltic pump tubing
Resolution:
Replace the Peristaltic Pump tubing
Test:
- Plot the OLV sensor traces.
- If the trace shows that no fluid is being dispensed, then replace the tubing. Also, inspect the fluid line that routes from the Universal Fluid drawer to the Peristaltic pump.
- If the fluid line is not primed from the drawer to the pump, then fluid may be leaking past the pump due to worn tubing.
Peri Pump Tubing Clips
Improperly installed Peristaltic Pump back plate or tubing mount clips.
Resolution:
Reinstall the clips correctly
Test:
- Verify that peristaltic pump back plates are properly installed. Verify that the tubing mount clips are properly installed in the peristaltic pump.
- Also make sure the tubing fittings are 5mm instead of 7mm long.
Leak
Leaky fitting, fluid line, pump, or valve
Resolution:
Correct the Leak
Test:
Check for leaks at all fittings, fluid lines, the pump, and the solenoid valve in the fluid path (from the Bleach and Deactivation Buffer bottles to the injector).
Kinked Fluid Line
Resolution:
- Remove the kink.
- Verify that the fluid line is not leaking at the kink location.
Test:
Inspect all Peristaltic Pump fluid lines for kinks.
Faulty OLV Sensor Circuit Board
Resolution:
Replace the PCB
Test:
- Plot the OLV sensor traces.
- If the trace has a near zero signal, then the PCB may be faulty. Also, inspect the PCB for moisture and/or dried fluid deposits
Output Queue Injector
Resolution:
Replace the Injector
Test:
- Check for kinks in Detect injector fluid lines. Inspect the injector housing for leaks.
- Verify that the OLV sight holes in the injector are clear and free of debris.
Faulty Peri Pump
RESOLUTION:
Replace the Peristaltic pump.
Test:
Check that the Peristaltic Pump is functioning properly.
Continuous Access Waste
Bleach and/or deactivation are not dispensing correctly.
- The sensor does not detect that bleach/deactivation dispenses correctly.
Note: Customers have only one removable bottle, so they will need to let assay processing finish before changing the waste.
RESOLUTION No Waste to Drain:
- Let assay processing finish before changing the waste.
- Perform normal troubleshooting, such as double bagging solid waste and adding bleach to liquid waste for one hour.
RESOLUTION Waste to Drain:
- The instrument will automatically stop pumping waste to the drain. Customer will need to change liquid waste manually.
- Let assay processing finish before changing the waste.
- Perform normal troubleshooting, such as double bagging solid waste and adding bleach to liquid waste for one hour.

## Reagent Bottle is Invalid
id="mc-main-content">
Reagent Bottle is Invalid
Error Codes
262.001.00010; 262.003.00010
Case 1
Warning 262.001.00010 The reagent bottle X Reagent in lane X , position X , is invalid after three consecutive RDV failures, where X is the reagent bottle or position.
Once you open the logs in ViewLog, the Z-Movement errors are pretty easy to spot:
Red circles and numbers in the image above indicate how to locate the error in the Errors tab.
When you find the error in the Errors tab, double-click it to return to the Log tab. Within the range of the RDV error, you see the Z-Movement error:
Red circles in the image above highlight a sample entry in the Log tab.
If you find this error, this should be an FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch. The FSE should go in with the white pipettor V and L bearings.
Also note, the messaging is confusing on this error. The Reagent kit is not actually invalid. The customer should be able to still use it.
Case 2
Warning 262.003.00010 The reagent bottle, Target Capture Reagent , in quadrant 1 is invalid after three consecutive RDV failures. Note: This could be any reagent, in any quadrant.
Also in the logs:
- RDV Error 64 during TCR Dispensing.
- RDFT flag.
- Rescheduling tests due to error. Any reagents already added to the invalidated MTU have been deducted from the available inventory. Test orders will be pipetted with the next MTU. [261.000.00012]
Reviewing the TCR level sense, aspiration and dispense curves:
For this case, capacitive sensor is working and detecting fluid.
But no fluid is being aspirated, so error during dispense
Advice:
- Run a PI test.
- Check for loose DiTi.
- Run some blld tests in SSW.
- Check consumables, such as cracked or broken tips.
For this specific case, the DiTi was loose.

Internal control pipetting failed for FCR/FER set in TCR Carousel position X.
Along with :
000.015.00159 Sample Pipettor error (pump move canceled due to overpressure detection) and 265.000.00003 Dispense of internal control failed.
Technical Support
- Sample shield placed incorrectly.
If you have a Panther Fusion customer calling and saying the they had an internal control pipetting error: Internal control pipetting failed for FCR/FER set in TCR Carousel position (5-7), have them check the sample shield. If it is not placed properly, when they load new FCR/FER and IC and the sample pipettor goes to try to pipette the IC it can cause that error.
If the customer tries to reload the same set of FCR/FER/IC, even though IC was probably never pipetted, it will think it has and will not use those extraction reagents again. Customer will have to discard that set of extraction reagents or use them in a different Panther Fusion (as long as they are not linked).
Have the customer fix sample shield and then load new set of FCR/FER/IC. Those reagents are free of charge, so they can order more, or if they need hem right away, we send them.
Field Service

## Analyze Flags and Message Codes
id="mc-main-content">
Analyze Flags and Message Codes
This topic explains how to analyze flags and message codes, to determine which module generated the code.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Recommended Analysis Procedure
for Error or Processing Code
-
Use the Results Log for Flags
-
Use the Message Log for Error Codes
-
Decipher the Event ID Number
-
Module ID Number
-
SubUnit Number
-
Message Number
-
Use the ViewLog
Recommended Analysis Procedure
for Error or Processing Code
Perform this procedure for either Error codes, or Processing codes:
- Review the Result Log for flags (i.e., result and assay processing codes) and Message (Event) Log for messages (i.e., message Event ID error codes).
If no Message/Event Log is available, then review the When Message/Event Log has been purged section below.
1 - PC Event                   2 - COP Event
The Event ID number signifies what type of event is occurring (i. e., PC or COP event as shown in the graphic above.)
- Review the Message (Event) Log to find the local time stamp and event/flag that was assigned during assay processing. Search for the oldest entry's local Date and Time and Event ID number.
When the Message/Event Log has been purged:
- Select Reports button in the Panther Menu bar.
The Report Menu will appear that shows all of the possible reports, checklists, worklists, and logs available for review.
- In the Report Menu, select the applicable Creation Date option to find the Panther's Historical Data that contains the particular time period that needs to be investigated in the Message/Event Log information.
- Select View (or Print ) to review the Message Log for the chosen Creation Date. (These buttons are located at the bottom edge of the Report Menu screen.)
Use the Results Log for Flags
Perform this procedure to find any result or assay processing codes:
- Select Results in the PANTHER Menu bar.
1 - Assay Processing Code                   2 - Result Processing Code(s)
- The Results Log for the selected Completion Date will appear.
- Review the entire fifth column (moving left-to-right) for both result and/or assay processing codes (i.e., for any result or assay flags).
Use the Message Log for Error Codes
Perform this procedure to find any result or assay processing codes:
- Select Messages button in the PANTHER Menu bar
- The Message Log (table) for the selected Completion Date will appear.
- Review the entire Event ID column for any suspectious result and/or assay processing codes (i.e., for any flags).
Decipher the Event ID Number
The Event ID number format is NNN .NNN.NNNNN, where:
- The first number set or NNN ." is the Module ID number for all events that post from any COP or device firmware.
- The second number set or ".NNN." is the SubUnit ID number which specifies the subunit in which the event occurred.
- The third number set or ".NNNNN" is the Message Number which specifies the acutal event that occurred. The message event numbers are documented in the module design description of the firmware. For PC event numbers are defined in the file PCEVENTS.TXT .
Module ID Number
As described in the last section, the Module ID number is the first number set of the Event ID Number.
Each PANTHER module's CAN Bus Address is the Module ID number which ranges from 0 to 255. On the PC side, the CAN Bus Address for the Module ID number ranges from 256 to 511.
The Module ID number is mapped to a certain dynamic link library (.dll) module, and from this library module is where the event is generated.
The tables of Module ID numbers for COP and PC Event Messages are provided as a reference guide for determining the effected module:

SubUnit Number
The SubUnit number further details the origin of the event.
Message Number
Both COP and PC events are subject to localization, specifically, during the build process, the two files are converted into a dot.net assembly file (i.e., Eventmessages.dll). This .dll file contains all Event messages as string resources, which in turn contain the Event ID number in a period-separated format.
Use the ViewLog
This log can be viewed by opening the ViewLog application from within PANTHER Tools or through the Remote Dashboard (using its menu path File > View Log . This log lists all the events or flags with assigned 'local time' and 'UTC GMT' time stamps.
While viewing the ViewLog data, the FSE Field Service Engineer.  should perform root cause analysis, then identify the instrument problem by using the step-by-step procedure in the Service Software.
<Photo of ViewLog with the EventLogEntries tab selected.>
The EventLogEntries tab
- Click the EventLogEntries tab to obtain the local and GMT time stamps for all events or flags that occurred during a particular day (see ViewLog capture above).
<Photo of ViewLog with the Log tab selected (with 7 elements in command string being number-labeled.>
- Click the Log tab to see specific error message codes (listed under the Content column). These message codes are listed by their occurrence associated Date, Time, Thread, Class Name, Category, and Error Level.
- The Content column contains the Receipt Command String for each message/flag code. This command string includes the affected:
- Device address
- Answer ID
- Receive State
- Subassembly name
- Error or warning
- Position
- Options

## Incorrect Large Valve Swap
id="mc-main-content">
Incorrect Large Valve Swap
Error Code
No error code.
Complaint Description:
Failed HPV PQ, but passed FC.
Technical Support
Incorrect swap of valve
Correct: blue tubing = deactivation, clear tubing = MW buffer
There is no signal at all for AC2. (400 RLUS for the controls).
Resolution:
Correctly route tubing.

## 025.000.00033
id="mc-main-content">
025.000.00033
Front Cover – COP System Message
Description
TCR Door not able to lock.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- It is possible the TCR door was pulled on while it was locked causing the locking pin to become stuck. This is a warning message only and should not cause a failure.
- Verify the TCR door is fully closed
- Apply pressure to the affected door to unlock the pin.
- TCR door is out of alignment or lock malfunction
- Message occurs during reagent loading or no message occurs because closing the door has no effect.
- During TCR/TER reagent loading the operator should apply pressure to the door to ensure that the door is fully closed while locking. Contact the FSE Field Service Engineer. to schedule a service visit to properly align the TCR door.
GP11-250 FSN TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment'
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- It is possible the TCR door was pulled on while it was locked causing the locking pin to become stuck. This is a warning message only and should not cause a failure.
- Verify the TCR door is fully closed.
- Apply pressure to the affected door to unlock the pin.
- TCR door misaligned
- Determine the cause of misalignment: Refer to 'TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment' FSN. If the door lock works properly if there is inward pressure applied on the door the lock is misaligned.
- Follow guidelines to ensure correct alignment. Correct the alignment issues and test door function in Service Software. Observe the operator load the reagent kits to verify correct operation. Refer to 'TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment' FSN.
- GP11-250 FSN TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment'
- Damaged or mis-seated cables
- Initialize the module in service software and check front cover and TCR door function. This is assuming that the cause of the problem is not TCR door alignment.
- Inspect all cables attached to the front cover PCB. Look for pinched/damaged cables or mis seated connectors. The ribbon cable running from the front cover PCB to the left side canopy LED indicator is commonly damaged when removing and replacing the front cover.
- TCR door interlock module is faulty
- After following the procedure in 'TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment' FSN and inspecting the electrical cables/connectors and the lock has shown to be defective still in service software testing.
- Replace the TCR door interlock.
- GP11-250 FSN TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment
- Front Cover Removal and Replacement Procedure

N/A

N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The instrument is in Power Save Mode when trying to unload Reagents

- Take Instrument out of Power Save mode first before unloading Reagents (Logoff/Shutdown screen).
- PANTHER System Operator's Manual
- The TCR door may have been pulled while it was locked, causing the locking pin to become stuck. This is a warning message only and should not cause a failure.

N/A
- TCR door is misaligned
