## 025.000.00035
id="mc-main-content">
025.000.00035
Front Cover – COP System Message
Description
TCR Door is open.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Technical Support / Customer Action
Reference
- The TCR door may have been pulled while it was locked, causing the locking pin to become stuck. This is a warning message only and should not cause a failure.
- Verify that the TCR door is fully closed.
- Apply pressure to the affected door to unlock the pin.
N/A
- The TCR door is out of alignment or the TCR door lock is malfunctioning.
- Message occurs during Reagent loading.
If the error occurs in Setup or Ready mode:
- Remove the Reagent Rack loaded when the error occurred.
- Navigate to the PANTHER Tasks screen and select Perform Maintenance .
- Select Clean Sample Shield and select Start .
- Apply inward pressure on the TCR door and then select Start to start to unlock the door.
- Load Reagent kits while applying inward pressure on the door until an FSE Field Service Engineer. can correct the issue.
N/A
Field Service
Possible Root Cause
Isolation Procedure
Service Action
Reference
- The TCR door may have been pulled while it was locked, causing the locking pin to become stuck. This is a warning message only and should not cause a failure.
- Verify that the TCR door is fully closed.
- Apply pressure to the affected door to unlock the pin.
N/A
- TCR door misaligned.
- Determine the cause of misalignment according to the TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment FSN.
- If the door lock works properly when inward pressure is applied to the door, the lock is misaligned.
- Follow guidelines in the FSN to ensure correct alignment.
- Correct the alignment issues and test door function in Service Software.
- Observe the operator load the Reagent kits to verify correct operation.
- GP11-250 FSN—TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment
- Damaged cables or improperly seated connectors.
- Using Service Software, initialize the module and check Front Cover and TCR door function. (This assumes that the cause of the problem is not TCR door misalignment.)
- Inspect all cables attached to the Front Cover PCB.
- Look for pinched/damaged cables, or improperly seated connectors.
- The ribbon cable running from the Front Cover PCB to the left side canopy LED indicator is commonly damaged when removing and replacing the Front Cover.
- TCR door interlock module is faulty.
- After following the TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment procedure, and inspecting the electrical cables/connectors, use Service Software to test the operation of the lock.
- If the lock is still defective, replace the lock.
- Replace the TCR door interlock.
- GP11-250 FSN—TCR Door Alignment and Adjustment

## Wash Pump Motor Step Loss or Stall
id="mc-main-content">
Wash Pump Motor Step Loss or Stall
Error Code
Dec
Hex
051.000.00010
0x33.0x00.0x000A
Complaint Description
Wash pump motor suffered step loss or stalled.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
Field Service
-
Pump Step Loss Due to Wash Buffer Crystallization
-
Pump Step Loss Due to Magwash Pump Failure
-
Pump Step Loss Due to MagWash Solenoid Failure
Technical Support
-
Ask if the instrument has been sitting idle for an extended period of time.
If yes, there may be some wash buffer that has crystalized. Customer can prime two times to clear any clogs.
- Customer can prime to clear the error.
Field Service
Pump Step Loss Due to Wash Buffer Crystallization
Look through the wash buffer line, to observe if crystallization is present.
Resolution
If crystallization is present, flush warm water through the pump until no crystals are present.
Test
Perform full system prime twice, to verify water is fully flushed from the lines, and the pump works as expected.
Pump Step Loss Due to Magwash Pump Failure
Isolate the error:
-
In the logs, observe during which command the step loss occurred. In this example, the step loss occurred during the Dispense Command (21):
-
In Service Software, perform a “Magnetic Wash Module Visual Dispense Verification” - search the service manual for instructions - for both MagWashes.
-
If the error occurs on both MagWashes, then the Pump has failed.
Notes:
-
If the error is not reproducible in Service Software, the most likely culprit is the Pump.
-
If the Pump is replaced, and the error repeats, most likely there is a failed MagWash Solenoid.
Resolution
Replace the MagWash LCM Pump.
Test
See Panther Service Manual, “Wash LCMP Removal and Replacement.”
Pump Step Loss Due to MagWash Solenoid Failure
Isolate the error:
-
In the logs, observe during which command the step loss occurred. In this example, the step loss occurred during the Dispense Command (21):
-
In Service Software, perform a “Magnetic Wash Module Visual Dispense Verification” - search the service manual for instructions - for both MagWashes.
-
In step 2, determine which MagWash has a failed Solenoid Valve.
Resolution
Replace the Solenoid Valves for the Wash Solution, for the affected MagWash.
Test
See Panther Service Manual, “Magnetic Wash Station Oil and Wash Solenoid Valve Removal and Replacement.”

## Incubator Carousel Error: Position at Home Pin
id="mc-main-content">
Incubator Carousel Error: Position at Home Pin
Error Codes:
Dec
Hex
032.002.00081
033.002.00081
034.002.00081
0x20.0x02.0x51
0x21.0x02.0x51
0x22.0x02.0x51
Complaint Description:
Carousel Motor drive position is greater than the allowed error at the home pin.
Incubator 1 = High Temperature Incubator
Incubator 2 = Transition Incubator
Incubator 3 = AMP Incubator
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Door Home Sensor or Pin
- Over-Torqued Door Fastener
- Pulley or Belt Tension
- Carousel Motor Encoder
- Carousel Motor
Technical Support
Restart instrument to verify problem persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem, and will require an FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch..
Field Service
Door Home Sensor or Pin
- Using Service Software, verify that the door sensor outputs “Open”/”Close”.
- Visually inspect the Home Sensor for any residue.
Resolution:
- Clean the door sensor of any residue using a swab and alcohol.
- Replace the Door Home Sensor if deemed faulty.
Test:
Perform a 2 cycle Incubator System OQ.
Over-Torqued Door Fastener
Over-torqueing of the screw can warp the screw hole and push the door open. It may be intermittent or permanently read “Open”. Using Service Software, determine if the door sensor is properly reading.
Resolution:
- Reduce torque.
- Replace the door if warped beyond repair.
Test:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Pulley or Belt Tension
-
Confirm the pulleys are the correct ones and not faulty – refer to the Panther Parts List for the most current version of pulley.
-
Verify belt tension is proper, and the belt is not faulty.
Resolution:
- Replace the pulleys.
- Re-tension the belt, or replace if faulty.
Test:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Motor Encoder
- Check that the encoder cable is fully connected and not faulty.
- Make sure the encoder is not dirty.
- Encoder is faulty.
Resolution:
- Replace the encoder cable.
- If possible, clean the encoder using alcohol and a swab.
- Replace the encoder/motor.
Test:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Motor
- Check the motor cable is fully connected and not faulty.
- Using Service Software move the carousel to multiple positions – make sure the motor is moving properly.
Resolution:
- Reseat or replace the motor cable.
- Replace the motor.
Test:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.

## Incubator Carousel Error: Light Barrier Trigger Failure
id="mc-main-content">
Incubator Carousel Error: Light Barrier Trigger Failure
Error Codes:
Dec
Hex
032.002.00082
033.002.00082
034.002.00082
0x20.0x02.0x52
0x21.0x02.0x52
0x22.0x02.0x52
Complaint Description:
The light barrier did not trigger within five continuous rotations.
Incubator 1 = High Temperature Incubator
Incubator 2 = Transition Incubator
Incubator 3 = AMP Incubator
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Poor Home Pin/Door Interaction
- Door Home Sensor or Pin
- Over-Torqued Door Fastener
- Carousel Home Sensor or Pin
- Door Assembly
- Pulley or Belt Tension
- Carousel Motor Encoder
- Carousel Motor
Technical Support
Restart instrument to verify problem persists. Although this error can be intermittent, it is usually a sign of a problem, and will require an FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch.
Field Service
Poor Home Pin/Door Interaction
Using Service Software, verify interaction between the home sensor and the home pin. The sensor output should correctly read “Open” or “Close”.
RESOLUTION:
Install the Door Clip per the Panther System Service Manual.
Note: In Panther SN’s 00919, and newer incubators have been redesigned to include screws that secure the incubator doors, eliminating the need for an incubator door clip.
TEST:
Verify the interaction between the home pin and the home sensor is optimal: the home pin should be reasonably centered in the home sensor, the home pin should not contact the home sensor during carousel movement.
Door Home Sensor or Pin
- Using Service Software, verify that the door sensor outputs “Open”/”Close”.
- Visually inspect the Home Sensor for any residue.
RESOLUTION:
- Clean the door sensor of any residue using a swab and alcohol.
- Replace the Door Home Sensor if deemed faulty.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Over-Torqued Door Fastener
Over-torqueing of the screw can warp the screw hole and push the door open. It may be intermittent or permanently read “Open”. Using Service Software determine if the door sensor is properly reading.
RESOLUTION:
- Reduce torque.
- Replace the door if warped beyond repair.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Home Sensor or Pin
- Using Service Software verify the sensor output is “In”/”Out”. Check the sensor and pin for residue or obstruction.
- Sensor is Faulty.
RESOLUTION:
- Using a swab and alcohol clean the carousel home sensor and pin.
- Replace the carousel home sensor.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Door Assembly
The Incubator cover, wiring, or over torqued door screw can skew the door away from the carousel home pin. Verify the door seats as flush as possible and the carousel home sensor correctly interacts with the carousel home pin.
RESOLUTION:
Reseat the door and make sure the incubator cover, wiring, or screws don’t cause the door to skew away from the carousel home pin.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Pulley or Belt Tension
-
Confirm the pulleys are the correct ones and not faulty – refer to the Panther Parts List for the most current version of pulley.
-
Check the belt tension is proper and the belt is not faulty.
RESOLUTION:
- Replace the pulleys.
- Retention the belt or replace if faulty.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Motor Encoder
- Check that the encoder cable is fully connected and not faulty.
- Make sure the encoder is not dirty.
- Encoder is faulty.
RESOLUTION:
- Replace the encoder cable.
- If possible, clean the encoder using alcohol and a swab.
- Replace the encoder/motor.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Carousel Motor
- Check the motor cable is fully connected and not faulty.
- Using Service Software move the carousel to multiple positions – make sure the motor is moving properly.
RESOLUTION:
- Reseat or replace the motor cable.
- Replace the motor.
TEST:
Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.

## Incubator Door Is Open
id="mc-main-content">
Incubator Door Is Open
Error Codes
Dec
Hex
032.002.00121
033.002.00121
034.002.00121
0x20.0x02.0x79
0x21.0x02.0x79
0x22.0x02.0x79
Complaint Description
Incubator Door is open, so no movement is allowed.
Incubator 1 = High Temperature Incubator
Incubator 2 = Transition Incubator
Incubator 3 = AMP Incubator
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
MTU Stuck Halfway in the Incubator
-
Door Home Sensor is Faulty
-
Door Stuck Open
-
Field Service
-
MTU Stuck in the Incubator
-
Incubator Door is Physically Stuck Open
-
Incubator Door Home Sensor is Faulty or Incorrectly Positioned
-
Incubator Main PCB is Faulty
-
Incubator Door Home Sensor Cable Disconnected or Damaged
-
Degraded Incubator Foam
Technical Support
MTU Stuck Halfway in the Incubator
The customer may be able to confirm that the MTU is stuck halfway in the incubator by opening the instrument left side panel, and looking down the Linear Distributor track. The problem could be related to distributor interference with the door.
Review logs for Distributor Lost Steps at the incubator position. Dispatch an FSE Field Service Engineer. if the problem persists.
Door Home Sensor is Faulty
The incubator door home sensor may be faulty if there is no MTU stuck in the incubator.
Shut down and restart the instrument, and monitor for recurrence. If issue recurs, dispatch an FSE.
Door Stuck Open
The door is physically stuck open without anything physically preventing it from closing. Either the door bearing is sticking or there is torsion on the door itself creating too much friction on the bearing.
The customer may be able to see the position of the Linear Distributor. If the distributor is not seen at the incubator door position – can they see if the door is stuck open? If so, dispatch an FSE.
Field Service
MTU Stuck in the Incubator
- Review Messages and/or Health Report and System logs to determine if there are any Linear Distributor lost steps at the incubator or any other positions.
- Restart the Panther Software and allow the system to deactivate and unload MTU’s prior to starting service. If unload will not complete use Service Software to check and unload MTU’s from the incubator. If any are present ensure they are properly deactivated before continuing.
Resolution
- Check incubator carousel belt tensioning and adjust if necessary.
- Check alignment of the incubator slots – refer to Incubator Slot Alignment in the Panther System Service Manual. The MTU should not be rubbing against the door when placed into the incubator.
- Inspect the Linear Distributor hook and theta drives for looseness or any other situation that could contribute to incorrect teaching.
- Teach the Linear Distributor to the Incubator or to all modules if the Linear Distributor is found to be the root cause.
Test
- If root cause is found to be at the incubator, perform a five-cycle System OQ to the incubator.
- If the Linear Distributor is at fault, perform a two-cycle System OQ to all modules.
Incubator Door is Physically Stuck Open
-
Manually cycle the door open and closed by hand ( gloves must be worn ). The door should move freely, and snap shut by the force of the spring in the door.
-
Verify the Incubator door clip is present if appropriate.
Note: Screws were cut into all Panthers above Serial #00919 – Incubators with a screw do not require installation of door clips. If Panther SN is above #00919 ensure screw is present and secure.
-
Restart the Panther Software, and allow the system to deactivate and unload MTU’s prior to starting service. Ensure there are no MTUs present in the incubator.
-
Check the seating of the Incubator cap against the door and check the seating and positioning of the incubator door.
Resolution
-
If debris is found on the door slide rail, clean the rail with ethanol and determine and address the source of the debris. LIGHTLY lubricate the rail with Teflon based oil.
-
If the incubator door is bent or warped – replace the door.
-
Install door clip per Panther System Service Manual.
Note: Screws were cut into all Panthers above Serial #00919 – Incubators with a screw do not require installation of door clips. If Panther SN is above #00919 ensure screw is present and secure.
Test
- Manually cycle the door open and closed by hand. (Gloves must be worn!) The door should move freely and snap closed by the force of the spring in the door.
- Perform a two-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Incubator Door Home Sensor is Faulty or Incorrectly Positioned
- Manually cycle the door open and closed, paying close attention to the way the edge of the door seats when it closes by spring force.
- In Service Software, read the incubator door sensor state – open the door by hand and let it close. Read the sensor. Repeat in order to duplicate the problem.
- Determine any physical cause of the door failing to fully seat – check for door bearings that have moved out of place, door warpage, and the like.
Resolution
- Reseat the door home sensor PCB by loosening the screws that hold the door in place.
- Clean the door home sensor.
- Replace the door home sensor PCB.
- Replace the door.
Test
Perform a five-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Incubator Main PCB is Faulty
Inspect the Incubator Main PCB for damage (for example, something leaked on the PCB).
Resolution
- If leaking is apparent, determine and address the source of the leak.
- Replace the Main PCB, and any other components damaged by the leak.
Test
Perform a five-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Incubator Door Home Sensor Cable Disconnected or Damaged
Inspect the incubator Door Home sensor cable and connector for damage or disconnection.
Resolution
Reconnect the cable or replace if necessary.
Test
Perform a five-cycle Incubator System OQ.
Degraded Incubator Foam
It seems that after several years, this black foam (see photographs below), on the HT incubators especially, can start to degrade.  This could cause Door sensor errors and possibly Carousel move errors.
Resolution
Inspect the incubator for degrading foam. Refer to images below. If it is not bad enough, then you could try to clean up the bits of foam and ensure that it does not interfere with door movement. Otherwise, a module replacement will be required.
If there was a Door or Carousel move error, then this should also definitely be looked at.  If degraded foam is found in an old HT incubator, then it probably requires a module replacement.  If it is a newer module or non-HT incubator and the FSE can identify piece(s) of foam that may have caused an obstruction, then it could be fixed.
Of the four pictures below, the first two were reported to be from an incubator that had Door errors.
These photographs were from an incubator that had Door errors.  This would likely require a module replacement.
Photographs below were from an old HT incubator in the lab, but has not reported Door errors.  It looks a bit different, as there is no indication of fine particles like the two pictures above.  I would not replace this during a PM, but ensure that there are no stray pieces of foam that could cause errors, and the door is moving smoothly.   If this were seen upon a Door failure, I would replace the module, unless I saw something that could be fixed, such as a piece of foam that caused the error and that could be removed.

## Incubator Troubleshooting Best Practices
id="mc-main-content">
Incubator Troubleshooting Best Practices
Topic covers best practices to troubleshoot the instrument's incubators. Sections include:
- Incubator Hardware Comparison
- Servicing
- Helpful Materials
- AMP Incubator and Real Time Fluorometers
- RTF Orientation and Dip Switch Settings
- Installation Issues and Common Errors for RTFs
Incubator Hardware Comparison
Servicing
- Review logs to help isolate the root cause.
- Use the Panther System Service Manual for Service Procedures.
- Important: Always use universal precautions when servicing any module on the Panther System.
- Important: Always ensure incubator is cleared of MTUs prior to servicing and/or removal.
-
Follow the Total Service Call guidelines whenever servicing the Panther System for any reason. For the incubators:
- Inspect all doors to ensure they open and close smoothly.
- Inspect all incubator belts for wear, and replace as necessary.
- Important: Never attempt to convert or interchange any of the incubators!
Helpful Materials
Bad Bearings: Axial and Vertical Bearing Slop
To view a one-minute video recording that illustrates slop in the axial and vertical bearings, click or tap the image below, then click or tap the play icon. The recording opens in your browser.
Error code 03x.002.00081 : Motor drive position is greater than the allowed error at the home pin.
Incubator Fan Differences
Table below shows differences among fans for each incubator.

AMP Incubator and Real Time Fluorometers
AMP Incubator currently uses four of six possible Real Time Fluorometers (RTFs).
Images below show two views of an RTF:
Table below shows specifications for RTFs in use, numbered 1, 2, 3, and 5.
RTF Orientation and Dip Switch Settings
To perform correctly, RTFs must be installed in the correct orientation, per the Panther Service Manual for Real Time Assays.
WARNING! The RTFs cannot be interchanged by readdressing the DIP switches!
Installation Issues and Common Errors for RTFs
Unable to Complete Instrument Setup or RTF Failure
- Check RTF1 LED – LED should blink at one-second intervals after initial power on. If one RTF in the chain is bad, subsequent RTFs after will not be lit, or will have a solid light.
- Check DIP switches on all RTFs.
- Check RTF cable – swap RTF1 position, or move cable to connector over.
Alignment Curve is Wavy or bumpy
- Check: carousel bearings, magnets, motor belt tension.
- MTU carriers in MTU are not loose.
FLSOR or Nominal ranges out of specification
-
Firmware issue – search for FLSOR in this guide.
-
Possible debris or dirty lens – clean RTFs.
- Without removing the incubator, remove Amp incubator’s shield, located underneath the incubator.
- Remove RTF X.  Important: Carefully remove the RTF from the instrument – from underneath – so you do not dislodge any dirt or debris from RTF, and carefully inspect it. Follow all procedures in Panther Service Manual.
- Check lens for debris - if you find debris, confirm what it is: glove, foam from incubator, dust, and the like.
- Clean lens, then run SSW check again.
- If you find no debris, shake the RTF lightly, and listen carefully for rattling. Replace RTF if you hear a rattling sound.
- Replace RTF if you find nothing apparent, or if issue continues after cleaning.
PQ fails with ebl flags on Calibrators
-
ROX and HEX RTFs in the wrong position.
Review RTF curves.
-
Wrong RTF shipped.
Verify Serial Number on RTF matches label on box.

## Linear Distributor: Sample Dispense Slot Errors       after Fusion Upgrade
id="mc-main-content">
Linear Distributor: Sample Dispense Slot Errors after Fusion Upgrade
Symptoms:
After a Fusion Upgrade, Linear Distributor OQ fails at Sample Dispense slots 2 and 3. Theta position of the Linear Distributor at slot 1 is correct, but at slots 2 and 3 are 90 degrees off.
Note: this only applies to a Fusion.
Solution:
First set the LD Authorization Code.
Then, redo Theta calculation:
- Click Distributor Tab.
- Click Teach Tab.
- Select Theta.
- Select Home Offset.
- Select Move All in the “Move Axis” section.
- Select Get All in the “Get Stored Teach Pos ” section.
- Select Get All in the “Get Current Position” section.
- Select Save All in the “Save Current Axis Position” section.
- Overwrite NVM.
- Select yes, when asked if you would like to set all other positions.

## Vacuum Duty Cycle Too Low (Quad)
id="mc-main-content">
Vacuum Duty Cycle Too Low (Quad)
Problem:
Vacuum pressure operating at higher end of range but vacuum would intermittently shut off.
Isolation:
Check if vacuum duty cycle in SSW lower than 50%, this can cause vacuum to cut out.
Service manual search:
Ported Vacuum Manifold Cover
Resolution:
Vacuum speed control is determined by flow rate using two threaded ports on vacuum manifold cover. In this case, the ports were not tapped through.
- Add or remove screws.
- If not screws are present, verify the ports are tapped through.
- Left and right ports are not the same size.

Complaint Description
Mixer motor did not reach the initialization sensor within the maximum allowed number of steps. For example: 73 21 03 02 72.
05/04/2022 03:56:24 (03 20:56:24)    [D] (Fatal       , High  ) [AmpLoadStation] Mixer motor did not reach the initialization sensor within the maximum allowed number of steps ID=9598 LoadStationMix 'Amp Mix' (Amplification) PlannedStart=03:55:56.287: , start=03:55:56.287 end=03:56:24.487 (MTU=10 BarcodeID=2184243609, samples=77640/68628/Normal, 77641/68629/Normal, 77650/68630/Normal, 77651/68631/Normal, , cmd params: AmpLoadStation  ). Event [0x72.0x02.0x0072] at 03:56:24.387 bytes:  72 21 03 02 72  [114.002.00114]
Resolution
Check for these problems on all three load stations and Mixers:
-
Half seated or not very well seated connectors?
-
Excessive grease on pulley, or on the sensor.
Image below shows excessive grease:
-
Also, check to see if the cables are under the strain relief:
Left image shows excessive grease, but correctly routed cables. Right image shows cables incorrectly routed outside of the strain relief.
Load Station Mixer Home Pin Issue
Image shows home pin touching sensor; the pin should pass in the middle of the sensor.
The lower image shows the pin is too short. Load station should be replaced.
Images below indicate a properly manufactured Load station. The pin passes through the middle of the sensor. The pin is the correct length.
Load Station Mixer Pulley Issue
Check for a loose Mixer pulley.
Replace the load station if a loose pulley is discovered.

## Invalid Kinetic Index
id="mc-main-content">
Invalid Kinetic Index
Error Code
None.
Table of Contents
Complaint Description
Technical Support
- Review Logs to Find the Kinetic Index
- KI is High
- KI is Low
- Next Steps
Field Service
- KI Issues Seen by FSE
- Resolution
Complaint Description
The Kinetic Index (KI) is the normalization factor determined for each run based upon the performance of the calibrators, to normalize flasher and glower signal to the ideal master curve.
Technical Support
- Kinetic Index is only used in the HPV and HPV GT assays.
- Request logs for a couple of HPV or HPV GT runs to review if KI is trending low or high.
Review Logs to Find the Kinetic Index
-
Open the Results Report, and find the date and time for the last calibrator.
-
In NotePad++, open the log_PantherMain file with a date/time at the same time or after the last calibrator.
-
Search the file for Kinetic Index .
-
See if the Kinetic Index is in the correct range for the assay:
- HPV: 0.85 – 1.30
- HPV GT: 0.85 – 1.55
KI is High
Check if the lab temperature is approaching 30C.
Check the temperature where the AD bottles are stored. If the bottles are warm, it can cause the KI to be high.
Review logs for luminometer curves to see if there are issues with the AD dispense.
Refer to AD1 and AD2 – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves .
KI is Low
Check if the lab temperature is <15C.
Check the temperature where the AD bottles are stored. If the bottles are cold, it can cause the KI to be low.
Instruct customer to check the AD bottles, caps, and connectors in the Universal Fluids Drawer.
Review logs for luminometer curves to see if there are issues with the AD dispense.
Refer to AD1 and AD2 – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves .
Next Steps
Review case history for previous KI errors. Notify FSE if there were recent cases.
Instruct customer to monitor and upload logs again if runs keep failing.
Field Service
KI Issues Seen by FSE
Looks like a micro fracture or leak in the AD2 LCMP.
Zoomed in a lot on the OLV, and all the delayed light offs correspond with the injection.
Have not looked into OLV acquisition rate vs. luminometer acquisition rate yet.
There is a slight leak: see blue line on first dispense immediately after priming.
Which corresponds to:
Resolution
The fittings need to be snug. Tighten them down more.
Any pullback >2600 should be reviewed by TSE Technical Service Engineer. .

Complaint Description
Luminometer Unknown Command
Technical Support
TBD
Field Support
2021-03-17
11:33:20,589
[MsgHandler]
EventLogMessenger
EventLogEntry
Error
(Fatal) 16:33:20.983: Luminometer error (Unknown Command) (Ev=02) [40.00.02] bytes: 40 DB 03 00 02
2021-03-17
11:33:20,592
[MsgHandler]
EventLogger
EventLogEntry
Error
3/17/2021 4:33:20 PM (17 11:33:20) [E] (Fatal, High) [Luminometer] Luminometer error (Unknown Command) (ErrorStatusReportCOP), at 16:33:20.983 [0x40.0x00.0x0002] [064.000.00002]
This error is almost never actually due to the Luminometer, rather a command execution timeout by another module. Need to look through the logs for a different fatal error (sometimes the fatal error will show up around the Luminometer Unknown Command error) Probably the easiest way is to open ViewLog, find the Luminometer error in the EventLogEntries Tab, then double-click to get to the Log Tab. In the Log Tab, Sort by Error Level. This will bring all of the Fatal (red) Errors to the top, and you should be able to find the error forcing the Luminometer Unknown Command error.
In this example:
-
ViewLog > EventLogEntries Tab: “Instrument reported a fatal timeout” occurs at same timestamp “00:16:58,375” as “Luminomer error (Unknown Command)”.
-
Clicking on the error, jumps back to the “ViewLog > Log” tab and identifies “MoveMTU” is a Linear Distributor command and is the command that has command execution timeout error.
-
Command execution timeout errors are most often associated with damaged CAN bus flex cables, CAN bus cables that are not plugged in or damaged PCB.
-
For this example:
- Inspect and reseat CAN bus cable at COP and Module side.
- Inspect PCB for damage
- Inspect flex cable for damage (dents in the cable trace). Replacing Linear Distributor x and theta flex cables will usually resolve this error as the flex cables are easily damaged.
Errors that have been known to cause this (others are possible)
-
LD

OR

-
RFID

## FlashCheck Evaluation
id="mc-main-content">
FlashCheck Evaluation
FlashCheck (FC) is simply a diagnostic tool used to help determine the efficacy of AutoDetect (AD) delivery and Injection, which produces the light-off in amplified reactions, as measured by the Luminometer. FC was created to mimic the performance of an amplified reaction without having to perform all the steps of the amplification process.
While there are many factors that can contribute to FlashCheck failures, any of the failures modes listed below can and most likely will be influenced by poor Lumo Injector performance, and in some cases, poor AD Pump(s) performance.
Error Modes
-
Interval 25 (I25) Failures (Most Common)
-
Interval 3 (I3) Failures
-
Outliers
-
A-Time Failures (Least Common)
Acceptance Criteria
The table below illustrates acceptance criteria for systems running HPV & non-HPV systems:
HPV
AC2 (non HPV)
Parvo/HAV
Rule of Thumb
I3 Average
≥ 0.16
≥ 0.0050
≥ 0.10
The higher, the
better
I25 Average
N/A
<= 0.0014
<= 0.0014
The lower, the
better
I25 %CV
→
→
→
The lower, the
better
Individual I25
<= 0.0014
<= 0.0010
<= 0.0010
The lower, the
better
Reference Material
Panther Dashboard auto-analyzes FC data for Pass/Fail criteria. However, it may not provide subtle details that could help identify underlying issues prior to becoming bigger problems later, which could potentially contribute to poor assay or system performance. This TSG entry assumes use of the FlashCheck Analysis Spreadsheet to analyze Panther FC data.
In HUB, go to Content > Panther (Service) > TBs (Panther) > Flashcheck/Syscheck for latest versions of:
- TB-01298: Instructions for utilizing the FlashCheck Analysis Spreadsheet to Analyze Panther FC Data.
- FlashCheck_Analysis_Spreadsheet vX.XX
Technical Support
NA
Field Service
Systematic Approach to Troubleshooting
- Perform Pre-Service System Inspection (see below).
- Perform Luminometer CAL Factor & OLV Trace inspection (see below).
- Perform pre-service baseline FlashCheck (save all FC data for comparisons).
- Address potential contributors to failing or borderline criteria:
- Flush/replace injectors…
- Swap/replace AD pumps…
- Etc….
- Repeat FlashCheck and compare data, looking for improvement.
Note— Try to label parts swapped between FC attempts in case those parts need to be reinstalled to achieve better results. Example, if original injectors (or a pump) are removed after baseline FC, label them “FC1”, and so on….
Pre-Service System Inspection
- Inspect potential points of air ingress along fluidic paths:
- Inspect AD bottle caps & fittings for cracks.
- Clean AD bottle caps & fittings with DI water, then shake/blot dry.
- Ensure fittings along fluidic path are snug (do NOT over-tighten, you will crack them!): AD bottle fittings > A/B switching solenoids > AD pump(s) inlet/outlet ports.
- Ensure the AD1 & AD2 lines are properly routed:
- From bottles to correct A/B Switching Solenoid/inlet ports.
- From correct A/B Switching Solenoid outlet ports to correct LCMP/inlet ports.
- From correct LCMP outlet ports to correct lines on Lumo Injectors (they are specific!)
Luminometer CAL Factor & OLV Trace Inspection
-
In Service Software, verify Luminometer CAL Factor.
If CAL Factor = 1.0, perform Syscheck to re-calibrate Luminometer CAL Factor.
-
In System Software, “Force Full Prime” to recalibrate Luminometer OLV.
-
Zip logs and inspect the ProcessControlData_Luminometerxxx.curve file.
-
Address any observable issues prior to performing Pre-Service Baseline FlashCheck
Luminometer OLV Trace Examples
FlashCheck – What To Look For: (More than Pass/Fail Criteria!)
- Lumo OLV Traces : Re-inspect for abnormalities between each FC attempt. If observed, address potential contributors prior to subsequent FC attempts.
- Raw Light-off Data: Inspect the first several rows of raw data for zeros/eight/low values into/past 3rd & 4th Raw Data intervals: (Front End Delay)
-
Kinetics/Curves for Each MTU: Inspect for
- Front End Delay…
- Jagged Leading Edges…
- Peak Amplitude / Dips…
- Double Humps on Trailing Edges…
- Poor Signal Decay at Interval 25 (I25)

10071 2021-02-02 11:07:46,199|[RS232Ctrl]|InstrumentCommObject|InstrumentEvent|Info|Normal|IMTUs: pos 87 status 1:MTU_EMPTY module Incubator3 i: 17
2021-02-02 11:07:46,200|[RS232Ctrl]|InstrumentCommObject|InstrumentEvent|Info|Normal|IMTUs: pos 88 status 1:MTU_EMPTY module Incubator3 i: 18
Resolution
Inspect incubator carefully:
- Debris
- Carousel, belt, teeth, mtu slots
- Sensor not calibrated
- Dirty sensor
- Misaligned sensor
- Damaged sensor
Panther Case Study – MTU Unload Unsuccessful. Instrument 01217, 2016.12.08.
Health Report shows:
“MTU Unload unsuccessful. Could not unload one position. Please run Force MTU Unload.”
Followed by:
“No MTU was detected, unloading of MTUs is completed.”
Health Report Screen Shot:
Background on how the instrument works:
When the instrument starts up, there is an MTU count. How this happens is the LD checks all of the slots, except the incubators. For the MTU check in the incubators, each incubator does a “check all slots” command (incubator command 54). This is how the instrument knows if there are any MTUs to unload.
What is happening on this Instrument:
What can happen is that the incubator MTU sensor gets dirty (or malfunctions), and the sensor sees an MTU when there isn’t actually one there. So, the incubator “tells” the Distributor there is an MTU to unload, and the Distributor goes to get it, but there isn’t actually an MTU, so the “MTU Unload Unsuccessful” error happens.
To find which incubator is faulty, you search the low level logs for the following strings:
Search String
Description
COP -> PC 20 54
HT Incubator Check all Slots Response
COP -> PC 21 54
Trans Incubator Check all Slots Response
COP -> PC 22 54
Amp Incubator Check all Slots Response
In this case, the Transition Incubator is the one sensing the Phantom MTU. Search Result:
2016-12-07 04:41:24,827|[StSerClient:COP->PC]|RS232Ctrl|RS232Communication|Info|Normal|COP->PC 21 54 00 02 00 00 08 00 00 .
If there are no MTUs present, then the last 4 bytes (highlighted in yellow) should be zeros. In this case, the last 4 bytes are 00 08 00 00. To see where the MTU is being sensed, you have to invert the bytes and convert from hex to binary:
- Invert: 00 08 00 00 inverts to 00 00 08 00.
- Remove the leading zeros and concatenate: 00 00 08 00 -> 800hex.
- Convert to Binary: 800hex = 100000000000 bin.
- Slots are counted right to left. So, the incubator is sensing an mtu in slot 12.
Service Plan
To service, first, always verify that there truly is not an MTU in the incubator slot. Also verify the Distributor teaching to the suspect incubator is good.
From there, check / replace the Incubator internal PCB (p/n 902789), which has the MTU sensor on it. (Part should be in trunk stock.)

Initialize mixer, aspirate, magnet drive.

## Magnetic Wash Tiplet Eject Unsuccessful
id="mc-main-content">
Magnetic Wash Tiplet Eject Unsuccessful
Error Codes
Dec
Hex
Arm
048.000.00034
0x30.0x00.0x0022
Magwash 1
049.000.00034
0x31.0x00.0x0022
Magwash 2
Complaint Description
[Fatal] Switched to error state as MagWash tip ejection could not be completed.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
Field Service
Technical Support
N/A
Field Service
[Fatal] Switched to error state as MagWash tip ejection could not be completed.
Possible root causes in order of likelihood:
-
An open circuit between an aspirator and the liquid level sense PCB.
-
A short/ground between an aspirator and the Magwash chassis.
-
A problem or defect with the liquid level sense PCB or ribbon cable.
-
A mechanical fault preventing the actual stripping of tiplets.
Troubleshooting steps:
-
Check that all aspirators are screwed tight onto the liquid level sense PCB so there is a good electrical connection.
-
Check that there is no debris between the aspirators and the liquid level sense PCB.
Debris such as broken pieces of the rubber o-ring can interrupt the signal from the aspirator to the PCB.
-
Check that there is not debris or liquid on the liquid level sense PCB. Clean the PCB and check for leaks at the connection between the tubing and the aspirators.
-
Check that the aspirators are clean and dry.
Events such as a fully clogged Magwash or a misaligned Wash injector, may wet the aspirators. Liquid on the aspirators will wick onto the chassis and ground the aspirators. If this event occurred after a clogging event, remove the aspirators, and ensure they are clean and dry.
-
In Service Software, inject fluid into all tubes of the MTU – remove the MTU and observe if there is stray wash solution splattered toward the top of the MTU. Check to see if there is any wash solution anywhere outside of the MTU.
-
Check the ribbon cable is undamaged and secured.
-
In Service Software, check that the movement of all motors is proper.
It is unusual for the module to fail to strip tiplets. But a sign that this may actually be the case is if the error happened in the middle of assay processing (as opposed to during instrument startup or prime), and with the absence of any ML2 clogging errors.

## Blue Screen
id="mc-main-content">
Blue Screen
Complaint Description:
Panther instrument freezes and presents Blue Screen.
If you are contacted regarding a Blue Screen failure, please perform or obtain the following:
- Ask the customer or service member to allow the memory dump to complete. This will be indicated by a numeric progress notification on the Blue Screen itself. If, after 10 minutes, no progress is observed, the PC can be rebooted.
- Inside the C:\Windows directory, obtain any MEMORY.DMP files that are present. They will be up to 16GB in size.
- Inside the C:\Windows\Minidump directory, obtain any other files with a .dmp extension.
- Obtain Panther logs.
- Obtain the Application and System categories of the Windows Event Logs.*
Gathering Windows Event Logs
- Open the Command Prompt.
- Type eventvwr and press Enter.
- Expand Windows Logs (left pane).
- Click Application, Security, Setup, System, or Forwarded Events depending on request.
- Click Save All Events As… (right pane).
- Name the file and save it to a directory you can access via PRO360 (or flash drive for FSE Field Service Engineer. ).
TSE Technical Service Engineer. Review Example:
Will need some details filled in.
-
The blue screen error shows: silabser.sys driver being the issue.
-
Blue screen image time stamp sample: is this accurate 9/9/21 7:41:08 am local time?
-
As …txt.122 ends abruptly appear power loss related.
-
This appears to be a power loss issue.
Check power cables at UPS/PC.
-
Appears issue is resolved with another PC restart, and is okay now?

## Panther PC Will Not Boot
id="mc-main-content">
Panther PC Will Not Boot
Error Code
Dec
Hex
N/A
N/A
Complaint Description
XE3 Blinking Power Button
Issue: When both instrument and PC are powered down: if the instrument is powered on before the PC, then PC will enter an error state.
Symptom:  Some Fusions with software version 7.1.5 on XE3 will not boot after shutdown.  The workstation power button LED will blink in 2-1 pattern.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
Technical Support
Clearing the error
-
Power down instrument.
-
At the UPS, identify and clearly label power cord for PC.
-
Unplug PC power cord at UPS.
-
Press and hold PC power button for three seconds to discharge.
-
Plug PC power back in.
-
Power on PC, then power on the instrument.
Workaround: When both instrument and PC are off, always turn on PC first.
Field Service
Issue
When both instrument and PC are powered down; if the instrument is powered on before the PC, then PC will enter an error state.
To clear the PC error state, the instrument needs to be powered down.  Unplug PC, press PC power button to discharge.  Plug PC back in.
Resolution
Clearing the error
-
Power down instrument.
-
At the UPS, identify and clearly label power cord for PC.
-
Unplug PC power cord at UPS.
-
Press and hold PC power button for three seconds to discharge.
-
Plug PC power back in.
-
Power on PC, then power on the instrument.

USB/Ethernet board has been identified as a root cause. When unplugging from the PC, then powering, allowed the PC to boot.
-
The other root cause has been an improper seating of the power cable into the PC. After unplugging and firmly seating the power cable, the XE3 was able to boot.
-
In general, a good troubleshooting approach would be to unplug connections in the PC that are not required for the PC to boot. For example, I generally unplug the breakout boards and CD/DVD drive leaving only the connection to the hard drive. Then try to boot. Plug one in at a time until the amber light shows.

If done correctly, Windows login screen opens.  User password is gpservice .

## Workstation Issues
id="mc-main-content">
Workstation Issues
Symptom:
Date and Time resets after each restart of the Panther PC
- Possible Root Cause:
- USB drive was inserted upside down into the USB hub board. That used slot/port short circuits the BIOS system on the Panther PC during boot up. The shorting of the BIOSWhich causes a reset of the date & time.
- Troubleshooting Procedure:
- Inspect at the external USB hub board . Green circle shows the correct orientation of the USB port, whereas the red circle shows an incorrect orientation of the USB ports.
- Determine which USB cable belongs to the USB hub board.
- Boot-up the Panther and login to the FSE Field Service Engineer. shield.
- Open Windows Explorer
- Go to Computer
- Plug in a USB drive into a working slot on the USB hub and check that it appears in Windows Explorer.
- Unplug each USB cable from the back of the computer (one by one) until the cable that was removed causes the USB drive to disappear from Windows Explorer.
- Reset the date and time. See Panther Service Manual for instructions.
- Plug in all USB cables except the USB cable for the hub board.
- Restart the computer.
- If the date and time does not reset, you have found the root cause.
- Replace the USB hub board.
Symptom:
Warning Message: " Monitor Out of Range"
- Reason Behind the Message:
-
The monitor out of range is raised when the graphics card has a higher resolution set or than what the monitor can support or an unsupported refresh rate. This can be because the cables, the power to the monitor, or a different monitor with higher resolution was plugged in, the OS bumped up the resolution then the monitor was switched back.
- Possible Root Cause:
- Very long video cable
-
Movements of the cables, can also lead to such issue.
- Monitor power supply
-
Not enough power may lead to strange side effects or resolutions.
- Troubleshooting Procedure:
-
I disconnected the VGA cable and re-inserted.
-
Perform the PC maintenance. Sequence of operations are:
-
Click on "Task, Perform maintenance"
-
Select weekly "PC maintenance".
-
Press "Start" button, and then press "Start" button to begin PC shut down. PC shuts down and automatically restarts to Shield screen.
-
Select Panther icon and GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. starts.
-
Screen should be okay, with no resolution problems.
-

## COP Pipettor State Error – Unable to Execute Command
id="mc-main-content">
COP Pipettor State Error – Unable to Execute Command
Error Code
Dec
Hex
005.001.00014
0x05.0x01.0x000E
Complaint Description
<>(Fatal) COP Pipettor state error (Unable to execute command). Event [0x05.0x01.0x000E]; [005.001.00014] 01 bytes: 05 20 03 0E FD D5 03 00 2E
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
Field Service
-
Incorrect Teaching to the Tip Eject Location
-
Faulty Pipettor Main PCB
-
Faulty Pipettor
-
Low Level Command Translation
Technical Support
Have the customer shut down. While the instrument is turned off, have the customer look to see if a tip is still attached to either pipettor. If there is still a tip present, carefully remove the tip and attempt to restart the instrument.
Field Service
Notes: This error can have multiple causes. It can help to look at the low-level error command to narrow down the root cause. Example:
<>(Fatal) 13:39:27.358: COP Pipettor state error (Unable to execute command). Event [0x05.0x01.0x000E] bytes: 05 20 03 01 0E FD D5 03 00 2E 01 24 00
The bit highlighted in blue above is the quickest way to determine which pipettor is erroring.
-
0x01 = left arm
-
0x02 = right arm
-
0x03 = both arms
Scroll to the bottom of this entry for more information on translating the above code.
Incorrect Teaching to the Tip Eject Location
Resolution
Panther 03633 2021.06.16
Panther 02932 2021.06.01 case 00865201
Logs show the following error (pipettor is failing initialization):
2021-06-17
10:40:08,817
[MA]
EventLogEntry
Error
<>(Fatal) 17:40:02.142: COP
Pipettor state error (Unable to execute command). Event [0x05.0x01.0x000E]
bytes:  05 20 03 01 0E FD D6 03 00 2F 02 24 00
D6 refers to the Sample pipettor , and 2F is your error code (which is not in the MDD).
We just saw this at another site in Texas. The FSE Field Service Engineer.  found the X and Y Flex cables had metal leads exposed. He replaced those cables, and still had to replace the pipettor.
So, this is my suggestion: Go through all of the flex cables for the pipettor (focusing especially on the Sample Pipettor), and look for exposed wiring. If you find broken flex cables, take some pictures.
Look first for places the flex cables are not well secured. Those would be the most likely locations for the flex cables to flap around or rub. Once you find the bad flex cable(s), replace. Then try to initialize the pipettors. If the pipettor(s) do not initialize, replace.
Here are the relevant part numbers. I would also order a pipettor and the PCBs listed, with the hope that you won’t actually need them. (I tend to over-order, then send back what I do not need.):
MEL-00790 PIPETTOR, REAGANT/SAMPLE, X-AXIS FLEXCABLE
902760 PIPETTOR, Y-AXIS FLEX CABLE
902758 PIPETTOR, SAMPLE, Z-AXIS FLEX CABLE
902796 PIPETTOR, X-SLEDGE PCB
902798 PIPETTOR, Y-SLEDGE PCB
MME-02171 PIPETTOR, MAIN PCB
(R)MME--03784 PIPETTOR, SAMPLE ASSY (RIGHT) BLDC. Or APP (R )903233
902770 COP, FUSE KIT
Faulty Pipettor Main PCB
Resolution
If the pipettor does not move at all during initialization, it may be a faulty Pipettor Main PCB.
Replace PCB
Faulty Pipettor
Resolution
Replace Pipettor.
Low Level Command Translation
Code Example:
<>(Fatal) 13:39:27.358: COP Pipettor state error (Unable to execute command). Event [0x05.0x01.0x000E] bytes: 05 20 03 01 0E FD D5 03 00 2E 01 24 00
COMGEN
-
05 – Cop Virtual Device Driver
-
20
-
03 – Fatal
-
01 – Cop Main
-
0E – Cop Error (Command Not Implemented) command execution error
The String now converts over to the Pipettor:
-
FD – Pipettor
-
D5 / D6 Diluter pump command, String type, or
7E/7F DiTi pickup / eject
-
03 – Fatal
-
00 –
-
2E – Left arm / 2D – Right arm (ZS6319 pump error on non-string type command )
-
01 – Left arm / 02 – Right arm

Complaint Description
- Reagent Pipettor error (pump move cancelled due to overpressure detection) – PFR flag
- Sample Pipettor error (pump move cancelled due to overpressure detection) – PFS flag
Technical Support
Sample Pipettor Error – pump move cancelled due to overpressure detection – associated with PFS flags
- Likely the sample shield is not seated properly. Advise to replace shield.
- Likely sample issue: viscous/mucoidal/precipitates/cotton pile.
- If there are many PFS in a row. Graph aspiration/dispense curves and compare to controls.
Sample Pipettor Error – pump move cancelled due to overpressure detection – during MW cleaning
- Likely the sample shield is not seated properly. Advise to replace shield and repeat MW cleaning.
Reagent Pipettor Error – pump move cancelled due to overpressure detection – associated with PFR flags
- Ask which tips customer is using. This could be a tip issue (e.g.,Tecan tips, PN 30180117 issue 2021 – CTB-00842).
- If tip issue, customer can continue to run.
- If not tip issue, notify FSE Field Service Engineer. .
- Prime or MW cleaning: do not test the reagent pipettor so it is risky to keep running. Likely service will be needed.
Field Service
Sample Pipettor error (pump move canceled due to overpressure detection) ID=14830 PipettorDispense 'Add TCR' (TCR) PlannedStart=23:43:18.121 worst event at 23:43:46.221, start=23:43:44.921 end=23:43:48.421 (MTU=34 BarcodeID=2026600884, samples=[0] , [1] 14051/LY00209, [2] , [3] , [4] , , cmd params: TCR (SP) Index=25 finalZ=4609, vol=117, track=70, fluid=33030 ) [0x00.0x0F.0x009F] [000.015.00159]
11/4/2021 11:43:48 PM (05 07:43:48) [D] (Warning , Low ) [TestOrderManagement] PFT flag assigned to SID LY00208 for HPV assay in lane 1 position 6. [261.000.00004]
MTU ending in …884, triggered overpressure.
Aspiration pressure for …884,
TCR aspiration is usually not smooth like the other reagents.
TCR is suspension of magnetic beads which can clump together.
The aspiration can also be affected by tip damage, variation.
C-LLD traces from 10/19 – 11/16:
-
First measurement is always lower red arrow.
-
GT HPV trace doesn’t follow HPV trace.
-
Both of these issues suggest an alignment related issue.
-
Incorrect tcr teach tool ( I think this is the issue)
-
Something going on with tcr cup/tcr module
Sample dispense, looks mucoidal, so could drag on sample shield.
Resolution:
Evaluation 1
TCR bottle Cuff, sample pipettor/tcr teaching, or tcr carousel can be improved.
Evaluation 2
Hardware Failing
Example of noise during aspiration, indicating the plunger motor is wearing out. In this instance, it should not affect assay processing results.
Evaluation 3
Logs show: PFR flags
03/09/2023 20:17:36 Warning 000.014.00159 Reagent Pipettor error (pump move canceled due to overpressure detection)
Some things to check:
Make sure the new cLLD washers are installed properly, and gold leads are clean.
Perform a cLLD test on the Reagent pipettor as a baseline to any position other than the Elution Track. If good, proceed with the following:
Check teaching of the Reagent Pipettor to the Elution Track – make sure the tip is centered in the pack. If necessary, teach manually.
If initial cLLD test is bad – replace Reagent Pipettor.

## Teaching Error – More Than 1mm Deviation Between Left and Right Arm in x Direction
id="mc-main-content">
Teaching Error – More Than 1mm Deviation Between Left and Right Arm in x Direction
Complaint
During Pipettor teaching to the Tip drawers, "More than 1mm deviation (11 steps) between left and right arm in x-direction!)"
Note – The allowed deviation in X-Direction is 1mm (0.9mm/step) = 10steps
Resolution
Could be a difference in teaching at the reference position. If the pipettors have already been taught to the reference position automatically, have them instead teach manually. Then try again.

## Teaching Error – Travel Height of Pipettor Must Be Greater Than the Longest Tip
id="mc-main-content">
Teaching Error – Travel Height of Pipettor Must Be Greater Than the Longest Tip
The distance from pipettor z-home to reference point should be at least 1649 steps.
Instrument does not calculate enough distance between z-home and reference point.
This can happen if:
- Z-home sensor is set incorrectly at factory.
- Excessive friction, teaching sw detects hard stop location early.
Resolution:
- Adjust the z-home sensor up.
- Z-motor/pipettor meshing.
- Clean pipettor surfaces that contact bearings.
- Replace white bearings "L" and "V" shaped.
- Inspect z-motor by unplugging and check winding resistance by hand (compare with another pipettor).
- Initialize after making sensor adjustment, and before re-attempting auto-teach.

## Pipettor Fails Pressure Integrity Test
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor Fails Pressure Integrity Test
Pressure Integrity Test – Service Software
Issue: Pipettor fails Pressure Integrity Test.
Root cause 1: Pin hole in teach cap – some have pin holes.
Resolution 1: Replace teach cap.
Root cause 2: Check DITI assembly: knurled nut is tight – both o-rings and DITI surface and inside are free of debris.
Note: Do not remove bottom o-ring seal.
Resolution 2: Remove debris.

## Biorear Double Filter
id="mc-main-content">
Biorear Double Filter
Issue: Biorear – Quaero - Two filters in tip-potential lots affected: L20201102, M20210103, H20210116.
Isolation: Inspect TCR/FCR dispense curves, as issue may be missed by examining aspiration pressure. More FCR is used than TCR, so it takes three aspiration trips to dispense the total volume.
Dispense pressure: Double filter elevates dispense pressures during final volume transfer.
Dark lines in plots below show elevated pressures as filter gets wet.
Aspiration pressure: First aspiration starting pressure is higher – no fluid in tip yet – and takes longer to complete, as it pulls dead volume. Second and third should have similar profiles, as the volumes are identical. As second and third pressure profiles are nearly identical, this indicates filter has not been wetted at this point.
Corrective action: Do not replace pipettor. Open complaint, if not already open. Record and quarantine tip lots being used – including partial trays. R&D will likely want tips back.

## Tecan *117 Tips
id="mc-main-content">
Tecan *117 Tips
Tecan *117 Tips cause pressure issues, not LLD issues.
Example of TCR dispense with Tecan *117 Tips:
RVHO-fusion:
The oil tracks correctly, measures too low (incorrectly), and then tracks correctly (but is now too high).
Now SW thinks it should be lower and cannot recover.
Run 1: 12/24 - too low, then too high:
RDFP:
Tecan *117 Tips with bLLD Assay SW
Resolution: this appears to be tip related. Since the SW is still on the bLLD level sense, it is behaving much like the pipettor in the Fusion side for Oil.
Basically, the filter density is higher. This causes the slow response, resulting in lower volume detected. The inventory adjusts lower. Then a normal tip measures the correct height, which is higher than the previous level sense. At this point, the kit is invalidated.
This evidence for the increased resistance to flow can also be seen in the Aspiration and Dispense Graphs:
If instrument runs SW 5.2, no Alt Tips SW is available. Upgrade to SW 7.2 as soon as possible.

## Printer – Not Available or Offline
id="mc-main-content">
Printer – Not Available or Offline
Error message: 406.001.00010 Printer HP Officejet Pro 6230 (Copy 2) is not installed.
Printer is not available. Please Check Printer.
Printer is Offline.
A test page from the printer works, but printing from Panther Main does not.
SW 6.2 and above. FSE Field Service Engineer. had accidently loaded the printer driver.
Option 1:
Delete the Drivers while Panther GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. is running.
-
Ensure Panther is not Assay Processing.
-
Disconnect USB cable that connects printer to the Panther CPU.
Note: Disconnecting either side of the cable will work, but disconnecting from the printer side may be more accessible.
-
Plug in the keyboard.
-
Select Help, then press the Print icon.
A new window will appear with available printers listed. Verify that multiple printers are available: for example, HP Officejet Pro 6230, and HP Officejet Pro 6230 (Copy 1).
-
Using the keyboard trackpad, right-click on HP Officejet Pro 6230, then select Delete.
-
Repeat the same procedure for the remaining printer, HP Officejet Pro 6230 (Copy 1).
-
Reconnect the USB cable from Printer to Panther CPU. The Panther should automatically recognize the printer, and name it HP Officejet Pro 6230.
-
Click Apply, then close the window by clicking the X in the upper right-hand corner.
-
Under the Admin menu, select System Configuration.
-
Scroll to the bottom, and expand the Printer Management drop-down.
-
Select the Default Printer Name text field and in the pop-up window.
Ensure there is only one printer available, and that printer is named HP Officejet Pro 6230. It should have a green check mark next to it, indicating that it is selected as the default printer.
-
Select OK in the pop-up window, then select Save at the bottom of the System Configuration page.
-
Test printer operation by printing any report.
Option 2:
-
Disconnect the printer from the computer.
-
Log into the FSE Shield.
-
Use the command prompt, and type printmanagement.msc.
-
Select the folder All Drivers .
-
Highlight all Drivers under Driver Name at the right.
-
Select Red X in the toolbar to delete all Drivers.
-
Restart the computer and the Panther GUI.
-
Plug in the printer.
-
Select the correct printer in Panther GUI > Admin > Configuration.

## New or Spare Deactivation Pump Rotates in Wrong Direction
id="mc-main-content">
New or Spare Deactivation Pump Rotates in Wrong Direction
Deactivation pump is also known as the peristaltic pump, or peripump.
Error Code:
Dec
Hex
n/a
n/a
Complaint Description:
New or spare peripump spins in wrong direction. Peripump should spin counter-clockwise after instrument setup is completed.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Check Parameter in Service Software
- Check Peripump PCB to Pump Motor Wiring
Technical Support
Not applicable, as this fault should be observed only by FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
Check Parameter in Service Software
In service software, check device 0x52, parameter 38 = 0 (counter-clockwise).
Resolution:
If value is set to 1, run instrument setup.
Test:
Check parameter value 38 = 0. Unclamp and remove tubing from peripump/DQ pump. Start pump and observe motor spins counter-clockwise. Stop pump, reassemble and prime instrument.
Check Peripump PCB to Pump Motor Wiring
Photograph below shows correctly wired pump motor: yellow, red, blue, and orange wires in order at the peripump PCB at the top, and at the pump motor.
Correctly wired connection from peripump PCB to pump motor.
Photograph below shows incorrectly wired pump motor. Red, yellow, red, blue, and orange wires in are out of order at the peripump PCB at the top. Correct order is yellow, red, blue, and orange, as shown at the pump motor on the bottom.
Incorrect wiring: red and yellow wires crossed at peripump PCB on top.
Resolution:
Option 1: Crossed wires at PCB connector can be rewired.
Option 2: Order new peripump/DQ pump.
Test:
Start pump and observe motor spins counter-clockwise. Stop pump, reassemble and prime instrument.

## Deactivation Pump Voltage Out of Range
id="mc-main-content">
Deactivation Pump Voltage Out of Range
Error Code
Dec
Hex
082.000.00006
Complaint Description
Deactivation Pump voltage is out of range.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- CAN Bus Cable
- Check Fuses
- Pump Monitor PCB
- Faulty Pump
Technical Support
Possible root cause:
- CAN Bus cable
- Damaged fuse
- Pump Monitor PCB
- Faulty pump
Technical support troubleshooting: obtain logs to review.
Field Service
CAN Bus Cable
Resolution:
Unplug and reseat cable.
Test:
Launch Service Software.
Initialize peristaltic pump, or output queue module.
Read voltage.
Check Fuses
Check glass fuse behind metal plate, and smaller fuse below corresponding pump monitor CAN bus connector.
Resolution:
Replace the fuse.
Test:
Launch Service Software.
Initialize peristaltic pump or output queue module.
Read voltage.
Pump Monitor PCB
Initialize pumps. Magwash and AD1 pump are on same rail. Peristaltic pump, AD2 and oil pumps share same rail.
Resolution:
Replace PCB.
Test:
- Launch Service Software.
- Initialize pumps.
- Read voltage.
Faulty Pump
Initialize pumps. Magwash and AD1 pump are on same rail. Peristaltic pump, AD2 pump, and oil pumps share same rail. If all pumps on same rail do not initialize, move pump connections around to test other pumps. Identify faulty pump.
Resolution:
Replace the faulty pump.
Test:
- Launch Service Software.
- Initialize pumps.
- Read voltage.

## RTF Error  –  Unable to Complete Instrument Setup or RTF Failure
id="mc-main-content">
RTF Error – Unable to Complete Instrument Setup or RTF Failure
Service Software Error Codes
22 20 02 03 30 – RTF#1, FAM
22 20 02 04 30 – RTF#2, RED 677
22 20 02 05 30 – RTF#3, HEX
22 20 02 06 30 – RTF#4, not used
22 20 02 07 30 – RTF#5, ROX
22 20 02 08 30 – RTF#6, not used
Connection Failed (Timeout Error)
Unable to complete instrument setup, in service software reset failure for this RTF.
Removing faulty RTF allows instrument setup to complete.
Identifying Failure
Refer to photograph below, where green light appears on the RTFs. If one RTF in the chain is bad, the ones after will not be lit, or have a solid light. Plugging in one at a time, and looking at the lights, can lead to the bad one.
RTF Indicator LED – Diode 7
Failed RTFs will be either:
-
Solid green
or
-
Dark, no light
If one RTF in the chain is bad, it can affect the others. For example, FAM failure can affect ROX. Test by unplugging FAM.
Proper Operation: LED should blink slowly when power is supplied.
Video – when power is supplied and blinking.
Schematic
Pin
Description
1
GND
2
GND
3
CAN H
4
CAN L
5
Flouro trigger
6
GND
7
24V
8
24V
9
GND
10
GND
Resolution
-
Check RTF1 LED. LED should blink at one-second intervals after initial power on.
Solid ON or OFF = Bad RTF.
-
Check DIP switches on RTFs – possibly two RTFs using same address.
-
Swap RTF1 position, or move the cable connector over – if so, replace RTF cable.

## RTF HCV Inhibition
id="mc-main-content">
RTF HCV Inhibition
The delay in ROX for the High Pos Control points to inhibition or contamination. The run on 03-26-2021 was heavily delayed in Ttime and it is possible the inhibition/contamination is getting worse. The other instrument in the lab (P03109) is running the same lots of calibrators, controls, and HCV master lots, and is completely fine (High Positive Control lots in blue and red).
I did not see any correlation with MagWash or tube position with delay in Ttime on P03253. I am unable to tell from the curves if the inhibition/contamination is coming from the instrument, or a prep area in the lab.

## Real Time Flourometer Installation Issues
id="mc-main-content">
Real Time Flourometer Installation Issues
Two real time fluorometer (RTF) installation issues have arisen:
- RTFs Installed in Swapped Locations
- Incorrect RTF Installed
RTFs Installed in Swapped Locations
During RTF install, FSE Field Service Engineer. failed PQ with ebl flags on the calibrators.
It is likely a simple swap of ROX and HEX RTFs in the wrong position; that is why you are seeing the timing shift in the curves.
The FSE should switch the RTFs to the correct position, and verify with the nominal check in SSW.
Another example:
- RTF 1 and RTF 2 signals rule out magnets and slot issue.
- Checked P128-P143, and delta is 1440 as expected.
- RTF FW versions check out.
Any troubleshooting we can recommend for FSE, and parts to have on hand?
RTF 1 (fam), RTF 2 (cy5.5) vs RTF 3 (hex), RTF 5 (rox)
By Hex/Rox by MTU:
Incorrect RTF Installed
FSE was shipped a FAM RTF in a RTF 677 (CY5.5) box. PQ failed because the IC did not light off for the negative control. Notice the FAM and 677 curves look almost identical. FSE pulled the 677 RTF, and PN showed it to actually be a FAM RTF.
Note: Request pictures of all boxes showing label and each RTF serialization.
RTF serial number should not repeat.
This is the IC for the Negatives. It did not light off because the wrong RTF was installed.

## UPS - Uninterruptible Power Supply
id="mc-main-content">
UPS - Uninterruptible Power Supply
Technical Support
General Troubleshooting - See Tables 1 and 31 below
-
Ask how often the beeping noise is (frequencies of beeps?).
-
Ask which LED indicator lights are on. If the system continues to beep, the alarm LED indicator (triangle) should be lit.
-
Reference the Eaten Powerware 9130 User Guide (Table 31).
Analyzing UPS Event Log
-
Press the Down Arrow to activate the LCD display.
-
Navigate to the 'Event Log' section using the up/down arrows. Hit 'Enter' when 'Event Log' is found.
-
Event Log entries are numbered -- XXX/XXX is the most recent entry, 1/XXX is the first entry.
-
Have customer read the entries, compare to the various conditions/alarms in the table.
Modes
Description
Lights
Normal Mode
UPS is powered from utility, provides 'filtered' power to Panther.
(-/-) indicator is solid.
Battery Mode
UPS is operating during a power outage. UPS alarm beeps once every 5 seconds. This will provide power to the Panther for approx. 5 minutes, at which time the operator should safely shutdown the instrument.
Battery (+/-) indicator is solid.
Bypass Mode
UPS has failed, Panther is powered directly by utility. This occurs when
-User activates Bypass mode manually
-UPS detects internal failure
-UPS is overtemperature
-UPS is overloaded
**Battery Mode is unavailable. If a power outage occurs, all power will be lost.
Bypass indicator (circle with arrow around) is solid.
Standby Mode
Typically not used -- only occurs when UPS is turned off.
(-/-) indicator is off.

## Cisco Advanced Password Reset
id="mc-main-content">
Cisco Advanced Password Reset
Error Code
No error code.
Complaint Description
When performing a password reset on the Cisco ASA 5506-X, the password either gets specified incorrectly (e.g. the designated password of gpservice has a typo), or another password gets specified, preventing the FSE Field Service Engineer. from performing password resets.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Reset the ASA
- Reset the Password via Command-Line
Technical Support
N/A
Field Service
There are two saved configurations on an ASA:
-
startup-config , which is the configuration that is loaded onto the ASA after a power cycle,
and
-
running-config , which is the configuration between when an ASA is powered on, and any changes a superuser makes (the delta, or Δ).
Reset the ASA
Reset the ASA reverts the running-config to the startup-config by power-cycling the ASA.
Resolution: Press the reset button on the back of the ASA.
Hold the reset button at the back of the ASA for five seconds. This causes the ASA to power-cycle.
Test: Retry Firewall Wizard.
If the ASA continues to display the password issue after power-cycle, it indicates that password is part of the startup-config , and must be reset via command-line interface.
Reset the Password via Command-Line
Note: For this procedure, access to ciscoasa# is required. If you are unable to get to this point (because the password is unknown), an ASA memory reset is required.
An ASA memory reset is not a field procedure. Order a new ASA and return the Firewall to the USTSESupport group for refurbishment.
Resolution: Reset the Password via Command-Line
To change the password via command-line:
- Using HyperTerminal or PuTTy, access ciscoasa# .
- From the ciscoasa# prompt, type the command ‘config t’, and press Enter. This will bring you to ciscoasa(config)# .
- From ciscoasa(config)# , type the command ‘enable password gpservice’. This command will change the password to gpservice. There is no expected output.
- From ciscoasa(config)# , type the command ‘copy run start’. This is short for copy running-config startup-config , and will save any changes from the current running-config to the startup-config .
- You will be prompted for a source filename, just press Enter.
- From ciscoasa(config)# , type the command ‘exit’. This will bring you to ciscoasa# .
- From ciscoasa# , type the command ‘exit’. This will bring you to ciscoasa> .
Validation:
From ciscoasa> , type the command ‘enable’. It will prompt for the password. Input the password as designated, and press Enter. This should bring you to ciscoasa# .
Test: Retry Firewall Wizard.

## Dashboard Connectivity DNS Lookup Failure
id="mc-main-content">
Dashboard Connectivity DNS Lookup Failure
Error Code
Domain Name Service (DNS) Look Up reports “Bad” when running the Connectivity Tester in Dashboard when testing for Remote Diagnostics (Pro360/SecureLink) and Remote Send Logs (RSL).
Complaint Description
When running the Dashboard Connectivity Tester, DNS Look Up reports “Bad”, including Access over 22/443. LAN Connection results “Good”.
Technical Support
Verify Physical Connectivity of Network Devices
It is possible that there could be a bad ethernet cable, or the network devices (Panther, switch, firewall, customer wall port) might not be correctly plugged into the appropriate network device.
Resolution:
Check Network Device Connectivity
- Verify that the Panther is properly plugged into the next network device.
- If the Panther is plugged into a switch, verify that the Panther is connected to the switch on ports 1-16. Look for the presence of link lights on either the switch or the Panther.
Figure 1: Example of Network Interface Card Link Lights
- If the Panther is plugged into a firewall, verify that the Panther is connected on ports 1-7 (5505) or 8 (5506-X). Look for the presence of link lights on either the firewall or the Panther.
- If applicable, verify the switch is plugged into the firewall on either port 7 (5505) or port 8 (5506-X). Look for the presence of link lights on either the firewall or the switch.
- Verify the firewall is plugged into the customer wall port on either port 0 (5505) or port 1 (5506-X). Look for the presence of link lights on the firewall.
Test:
Retry Connectivity Tester.
Field Service
Network Interface Card (NIC) DNS Server Address Configuration
The Panther NIC may not have been correctly configured to include the appropriate DNS server, as designated by the customer.
Resolution:
Configure or validate the DNS Server into the NIC.
- At the Panther Command Prompt, type “control ncpa.cpl”.
- Right-click on the NIC and click “Properties”.
- Click on Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and click “Properties”.
- Click the radio button for “Use the following DNS server addresses:” and input the following addresses:
- Preferred DNS server: Customer Specific
- Alternate DNS server: Customer Specific
Note— The DNS server is customer specific. Please refer to the generated instructions.txt file when programming the firewall to determine the IP address.
Test:
Retry Connectivity Tester.
Firewall DNS Server Address Configuration
When configuring the firewall, the customer determines whether they would like to use their local DNS servers or if they want to use a publicly available DNS server (e.g., Google DNS, OpenDNS). The firewall is configured to only allow traffic to two specific DNS servers. These servers must match between the Panther NIC and the firewall.
Resolution:
Verify the DNS server IPs are programmed into the firewall.
- Connect to the console port of the firewall.
- Using Firewall Wizard 6.1.0.4, select the option “Save the current firewall configuration.”
- Select the appropriate location to save the files.
- Run Wizard to completion, navigate to the saved location from Step 3 and open the output.txt file.
- In the file, search for “object-group network DNS” servers. Below that line there are two lines that start with “network-object”. Immediately following “network-object” are the IPs of the DNS servers.
Test:
Validate DNS servers match between firewall and Panther NIC, Retry Connectivity Tester
Customer IT Escalation
If the Connectivity Tester reports “Bad” after confirming the DNS servers match, contact the customer’s IT department to determine if these are the correct DNS match.
Resolution:
Contact Customer IT for further instructions.
Test:
Retry Connectivity Tester.

## Dashboard Connectivity LAN Failure
id="mc-main-content">
Dashboard Connectivity LAN Failure
Error Code
Local Area Network (LAN) Connection Fails reports “Bad” when running the Connectivity Tester in Dashboard when testing for Remote Diagnostics (Pro360/SecureLink) and Remote Send Logs (RSL).
Complaint Description
When running the Dashboard Connectivity Tester, all tests result “Bad”, including Domain Name Service (DNS) Lookup, Access over 22/443, and LAN Connection.
Technical Support
Verify Physical Connectivity of Network Devices
There could be a bad ethernet cable, or the network devices are not correctly plugged into the appropriate network device, or that the network devices are off.
Resolution:
Check Network Device Connectivity:
- Verify that the Panther is properly plugged into the next network device.
- If the Panther is plugged into a switch, verify that the Panther is connected to the switch on ports 1-16. Look for the presence of link lights on either the switch or the Panther.
Figure 1: Example of Network Interface Card Link Lights
- If the Panther is plugged into a firewall, verify that the Panther is connected on ports 1-7 (5505) or 8 (5506-X). Look for the presence of link lights on either the firewall or the Panther.
- If applicable, verify the switch is plugged into the firewall on either port 7 (5505) or port 8 (5506-X). Look for the presence of link lights on either the firewall or the switch.
- Verify the firewall is plugged into the customer wall port on either port 0 (5505) or port 1 (5506-X). Look for the presence of link lights on the firewall.
Test:
Retry Connectivity Tester
Field Service
Network Interface Card (NIC) IP Address Configuration
After running the Dashboard Test, the LAN Connection field should report the IP address configured on the NIC. Subsequently, the NIC Configuration arrow on the right side of the Connectivity Tester can be used to check which IP is configured on the NIC. If the address is not within the format 172.23.1.X, it will fail.
Resolution:
Configure or validate the NIC IP Address:
- At the Panther Command Prompt, type “control ncpa.cpl”.
- Right-click on the NIC and click “Properties.”
- Click on Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and click “Properties”.
- Click the radio button for “Use the following IP address:” and input the following addresses-
- IP address: 172.23.1.X
Note— The IP address is system configuration specific. Please refer to the generated instructions.txt file when programming the firewall to determine the IP address.
Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0
Default gateway: 172.23.1.1
- Click the radio button for “Use the following DNS server addresses:” and input the following addresses-
- Preferred DNS server: Customer Specific
- Alternate DNS server: Customer Specific
Note— The DNS server is customer specific. Please refer to the generated instructions.txt file when programming the firewall to determine the IP address.
Test:
Retry Connectivity Tester

id="mc-main-content">
Error While Transmitting Data to LIS
Error Code
272.000.00006 – Error while transmitting data to LIS Laboratory Information System. .
Complaint Description
Panther does not receive acknowledgements (ACK) from the LIS. Confirm in LIS messages in Panther GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. , or ASTM 1381 A Low-level protocol that is used to transfer Messages between Clinical Laboratory Instruments and Computer Systems. Logs.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support

Serial and TCP/IP

Click LIS Configuration .

To disable the LIS, uncheck the Enable LIS connection checkbox.
-
Click Save at the bottom of the screen.
-
Wait one minute for the connection to reset.
-
To enable the LIS, check the Enable LIS connection checkbox.
-
Click Save .

Click Start to restart the LIS connection.

Instruct Customer to Restart LIS Server

Confirm no errors result while transmtting data to LIS messages.

Resolution
Instruct customer to reseat the connection at the workstation serial port. It may be a serial cable, but is more likely a Serial-to-Ethernet Adaptor (e.g. Lantronix).

Click Results in the top menu bar.

Select a patient result to send to the LIS.

Click Send results to LIS at the bottom of the screen.
- Confirm no errors result while transmtting data to LIS messages.
Replace Cables (Serial or Ethernet)
Cabling may be broken or defective.

Test

Select a patient result to send to the LIS.

Click Send results to LIS at the bottom of the screen.
- Confirm no errors result while transmtting data to LIS messages.
Instruct Customer to Confirm Connectivity (such as cables, wall ports, and network closets)
