## Can I Unload Fusion Cartridges and Store At Room Temperature? If so, for how long?
id="mc-main-content">
Can I Unload Fusion Cartridges and Store At Room Temperature? If so, for how long?
- The recommended storage conditions for the cartridges are refrigerated (2 - 8°C).
- The cartridges are stable in the system for up to 60 days, and there is room to hold up to 28 cartridges at one time, so there should be little need to take them back out of the system.
- If the cartridge must be unloaded, then it should be placed in an airtight container with a desiccant and stored at 2 - 8°C.

## How Do I Find the RFU / Passing Criteria for Fusion Assays?
id="mc-main-content">
How Do I Find the RFU / Passing Criteria for Fusion Assays?
-
TSR files contain detailed cutoff information for each assay. Note: Information is stored in the Fusion folder, and is also available in Agile.
-
The PCR data file has a column for ""RFU Range (column "" which is the only cutoff for ""Wave 1 (respiratory)"" assays. Future assays may incorporate slope, or other factors.

## How Many Assays Can the Fusion Slide Hold?
id="mc-main-content">
How Many Assays Can the Fusion Slide Hold?
- You can load up to 28 reagent cartridges, with 12 tests each, at one time, for a total of 336 tests.
- This can be any mix of assay cartridges, both IVD and Open Access cartridges.
- Up to 4 Aptima assays can be loaded at one time, in addition to the Panther Fusion reagent cartridges.

## Why Are Controls Not “Green”? Why Are Controls Not Pipetting?
id="mc-main-content">
Why Are Controls Not “Green”? Why Are Controls Not Pipetting?
Instrument will not run only controls; it needs a sample to start processing.
Controls will show white with a C. The same holds for open access controls, and for SARS-CoV-2. Once a sample is loaded, and assigned a test order for assay of the controls loaded, the controls illuminate Green, and the instrument starts pipetting.

## How can I find the Fusion SN?
id="mc-main-content">
How can I find the Fusion SN?
Open a log.0 file; search for “RadiumCallback.VersionInfo” or filter the class name field in ViewLog. This will include the dump of all Fusion FW and module PCB SNs. E.i. for Fusion 105-> RadiumCallback. VersionInfo (List: [VersionItem module:[COP;0x00;0x00], version:03.0208 2101 COP, serial:2101000105, article:1000000000 completed]).

## How long does it take for the Thermocycler – under software v7.1, only TC – to go into the Power Save mode?
id="mc-main-content">
How long does it take for the Thermocycler – under software v7.1, only TC – to go into the Power Save mode?
The system looks and waits for two introduction cycles (10 minutes) with no samples, before it transitions into the power save / sleep mode.

## How many tecan tips are used per sample for one Fusion assay?
id="mc-main-content">
How many tecan tips are used per sample for one Fusion assay?
- When a complete MTU is pipetted at the same time to test one assay.
Panther Side:
- 0.2 for FCR (sample pipettor)
- 0.2 for FER (sample pipettor)
- 1 for sample aliquot
- 0.2 for elution buffer (reag pipettor)
Fusion side:
- 0.2 for oil (Fusion pipettor)
- 1 for recon buffer (IVD) or PPR (Open Access) (Fusion pipettor)
- 1 for eluate (NAs extracted from sample) (Fusion pipettor)
- Total = 3.8 tips per sample

## How many tecan tips are used per sample if testing multiple Fusion assays for one sample in the same extraction?
id="mc-main-content">
How many tecan tips are used per sample if testing multiple Fusion assays for one sample in the same extraction?
Information regarding number of tips used per sample when testing multiple fusion assays for single same in same extraction.
- When a complete MTU is pipetted at the same time to test N number of assays requested at the same time (same extraction).
Panther Side (same as above):
- 0.2 for FCR (sample pipettor)
- 0.2 for FER (sample pipettor)
- 1 for sample aliquot
- 0.2 for elution buffer (reag pipettor)
Fusion side (multiply by the number of assays being tested (N):
- 0.2 for oil (Fusion pipettor) x N
- 1 for recon buffer (IVD) or PPR (Open Access) (Fusion pipettor) x N
- 1 for eluate (NAs extracted from sample) (Fusion pipettor) x N
- Total = 1.6 (panther side)+2.2 x N (Fusion side)
- ex/Sample tested for FluA/B/RSV and Paraflu (N = 2)
- 1.6 + (2.2 x 2) = 6

## Tecan Tips Per Sample
id="mc-main-content">
Tecan Tips Per Sample
How many tecan tips are used per sample for one TMA assay?
Note: When a complete MTU is pipetted at the same time to test one assay.
Panther Side:
-
0.2 for TCR (sample pipettor)
-
1 for sample aliquot
-
0.2 for amp reagent (reag pipettor)
-
0.2 for enzyme reagent (reag pipettor)
-
0.2 for probe reagent (reagent pipettor)
-
0.4 for selection reagent (reagent pipettor)
Total = 2.2 tips per sample
How many tecan tips are used per sample for one RT-TMA assay?
Panther Side:
-
0.2 for TCR (sample pipettor)
-
1 for sample aliquot
-
0.2 for amp reagent (reag pipettor)
-
0.2 for enzyme reagent (reag pipettor)
-
0.2 for promoter reagent (reagent pipettor)
Total = 1.8 tips per sample
How many tecan tips are used per sample for one Fusion assay?
Note: When a complete MTU is pipetted at the same time to test one assay.
Panther Side:
-
0.2 for FCR (sample pipettor)
-
0.2 for FER (sample pipettor)
-
1 for sample aliquot
-
0.2 for elution buffer (reag pipettor)
Fusion side:
-
0.2 for oil (Fusion pipettor)
-
1 for recon buffer (IVD) or PPR (Open Access) (Fusion pipettor)
-
1 for eluate (NAs extracted from sample) (Fusion pipettor)
Total = 3.8 tips per sample
How many tecan tips are used per sample if testing multiple Fusion assays for one sample in the same extraction?
Note: When a complete MTU is pipetted at the same time to test N number of assays requested at the same time (same extraction).
Panther Side (same as above):
-
0.2 for FCR (sample pipettor)
-
0.2 for FER (sample pipettor)
-
1 for sample aliquot
-
0.2 for elution buffer (reagent pipettor)
Fusion side (multiply by the number of assays being tested (N):
-
0.2 for oil (Fusion pipettor) x N
-
1 for recon buffer (IVD) or PPR (Open Access) (Fusion pipettor) x N
-
1 for eluate (NAs extracted from sample) (Fusion pipettor) x N
Total = 1.6 (Panther side) + 2.2 x N (Fusion side)
ex/Sample tested for FluA/B/RSV and Paraflu (N = 2)
1.6 + (2.2 x 2) = 6

## Instrument displays “Ready” state, but Thermocycler displays "Not Ready” state
id="mc-main-content">
Instrument displays “Ready” state, but Thermocycler displays "Not Ready” state
Complaint Description
Information regarding instrument readiness when Thermocycler is in Not Ready state.
Technical Support
Under software v7.1 admin above, the Thermocycler will "turn on" once the Fusion sample is loaded. The software v7.1 preserves the Thermocycler LEDs by not “turning them on” until needed.

## Internal control pipetting failed for FCR/FER set in TCR Carousel position (5-7)
id="mc-main-content">
Internal control pipetting failed for FCR/FER set in TCR Carousel position (5-7)
Complaint Description
Information regarding internal control pipetting failure.
Technical Support
If you have a Panther Fusion customer calling and saying they had an internal control pipetting error: Internal control pipetting failed for FCR/FER set in TCR Carousel position (5-7), have them check the sample shield. If it is not placed properly, when they load new FCR/FER and IC and the sample pipettor goes to try to pipette the IC, it can cause that error.
If the customer tries to reload the same set of FCR/FER/IC, even though IC was probably never pipetted, it will think it has and will not use those extraction reagents again. Customer will have to discard that set of extraction reagents or use them in a different Panther Fusion (as long as they are not linked).
Have the customer fix sample shield, and then load new set of FCR/FER/IC. Those reagents are free of charge, so they can order more, or if they need them right away we send them.

## Perform a Shutdown Restart
id="mc-main-content">
Perform a Shutdown Restart
Complaint Description
Information regarding a shutdown restart.
Technical Support
Follow this guidance and mainly remind customers when shutting down the instrument:
Ensure instrument is in error state. If tests are in the Thermocycler it will likely continue in error assay processing until those results are out (the message will show: Tests that were in the Thermocycler at the time the error occurred will continue to be processed. Do not shutdown the system until the Shutdown or Instrument shutdown buttons are available). If status is Panther Only and customer is not running Fusion tests, perform shutdown when convenient. If in Panther only status and instrument is currently running Panther tests, do shutdown when those tests are completed.
If the Logoff screen is grayed out, there is another Shutdown button in the Messages screen.
Do not use the PC workstation power button while Panther GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. Main is running, as this can cause file or database corruption.
Sometimes the screen is frozen and there is no other way, but if that is the case (and customer has waited long enough and software is not responding), guide customer to do a quick click on PC power button to shutdown PC, and please note this in the case.
Open access packs must come out for the instrument to restart, cartridges do not, if FCR/FER is not removed it is like TCR, it does not prevent restart but customer, once instrument restart, will have to go through steps on UI to load FCR/FER so they are rescanned.
Once PC is off, shutdown power switch in the left side. Restart Analyzer, wait 30 sec and then restart PC.
Check critical notes under instrument in case the order of restart is different (refer to Fusion - XE3 - power button blinking error).

## PPR Prioritization Logic
id="mc-main-content">
PPR Prioritization Logic
Complaint Description
Information regarding PPR prioritization logic.
Technical Support
PPR tubes are prioritized on the Panther Fusion System in the following order when running multiple PPR tubes with the same protocol:
- PPR lot with a valid set of controls.
- PPR lot with the lowest amount of time remaining for controls or associated cartridge lot.
- PPR lot with the lowest remaining test count (sum of all loaded tubes per lot loaded on the system).
- PPR pack that has the lowest remaining test count (sum of all tubes in a single pack).
- The tube with the lowest number of remaining tests per tube.
- If the tubes have the same number of tests, PPR tubes will be processed from Position A to D, from pack 1 to 4.

## Processing Flags
id="mc-main-content">
Processing Flags
Complaint Description
Information regarding internal control pipetting failure.
Technical Support
dc (1-5) – Invalid fluorescent curve profile. Curve double-crossed the threshold. Sample is invalid.
ebl (1-5) – The calculated estimated baseline is below the threshold value. Sample is invalid.
ebh (1-5) – The calculated estimated baseline is above the threshold value. Sample is invalid.
mrr (1-5) – The maximum raw RFU value is greater than the maximum cutoff value for the assay. Sample is invalid.
For mrr flag, sample is invalid statement is incorrect, it will be corrected in a future ops manual revision. It is usually a warning or informational flag. If running Adv/hMPV/RV assay, look at limitations on the PI.
Channels:
- 1 - FAM
- 2 - HEX
- 3 - ROX
- 4 - Red647/Quasar670
- 5 - Redd677/Quasar705(IC)

## What Collection Device Is Used for GBS Samples?
id="mc-main-content">
What Collection Device Is Used for GBS Samples?
- No Hologic-specific collection devices are required or offered.
- Vaginal or Rectal swab into liquid Aimes or Stuarts media (non-nutritive).
- Inoculate swabs directly into enrichment broth Lim Broth or Carrot Broth) and incubate for 18 - 24 hours at 35 - 37 C.

## What Collection Device Is Used for Respiratory Samples?
id="mc-main-content">
What Collection Device Is Used for Respiratory Samples?
- No Hologic-specific collection devices are required or offered.
- NP swabs can be collected in any of the 6 VTMs (RemelM4, M5, M6 or M4RT, BD and/or Copan) as they are today.
- BALs and Bronchwashes are collected per normal procedures. Once in the lab, and the aliquot of the primary sample is transferred to the STM tube and loaded into the Panther sample racks. This allows the transfer to be done in the hood if desired.
- No live virus is loaded into the Panther Fusion.
- The primary sample is still intact in the event that additional testing or culture is required.

## What Is the On-board Capacity for the Different Fusion Consumables?
id="mc-main-content">
What Is the On-board Capacity for the Different Fusion Consumables?
- Panther Fusion Tubes: 224 (4 trays of 56)
- 4 recon packs with 960 reactions each = 3840 reactions
- Recon packs can be swapped out for PPR packs to allow Open Access
- 2 Oil Packs at 960 reactions each = 1920 reactions
- 2 Elution packs at 1200 tests each = 2400 tests

## What is the Fusion Throughput?
id="mc-main-content">
What is the Fusion Throughput?
-
Panther Fusion can run 335 PCR tests in an 8-hour shift.
-
When combined with the Aptima assays, there is a potential for 500 results in an 8 hour shift. This requires an optimal loading sequence by the user and will probably not be achieved in most situations. However, given a mixture of Fusion PCR assays with multiple tests per sample and Aptima RT-TMA assays, the user will see between 335 and 500 results in 8 hours.
-
Generally, for best throughput, load PCR assays first, RT-TMA next, and TMA last.

## What is the “Time to Result” on Fusion?
id="mc-main-content">
What is the “Time to Result” on Fusion?
- PCR only – 2:25.
- Part 1: 1h20m to get to the point when the MTU is transferred to the Fusion side.
- Part 2: 1h6m to complete PCR in Fusion side.
- Results in 8 hrs: 335.

## When are new controls needed?
id="mc-main-content">
When are new controls needed?
Complaint Description
Information regarding new controls.
Technical Support
Once the control tubes are pipetted, processed, and valid for the Panther Fusion assays, they are active for up to 30 days, unless the control results are invalid, or a new assay cartridge lot is loaded.
Administrator configures the control frequency.

## When is the IC added?
id="mc-main-content">
When is the IC added?
Complaint Description
Information regarding addition of IC.
Technical Support
As soon as the instrument scans and detects a new set of FCR/FER and IC, the IC is added to the FCR.

## Will we have access to the eluate after extraction?
id="mc-main-content">
Will we have access to the eluate after extraction?
Does the instrument hold the extracted material for Reflex testing?
-
At this time, there is not a way to retrieve the nucleic acids or reflex from nucleic acids, but we are aware of this customer desire.
-
Regarding reflexing, however, one respiratory STM tube loaded into Panther has sufficient volumes to extract three times. Each extract can be set up with multiple PCRs. If additional testing is requested, the same STM tube can be reloaded without going back to the primary specimen.

id="mc-main-content">
CHF

In this situation, CHF errors were caused by tips.

## icrfu / icneg
id="mc-main-content">
icrfu / icneg
Complaint Description
Panther Fusion
Internal Control (IC) is negative. Poor or no amplification.
icrfu and icneg are results processing flags, i.e., lowercase flags versus assay processing flags, which are uppercase and suggest a hardware failure.
These are new processing flags, only for open access in sw 7.1, and for open access and IVD in sw 7.2.
Results report legend displays:
icrfu – IC is negative.
icneg – IC is negative.
Additional information to distinguish between these two similar flags:
icrfu IC is negative. No amplification in any channel, with no Ct calculated for IC.
icneg IC is negative. IC amplifies, but does not meet maximum Ct cut off (i.e., Ct too late).
Both flags may be seen in a run report where an issue affects an entire run or entire PPR pack, with some samples having icrfu and other samples having icneg. It depends on the raw data for that particular sample.
The flag occurs when there is little or no amplification of the Internal control for a Fusion RT-PCR assay. The sample having this flag is invalid. For a sample to be called Negative (i.e. no amplification in analyte channel), the IC acceptance criteria must be meet. If not, then the sample is invalidated with one of these flags. If the sample has amplification and is deemed positive by sw algorithm, then the IC criteria is not required.
Additional Note: Unlike the Aptima TMA and RT-TMA assays where IC is added to TCR by operator, for Fusion and open access assays, the IC is added to the Fusion Capture Reagent (FCR) by the Panther-side sample pipettor when the FCR/FER/IC bottles are initially loaded, and thereafter becomes wFCR. This avoids the possibility of operator error in not adding the IC.
Table of Contents
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- TSE Review
- TSE Review Example
Technical Support
Review the run report.
-
Is the icrfu or icneg flag on one isolated sample or on several samples?
If only one sample in a run has the flag, then it can be an isolated case where there is something inhibitory in the sample. What is the sample type? Is this a validated sample type?
-
If there are many affected samples in the run, is there something in common with the samples having the icrfu or icneg flag, such as isolated to the same PCR cartridge, or to the same PPR tube (in the case of SARS PCR or open access LDTs).
If isolated to a certain PPR tube, was there a handling error or preparation error? Have customer prepare/load a new vial of PPR and monitor.
If isolated to a certain PCR cartridge, was there a storage, shipping, or handling issue? Get the LN from customer.
Are there any additional flags associated with the sample, besides the icrfu or icneg? These results processing flags will often occur as a downstream result of another uppercase flag, which has previously affected the assay processing of the sample.
Below are some other flags seen with icrfu. The flags below are assay processing flags, and are related to various hardware issues. In these cases, one should address the hardware failure.

## PPFR
id="mc-main-content">
PPFR
PPFR when it occurs with an RDFL flag.
Fusion Pipettor Driver pump move canceled, excessive pressure 1239.001.00169 .
RDFL: 283.000.00010 , // SRS-EEH-1431 : The system shall apply an RDFL flag to affected tests when a PCR LDT Reagent dispense verification fails.
PPFR: 283.000.00002
Troubleshooting: Confirm customer is inspecting open access (OA) tube volumes, and entering accurate test counts. OA will not update volume or tests.
Corrective action: Remind customers to reject underfilled tubes, and enter correct test numbers for open access tubes.

OA, or open access tubes 1, 2, 4, and 5 - located in Recon Buffer of Fusion fluids drawer - are correctly filled to roughly 500 steps, which is safe for 40 tests.
Tube 3 is about 5mm lower (400 steps).

As the fluid level is not sufficient, the level sense flat lines as the bottom of the tube is reached, highlighted in blue below.

## RBEEB
id="mc-main-content">
RBEEB
Elution Bottle Empty, or Elution Buffer not enough liquid detected.
In Figure 1 below, the two longest C-LLD curves graphed, indicates the pipettor reached end of travel - zmax, index calue reached almost 200 - without detecting a large enough state change (insufficient y-value change).
If pipettor reaches zmax without successful trigger on state change, means no liquid is detected.
Resolution:
-
Verify elution track bucket makes good contact with grounding brush on panther side.
-
Inspect bucket metal coating for wear.
-
Inspect brush.
-
Attempt to replicate using clld in ssw (if reproducible, clean diti/contacts and repeat).
-
Otherwise pipettor replacement may be necessary.
-
Inspect teaching, pipettor skew and elution track to Panther alignment (see *.coo file group 18 or 19 depending on *.coo file executable - use reagent bay positions 56, 57, and 58 to compare to sample bays 62, 63, and 64, because elution track is single point.
- CooEdit = group 19
- Coordinate Editor = group 18
Ideally, we identify a minor mechanical adjustment to address these.
- Pipettor alignment
- Elution track alignment
- Elution track distance variance relative to ground plate
- Cable routing around the ground plate
- Pipettor type APP v BLDC
- Tip mfr + lot #
CASE 1
Capacitive Circuit is not well grounded.
Figure 1. Capacitive sensor with poor grounding, leading to inconsistent level sense results. Most times liquid is detected around index = 120. Two traces where pipettor reaches index=190-200, pipettor end of travel (no liquid detected).
Figure 2. LLDHeight representation of level sense results from Figure 1. Notice most measurments are around 1000. And two results at 0. The very last measurement is higher could be bubble or new recon buffer pack.
CASE 2
Another, RBEEB but less common:
The Elution capacitive limit threshold of 800 is not met due to the gradual rise of the curve (see red box below). While it’s clear by eye liquid has been detected, the threshold algorithm is less sensitive as it needs to reject CASE 3.
This causes the LLD height to not be detected (height 0, RBEEB), and the tip deep dives into the pack.
This case is being investigated (as of 1/26/2022) to determine if threshold can be adjusted.
We have not seen any capacitive signal difference between Tecan and Biorear – in fact this curve first appeared using Tecan tips.
I do not know of any sure fix for this, other than playing around with the grounding of the elution dump truck, pipettor teaching, and opening up the elution pack completely.
Hopefully the FSEs are able to fix this type of curve by hardware intervention (elution dump truck, reagent pipettor, etc.).
CASE 3
The teaching is variance in x-axis appears larger than expected.
Reagent bay front to back is off by almost 6 steps in x-direction.
Sample bay front to back (roughly 2x distance of reagent bay), but difference in x-axis is only 2 steps.

7845, 16068, 2658, 0; // Pos 57 – reagent bay lane 2 - front
9035, 16068, 2661, 0; // Pos 58 – reagent bay lane 4 - front

14260, 15757, 66, 0; // Pos 63 – sample bay cover teach 2
14262, 11434, 81, 0; // Pos 64 – sample bay cover – teach 3
Please order a set of x-axis belts long, x-axis motor.
I don’t think the reagent pipettor is square up correctly and causing these edge effects on pipettor centering and poor centering.

## RDFSE
id="mc-main-content">
RDFSE
RDV 512 and no RDV code.
RDFSE – Reagent Dispense Failure Sample Eluate, same flag for Aspiration failure (e.g., no RAFSE flag).
RDV 512 = Failure code, Pmaxmin not met (see MDD_FW_APP or CDD_… Aspirate and Dispense Analysis).
RDFSE will occur at either:
-
Aspirate from MTU at magnetic elution slot 0 or 1 (no RAFSE flag).
-
Dispense into vial at cap and vial station.
RDV codes used and thresholds:
-
Eluate Aspirate*
- PMaxMax = RDV 2 (Pmax < approx. -320)
- PMaxMin = RDV 512 (Pmax > approx. -95)
-
Eluate dispense*
- PMaxMax = RDV 2 (Pmax > 5000)
- PMaxMin = RDV 512 (Pmax < 1580)
See corresponding sequence file: C:\Panther\Software\PC\Bin\Input .
Example, Flu_A_B_RSV:
CurveID: 00141
RunName: 2021_01_13_08-50-25
Assay: Paraflu

CommandDescription: Eluate Dispense
DateTime: 01/13/2021 20:08:49
TestOrderId: 112
TestOrderBatchNumber: 0013
TestOrderPosition: 4
TestOrderBatch: [104 109 111 112 113 ]
SampleID: UNVPANELA-284253
MTUNumber: 0003
MTUID: 1946981055
TubeNumber: 5
Fusion pipettor does the following (to audit pipettor moves, inspect Sidecar Aspiration curve, sorting by TO, and checking timestamps):
-
Aspirate oil from pack and dispense in vial.
-
Aspirate recon from pack, dispense in cartridge, mix (aspirate/dispense) in cartridge, final aspiration in cartridge, dispense in vial.
-
Aspirate sample eluate from MTU, and dispense in vial.
-
Repeat for each tube in MTU.

Issue:

Verified teaching of Fusion pipettor was centered over dimple at teach point.
Verified meshing of pipettor to z-motor.
Looking more closely at curve data shows PRiseDelayed = True(Figure 5) , indicating the process control was outside acceptable limits. (Note: sequence file indicates this process should not be enabled)
Inspected FW version was up to date, but par.135 = 1
2022-01-07 13:41:36,011|[SC StartupManager]|SidecarFwHwVersion|SWConfiguration|Info|Normal|FW Version VersionItem module:[RobotArm;0xFD;0x05], version:01.0109.1 6319 APE Airpip-EC, serial:68, article:1 completed
2022-01-07 13:41:36,370|[SC StartupManager]|SidecarParameterManager|SidecarMA|Info|Normal|SCFWP: PipettorSystem[FD][05]: 135: next index: 136, type SignedIntParameter DefaultValue 1 Value 1
How this occurred:
If either of the following messages occur during instrument setup, repeat instrument setup again:
Resolution:
Run instrument setup again, and verify par.135 = -16127. Verify PRiseDelayed issue was resolved (Figure 6).
2022-01-11 17:51:25,097|[SC StartupManager]|SidecarFwHwVersion|SWConfiguration|Info|Normal|FW Version VersionItem module:[RobotArm;0xFD;0x05], version:01.0109.1 6319 APE Airpip-EC, serial:100, article:1 completed
2022-01-11 17:51:25,462|[SC StartupManager]|SidecarParameterManager|SidecarMA|Info|Normal|SCFWP: PipettorSystem[FD][05]: 135: next index: 136, type SignedIntParameter DefaultValue 1 Value -16127
Figure 5. BLDC pipettor Prisedelayed.
Figure 6. After BLDC pipettor replaced, retrospectively instrument setup running correctly resolved the problem.

From logs:
RPTL - Fusion tube loss detected on the Tube Handling Robot.
Grab sample IDs with RPTL errors:

Invalidated Sample ID 1104604589A for LDT-SARS-CoV-2 assay in lane 2 position 9 due to RPTL flag. Sample will need to be retested.

Invalidated Sample ID 1104602659A for LDT-SARS-CoV-2 assay in lane 3 position 11 due to RPTL flag. Sample will need to be retested.
Yellow = cap vial Lot#
Blue = seems to be cap vial box ID

Resolution: Diti cleaning, new tip eject sleeves, meshing, teaching can resolve tube loss and zmax errors (if it is not vial lot related). If vial lot related, thermocycler deep cleaning.

## RVHEB
id="mc-main-content">
RVHEB
Complaint Description
RVHE: Reagent volume high for Enzyme reagent.
Technical Support
-
Bad Elution pack.
-
Elution Buffer Transfer Mechanism (Dump Truck) may be impeded by tubing/cables causing the reading to be artificially high.
-
Tips being used.
-
Have customer visually inspect Elution buffer pack, make sure septum properly in place.
-
With instrument off, have customer check the movement of the "dump truck" to make sure nothing in impeding, specifically on the Panther side. Logs/curves may show a LLS higher than previous after the transfer mechanism has moved back.
-
Just like with RVHO, best to have customer replace the elution pack that triggered the error (see RVHO entry for reasoning).
Questions to Ask Customer
Request logs.
Log Review
Check c-LLD, reagent aspiration and dispense curves to determine if the issue is related to the reagents or the instrument.
If there are no c-LLD curves for some of the reagents, it is likely instrument is still on a lower SW version using b-LLD instead of c-LLD. See example curves below.
Example Curves
The level sense data after cleaning suggest the capacitive circuit is still a little dirty.
But the level sense data suggest the pipettor is triggering on something else.
-
Check pipettor alignment to elution buffer.
- Inspect elution buffer septum.
- When the pipettor is too close to side walls it can cause fluid to wick up the sides.
- The septum can get wet and pipettor may trigger off the septum.
-
Replace the reagent pipettor.
Pay attention to pipettor mounting and meshing.
Mtus 86, 87, and 88.
Blue line shows last correct level sense. Red line shows the level sense high; R denotes retries.
Field Service
TBD

## RVHO
id="mc-main-content">
RVHO
Reagent Volume High for Oil
Fusion RVHO Flag contains these sections:
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
-
Technical Support
-
RVHO – Why Software Cannot Reschedule Tests
-
RVHO Due to Tecan *117 Tips
-
RVHO with RDFO Due to Pipettor Sticky Plunger
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
Tips.
TS Troubleshooting
Once a Fusion oil pack gets an RVHO flag, the rest of the test orders of that pack will be flagged with RVHO regardless of tips used. This is to prevent customers from refilling reagents themselves.
Customer needs to load a new oil pack and discard the one flagged with RVHO.
Why does it not change to the other oil pack?
From Matt B in sw:
Given the way that the Panther SW has been built, it’s difficult for the system to reschedule tests that are already in process. The system plans out the entire process for each MTU and can’t immediately change to a different fluid or reagent if a problem with that fluid or reagent is discovered. So, if a Fusion pack is found to be faulty then unfortunately all MTUs that were already to use that pack remain scheduled to that pack. There is a complaint opened against the way this works but again, given how the SW already works, it’s not an easy update and has not been prioritized.
Field Service
RVHO – Lookup Oil Pack
Issue:
Customer reported new RVHO after getting new tips, but did not replace oil pack between 2/15 and 2/22.
Search:
Higher liquid level detected by universal reagent.
Same DBID, same oil barcode.
2021-02-15 12:14:06,612|[SCPMThread]|SidecarReagentsManager|SidecarInv|Info|Normal|ScRM.HandleUniversalReagentLldResponse: Higher liquid level detected by universal reagent 'UniversalReagentOilA'. Difference 8585 microliters. Status: (3128,000227422515012200919,2,0,00,02,Oil,Valid,InUse,670,671,0,0,354).
2021-02-22 16:16:07,365|[SCPMThread]|SidecarReagentsManager|SidecarInv|Info|Normal|ScRM.HandleUniversalReagentLldResponse: Higher liquid level detected by universal reagent 'UniversalReagentOilA'. Difference 8552 microliters. Status: (3128,000227422515012200919,2,0,00,02,Oil,Valid,InUse,646,650,0,0,354).
Resolution:
Oil pack must be replaced if RVHO caused by tips. Oil pack can be reused if caused by pipettor.
RVHO – Why Software Cannot Reschedule Tests
Per SW team:
"Given the way that the Panther SW has been built, it’s difficult for the system to reschedule tests that are already in process. The system plans out the entire process for each MTU and can’t immediately change to a different fluid or reagent if a problem with that fluid or reagent is discovered. So, if a Fusion pack is found to be faulty then unfortunately all MTUs that were already to use that pack remain scheduled to that pack. There is a complaint opened against the way this works but again, given how the SW already works, it’s not an easy update and has not been prioritized."
RVHO Due to Tecan *117 Tips
Fusion Pipettor Oil uses Barometric.
1/13: LLD values bounce around a bit. The oil aspiration/dispense pressure suggests extra resistance to flow.
1/17:
Comparing oil against another instrument:
Comparing recon fluid dispense against another instrument – LDT-SARS-CoV2:
RVHO with RDFO Due to Pipettor Sticky Plunger
This looks like a real pipettor problem. (Replace pip.)
Two flags…
-
RVHO: oil too high measurement is truly detecting a liquid level above actual fluid level.
- Level sense detected above – no oil aspirated, will get RDFO flag.
- Level sense detected below fluid level – oil aspirated, usually no flag as oil is still aspirated.
-
RDFO: Oil aspiration/dispense curves show no oil aspirated/dispensed.
Note: The oil pack can be reused as a new pipettor will find correct oil level.
Early trigger from LLD values, close to entry point into oil pack.
Inspecting pressure trace curve (zoom in!).
450-500, the plunger is sticking a bit – highlighted in green.
Red circled is correct fluid height.
No flag on aspirate as we turn off process control here.
But flat line shows air.
RDFO have the Pmax values under 1000.

Customer using multiple PPR tubes and two different recon packs.
Consulted with R&D, and it is spread out in different wells – this looks like leaky vials.
Confirmed with FSE Field Service Engineer. that the customer received CTB-00855, and had a bad lot and was still using it.

The EBH3 flag is high estimated background on channel 3 (ROX). Looking at the before/after scans there is a significant difference in the percent difference from the PEEK sheet values on ROX:

Looking at a well by well analysis you can clearly see the ROX channel and to a lesser extent the other channels were reading low as well.
I would suspect that leaking vials over many runs may have left residue that fluoresced in ROX. Sometimes the liquid that leaks out of the tube drips down the fibers and into the fiber reformatter rather than clustering on the top of the well, however it is a little surprising that there were no signs of any crystals or residue.

Method 3
-
From logs grab @DI files with ebl3 errors.
-
Paste values into excel as text.
-
Sort flag column (sw7.1 = column AY) for contains ebl3 errors.
-
Can use filter again on bank-well column and specific wells should be clear (sw7.1 = column AI).
Alternative filter methods:
- Use pivot table.
- Use excel function "Unique" to bank/well column.
Corrective Action:
-
Establish baseline before cleaning thermocycler by performing all 3 thermocycler scans in service software.
-
Run PantherMain Background, Background and PEEK.
-
Save/record data.
-
PEEK scan decay will determine if TC replacement is necessary.
-
Note: Debris will typically:
- No vial in well: read higher because light reflects off debris.
- Vial in well: read lower as debris blocks the amplified product.
-
Inspect using scope to take pictures and clean wells. Thermal bank should be removed to properly clean fiber heads. Often requires hard scrubbing with supplied optic cleaners.
-
Perform scans again to verify cleaning was effective (repeat as needed).
In this case PEEK scan was more effective than Panther Background Main scan.
Residue around the edge of the fiber head.
TC bank needed to be removed to access the debris.

Install Fusion and Panther Plus COP Config
If a Fusion is being added to a Panther Plus, the Fusion is plugged into J12 on the COP, and the Jumper is discarded.

## Assay  Cartridge Carousel Drawer Target Not Reached
id="mc-main-content">
Assay Cartridge Carousel Drawer Target Not Reached
Topic contains information about how to troubleshoot error code and complaint below.
Error Code
Dec
Location
1096.001.00010
Complaint Description
Assay Cartridge Carousel Drawer target not reached.
Technical Support
- Incorrect loading of cartridge by operator, likely if they try to load cartridges in the back of the drawer, pictured below.
- Dirty home sensor, cartridge carousel PCB connections are loose.
Instrument goes into Panther-only mode, but will continue and finish any Fusion samples already in the thermocycler. To continue running Fusion side:
- Have Customer shutdown the system.
- Open cartridge drawer, and spin the cartridge carousel counterclockwise.
- Remove any cartridge that may be protruding (see picture), rotate carousel clockwise, and reseat the cartridge properly.
- Restart instrument.
In order to avoid error, if loading all cartridges, carousel can be rotated manually to allow empty spots to come to the front and facilitate cartridge loading without errors.
Field Service
If Technical Support troubleshooting above does not work, it will require an FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch.
- Clean Cartridge Carousel home sensor.
- Reseat all connections on Cartridge Carousel PCB.

04/25/2020 06:36:20 Warning 277.000.00029 The temperature between the sensors is out of range within the Assay Cartridge Storage Carousel. The system is unable to start pipetting samples for PCR tests.
04/25/2020 09:45:25 Warning 277.000.00030 The temperature between the sensors is out of range within the Assay Cartridge Storage Carousel. Paused sample pipetting for PCR tests.
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [TemperatureDiffOutErr] from CartridgeCarousel (Critical) [Temperature1: 1507 0.01 degrees C; Temperature2: 1303 0.01 degrees C; ]: 60 00 02 03 4B 00 E3 05 17 05
04/25/2020 12:36:20 (25 05:36:20) [D] (Warning , Low ) [CartridgeCarousel] Assay Cartridge Carousel temperature difference is out of range [Temperature1: 1507 0.01 degrees C; Temperature2: 1303 0.01 degrees C; ] [ 1096.003.00075 ]
60 = Cartridge Carousel
00 = Answer
02 = Send State
03 = Cooling
4B = Temperature Difference out of range
00 = No command responsible
E3 = Temperature 1 reading
05 = Temperature 2 reading
CAN trace (Cycle = 245/1738, Time = 81060.57513) Out: 60 07 00 00 00 05 01 E3 05 00 00 E0 2E
CAN trace (Cycle = 245/1738, Time = 81060.57519) Out: 60 07 00 00 00 06 01 17 05 00 00 E0 2E
Check the cartridge carousel fan – make sure it is the new style (green shrink wrap) PN FAN-00145.
Check/replace storage thermistor – MEL-00995.
If the issue is a failing Peltier, you will need a new Cartridge Carousel – (R)ASY-11379.

## Elution Track Catching
id="mc-main-content">
Elution Track Catching
Complaint: Elution Track catches when moving, and does not fully seat down.
Resolution: Adjust screws underneath the bucket, as Elution Track catches on the black interlock. Reteach to that position.

## Elution Track – Loose Screws
id="mc-main-content">
Elution Track – Loose Screws
Panther Fusion Dump Truck Screws. We have started to notice that the dump truck carrier becomes loose, causing LLD errors on the Panther side during pipetting. We feel that an inspection of the dump truck (2 screws) and arm (1 screw) need to be checked during a TSC. So, please inspect and tighten on all TSCs. This will be added to next revision.

## Fusion Pipettor – Position Out of Tolerance
id="mc-main-content">
Fusion Pipettor – Position Out of Tolerance
Error Codes
Dec
Location
1253.001.00140
1253.001.00141
1253.001.00142
X Axis
Y Axis
Z Axis
Complaint Description
Pipettors (Fusion reagent pipettor and Tube handling robot) movement errors, step loss errors, position out of tolerance.
Technical Support
Troubleshoot similar to Panther errors.
X and Y axis rotated, X is front to back, Y is side to side.
Coordinate may not appear in the messages or health report. Use time stamp and check diagnostic logs or view logs to find coordinate.
Look at Fusion Coordinates sheet to determine location, perform a shutdown, have customer visually inspect.
Refer to Fusion Coordinates .
Restart. If it does not reset, FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch.
If it resets, fusion reagent pipettor is only tested running Fusion samples. Tube handling robot will perform "fusion tubes clearing" during restart from centrifuge and Thermocycler.
For Z axis errors over tube trays check that the tube drawer shutters are in position refer to error: Tube Drawer (Motor 1 or 2) failed to clear light barrier during initialization (1112.004.00038)
Field Service

## Fusion Waste Bag Not Present
id="mc-main-content">
Fusion Waste Bag Not Present
Error Code
Dec
Location
407.051.00007
Complaint Description
The Fusion Waste bag was not emptied/count not resetting.
Technical Support
-
Waste bag not positioned correctly.
-
Waste bag sensors not working or misaligned.
-
Make sure Waste bag has been removed completely and then placed properly so that it blocks the sensors.
-
Look and make sure sensors have not been disconnected or are out of position. Try to reconnect or reposition.
-
To test if a sensor is misaligned or broken: if you remove the bag and the screen still shows it green, the receiving sensor is not seeing the light.
Shine a light from the inside to the right sensor. If receiver sensor is working and received that light, the solid waste will go red on screen, and should go back to green when bag is replaced.
This is a temporary fix to get the waste to reset. FSE Field Service Engineer. should be dispatched.
Field Service
TBD

## PCR Assay Storage Carousel Has Experienced an Error with Its Internal Fan
id="mc-main-content">
PCR Assay Storage Carousel Has Experienced an Error with Its Internal Fan
Error Code
Dec
Location
277.000.00031
Complaint Description
The PCR Assay Storage Carousel has experienced an error with its internal fan. Please contact Technical Support for further guidance with this issue.
Technical Support
Warning message, does not prevent the instrument from running, but in some cases the message is so prevalent (coming up multiple times a minute, ex case 00391754) that the operator cannot work as it puts them back on the messages screen every time it happens. Error refers to the speed of the fan being inadequate, not the carousel temperature. It can happen to all Fusions with original PCR Assay storage cartridge carousel fan (PN-00135)Waste bag sensors not working or misaligned.
Dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. to replace FAN with PN FAN-00145 on next PM. The new fan is cut in to Fusion S/N F217. Also cut into cartridge carousel module PN ASY-12949 NOT in ASY-11379. If ASY-11379 is ordered, a new FAN-00145 needs to be ordered. This is all in TB-01358 (Cartridge Carousel Fan replacement procedure).
Field Service
TBD

## Vial Presence Check Failed at Centrifuge Load for Fusion Pipettor Driver and Arm
id="mc-main-content">
Vial Presence Check Failed at Centrifuge Load for Fusion Pipettor Driver and Arm
Error Code
Dec
Hex
1239.001.00163
N/A
Complaint Description
Pipettor Driver (Fusion Pipettor) Pipettor arm, vial presence check failed at centrifuge load. Fusion Pipettor Driver cap and vial pick retry delay error. Uncapped tube present in associated tube tray. Properly dispose of tray when processing has completed. (DCR flag)
Technical Support
-
Sensor failed at centrifuge load
-
Dropped vial, DITI issue
Have customer look for a dropped vial. If capped and accessible through the front, shutdown instrument, remove vial and put in waste. Also remove tube tray that instrument was picking from, replace with a full one.
Opening log files on viewlogs or Notepad+ you can find the error and the coordinate at the time of the error to find out which tube tray it was using if unclear.
Customer or FSE Field Service Engineer. should clean the diti to help with this issue. Clean with alcohol wipe. Restart instrument, upon restart thermocyler and centrifuge positions will be checked and the vial will be unloaded if present.
Field Service
FSE should install new diti sleeve if not already done. (TB-01627) If sensor is faulty, FSE will replace sensor on load side. Only way to test it is running Fusion samples.
Fusion Coordinates:
Note: Picture with trays and TC positions at the end of the document.
Remember on Fusion side:
-
X axis is front to back.
-
Y axis is left to right.
Coordinates do not show in the messages, you have to find them with the time stamp in the diagnostics log report or health report, or use view logs.

## Pipettor Driver – Tube Handling Robot – Vial Presence  Check Failed at Centrifuge Unload
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor Driver – Tube Handling Robot – Vial Presence Check Failed at Centrifuge Unload
Error Code
Dec
Location
1239.000.00162
0x00.0x00.0x01
Complaint Description
Pipettor Driver (Tube Handling Robot) vial presence check failed at centrifuge unload. PCR tests cannot be started because of an unhandled tube loss in the Fusion centrifuge. Please call technical support. An unrecoverable error occurred within the Fusion sidecar causing the system to move to a Panther Only state
Technical Support
- Sensor failed at centrifuge unload
- Dropped vial, DITI issue
Do not have the customer remove the consumable, but look for where it was dropped. An FSE Field Service Engineer. must be dispatched in order to enable the thermocycler and Fusion side, unless the FSE remotes in to enable the Fusion side.
Customer/FSE should clean the diti to help with this issue. Clean with alcohol wipe.
FSE should install new DITI sleeve if not already done.
If sensor is faulty, FSE will replace sensor on unload side.
Field Service
2020-09-10 22:06:12,023|[COP_ChannelAsyncQueue_TransferThreadWorker]|SideCarMsgHandler|SidecarComm|Info|Error|SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [Vialpresencecheckfail_CfUnldErr] from ComGenDriver (Fatal) [SourceCoo: 54; VialSensor_Centrifuge: NoPresenceDetected; CapSensor_Arm: NoPresenceDetected; ]: EF 00 03 00 A2 3B 36 00 00 00
2020-09-10 22:06:12,023|[COP_ChannelAsyncQueue_TransferThreadWorker]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error|09/11/2020 03:06:12 (10 22:06:12) [E] (Critical , High ) [ComGenDriver] Pipettor Driver (Tube Handling Robot) vial presence check failed at centrifuge unload [SourceCoo: 54; VialSensor_Centrifuge: NoPresenceDetected; CapSensor_Arm: NoPresenceDetected; ] [1239.000.00162]
Recommend the following:
With CapSensor_Arm: NoPresenceDetected errors, e.g. failing to pick or picks and loses the cap/vial.
Resolution: We’ve found good success cleaning surfaces where the caps and vial contact.
Thermal cycler bank wells – only clean surfaces with the thermal cycler cleaning solution.
Centrifuge buckets – can be cleaned with alcohol/DI water
Diti (Vial/Reagent) - make sure to wipe the diti area well. This can be cleaned with alcohol/DI water.
Check the centrifuge for dropped cap/vial.
Forgot to mention – check the unload cap/vial sensor (on the centrifuge).
Check/clean diti and eject sleeve on pipettor, install new diti sleeve if not already done.
Verify Pipettor and Vial Robot teaching.
In the GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. Enable Thermocycler Banks and Centrifuge (procedure in the SM).

## Pipettor Failed to Eject Tip
id="mc-main-content">
Pipettor Failed to Eject Tip
Error Code
Dec
Location
Complaint Description
Fusion reagent pipettor, failed to eject tip.
Technical Support
Possible Root Cause
- Dirty DITI
- Plastic accumulating on DITI
TS Troubleshooting
- Shutdown instrument.
- If tip is still present on pipettor, remove tip with a kimwipe, wearing gloves, dispose in the Fusion waste.
- Clean pipettor DITI with alcohol wipe/swab. Make sure they wipe the rounded section of the DITI real well. There’s some plastic that can accumulate there
- Restart instrument.
Fusion reagent pipettor can only be tested running Fusion samples.
FSE Field Service Engineer. should install new DITI sleeve, if not already done. (TB-01627)
Field Service

Panther Reagent Pipettor
Panther Sample Pipettor
Panther Reagent Pipettor
Fusion Tube Handling Robot
Fusion Reagent Pipettor
Complaint Description
Fusion reagent pipettor, No Encoder Steps Detected, unrecoverable error Fusion side.
Technical Support
- Possible Flex cable issue
Customer can try shutdown restart, if there are pipettor communication errors during restart FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch is needed. If it resets OK, only way to test is to run Fusion samples.
Field Service
2020-10-16 16:06:39,085|[ProcessEvent]|EventLogMessenger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error| <>(Fatal) 20:06:38.749: Reagent Pipettor Z-axis encoder failure (no encoder steps detected) (Ev=84) [FD.0E.84] bytes: FD 7E 03 0E 84 01
2020-10-16 16:06:39,087|[ProcessEvent]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error|10/16/2020 20:06:39 (16 16:06:39) [E] (Fatal , High ) [PipettorSystem] Reagent Pipettor Z-axis encoder failure (no encoder steps detected) ID=6998 PickupDiTi 'AmpReagentPipettingStep' (Amplification) PlannedStart=20:06:37.249 worst event at 20:06:38.749, start=20:06:38.149 end=20:06:39.049 (MTU=1 BarcodeID=1964241333, samples=[0] 131058/011126894715032248081, [1] 131059/011226929815032250230, [2] 131018/0001, [3] 131019/0002, [4] 131020/0003, , cmd params: Amplification (RP) Index=0 finalZ=0 ) [0xFD.0x0E.0x0084] [253.014.00132]
I do not know what is going on, but these are the parts:
- reagent pip z-motor
- y-sledge board
- x-sledge board
- y-flex
- x-flex
- pipmain board

## Rotary Distributor Cartridge Present After Place
id="mc-main-content">
Rotary Distributor Cartridge Present After Place
Error Code
Dec
Hex
1032.003.00056
Complaint Description
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [CartridgePresentAfterPlaceErr] from RotaryDistributor (Fatal) []: 20 00 03 03 38 21
01/14/2021 16:54:07 (14 11:54:07) [E] (Critical , High ) [RotaryDistributor] Rotary Distributor cartridge present after place [] [1032.003.00056]
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [TaskProcessingErr] from DistributorCarouselDriver (Fatal) [Task: CartridgeTransfer; ]: E1 00 03 00 50 64 02
Technical Support
Data pending.
Field Service
The Cartridge Carousel sensor may be stuck.
This happened on another instrument back in April. After cleaning and clearing, it has not returned.
Looking at the ROT distributor head board, that sensor is not replaceable.
- I would verify in ssw it is working correctly before cleaning.
- Inspect the sensor for damage.
- Unplug/reseat.
FSE replaced Rotary distributor MTU presence switch.
Rotary Distributor: Cartridge and MTU presence sensors.

## Rotary Distributor Driver – ID Is Unknown, Cannot Pick Unit
id="mc-main-content">
Rotary Distributor Driver – ID Is Unknown, Cannot Pick Unit
Error Code
Dec
Hex
1225.000.00033
Complaint Description
[DistributorCarouselDriver] Rotary Distributor Driver (ID is unknown, cannot pick unit)
Technical Support
Data pending.
Field Service
Notes: This is a downstream processing error. Logs need to be reviewed to find upstream errors that would cause timing delays.
Running XE2
Resolution:
Upgrade to XE3 or later.
Computer Time Drift Errors
Resolution:
In the logs, look for computer time drift errors preceding the Rotary Distributor Error. MKS #2875603.
-
Set up auto purge for Results, Activity Logs, Maintenance Logs, Message Logs for ninety days.
-
Optimize the hard drive.
-
Replace the COP board.
-
If that does not work, replace the computer.
Too Many Results Selected
Resolution:
This occurred because the operator selected 3,420 results to be sent while the system was in assay processing.
2020-04-25 13:06:16,250 DoShowMessage[211]: modal dialog activated, text: 3420 results selected. Transmission will take approximately 26 minutes. Do you want to continue?
2020-04-25 13:20:48,197 SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [UnknownIDErr] from DistributorCarouselDriver (Fatal) [ID: 63; ]: E1 00 03 00 21 51 3F 00
2020-04-25 13:20:48,200 04/25/2020 17:20:48 (25 13:20:48) [E] (Critical , High ) [DistributorCarouselDriver] Rotary Distributor Driver (ID is unknown, can not pick unit) [ID: 63; ] [1225.000.00033]
This puts a huge stress on the system. Due to this, system software became bogged down attempting to process the request, and eventually led to the unknown ID error.
They should be able to run without issue, but we should recommend that they do not send a large amount of results to the LIS Laboratory Information System. manually while in AP. We have a known issue with the way our software handles these big requests, and it will lead to these types of errors.

id="mc-main-content">
Rotary Distributor Hook Drive Suffered Step Loss or Stalled
Error Codes

Hook Drive
1032.018.00081
Hook Drive Head
Complaint Description
Rotary Distributor hook drive suffered step loss or stalled.
Technical Support
Obstruction or stuck MTU.
-
Use diagnostic logs or View logs to find out the position. Rotary positions at T:\Technical Service\Fusion.Fusion Team\Fusion\Troubleshooting and Tips , and below.
-
Instrument will go into Panther Only mode. When possible, do a full shutdown-restart.
-
During initialization, instrument will use Rotary distributor hook to unload MTUs (serves as test).
-
If reset works, try a small untested load for Fusion.
-
If error repeats, customer can use instrument in Panther only mode. FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch needed.
-
If it is a repeating error, FSE dispatch recommended.
Field Service
Example:
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [NotMovingSequenceErr] from RotaryDistributor (Fatal) [AccessPosition: MagneticElution0; ]: 20 00 03 12 51 21 0C
>01/11/2023 04:32:28 (10 20:32:28) [D] (Critical , High ) [RotaryDistributor] Rotary Distributor (HookDriveHead) step loss or stall at MagneticElution0 [AccessPosition: MagneticElution0; ] [1032.018.00081]
>SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [NotMovingErr] from RotaryDistributor (Fatal) [StallPositionSI: 456 0,1 degrees; StallPositionMS: 652 micro steps; TargetPositionSI: 1104 0,1 degrees; TargetPositionMS: 1577 micro steps; ]: 20 00 03 12 0A 03 C8 01 8C 02 50 04 29 06
>01/11/2023 04:32:28 (10 20:32:28) [E] (Critical , High ) [RotaryDistributor] Rotary Distributor hook drive suffered step loss or stalled (stall position 456 SI, 652 MS) [StallPositionSI: 456 0,1 degrees; StallPositionMS: 652 micro steps; TargetPositionSI: 1104 0,1 degrees; TargetPositionMS: 1577 micro steps; ] [1032.018.00010]
>SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [TaskProcessingErr] from DistributorCarouselDriver (Fatal) [Task: MTUTransfer; ]: E1 00 03 00 50 51 01
>01/11/2023 04:32:28 (10 20:32:28) [D] (Critical , High ) [DistributorCarouselDriver] Rotary Distributor Driver Error [Task: MTUTransfer; ] [1225.000.00080]
The spindle (1) is missing the screw (2) which attaches to the plate. This spindle prevents the head from rocking. Consequently, RD flops around.

2022-04-01 16:45:41,437|[ProcessEvent]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Normal|04/01/2022 23:45:41 (01 16:45:41) [D] (Message , Info ) [LinearDistributor] Linear Distributor theta motor lost some steps. Position 1 ID=7535 MoveMTU 'Amp Reagent Addition' PlannedStart=23:45:34.872: , start=23:45:36.772 end=23:45:41.372 (MTU=3 BarcodeID=2172122782, samples=461588/631131190815102262909, 461589/631231191715112239996, , cmd params: LinearDistributor.0 -> AmpLoadStation.0 ). Event [0x10.0x00.0x0061] at 23:45:41.372 bytes: 10 21 01 00 61 01 06 [016.000.00097]
Troubleshooting: Perform HO test in service software. Watch LD to HO interaction, likely LD is too close to HO in x-direction causing interference between LD/HO.
Resolution: Teach LD, move LD farther away from HO in x-direction and reteach so hook will compensate for distance. This allows HO and LD to rotate without interference.

## Thermocycler Background RFU Too High
id="mc-main-content">
Thermocycler Background RFU Too High
Error Codes
Dec

1160.001.00086

Bank 12
Complaint Description
Background RFU reading too high.
Thermocycler (Bank X): Thermocycler background RFU too high, vial position Y.
The sidecar can only process at a reduced throughput. Disabled Thermocycler Banks X.
Technical Support
May be seen in specific thermocycler wells.
Possible Root Cause
-
Debris/dust in TC well.
-
Issue with thermocycler/lamp/optics.
TS Troubleshooting
Customer can run with banks disabled.
The Thermocycler (TC) performs bank self-test across ALL 12 banks:
-
Upon initialization (sw 6.2 and 7.1).
-
Upon exiting TC power save (sw 7.1 and above).
- Explain the issue to the customer, you can relay “Samples go from 1 min between sample results to 1 min 20 seconds in between sample results" when 1 bank is disabled, so customer can better understand the impact.
- Shutdown restart to bring bank back to operation with sw 6.2 can be done, but when convenient for the customer, not necessary right away if only running Panther side.
- If customer has 7.2 SW and above, you could ask to do a TC cleaning.
- Ask the customer to continue to run and notify us if other banks become impacted or the same bank keeps getting disabled.
- If customer is not satisfied or you feel resistance on their part to continue to run, notify FSEs and dispatch.
- If they report multiple banks disabled or the same bank disabled over and over communicate to the FSEs and dispatch.
- Follow-up with the customer to see if the bank went back into operation (like a Magwash), if this is the situation, close the case as you would normally. If the issue persists as mentioned above, please let the FSE Field Service Engineer. know and dispatch.
- See also Thermocycler Background RFU Too Low .
Field Service
-
FSE should perform a visual check using scope on affected wells, and clean if needed.
-
FSE can compare background readings from current and previous logs to determine if they have shifted. May be on half of TC wells, as there are two Fluorometers, one for banks 1-6, one for 7-12.
The FSE should clean those specific wells or upgrade to the automatic nest cleaner. Scan background and peek lid. No thermocycler replacement is needed if no troubleshooting has been done. This is documented in TB-01457 (Thermocycler Scanning and Cleaning instructions) and TB-01078 (Fiber Nest Installation and Cleaning Procedure)
Fusion Thermocycler is designed to run with banks out of service. This allows customer to run with reduced throughput. When a well fails PantherMain Background scan, the entire banks will be taken out of service. A bank may come back into service if it passes the next PantherMain Background scan.
Background RFU too high or low error can occur when PantherMain Background scan is performed:
- Shortly after initialization, after thermocycler unload process has completed and no vials are present in thermocycler.
- Upon exit of thermocycler power save.
Background RFU failure should not be confused with “ebl” or “ebh” errors. “ebl” and “ebh” occur with an actual specimen vial in the well during assay processing.
Log example of banks taken out of service:
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [BACKGROUND_RFU_LOWErr] from ThermoCycler (Critical) [Rfu: 265; ColorId: 0; VialPosition: 56;
]: A0 00 02 0C 55 00 09 01 00 00 00 00 38 00
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [BACKGROUND_RFU_LOWErr] from ThermoCycler (Critical) [Rfu: 118; ColorId: 0; VialPosition: 39; ]: A0 00 02 08 55 00 76 00 00 00 00 00 27 00
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [BACKGROUND_RFU_LOWErr] from ThermoCycler (Critical) [Rfu: 37; ColorId: 0; VialPosition: 34; ]: A0 00 02 07 55 00 25 00 00 00 00 00 22 00
-
RFU value (scan value)
-
ColorId (flurometer channel 0 = fam, 1 = hex, 2= rox, 3= red647, 4 = red677)
-
Vial position 56 (bank 12), position 39 (bank 8), position 34 (bank 7).
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [BankStatesChangedErr] from ThermocyclerDriver (Message) [ExceptionCommandId: 0; [Bank: 1; BankState: Enabled; ]; [Bank: 2; BankState: Enabled; ]; [Bank: 3; BankState: Enabled; ]; [Bank: 4; BankState: Enabled; ]; [Bank: 5; BankState: Enabled; ]; [Bank: 6; BankState: Enabled; ]; [Bank: 7; BankState: Disabled; ]; [Bank: 8; BankState: Disabled; ]; [Bank: 9; BankState: Disabled; ]; [Bank: 10; BankState: Disabled; ]; [Bank: 11; BankState: Disabled; ]; [Bank: 12; BankState: Disabled; ]; ]: E4 00 00 00 52 00 01 00 02 00 03 00 04 00 05 00 06 00 07 01 08 01 09 01 0A 01 0B 01 0C 01
2020-05 14 23:28:54,766 [SCPMThread] EventLogger EventLogEntry Error 05/15/2020 06:28:54 (14 23:28:54) [E] (Critical , High ) [SidecarProcessManagement] The sidecar can only process at a reduced throughput. Disabled Thermocycler Banks: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. [278.000.00002]
-
This line indicates banks taken out of service.
Common failures and fixes:
Best practice – record thermocycler serial number, inspect well positions using camera/scope, and perform thermocycler scans. Scans are saved at C:\Panther\Panther Service Software\log\RFUTest.
-
Background too high, typically debris or salts from leaky vials.
- Inspect wells, perform scans.
- Clean wells: remove banks, used DI water and cleaning solution, repeat until scans are good.
TSE Example
TBD
Related flag
ebl3

## Thermocycler Driver – Command ID Not Implemented or Wrong Command Length
id="mc-main-content">

Complaint Description
Fatal errors due to firmware not up to date.
Problem: Thermocycler communication error preceded main controller command failed.
Technical Support
Data pending.
Field Service
Isolation: Verify FW is up to date across the modules.
Fix: Run instrument setup for sidecar.
Fusion COP is wrong: 4.0000 should be 4.0012.

## Thermocycler Fluorometer/Motor Assembly APV Error
id="mc-main-content">
Thermocycler Fluorometer/Motor Assembly APV Error
Error Codes
Dec
Fluorometer
1160.015.00095
1160.016.00095
1
2
Complaint Description
Thermocycler (Fluorometer X): Thermocycler
fluorometer/motor assembly APV error.
The sidecar can only process at a reduced throughput.
Disabled Thermocycler Banks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Or the sidecar can only process at a reduced throughput.
Disabled Thermocycler Banks: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12.
Runs display TCF flags.
Technical Support
Thermocycler error is on the fluorometer motor. The thermocycler APV error is due to a worn slip ring on RTF-1 (banks 1-6) or RTF-2 (banks 7-12).
FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch needed, but instrument will run with the other half of the thermocycler if customer needs to continue running.
Field Service
Problem:
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [APV_FLUORASSYErr] from ThermoCycler (Critical) [ApvOperation: RfuMeasurement; ApvLateEarlyFlag: Late; TimeError: 22; ]: A0 00 02 0F 5F 00 05 00 00 00 16 00 00 00
08/22/2020 01:42:37 (21 20:42:37) [E] (Warning , Low ) [ThermoCycler] Thermocycler (Fluorometer1) :Thermocycler fluorometer/motor assembly APV error. [ApvOperation: RfuMeasurement;
ApvLateEarlyFlag: Late; TimeError: 22; ] [1160.015.00095]
Issue: Due to slip ring assembly wear. Sometimes the slip ring fails and causes loss in electrical signal. Because the fluorometer is rotating, the slip ring is needed to transfer information from the spinning assembly to the mounting cable connection.
Resolution: When this occurs, best practice is to replace both slip rings. Will need to order quantity: 2, to replace both.
FUSION, THERMOCYCLER, WIRE HARNESS, SLIP RING
CBL-02987

## Thermocycler Fluorometer Motor Assembly APV Motor Movement Error
id="mc-main-content">
Thermocycler Fluorometer Motor Assembly APV Motor Movement Error
Error Codes
Dec
Motor
1160.013.00095
1160.014.00095
1
2
Complaint Description
Thermocycler Flourometer Motor assembly movement error.
Technical Support
Data pending.
Field Service
2022-05-02 02:13:11,696|[COP_ChannelAsyncQueue_TransferThreadWorker]|SideCarMsgHandler|SidecarComm|Info|Error|SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [EXCESSIVE_MOTOR_ERRORSErr] from ThermoCycler (Critical) [Steps: 4808; StepLimit: 8; ]: A0 00 02 0E CA 00 C8 12 00 00 08 00 00 00
2022-05-02 02:13:11,700|[COP_ChannelAsyncQueue_TransferThreadWorker]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error|05/02/2022 06:13:11 (02 02:13:11) [E] (Warning , Low ) [ThermoCycler] Thermocycler (Motor2) :Thermocycler fluorometer/motor assembly movement error. [Steps: 4808; StepLimit: 8; ] [1160.014.00202]
Issue: Movement failure – suspect failure of belt drive, encoder, motor.
- FL2 Belt may be too tight.
- The home flag may be loose or askew.
- Connector cables may be loose.
Things to check:
- Verify that all connections to and from fluorometer 2 to the TCM board are plugged in correctly.
- Verify that the slip ring is installed properly in fluorometer 2.
- Check if the belt on FL2 is extremely tight (if so, then RMA the unit).
Resolution:
A. When this occurs, best practice is to replace both slip rings. Will need to order quantity: 2, to replace both.
FUSION, THERMOCYCLER, WIRE HARNESS,SLIP RING – CBL-02987
B. Thermocycler replacement.

08/22/2020 04:05:45 (21 23:05:45) [E] (Warning , Low ) [ThermoCycler] Thermocycler (MainController) :Thermocycler main controller command failed. [Data1: 0; Data2: 0; ] [1160.000.00042]
SMH.OnPayloadReceived: [INVALID_CMD_STATEErr] from ThermoCycler (Critical) [Data1: 0; Data2: 0; ]: A0 00 02 00 2A 4B 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
Resolution
On restart, there iss a failure to establish connection with Fusion COP.
Not sure if they have restarted since.
I would inspect CAN connection between Panther and Fusion.
Inspect connections from power supply to Fusion board.
Proactively replace the black fuse where the Fusion CAN bus plugs into Panther CAN bus port.

## Thermocycler  Scans Examples
id="mc-main-content">
Thermocycler Scans Examples
Example 1
We are experiencing a reading ranging from about 278 to 290 on position 4;3 of the thermocycler in Scan Back Ground, which is flagging. In Panther Main BackGround Scan it is not flagging. Attached are well photos and the RFU scan. "
Reviewed scans and confirmed it was flagging 4-3 on Hex channel.
Per Ayra
The same fiber core stays illuminated regardless of angle viewed with camera, it could be debris on the bottom side
Manually cleaned with cleaner and water with same result, but a cloudy chunk fell off.
Ayra suggested having FSEs remove the rear of the Thermocycler housing. Pulled fluorometer out.
Then following this routing find the fiber and inspect for any debris.
FSEs found apparent dust/spec on that fiber of the fluorometer. Cleaned this off with TC manual cleaning solution. Reassembled Thermocycler. Scans passed.

## Tube Drawer  (Motor 1 or 2) Failed to Clear Light Barrier During Initialization
id="mc-main-content">
Tube Drawer (Motor 1 or 2) Failed to Clear Light Barrier During Initialization
Error Code
Dec
Hex
1112.003.00038
1112.004.00038
Motor 1
Motor 2
Complaint Description
Tube Drawer (Motor 1 or 2) failed to clear light barrier during initialization.
Technical Support
-
Reaction Tube shutter motor failed.
-
Reaction Tube Shutter misplaced.
With instrument off, have the customer check the reaction tube shutters placement, make sure it is flushed and the motor pin is in the shutter slot.
Check if the motors turn smoothly and the same. If okay, restart instrument, runs controls and blank to test dispatch if error repeats during initializaton. Instrument will start up on Panther Only mode, okay to run Panther side.
If motors do not turn smoothly, dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
TBD

## Tube Handling  Robot Driver Vial Presence Check Failed at Thermocycler Unload
id="mc-main-content">
Tube Handling Robot Driver Vial Presence Check Failed at Thermocycler Unload
Error Code
Dec
Hex
1239.000.00174
0x00.0x00.0x01
Complaint Description
Tube Handling Robot Driver vial presence check failed at thermocycler unload.
The sidecar can only process at a reduced throughput.
Disabled Thermocycler Banks X.
Technical Support
- Sensor failed at centrifuge load.
- Dropped vial, DITI issue.
Customer can continue running with disabled TC bank. In order to see if bank can be placed in operation again.
-
Shutdown instrument.
-
Have customer look for a dropped vial. If capped and accessible through the front, shutdown instrument, remove vial and put in waste.
-
Customer/ FSE Field Service Engineer. should clean the DITI to help with this issue. Clean with alcohol wipe.
FSE should install new DITI sleeve if not already done. (TB-01627)
-
Restart instrument. Upon restart, Handling Robot Driver checks for tubes in thermocycler and centrifuge positions, and will unload if possible. If unable to unload, it will likely give a background reading message/error during restart keeping the bank disabled, but not the whole TC.
-
FSE will have to be dispatched to remove vial.
If sensor is faulty, FSE will replace sensor on unload side.
Field Service

## Tube Handling Robot Eject Motor Overload
id="mc-main-content">
Tube Handling Robot Eject Motor Overload
Error Code
Dec
Hex
1253.004.00010
0x4E5.0x00.0x0A
Complaint Description
Tube Handling Robot Eject Motor overload detected.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
Field Service
- <Evaluation 1>
- <Evaluation 2>
Technical Support
-
Locate Tube Handling Robot
Verify if the Tube handling Robot is over the Waste Chute.
-
If Robot is Over the Waste Chute, have operator check for Tips and Vials jammed in the Waste Chute.
-
Open Fusion Waste Drawer slowly, as Tips are likely to be jammed on top of the Waste Bag.
-
Remove any Tips or Vials from Fusion Waste Drawer area.
-
Ensure the operator has Fusion Waste Bag is fully seated.
-
The Waste Chute will need to be completely empty before attempting to process samples. FSE Field Service Engineer. dispatch is likely, due to difficulty of removing all obstructions from the Waste Chute.
-
If the Tube Handling Robot is anywhere other than the Waste Chute:
Attempt to perform a full system shutdown and restart.
If initialization passes, have customer run and monitor.
Field Service

TEST:

## Customer Cannot Replace Fluid Kit
id="mc-main-content">
Customer Cannot Replace Fluid Kit
Error Code:
Dec
Hex
ARM
No error code
Complaint Description:
- Both fluid kits are being used at the same time. Note: This is normal. The instrument will use both kits to continue processing samples.
- Fluid kit count has not reached 0.
- MKS 2472203 - Panther SW 7.1 & 7.2 (Very Rare). Note: If waste is unloaded (during assay processing) at the same time that a leading prime MTU was to be disposed, both kits could remain in the "In Use" state.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
Technical Support
Note: As samples are loaded on the instrument, the test count shown to customers can drop to 0. However, the fluids may not have actually been used yet. The customer will need to wait until one of the kits is not In Use to replace the kit.
Instruct customer to wait until one fluid kit is not In Use (on Universal Fluid Bay screen) to replace. Note: Yellow Continuous Arrows will show when a kit is ready to be replaced.
Instruct customer to wait until a fluid kit has 0 tests left and is not In Use (on Universal Fluid Bay screen) to replace. Note: Yellow Continuous Arrows will show when a kit is ready to be replaced.
Wait until assay processing finishes to replace the fluid kit(s). Note: This is the solution for MKS 2472203.
Field Service
TBD

## MTU Sidecar Carrier Was Not Picked or Placed Correctly
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Sidecar Carrier Was Not Picked or Placed Correctly
Error Code:
Dec
Hex
083.001.00055
0x53.0x01.0x0037
Complaint Description:
MTU Sidecar Carrier was not picked or placed correctly.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Sensor is obstructed
- Poorly placed carrier
Technical Support
- Make sure the sensor is not blocked. Ask customer to check for dropped tiplets or obstructions and remove them.
- Shutdown and restart instrument.
- Dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
Sensor is obstructed
Check for an object (e.g. tiplet) obstructing the sensor.
Check that carrier is fully seated on loading bay drawer or on scissor.
Resolution
Remove obstruction.
Clean sensor if necessary.
Test
Reset and perform MTU Expansion OQ X2.
Images show clean and unobstructed sensors.
Images show clean and unobstructed sensors.
Poorly placed carrier
Check that the carrier is fully seated, and seated correctly on pins of the scissors or loading bay drawer.
Check for any obstruction, such as cables out of place.
Resolution
Properly seat carrier.
Secure cables as necessary.
Check sidecar alignment to Panther.
Check teaching and reteach as necessary.
Test
Reset and perform MTU Expansion OQ X2.
TSE Technical Service Engineer. Review
In some cases, the scissor home sensor is not properly mounted or adjusted.
Left: MTU spacing as received from Stratec. // Right: Scissors at position 2.
Left: MTU spacing after home sensor adjustment. Right: Scissors at position 2.

## MTU Sidecar Door Failed to Unlock
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Sidecar Door Failed to Unlock
Error Code
Dec
Hex
258.000.00029
Complaint Description
Warning: Unlocking of MTU Expansion module door failed. The system will retry. Please ensure the door is not pushed!
Detailed description: Solenoid locking pin scraping on edge of hole during unlock.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
Field Service
- MTU Sidecar Door Failed to Unlock
- Hard stop not being adjusted correctly
- Additional metadata
- Mounting bracket not being adjusted correctly
Technical Support
- Ensure customer is not pulling on or attempting to open the MTU Door while the Door is unlocking.
- Perform a system shutdown and restart. If issue reoccurs after restart dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
User is pulling on flap while door is locked
Description: Solenoid locking pin scraping on edge of hole during unlock because user pulled on the flap at an inappropriate time.
Diagnostic: Door is in correct position when closed.
Containment: Instruct user to let go of flap if door does not unlock. Push it closed if necessary. If retries are exhausted, the following message appears: Warning 258.000.00036 MTU Expansion module experienced a problem with drawer. Please try to shake the flap to unlock it. Then open and close the flap again.
Solenoid will depower. User needs to open the flap, pull out the drawer, close the drawer and the flap, and MTU inventory should proceed normally.
Solution: Not needed.
Hard stop not being adjusted correctly
Description: Solenoid locking pin scraping on edge of hole during unlock as a result of hard stop not being adjusted correctly.
Diagnostic: Door is visibly not in correct position when closed. There is a gap between loading flap and cover. User pushes door closed and friction between interlock pin and hole keeps pin from retracting for unlock.
Verify user is not interacting with door's initial attempts to unlock, causing pin to scrape.
Valid diagnostics include:
- Logging - Panther / Fusion log, GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. log, Service Software log.
- Panther/Fusion DB’s, such as Waveform DB, Reliability DB.
- Visual inspection of the state of a mechanical component, LED, jumper settings, cables seating, or GUI in Service Software.
- Audible noise.
- OQ tests results.
- Voltages measured with a voltmeter or oscilloscope traces.
If possible, provide an example of the diagnostic that confirms the failure mode, and what the diagnostic looks like when everything is OK.
Containment: Fill in the gap with lab tape. Instruct users to let the spring pull the door closed.
Solution: Adjust hard stop so that position of door is correct when closed, and locking pin is centered in hole – may also require adjustment of solenoid mounting bracket.
It should be able to reset, as hard stop is not in play during homing.
Lift home is at the bottom of the sidecar unit, so counter-balance would be close to top of MTU sidecar.
Hardstop comes into play when lift moves to loading position.
Notes:
Move the weight all the way down against the stop.
Define a distance of 50mm + 5mm between the two z-guidance-lays / right, and the roof of the Frame A subdivision of a Message, used to allow periodic communication housekeeping such as error checks and acknowledgements. -MTU-Loader.
Additional metadata
- SR #
- Logfile location
- RCC Code
- Submitter's name
- Module
Mounting bracket not being adjusted correctly
Description: Solenoid locking pin scraping on edge of hole during unlock, as a result of interlock mounting bracket not being adjusted correctly.
Diagnostic: Door is visibly in correct position when closed, but pin is not aligned with hole. User pushes door closed, and friction between interlock pin and hole keeps pin from retracting for unlock.
Verify user is not interacting with door's initial attempts to unlock, causing pin to scrape.
Containment: Instruct users to let the spring pull the door closed. There will be a gap. Fill in the gap with lab tape.
Solution: Adjust hard stop so that position of door is correct when closed and locking pin is centered in hole – may also require adjustment of solenoid mounting bracket.

## MTU Sidecar Lift Drive Target Not Reached
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Sidecar Lift Drive Target Not Reached
Error Code
Dec
Hex
083.003.00010
0x53.0x03.0x000A
Complaint Description
10/24/2022 17:20:59 (24 13:20:59) [E] (Critical , High ) [MtuExpansion] MTU Sidecar Lift Drive Target (3) not reached, stopped at 178 (AutomaticModuleEvent) [0x53.0x03.0x000A] bytes: 53 00 03 03 0A 03 B2 FF 6E FF [083.003.00010]
Technical Support
Pending.
Field Service
Reminder: Ensure Midbay is completely closed and locked.
Interference with Counterbalance
Resolution
Is the failure occurring at approximately the same spot? Maybe +/- 10 steps, indicating something is challenging movement.
Check the counterbalance and its track for any obstruction or interference, and remove the foreign object.
Belt Tension
Resolution
Are the belt tensions off between each other, causing binding with the guide rails? Check and retension belts as needed.
Case 1
Failed while moving carrier from storage #3 to Loading Position.
Error from Log Files:
2023-05-05 04:38:53,538 [StSerClient:COP->PC] MessageHandler RS232 NormalCOP->PC  53 23 03 01 B3 53 00 03 03 0A 03 E8 29 53 29 53 29
Errored out moving carrier from Loading Position to Storage #3:
-
53 - 53 – MTU Expansion Unit
-
23 - 23 – Move Carrier
-
03 - 03 - Fatal
-
01 - 01 – Subassembly Sidecar Motion Control
-
B3 - B3 – Sub Module Fatal Error Occurred
00 – Position A (Loading Position)
03 – Position B (Storage Position 3)
Description
While servicing because of a hardware failure due to an MTU jam I observed that the Lift drive rubs against the metal plate at the bottom/front of the MTU loading drawer of the sidecar. When the scissor drive attempts to pick up a carrier at the loading position you can hear a metal-on-metal rubbing. Sometimes, while in service mode, it would jam because of the contact. You can see the wear from the rubbing on the lift drive.
I could not see any way of adjusting the scissor drive to allow for clearance when it extends to pick up a carrier at the loading position. The plate in question (at front bottom of the sliding drawer) has two screws at the bottom but it also has pins that keep it aligned with no play to allow for adjustment. I was having trouble reteaching the loading position because the Lift kept hitting the drawer plate causing a failure of the teaching. This was until I realized that there is a tiny bit of play in the drawer when closed. If the drawer is slammed shut the plate interferes with the lift. If however, you pull back on the drawer slightly after closing, this gives enough clearance to allow for teaching and for the Lift to pick up a carrier without jamming (you often still hear the rubbing though).
Resolution
There was not enough clearance for the scissors to go into the MTU loading drawer. This clearance has to do with the latch position. The latch adjustment is very critical. The optimal clearance is about 1/8” inch between the scissors and the edge of the opening of the MTU loading drawer.
We used an Allen wrench set as gage, positioning the key in between the latch and the plate behind the latch, to get to the right position of the latch, so that when the drawer is closed, the drawer is flush with the sensor plate. Refer to second image below. Maximize the gap between the scissors and the drawer opening space for the scissors to move into drawer. We tried Allen keys from 1.5mm to 5mm. The one that worked the best was 3mm.
Bottom view, to show sensor plate and the MTU loading drawer above it.
