## MTU Sidecar Pusher Drive Target (0) Not Reached, Stopped at 0
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Sidecar Pusher Drive Target (0) Not Reached, Stopped at 0
Error Code:
Dec
Hex
083.002.00010
0x53.0x02.0x0A
Complaint Description:
MTU Sidecar Pusher Drive target (0) not reached, stopped at 0.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Dirty Sensor
- Bad Main PCB (MME-03794)
Technical Support
Technical support to put desired troubleshooting information here.
Field Service
Dirty Sensor
This error occurs in Panther system or in Service SW, when there is a carrier in the MTU Sidecar Loader Drawer, the carrier is empty, and "Push MTU" dialog button is pushed. It does not fail when MTU is present on the carrier, so MTU sidecar OQ passes test. The equivalent error in SSW comes with the message in the attached picture.
RESOLUTION:
Replacing PCB did not work.
Moved pusher into home sensor to verify triggering properly.
Cleaned sensor and flag.
Perform AutoTeach End of Travel and ensure there is an empty carrier installed in the loading drawer.
TEST:
Run a prime in GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. with only 10 MTU’s to ensure all MTU’s will exhaust and no errors noted.
Bad Main PCB (MME-03794)
The pusher will initialize and home (in the back) ok. But as the pusher reaches the very front (no MTU/empty position), it does not stop and continues to try and push forward.
RESOLUTION:
Replace the PCB, perform AutoTeach End of Travel, and ensure there is an empty carrier installed in the loading drawer.
TEST:
Verify in SSW.

## MTU Sidecar Reports Too Many or Too Few Tests
id="mc-main-content">
MTU Sidecar Reports Too Many or Too Few Tests
Complaint Description
MTU Sidecar reports too many or too few tests.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
End of travel teaching is incorrect
Technical Support
N/A
Field Service
End of travel teaching is incorrect
Teaching was performed without a carrier in the Loading Drawer.
Teaching was performed with MTUs in the carrier.
Resolution:
Perform AutoTeach End of Travel, and ensure there is an empty carrier installed in the Loading Drawer.
Test:
Start Panther, load MTUs, and verify GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. count matches actual count.
To check if the teaching is incorrect, use the following regex search in file locator lite:
fwp.*mtuexpansion: 288 OR viewlog 0x2c24[11300]
Expected value is around 11300. this would be 20 MTUs, or 100 tests. For example:
2022-12-10 19:12:40,660|[FWParam]|ManualActions|ManualActions|Info|Norma|FWP: MtuExpansion: 288: nelxt index: 290, type UnsignedInt DefaultValue 0x2C24[11300] Value 0x2C04[11268]
Each MTU is 508 steps in width. So, if the teaching is incorrect, expect the parameter value to be around 12300, if the FSE Field Service Engineer. taught without a carrier installed. For example:
2022-12-14 12:49:22,358|[FWParam]|ManualActions|ManualActions|Info|Normal|FWP: MtuExpansion: 288: next index: 290, type UnsignedInt DefaultValue 0x2C24[11300] Value 0x2F8C[12172]
If it is taught wrong, then you can get funky errors, like the expansion queue is empty because it is expecting 110 tests, but there are only 100 in there.
This can also cause this error: (03866, 2022.12.22)
2022-12-22 15:55:13,561 [E] COP Fatal High COP error (Worklist command execution timeout Device 0x7, SubAssembly: 0x1) (LowLevelEvent) [0x00.0x06.0x0010] bytes: 00 06 03 06 10 14 06 58 01 58 02 58 01 58 01 58 01 58 01 02 57 4C 07 40 00 01 [000.006.00016]

id="mc-main-content">

MTU tray was not placed correctly.
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
-
Sensor Is Obstructed
-
Poorly Placed Carrier
-
Bad Scissor Sensor
-
Misaligned Pins
Technical Support
-
Shutdown and restart instrument. Do not try to load MTUs until initialization completes.
-
Dispatch FSE Field Service Engineer. .
Field Service
COP->PC 53 00 03 05 0A 21 D8 FD 6E FE
11/13/2020 08:12:26 (13 01:12:26) [E] (Critical , High ) [MtuExpansion] MTU Sidecar Scissors Drive Target (33) not reached, stopped at 216 (AutomaticModuleEvent) [0x53.0x05.0x000A] bytes: 53 00 03 05 0A 21 D8 FD 6A FE [083.005.00010 ]
Sensor Is Obstructed
Check for an object, such as a tiplet, obstructing the sensor.
Check that carrier is fully seated on loading bay drawer or on scissor.
Resolution
Remove obstruction.
Clean sensor if necessary.
Test
Reset and perform MTU Expansion OQ X2.
Poorly Placed Carrier
Check that the carrier is fully seated and seated correctly on pins of the scissors or loading bay drawer.
Check for any obstruction, such as cables out of place.
Resolution
Properly seat carrier.
Secure cables as necessary.
Check sidecar alignment to Panther.
Check teaching, and reteach as necessary.
Test
Reset and perform MTU Expansion OQ X2.
MTUs oriented incorrectly.
Bad Scissor Sensor
The Scissor Sensor is incorrectly detecting State changes. This fault mode is usually manifested if the scissor is attempting to push out the side of the MTU expansion sidecar.
Resolution
Replace the Sensor.
Test
Reset and perform MTU Expansion OQ X2.
Misaligned Pins
Picking or placing showed that the carrier was not lining up with the pins, and it was tilting on the way down the pin.
The issue was misalignment in the forward or backward direction, and the hole the back pin is in allows for adjustment in the forward or backward directions. The current position of the back pin in this storage spot was too far forward compared to the other back pins.
Resolution
By turning the nut underneath, I was able to align the pin, which gave me smoother picks and places.

Loading drawer is on edge of presence sensor range
Alignment problem. Loading drawer was pulled out to load MTUs. When it was pushed back in, it did not trip the carrier presence sensor, because the carrier tab is not within the sensor.

Align the presence sensor closer to the drawer.

## Implausible Status of Panther Plus Liquid Waste Permanent Bottle
id="mc-main-content">
Implausible Status of Panther Plus Liquid Waste Permanent Bottle
Error Code
Dec
Hex
258.000.00018
0x13.0x00.0012
Complaint Description
An implausibility error for the Panther Plus Liquid Waste-on-the-Fly Permanent Bottle occurs in the following scenarios:
- Transfer pump displacement cup leak.
- Transfer pump bellows leak.
- Transfer pump poppet valve obstruction.
- Transfer pump motor failure.
- Kink in tubing.
- Liquid level sensor float failure.
-
WHEN TRANSFER PUMP IS PUMPING LIQUID FROM PERMANENT BOTTLE TO REMOVABLE BOTTLE: System checks that liquid level has decreased within a specified time interval [10s] (controlled by parameter DurationToCheckForLevelDecrease = 10s). If no liquid level decrease is detected, error occurs.
-
DURING ASSAY PROCESSING: When the liquid level of the permanent bottle exceeds the maximum level (controlled by parameter PermanentBottleMaxWasteLevel = 80%) and pumping should be initiated, system checks if test count in the permanent bottle is greater than 0. If the test count is 0, error occurs. Note: This has been adjusted down to 40% in System SW v7.2.5, to better mitigate foaming related issues.
-
DURING ASSAY PROCESSING: When the test count in the permanent bottle exceeds the maximum count (controlled by parameter PermanentBottleMaxWasteCount = 160) and pumping should be initiated, system checks if liquid level in the permanent bottle is greater than 0. If the liquid level is 0, error occurs. Note: This has been adjusted down to 80 tests in System SW v7.2.5, to better mitigate foaming related issues.
Keywords: ActivateWasteBellowPumpStarted emptying|Started the bellow |state of permanent waste |PC 13 00 00 00 21|PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 01|PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 00|implausible
PC 13 00 00 00 21 00 01 xx = report permanent waste bottle fluid level, xx = reported % fill volume
PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 01 = start pump
PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 00 = stop pump
TABLE OF CONTENTS
-
Technical Support
-
Field Service
- Inspect plumbing and fluid flow from permanent to removable waste bottle
- Review the logs
- Permanent bottle
- Transfer pump
- Inspect permanent waste bottle and float sensor
- Implausible Status of Panther Plus Liquid Waste Permanent Bottle
Technical Support
Mandatory Dispatch: Classify all Implausible Status of Panther Plus Liquid Waste Permanent Bottle errors as a Severity 2. Troubleshoot error as normal. Inform customers FSE Field Service Engineer. will contact them to set up the service. Customer can continue to process samples if instrument restart is successful.
- Instruct customer to make sure the Removable Liquid Waste Bottle is seated correctly.
- Reset instrument.
- Ignore the implausible waste on startup (this is triggered when sensor is empty but database thinks there more fluid in permanent waste bottle).
- Request logs (in case internal teams want to look into this).
- Notify FSE as this is likely going to recur. (WO Sev 2)
Questions to document in Case:
- Ask the customer what type of samples they are running.
- Ask customer if they have other Waste on the Fly (WOF) units and if they have recurring issues.
- Ask customer how long the unit has been running WOF.
Field Service
Identify in logs the sensor reading levels and record in case notes. This information will be useful if FSE needs to be dispatched to check sensor.
Figure 1. Find in logs "implausible state"
Figure 2. Navigate to …\Output\Log folder and Select all files. Note: This can also be performed on local Panther Instrument. From C:\Panther\Software\PC\Bin , launch ViewLog.exe. Logs are located in C:\Panther\Software\PC\Bin\Output\Log directory.
Figure 3. If results are present, expand and view. Waste implausible occurs during assay processing when pump is ON and Last checked level is the same as current level after 10 seconds. Level value is the reported percentage filled of permanent bottle. These levels indicate the float is getting stuck in the range of 58-87% fill capacity.
Inspect plumbing and fluid flow from permanent to removable waste bottle
Open waste drawer and inspect plumbing, check for obstructions or bubbles in line. Launch service software and permanent sensor reading, start transfer pump and verify fluid moves to removable waste bottle. Air bubbles should not be present until straw is pulling fluid from bottom of permanent waste bottle.
Figure 4. Purple dotted lines show fluid from Panther aspirators to permanent waste bottle. Red dotted lines show fluid flow from permanent waste bottle to transfer pump to removable waste bottle. Green circles indicate common pinch points and tube routing problems.
Review the logs
Search by keywords:
ActivateWasteBellowPumpStarted emptying|Started the bellow |state of permanent waste |PC 13 00 00 00 21|PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 01|PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 00|implausible
PC 13 00 00 00 21 00 01 xx = report permanent waste bottle fluid level, xx= reported % fill volume
PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 01 = start pump
PC 13 08 00 00 00 00 00 = stop pump
PC 13 00 00 00 21 00 01 50 = 80%
Permanent bottle
-
Check:
-
Sensor level in Service Software.
-
Fluid level in permanent waste bottle.
-
Fill permanent waste bottle to 78%, and run prime in Panther GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. to see if transfer pump turns on.
-
Run prime again to trigger the 160 test transfer.
Note: PermanentBottleWasteCount = 160 or 80% sensor reading will start transfer pump process.
In Service Software:
-
Fill permanent waste bottle to % fill level range error occurred. Enable vacuum and pump, make sure fill level goes down within 10s .
-
Normal pump operation should drop approximately 1% per second. Service Software readout appears to update around 3 - 4% every 3 - 4 seconds.
-
Inspect:
- Tubing for kinks
- Straw inside bottle is rigid and should have a v-cut
- Debris in bottom of permanent bottle
- Sensor float for sticking
- Inspect/reseat pump and sensor cables
Resolution:
Unkink or replace kinked tubing.
Replace Permanent Bottle if straw is damaged.
For debris in the bottom of the permanent bottle:
Fill the bottle with very hot water up to around 80%, drain and repeat five times.
If unable to clear – replace bottle.
For a sticky float sensor:
- Remove the vacuum filter and removable waste bottle. Unplug the sensor cable.
- Loosen the sensor by turning the nut on the sensor one revolution – it just needs to be cracked loose.
- You remove the sensor by grabbing the white part of the sensor and turning counterclockwise. It will require you to turn about 20 revolutions.
- If unable to resolve – replace the permanent bottle.
Test:
Perform WOTF OQ – refer to Panther System Service Manual .
In Panther – Prime 5x, or enough to trigger activation of the transfer pump.
Transfer pump
Fill permanent waste bottle until sensor reading shows 80% (this is approximately 1L of fluid), leave vacuum off. Begin transfer and verify fluid moves as expected. If fluid is not moving, inspect pump.
DIRTY OR DAMAGED POPPET VALVE
Resolution:
Clean or replace poppet valve.
Test:
Perform WOTF OQ – refer to Panther System Service Manual.
LEAKING DISPLACEMENT CUP
In Service Software:
Verify that liquid is present in the permanent bottle:
Disconnect the bleach filter to gain viewing access to the permanent bottle. Shine light onto the side of the bottle to see if liquid is present.
Check that liquid level in Permanent Bottle in SSW is above 0%.
If no liquid is present, follow steps in the Liquid Waste on the Fly Verification found in the Service Manual to add liquid to the permanent bottle.
Remove cap of removable bottle to view inside bottle.
Turn on transfer pump. Listen for sound of transfer pump motor running. A leak in the bellows is present if:
The pump motor is running.
Little or no liquid is seen pumped into the removable bottle.
The liquid level in the Permanent Bottle is not decreasing (both in SSW and by visual inspection of the liquid level in the bottle and the tubing from the bottle to the pump).
Turn off transfer pump.
Resolution:
Replace Transfer Pump Bellows.
Test:
Perform WOTF OQ – refer to Panther System Service Manual .
Inspect permanent waste bottle and float sensor
Solid waste can build up on inside of permanent waste bottle, causing float to stick against sensor.
Also, in some instances the rod that the sensor is mounted on is not allowing the float sensor to travel freely along the rod, contacting the inner wall of the bottle. Rotating the sensor counterclockwise 180 degrees may help. To remove the bow in the rod altogether, or to orient the bow toward the inside of the bottle, allowing the float sensor to move more freely without contacting the inner bottle wall: simply loosen the lock nut, rotate the entire sensor counterclockwise 180 degrees, then resecure sensor in place by re-tightening the lock nut.
Resolution:
Clean permanent waste bottle:
- Hot water and endozime flush can be used to help remove the buildup.
- With vacuum off, fill permanent waste bottle with hot water. Do not over fill permanent waste bottle and do not turn on vacuum during this process. (Vacuum filter can be damaged). Permanent waste bottle can also be removed. (Note: Removing static bottle from drawer is an option.)
- Allow hot water to sit in waste bottle to dissolve solid wastes.
- Empty permanent waste bottle using transfer pump.
- Repeat as many times as necessary. (Usually four flushes is sufficient)
- Pour bottle of endozime into permanent waste bottle and fill with hot water. Allow time to soak.
- Empty permanent waste bottle.
Cleaning sensor:
- Remove the vacuum filter (this is for more working space).
- Unplug the sensor cable.
- Mark or measure the existing nut location.
- Loosen the sensor by turning the nut on the sensor one revolution – it just needs to be cracked loose.
- Remove the sensor by grabbing the white part of the sensor and turning counterclockwise. It will require you to turn about 20 revolutions.
- Take pictures and clean the sensor float and internal tube.
- Replace sensor and set back to original position. If original position is too deep in bottle back the sensor out by two revolutions.
If sensor is broken or not responsive, sensor cable should be checked (MME-04468 Panther Plus, Continuous Access, Fixed Waste Reservoir, Level Sensor). In the event sensor is damaged, a permanent bottle will need to be ordered.
Test:
Verify sensor is working as expected during fluid transfer from permanent to removable waste bottle.
Normal pump operation sensor reading should drop approximately 1% / second. SSW readout appears to update around 3 - 4% every 3 - 4 seconds (in 10 seconds, the sensor should read 10% lower).
Operational check in Panther GUI:
-
Trigger using % fluid
- Fill permanent waste bottle to 75%* level *35% can be used for sw v7.2.5.
- Start Panther GUI, perform prime which should trigger SW to pump fluid over.
-
Trigger by waste count
- 160 tests = 3 full primes + 1 mini prime (full prime = 50 tests, miniprime = 10 tests).
Inspect vacuum filter
Stop! This does not affect fluid transfer from permanent waste bottle to removable waste bottle.
Resolution:
Replacing vacuum filter will not address waste implausibility errors.
Test:
Not applicable.

## Output Queue – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves
id="mc-main-content">
Output Queue – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves
Channel
Description
0
Deactivation Buffer
1
Bleach
Examples of good curves and bad curves for the Output Queue appear below.
-
Output Queue: Process Control Region Definitions
-
Normal Buffer and Bleach Dispense Curves
-
Buffer and Bleach Dispense Curves with Bubbles
-
Buffer and Bleach Dispense Curves: Fully Air
-
Output Queue: Bleach, Fully Fluid
-
Output Queue: Process Control, More Information
Output Queue: Process Control Region Definitions
The OLV system incorporates a liquid/air sensor near the injector orifice. The sensor signal for a “good” dispense will start with air (a high signal), then transition to liquid (a low signal) as fluid is dispensed, then remain sensing liquid as the pullback begins, and finally transition to air as the air/liquid interface is drawn up past the sensor.
The Output Queue Process Control algorithm splits this “air-liquid-air” signal into three distinct regions:
- Region 1: Start (air)
- Region 2: Middle (fluid)
- Region 3: End (air)
Refer to end of topic for information about how these regions are defined.
Normal Buffer and Bleach Dispense Curves
Buffer and Bleach Dispense Curves with Bubbles
OLV curves indicate bubbles in the line that may lead to undeactivated waste errors.
See also Error Code 262.000.00054 for undeactivated waste.
Buffer and Bleach Dispense Curves: Fully Air
Output Queue: Bleach, Fully Fluid
OLV curves indicate the OLV sensor is always detecting fluid. This can have a few causes:
- Fluid/ Debris blocking the sight holes in the OLV Housing.
- Fluid/ Debris on the OLV Board
- OLV Cable
Example of Output Queue losing prime:
Between PRIME and 1st MTUs through during sample processing, there appears to be loss of prime on the Bleach line affecting the front end of the trace {Region 1 or A} through the first 2 tubes/dispenses though MTU4.
It resolves by MTU5. Need to investigate the fluidic path for bleach to look for areas that could be contributing to loss of Prime on that line.
Output Queue: Process Control, More Information
The OLV system incorporates a liquid/air sensor near the injector orifice. Each dispense is followed by an airgap pullback. This pulls air back up past the sensor after each dispense. Therefore, the subsequent dispense starts with air in the tubing in front of the sensor. The sensor signal for a “good” dispense will start with air (a high signal), then transition to liquid (a low signal) as fluid is dispensed, then remain sensing liquid as the pullback begins, and finally transition to air as the air/liquid interface is drawn up past the sensor.
The Output Queue Process Control algorithm splits this “air-liquid-air” signal into 3 distinct regions. These regions are each defined by 4 parameters: Start point, end point, criteria (air or liquid), and minimum number of points required to meet the criteria. A threshold defined during sensor calibration, as part of the full-priming routine, is used to determine if each data point is considered as “air” or “liquid”. The threshold calculation sets the threshold at 1/3.5 of the way from the liquid value to the air value.
For a dispense to be considered “good”, the following conditions must be met:
- Region 2 check passes (this is the liquid phase check).
- Region 1 and/or 3 passes (these are the initial and final air pullback check).
The “Non-Deactivated waste” message will only appear to the instrument operator after 4 dispense failures in a row or 6 failures out of 20 dispenses.
The specific region parameters and the acquired sensor signal for each dispense are logged in the ‘Output Queue.curve’ file. Sensor ID “0” corresponds to Buffer and Sensor ID “1” corresponds to Bleach.
Reading the Output Queue Process Control Curves Offline
Open the ProcessControlData_OutputQueue OLV curve in CurveTrend
The Sections on the right side of Curve Trend list data and results for each curve.
- Overview Table, listing all MTUs
- Table with the data from only the selected Curve.
Explanation of the Process Control Data Curve File: Output Queue
- TimeStamp: The timestamp of when the process control curve was generated.
- TestOrderID: Test order ID assigned by the system. ID numbers that are -1 occur on curves generated during System Prime.
- SampleID: An ID generated from the barcode scanned into the system during sample loading. ‘Unknown’ ID numbers occur on curves generated during System Prime.
- MTUID: The ID of the MTU scanned when scanned by the input queue MTU barcode scanner.
- Tube Number: This is the tube number of the MTU (ranges from 0 to 4 for tubes 1 to 5). Tube 1 is closest to the MTU barcode and tube 5 is closest to the MTU tab for the distributor hook.
- Sensor ID: The sensor ID indicates which OLV channel generated the curve (0 or 1). The injector only goes in one way… Channel 0 measures the Buffer dispenses. Channel 1 measures the Bleach dispenses.
A note on sections of the process control curve known as Regions 1 through 3:
The Output Queue OLV Algorithm checks 3 regions of interest which are defined by the headers in the curve file.
Region 1: The region at the beginning of the curve where air is seen before fluid is dispensed. (high)
Region 2: The region of the curve while fluid is being dispensed. (low)
Region 3: The region of the curve which has undergone fluid pull back by the LCMP and air is observed. (high)
These Regions are defined by a set of parameters that can be found in the Output Queue OLV Curve File.
Note: The Parameters are labeled differently in CurveTrend, vs. the raw OutputQueue.curve file. In CurveTrend, the region definition parameters start at 4. In the raw OutputQueue.curve file, they start at 1:

Output Queue Process Control Troubleshooting
Typically, the process control system will generate failure flags when the system is dispensing air instead of liquid. This may be observed in the curve file data as Region 2 failures. In this case, the instrument should be inspected for:
- An empty bleach or buffer bottle
- A disconnected bleach or buffer bottle
- Loose fitting in the fluid line from the bottles to the injector
- Damaged fitting or tubing in the fluid line from the bottle to the injector
- Kinked or crushed tubing in the fluid line from the bottle to the injector (** This tubing is very thin walled and can easily kink and occlude, particularly when routed through grommets and clips.)
- Air or occlusion in the fluid line from the bottles to the injector
- Old or worn peristaltic pump tubing
If the injector is actually dispensing properly and the failure is a false flag due to a problem with the process control system, then the instrument should be inspected for:
- Wet or damaged process control circuit board in the Output Queue injector mount assembly.
- Damaged or unplugged process control cable in the Output Queue (from the main PCB to the process control PCB).
- Poor quality of the air/liquid meniscus in the injector tubing during pullback. Droplets left behind on the inner wall of the tubing in front of the sensor.
If the instrument has an Output Queue process control system failure, this failure may occur while performing full-prime because the process control system is calibrated during full-prime and is used to check that the bottles are correctly connected during full-prime. The process control system is not exercised during mini-prime.

## Oil – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves
id="mc-main-content">
Oil – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves
This topic compares normal oil dispense curves with curves that result from faults. The first section explains how to identify oil dispense errors.
-
Oil – Good Curves vs. Bad Curves
-
Normal Oil Dispense Curves
-
Oil – PCO – Running Out of Oil
-
Oil – PCO – Bad Sensor or Empty Oil Bottle
-
Oil Pump Process Control
Oil Dispense Curves: Introduction
Oil dispense curves are useful for identifying a problematic oil pump, empty oil bottle, leaks in the oil line, a disconnected fitting, or a problematic oil solenoid valve.
Columns of Interest
Column
Description
Tube Number
Identifies the tube within the MTU: O is the tube closest to the barcode.
ErrorCode
Displays 0 if no error occurred during the step. Displays a number – typically 2 – if an oil dispense error occurred.
Oil Dispense
If oil dispense errors are reported, note the pattern in faulted dispenses ( ErrorCode = 2 ). Note the following occurrences:
-
Runs in which all oil dispenses are bad. This may indicate a bad sensor, or a leak in the lines.
-
Runs that start with good oil dispenses ( ErrorCode = 0 ), then become bad, then become good again. This may indicate an oil bottle running dry before switching to the other bottle.
-
Runs that contain sporadic bad dispenses. This may indicate air bubbles in the line, faulty fittings or connections, or a bad sensor.
Normal Oil Dispense Curves
The graph below illustrates a normal oil dispense curve:
Oil – PCO – Running Out of Oil
The graph below illustrates a system that is running out of oil:
Oil – PCO – Bad Sensor or Empty Oil Bottle
The graph below illustrates a system that has a bad sensor, or is running out of oil:
Oil Pump Process Control
Graphs below compare good and bad curves for process control data.
Usual Error
Oil bottle A/B is empty or not connected, usually during Prime.
Good Curve
Upside-down square curve. Humps at the beginning and end are normal.
Bad Curve
Failing pump: not a nice, sharp upside-down square curve. Slope indicates either air is getting in, or the pump is failing.

## How to Filter for Different Data
id="mc-main-content">
How to Filter for Different Data
- Open Excel application.
- Select the " Open" option from MS Office button , and navigate to the folder where the desired curve file is found.
- Under the “Files of type” section, from the drop menu select “All Files (*.*)”. Highlight “log_PantherMain_yyyy_mm_dd-#.txt.#” file, and click the “ Open ” button.
- Select “ Delimited ”, then click on “Next >” button.
- Select “Tab”, “Comma” and under "Other", type in "(" and then click “Next >” button.
- Select “ General ”, followed by “ Finish ” button.
- Highlight entire "C" column, then click on the “ Text to Column ” button.
- Select "Tab" and under other option, type "=" , then click "Next" button.
- Select “ General ”, followed by "Finish” button.
- Click “OK" .
- Highlight the entire worksheet by clicking on the upper left corner, then click on the "Filter” button.
- Under the "C" column, select desired option to filter data .
Ambience Temp
Incubator63 Temp
HPALoadStation Temp
VacuumPressure
AmpLoadStation Temp
Incubator43 Temp
InputQueueMTUInfo:count
VacuumCoolingSystem Temp
Chiller Temp
Incubator42 Temp
ReagentCompartment Temp
- Highlight the entire column (previously chosen).
- Select the “Insert” tab, click on “Line” button.
- Right click on the curve, and select “Move Chart” .
- Select “New sheet” and name it as desired.
- Edit the graph as desired.

## How to Graph Aspiration Curves
id="mc-main-content">
How to Graph Aspiration Curves
- Open Excel application.
- Select the " Open" option from MS Office button , and navigate to the folder where the desired curve file is found.
- Under the “Files of type” section, from the drop menu select “All Files (*.*)”. Highlight AspirationPressureCurve_yyyy_mm_dd-#.curve” file, and click the “ Open ” button.
- Select “ Delimited ”, then click on “Next >” button.
- Select “Tab”, “Semicolon” delimiters and then click “Next >” button.
- Select “ General ”, followed by “ Finish ” button.
- Highlight entire worksheet by clicking on the upper left corner, then click on the “ Filter ” button.
- Under the "Command Description" column, from the drop menu, select "TCR" .
- Scroll to the right and find the “ SampleID ” column and select the desired Sample.
- Scroll to the right until the “Value" column is encountered, and then highlight data on and after the "Value" column.
- Select the "Insert" tab, click on "Line" button.
- Choose the Graph Type desired.
- Right click on the curve, and select "Move Chart" .
- Select "New sheet" and name it as desired.
- Edit the graph as desired (TCR Graph) .
- To graph "Sample" , follow same steps 1-14 but in step 8, select " Sample".
- To graph "Amp" , follow same step 1-14 but in step 8, select "Amp".
- To graph "Enzyme" , follow same step 1-14 but in step 8, select "Enzyme".
- To graph "Probe" , follow same step 1-14 but in step 8, select "Probe".

## Database Restore Issues – Suggestions
id="mc-main-content">
Database Restore Issues – Suggestions
Complaint:
DB could not be restored, SW 5.3 to SW 7.2.
Message: "Legacy database PantherDM34 cannot be restored while Radium01 database is present. Delete Radium01 and try again."
- Verify DB from 5.3 is viable.
- Verify there are no existing customer controls with same names.
- Radium01 will not allow entries with same name but different case.
- Example: panther and Panther will not be allowed in new DB.
- Backup and attempt to restore on 5.3 PC as is (first do this without dashboard data)
- DB does not restore = DB is corrupted
- DB restores successful, the try again with dashboard data
- Prepare to migrate, perform DART.
- Backup DB.
- Test DB restore on 5.3 PC.
- On 7.2 PC, delete the Radium01 DB.
- Restore 5.3 DB.bak.
- Launch Panther, at this point the 5.3 will be converted to Radium DB.
- Use correct format usb (TB-01599) NOT FAT32 or exFAT but NTFS.

## SW 7.1 - Sample Pipetting Slower Than Expected
id="mc-main-content">
SW 7.1 - Sample Pipetting Slower Than Expected
MKS 2133932
Issue:
When starting assay processing, a condition exists when one of the UF kits is invalid. An invalid kit is either an expired or empty kit. The system will report that it is in the Ready state as there is still a valid UF kit on board. When AP is started, the system must introduce an LPM (Leading Prime MTU) to prime both MW stations. Even though the kit is invalid, the system allows it to be scheduled for prime even though it is invalid. However, because the fluid kit is invalid, a secondary check stops it from being used for priming. Leading to the condition where a MW station cannot be used for AP and thus results in a 10 minute MTU introduction cycle.
Systems which are not configured for OTF fluids will only experience the defect during AP. It will not occur at initial startup of the instrument because the Prime task requires both kits to be valid. It can occur when the system has completed an AP session and moves to the Ready state. In this case, the defect will occur if AP is started with an invalid kit or a kit moves to invalid during AP and an LPM is required. An LPM would be needed by the system if the current assay being processed switches between TMA, Fusion, or RT.
Systems which are configured for OTF fluids may also experience a defect relating to the system continuously transitioning from AP to Ready (MKS# 2047987). It has the same root cause but, a different user experience. However, systems configured for OTF fluids can experience the defect during AP if a kit moves to invalid during AP and an LPM is required.
Affected:
7.1.5.4
Fix Implemented:
7.2
Workaround:
The customer must check the UF status when in the Ready state. If one of the kits shows as invalid, it must be replaced. This will bring the system back to the Setup state and require a Prime of the system in order to continue to AP. For systems that are configured for OTF fluids, the customer should ensure that they attempt to replace the kit as soon as it becomes empty if they are running assays of different types (TMA, Fusion, or RT).

A similar error exists in SW 7.2. For Universal Fluids on the Fly, it will bounce between Assay Processing and Ready state. Activity Report will show the instrument go into Assay Processing, then 1 second later go to Ready state. This will happen about every minute.
I need to open an MKS as this does look to be a defect. From what I can gather, the issue was possibly introduced the previous day. At least, that is where kit B incorrectly picked up an extra bottle. Looks like when they opened the fluids drawer during prime AD 2B was detected as removed. Shortly after, they did a fluid inventory and replaced the bottle but, the system did not correctly release the old bottle from the kit. However, this might be a red herring as I do see that after that event, they ran some samples. It was not until today that the system started complaining about not being able to create leading prime MTUs. In any case, I would have them restart the instrument to clear out kit B. On reboot, it should detect what bottles are loaded correctly.

## Disable RTFs Through Remote Diagnostics
id="mc-main-content">
Disable RTFs Through Remote Diagnostics
Error Code
Dec
Location
N/A
Complaint Description
Unable to run the Panther system due to a Real Time Flourometer fault.
Technical Support
Warning: Never perform any electromechanical operations while connected remotely to the Panther System.
-
SecureLink only applies to Panther Systems (Panther, Panther Fusion, or Panther Plus) running on System software v7.2 and above. Remote support is limited to agents with access to account asset information within the Salesforce CRM application.
-
Agents will only be able to access the customer’s system when it is in an idle or error state, and not while the system is processing a run.
-
It is against HIPAA rules to match patient identification with patient results.
-
Transfer of log files shall occur within the Hologic network: that is, with in-house login on support workstation, or remotely through VPN.
-
Agent shall not modify or delete files via remote connection.
-
Support users are not allowed to change or alter Panther software or firmware configurations, settings, or parameters.
-
Agent shall terminate the remote session when troubleshooting is finished, either by closing out the session or the software completely.
Procedure
-
Ask the customer to start the SecureLink gatekeeper service on the Panther by going to Messages tab, and clicking Remote Diagnostics .
-
Search for Panther Serial Number within Salesforce.
Note: Google Chrome is the preferred web browser.
-
From Asset level or Case level, click SecureLink .
-
Log into SecureLink with Single Sign On.
-
Click Connect .
-
A pop-up window prompts user to click Connect using SecureLink connection manager.
-
A download appears to launch.securelinkcm.
-
Click on it. Another window reports SecureLink Connection Manager starting.
-
A new window with Connection Form Information opens.
-
Enter Reason for Connection.
-
Enter Person Who Authorized Access (customer contact).
-
Click Submit .
-
System prompts to use Administrator Privileges. Click OK .
-
There will be two options – Desktop Sharing or File Transfer (Read / Write) .
-
Click Desktop Sharing .
-
Now agent has control over the customer’s Panther computer, and is able to: (1) navigate to different screens; (2) perform the Send Logs function.
Warning: Never perform any electromechanical operations while connected remotely to the Panther System.
-
Log into Service Software, and disable the RTFs as shown.
Field Service
N/A

## Service Software: Fusion Handoff Teach with MTU Sidecar – Missing Carrier
id="mc-main-content">
Service Software: Fusion Handoff Teach with MTU Sidecar – Missing Carrier
Error Code
50 21 01 00 30
Complaint Description
Service software reports unlock drawer.
This error code is incorrectly translated.
Both of these codes refer to missing MTU carrier:
50 21 01 00 30
[WARNING] 0x30
Field Service
Insert MTU carrier
Resolution
-
Place MTU carrier in location, as shown.
-
If error encountered during handoff teach or System OQ, add two or more MTUs in this carrier location.
Test
Repeat handoff teach or System OQ until error does not repeat.
MTU Carrier Sensor
Resolution
-
Verify MTU queue recognizes MTU carrier is present and correctly seated.
-
Verify presence check indicates sensor detects MTU carrier.
-
Check if sensor is plugged in and functioning properly.
Presence check indicating no carriers present in any location.
MTU carrier sensor in MTU queue.

## SW 7.1 – GUI Frozen and Unresponsive
id="mc-main-content">
SW 7.1 – GUI Frozen and Unresponsive
MKS 1849332
Summary:
XE3 - 7.1.5.4 - BIOS correct, customer experiencing intermittent
Identification #1:
Similar to MKS# 1849332
It looks like it happened during sample rack loading. Maybe we can ask the customer to ensure that pop-up dialogs are dealt with correctly.
2020-10-23 06:43:47,377 Navigate[1217]: UI_Activity Main screen switched to SampleRackLoad
2020-10-23 06:43:47,377 PrepareForDisplay[65]: UI_Activity RichTextConfirm dialog activated, text: <u>To correct Patient Sample unreadable barcodes:</u><br/>
-
Select OK to exit.
-
Remove Sample Rack from the bay.
-
Check sample barcode to ensure it is facing the scanner. Adjust as needed.
-
If barcode is damaged or unreadable:
- Use the handheld scanner to scan the tube position barcode on the rack.
- Use the handheld scanner or the keyboard to enter the sample barcode ID.
-
Upon completion of barcode correction, load the Sample Rack back into the original lane.
If EQC is unlabeled:
- Select OK to exit
- Select the message in the Status column
- Select the Assign EQC button to assign a name to the unlabeled EQC
2020-10-23 06:43:47,377 Show[151]: UI_Activity Modal dialog activated: GenProbe.Panther.UI.SubPages.RichTextConfirmPage ß Modal dialog popped up
2020-10-23 06:43:56,028 Navigate[1217]: UI_Activity Main screen switched to SampleRackBay ß System switched to another page, hiding the dialog
Workaround/Recommendation:
*Customer to ensure that pop-up dialogs are dealt with correctly.
*If they have samples running, they can let the system continue to run until finished. No need to shut it down until everything finishes processing. The UI should still be updating itself so they should be able to see the instrument state
*Restart GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. , Quick press on the power button is the best option. That will at least do a semi-safe shutdown. Holding the power button would be last resort.
Identification #2:
Customer attempted to pull several reports, and when they did the PC locked up for over an hour, then crashed.
This one looks like a previously reported issue. MKS# 2216042 covers it.
The UI status can be gauged by looking for the ticks that are logged every second. Below is the last tick from the UI, indicating that it is unresponsive from this point forward.
2021-01-13 16:44:31,333 periodicTimer_Tick[2022]: Tick
The last UI activity I can see they were on the Results screen.
2021-01-13 16:43:34,332 Navigate[1217]: UI_Activity Main screen switched to Results
This is the first exception. Almost exactly an hour after the last tick, we see an exception from the UI. This is the one-hour timeout that is configured for threads in our system.
2021-01-13 17:44:31,693 Software exception occurred [406.001.00001]
2021-01-13 17:44:31,693 Exception caught by UI: Operation Timeout: ResultPage.ResultProvider.ChangeHandlerDM (c:149,s:118)(Running) TD:01:00:00.0006512 RD:01:00:00.0006512 TO:01:00:00(True) CD:00:00:00, trace: [406.001.00002]
The two items that point to 2216042 are the fact that they were last at the Results screen and the ResultPage.ResultProvider.ChangeHandlerDM exception that occurred almost exactly an hour later.
Resolution:
This would be more a monitoring situation if it keeps occurring. It should be a fairly rare defect, and unfortunately, no workaround.

## SW 7.1 – Mismatch of Quested and Stored MTU ID
id="mc-main-content">
SW 7.1 – Mismatch of Quested and Stored MTU ID
Root cause:
Bios is at A24, so it should be downgraded to A07 (TB-01507).
USB situation also looked at.
Root Cause #1:
2020-09-19 11:41:33,880 [MsgHandler] EventLogger EventLogEntry Error 09/19/2020 18:41:33 (19 11:41:33) [E] (Fatal , High ) [SidecarSlaveDriver] Mismatch of quested and stored MTU ID (InstrumentEvent) [0x16.0x01.0x0024] bytes: 16 00 03 01 24 54 00 00 D7 00 [022.001.00036]
2020-09-19 11:41:33,880 [ProcessEvent] ProcessEventHandler ProcessManagement Error ManageFatalError triggered by InstrumentEvent - Device=SidecarSlaveDriver Cmd=0x0 Subass=0x1 EventID=0x24 Severity=Fatal. Fatal error of SidecarSlaveDriver,
Root Cause #2:
7.1 failure mode MKS 2042330
There are no DM requests larger than four seconds (requested from UI).
-----------------------------------------
D:\2090\Complaints\2042330\Output\Log\log_PantherMain_20200323-124500022.txt.758
2020-03-26 22:09:18,941|[MsgHandler]|TestOrderManager|OrderManagement|Info|Normal|<<TOM.InternalMessageReceive: (InternalMsg 369603 TransmitSidecarResultsToLis System.Collections.Generic.List`1[CommonLib.PantherDataModel.OrderManagement.TestOrder])
-----------------------------------------
D:\2090\Complaints\2042330\Output\Log\log_PantherMain_20200323-124500022.txt.763
2020-03-26 22:34:49,214|[MsgHandler]|LisHelper| LIS Laboratory Information System. |Info|Normal|<<LIS: Results queued for sending to LIS.
2020-03-26 22:34:49,214|[MsgHandler]|TestOrderFactory|OrderManagement|Info|Normal|TOF.AutomaticallySaveAndSendToLis: transmitted=1, sent to LIS=1.
2020-03-26 22:34:49,214|[MsgHandler]|MessageHandler|MHTimesMain|Info|Problem|Timespan 00:25:30.2727585 for executing in TestOrderManagement module; InternalMsg 369603 TransmitSidecarResultsToLis System.Collections.Generic.List`1[CommonLib.PantherDataModel.OrderManagement.TestOrder]. Exceeded limit: 3000ms
MsgHandler thread could not continue until after the m_bgtLock was released when SendResults to LIS finished (32 minutes) -> while MsgHandler thread is blocked the internal messages are not sent -> the commands to COP are sent with delay -> the exception "Rotary Distributor Driver (ID is unknown, can not pick unit)" is raised.
The system transitions to error state when a large amount of results is sent to LIS.
Root Cause #3:
MKS# 2273693 which is targeted to be fixed in the 7.2.5.
Panther Sample Pipettor had a Non-String Type 3 error. From Mike Despars:
It is similar to MKS# 1216571, which is targeted to be fixed in the 7.2.5 Trax release coming this year.
It is due to a defect with how we handle the Error Assay Processing completing state. The pipettor error (nonstr-type 3) error set the instrument in Error AP Completing. However, the sidecar did not handle this correctly. It set itself back into a Ready state and asked for more MTUs to be introduced. Since the MTUs could not be handled, it resulted in the Mismatch of quested and stored MTU ID error.
Root Cause #4:
Operator called to report the Panther automatically shut down last night.
The Panther was processing SARS specimens last night and had started alarming at 10:10pm, the same time a clot was detected on a sample.
Clots are often detected on SARS specimens, but the Panther never just shuts down.
At the same time, there was Software Exception Occurred error.
She said they had reset the Panther, and prime had passed.
Looks like a variation of “Mismatched of quested and stored MTU ID error”, except it occurs much sooner because clot forces deletion of test order.
Clot detected with TestOrder = 380770 SampleID=20064292
TO 380770 was created:
2022-11-08 22:08:36,006|[100]|TestOrderFactory|OrderManagement|Info|Normal|OnTestOrderCreated:380772, 380769, 380774, 380780, 380775, 380770, 380773, 380778, 380777, 380776
LIS already set to run the following tests:
11/08/2022 10:08:41 PM LAC1 Test Order deleted from Sample 20064292: Assay LDT-SARS-CoV-2, Analytes SARS-CoV-2
TO deleted:
2022-11-08 22:08:41,813|[PI.TestOrderManager:.#0]|TestOrderManager|PantherUI|Info|Normal|OnDmCallbackTestOrderDeleted[956]: eventType: Deleted; dbIds: 380769,380770,380771,380772,380773,380774,380775,380776,380777,380778,380779,380780;
New test associated:
11/08/2022 10:08:47 PM LAC1 Test Order added to Sample 20064292: Assay SARSCoV2
CLT error:
2022-11-08 22:10:49,683|[ProcessEvent]|EventLogger|EventLogEntry|Info|Error|11/09/2022 03:10:49 (08 22:10:49) [E] (Warning , Low ) [COP] Sample Pipettor clot detected ID=112538 PipettorAspirate 'Add Sample' (Sample) PlannedStart=03:10:34.591: , start=03:10:34.591 end=03:10:47.191 (MTU=372 BarcodeID=2293936880, samples=380770/20064292/Normal, , cmd params: Sample (SP) [coo=229,fZ=149] , vol=381, track=64, fluid=32776 ). Event [0x00.0x0F.0x00C3] at 03:10:43.691 bytes: 00 00 02 0F C3 01 00 [000.015.00195]
SW received empty set when test order 380770 was retrieved.

## Fusion Software – Pipetting Slower Than Expected
id="mc-main-content">
Fusion Software – Pipetting Slower Than Expected
Issue: Multiple Quest sites running SW 7.1.5 are encountering a pipetting delay. Normal introduction cycle is five minutes, but instrument goes to ten-minute introduction cycle after being on for several days.
Possible cause: MW2 is out of service due to insufficient fluids remaining in Kit A.
MKS: TBD.
What I am seeing on 3381 is correlating to the OTF fluids workflow. Essentially, fluid kit A has 0 tests in it, but a leading prime MTU is needed for MW 2. This MTU cannot be scheduled, as there are 0 tests in kit A, and therefore MW 2 is technically out of service. The system is operating with a single MW, which is leading to the 10 minute cycles. Will need logs from 7/10 – 7/13 to confirm the operator workflow. Seems to be a defect, but will need further investigation to identify any workarounds or ways to prevent this in the future.
2020-07-12 23:54:16,687 CanGenerateNewMtuProcess: 1 prime MTUs needed in total at 04:54:45 for MagWash2
2020-07-12 23:54:16,687 PMH. GetMinimumNeededUniversalFluid:
- BUFFER_A: 1026 uL, 5 tests => 0 bottle tests
- Bleach: 1026 uL, 5 tests => 0 bottle tests
- OIL_A: 200 uL, 5 tests => 0 bottle tests
- WASH_A: 2000 uL, 5 tests => 0 bottle tests
2020-07-12 23:54:16,687 CanGenerateNewMtuProcess: Didn't create MTU at 07/13/2020 04:54:16 as leading prime preconditions were not met.

## Fusion Handoff Teaching – SSW
id="mc-main-content">
Fusion Handoff Teaching – SSW
Issue: Unable to teach Handoff (HO) station and LD would not clear amp load station door pin during LD/HO teach. While a regular LD move to HO would clear the amp load station door pin.
Root cause: FW mismatch due to botched LD theta teach. After squaring to luminometer, Get ALL current was not performed. This set the LD theta home towards service queue/handoff location.
Found out LD > Parameter > Set to factory Default Values was used to reset home position.
This did something to the teaching HO algorithm.
When this is used, instrument setup should be run prior to teaching.
Video of LD teaching to Handoff station: LD to HO teach.mp4 .
Notice teaching extends hook and sweeps theta to find edges.
When LD teaches to handoff it uses par. 320 (x), 321 (z), 322 (th), 323 (h).
Resolution: if Set to factory Default Values is used, instrument setup must be run afterwards.

## Panther Main Fails to Load
id="mc-main-content">
Panther Main Fails to Load
Symptoms
After restart, workstation starts Windows loading screen works as expected. Panther Shield launches, but Panther Main fails to load.
Avoiding the Problem
-
Make sure SW dialogs in GUI Graphical User Interface – allows users to interact with the software using images, graphical icons, and visual indicators rather than text commands. are properly addressed, to avoid "Frozen GUI" situation.
-
Unsafe shutdown.
- PC workstation power button, quick short press will activate Windows shutdown sequence.
- PC workstation power button, should not be held down unless instructed to do so (this can corrupt data).
-
Removing Power when PC is on.
SW 6.x
-
Upgrade to 7.x.
-
If required to stay on SW 6.x, disable “Dashboard services”.
Troubleshooting
In Vista/Win7, while Windows is booting up, alternate Left Shift and Right Shift keys.
This allows access to gpservice account where some items can be recovered.
Should attempt to launch PantherMain.exe, this will likely fail.
Database issue:
-
Back up database without dashboard to local C drive, e.g., C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\DBbackup\.
-
Verify database can be restored.
-
Repeat steps with dashboard database.
-
Once database integrity has been verified, save a copy to USB stick.
-
Delete the Database > Restart PC > see if PantherMain will restart successfully.
-
If DB cannot be backed up or restored, database is is corrupted and requires reimage.
User Settings issue:
-
Attempt to open C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\Configuration\ChangedUserSettings.xml with Notepad. Navigate to file, double click on file. Select Notepad when present option.
-
Check if file was corrupted: ChangedUserSettings.xml entire contents should be legible. Scroll to end of file and inspect for partial xml tags or weird symbols.
-
If this file is corrupted, <delete> “ChangedUserSettings.xml” and only “UserSettings.xml” will be present.
- Option 1: If send logs was performed recently*, <copy> “ChangedUserSettings.xml” from send logs \configuration folder and <paste> into the folder: C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\Configuration\ *Note: any changes to settings between send logs and failure event will be lost. Settings that can be affected are all settings found under “Admin” tab AND “Tasks > Service Settings”.
-
Option 2: If no send logs are available, restart PantherMain. (system will use the default UserSettings.xml file)
Launch PantherMain launches as expected, verify Admin > System Setting
Other issues:
-
If PantherMain still does not launch, review logs and identify failure. Logs are located in: C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\Output\Log
-
If failure mode cannot be identified, reimage will be necessary.
Reimage Required…
**This only works when staying on exact same software version, access to these files may be lost in future software releases**
- Backup the following to your USB stick:
- C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\Configuration\ChangedUserSettings.xml (this saves user settings, do not save if deleting ChangedUserSettings.xml resolved issue)
- C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\Configuration\Lis\Panther_ LIS Laboratory Information System. .xml (this saves LIS configuration)
- C:\Panther\Software\PC\bin\Configuration\LAS\Panther_LAS.xml (saves LAS configuration)
- C:\Panther\Software\PC\Data\Coordinate.coo (this saves coordinate.coo) *SidecarCoordinate.coo for Fusion
- C:\Panther\Software\PC\Data\InstrumentDescription.xml
- Zip: C:\Panther\Panther Service Software\Log
- Zip: C:\Stratec\Logs
- Reimage Workstation.
- Install all SW.
- Set your computer name, timezone, etc.
- Paste the files and unzipped folders back where they belong.
- Launch PantherMain GUI.
- If PantherMain GUI launches successfully, exit PantherMain.
- Restore Database.
- Launch PantherMain GUI.

## SW 6.2 – Panther Shield Fails to Load
id="mc-main-content">
SW 6.2 – Panther Shield Fails to Load
Symptoms:
After restart, workstation starts windows, loading screen works as expected. Panther shield never comes up, so black screen appears.
Troubleshooting:
In Vista/Win7, while Windows is booting up, alternate Left Shift and Right Shift keys.
This allows access to gpservice account, where some items can be recovered.
Should attempt to launch PantherMain.exe, this will likely fail.
Avoiding the problem:
- Unsafe shutdown. PC workstation power button should not be held down unless instructed to do so.
- This issue appears more frequently with SW 6.x versions, as there are more Database related issues.
- Make sure dashboard service is disabled for customer.

## SSW Bricked Thermocycler During Instrument Setup
id="mc-main-content">
SSW Bricked Thermocycler During Instrument Setup
Issue: After a thermocycler replacement, thermocycler Lid Open as well as other errors are reported, as shown below.
In Service Software, there is also the following under Thermocycler > TC States > TC States – I don’t recall seeing this – and am not seeing this on my virtual SSW. I know there are no lid sensors.
Root cause:
Possible Service Software bug, or a thermocycler has the incorrect firmware version.
TC Shutter was an old engineering use only feature not incorporated in the released product. It should not appear in Service Software.
Resolution:
-
Possible thermocycler firmware update required.
-
Contact USTSESupport for instructions.
-
Bricked thermocycler – instrument setup.

## Service Software: Luminometer – PMT – High Voltage
id="mc-main-content">
Service Software: Luminometer – PMT – High Voltage
Error Code
No error code applies.
Associated errors: dark count low, no RLU, failed system check.
Complaint Description
After replacing PMT: low RLUs, high voltage errors, or failed system check.
Certain versions of service software display either an incorrect high voltage parameter range, or incorrect high voltage parameter.
SSW 5.0.22: Ignore HV parameter range.
SSW 5.1.0.3: High voltage parameter should be equal to twice the Operation Voltage value from the sheet that comes with PMT. Enter this value in the High Volt field within Service Software, Luminometer > Measure Get/Set Parameter . The HV Parameter Value is twice the Operation Voltage .
TABLE OF CONTENTS
Technical Support
Field Service
Technical Support
Not applicable. Field Engineer must resolve.
Field Service
Check and correct High Voltage
Resolution
High Voltage parameter value should be twice the Operation Voltage.
-
<Get> High Volt to determine current HV Parameter Value .
-
HV Parameter Value should be twice the Operation Voltage .
-
Enter High Voltage value and <Set> until HV Parameter Value is twice Operation Voltage.
-
SSW 5.0.22 and below: use Operation Voltage. Notice range under HV Parameter Value range is highlighted red, but range is correct.
-
SSW 5.1.0.3: use Operation Voltage * 4.
Test
Verify Dark Counts and system check pass.

During assay processing the system brings on two MTUs to be used as “Leading Prime MTUs”. These are used to prime the Mag Wash units prior to them being used, they will also be used to prime the Luminometer if a Standard TMA test has also been scheduled. Since the customer loaded only RT-TMA assays initially, the leading prime MTUs were discarded prior to loading and scheduling of any Trich samples. After the customer loaded the Trich assay, the system could not re-schedule a new leading prime for over an hour. This is what caused the delay in starting Trich sample processing.
Ask customer to load TMA assay first, then RT-TMA

7.1
1340912
APV
APV flags occur when the TCR was mixed too long before assay processing. The instrument registers this extra mixing time in the output logs under SRS-EEH-1461. The SRS-EEH-1461
The APV flags seen in the related complaints trigger when a TCR Carousel reagent (e.g. TCR, TER, FCR, FER) mixes for a longer time than expected. The incorrect flagging is related to maintenance tasks as follows: disruption of the scheduled TCR mix cycle due to the Replace Mag Wash Cleaning Solution maintenance task causes the next mix to occur to be a 90-second mix when the expected duration by the APV was 45 seconds. Therefore, the actual mix time is above the expected mix time of the TCR Carousel reagents that were loaded and will lead to APV flagging when used to perform an assay.
Corrected in SW 6.2.5.1 (CTB-00507)
Workaround in CTB-00578
Operator workaround:
Based on additional investigation, the previously provided workaround instructions, that were provided to help prevent APV flags from occurring in the next run have been revised to reduce customer effort.
First, any need to perform reagent loading/unloading prior to assay processing can be avoided by performing the Replace Mag Wash Cleaning Solution task at a time when no reagents are loaded. Reagents can either be unloaded before performing this task or this task can be completed at a time when reagents need to be unloaded (e.g., before or after a PC Reboot maintenance task is performed).
However, if a Replace Mag Wash Cleaning Solution maintenance task was performed while reagents were loaded, the operator may help prevent APV flags from occurring in the next run by performing any non-maintenance activity that unlocks the TCR Door prior to initiating assay processing. The TCR door can be opened by:
• Unloading any reagent kit
• Loading or reloading any reagent kit.
Per Panther Operator’s manual, a new set of controls/calibrators is required when a reagent kit is removed and then reloaded on the system, therefore, this workaround may require that new controls/calibrators be loaded.

2074692
Master lot
Customer was also unable to load an
ATV kit onto the instrument and would get an “invalid kit” message error by
either loading kit or scanning MLBS (ML266751).
Software team found that the issue was caused by the failing hard drive on
the previous PC. When the user activated the lot for the first time, there
are CommitFailedExceptions which occurred when attempting to write the ML
into the database. When these exceptions occur, the system retries the
transaction, even though we do not know whether the commit failed or was
successful. In this case, the system successfully committed the row twice
prior to the transaction completing successfully with confirmation. Meaning,
there are now three items in the DB which correspond to this ML. This then
leads to an ambiguous master lot check and thus the kit for this ML cannot be
loaded.
We recommend that the customer
backs up all necessary data from the system and deletes the database.

Software exception
Customer experienced a SW exception
shortly after assignment on an LDT Control.
Root Cause:
1. User manually deletes the test
orders that were assigned via sample defaults.
2. Shortly after, the user selects
the sample to be assigned as a control.
3. The UI thinks that test orders
are still available to be deleted and attempts to do so.
4. The test orders have already
been deleted though and thus the “Sequence contains no elements” error occurs
because UI expected the command to return the deleted DBIds.
A workflow change could help to
mitigate this issue. The customer is using sample defaults to assign the test
orders. Which forces them to delete the test orders and thus helps to lead to
this exception.
1. Turn off sample defaults when loading the rack with controls. Turn back on
after loading the rack.
2. Load the rack with controls first, delete the test orders, load all
remaining specimen racks, and then assign as an LDT control.
The key is that we need to give some time for the delete to successfully take
place and propagate to the UI. Or to eliminate the delete by turning off
sample defaults.

2139332
Slow
The short description:
Customer is reporting Instrument is pipetting slower than expected. It takes
10 min to pipet 5 samples instead of 5 min
When does this issue occur (on Panther only)? On instruments with software
7.1 when one of the Universal fluids kits is empty at the beginning of assay
processing.
What is the software anomaly? Even though one of the fluids kit is invalid,
the system allows it to be scheduled for Lead prime MTU (LPM). The system
should be taking into account kit validity when selecting the kit for leading
prime.
The longer description:
When starting assay processing, a condition exists when one of the UF kits is
invalid. An invalid kit is either an expired or empty kit. The system will
report that it is in the Ready state as there is still a valid UF kit on
board. When AP is started, the system must introduce an LPM (Leading Prime
MTU) to prime both MW stations. Even though the kit is invalid, the system
allows it to be scheduled for LPM. Because the fluid kit is invalid, however,
a secondary check stops it from being used for priming. Leading to the
condition where a MW station cannot be used for AP and thus results in a 10-minute MTU introduction cycle.
Regular Panthers will only experience the defect during AP. It will not occur
at initial startup of the instrument because the Prime task requires both
kits to be valid. It can occur when the system has completed an AP session
and moves to the Ready state. In this case, the defect will occur if AP is
started with an invalid kit or a kit moves to invalid during AP and an LPM is
required. An LPM would be needed by the system if the current assay being
processed switches between TMA, Fusion, or RT.
On Panther Plus: there are 2 different customer perceived scenarios depending
on which fluids kit the instrument decides to use for the LPM.
If kit A is empty and instrument decides to use kit A for LPM à Instrument
continuously transitions from Assay Processing to Ready (see MKS# 2047987)
If kit A is empty and instrument decides to use kit B for LPM same as on Panther:
Pipetting is slower than expected. It takes 10 min to pipet 5 samples instead
of 5 min. (MKS# 2139332).
The customer must check the UF
status when in the Ready state. If one of the kits shows as invalid, it must
be replaced. This will bring the system back to the Setup state and require a
Prime of the system in order to continue to AP.

2664872
LIS communication
Messages show "Error while transmitting data to LIS."
ASTM 1381 A Low-level protocol that is used to transfer Messages between Clinical Laboratory Instruments and Computer Systems. logs show the Panther and LIS send an ENQ at almost the exact same time. LIS sends an ACK shortly after but Panther does not recognize it and sends an EOT 15 seconds later at the frame sending timeout, which causes the Error while transmitting data message.
No workaround at this time. SW is looking into the issue.
2651372
LIS results
Panther is incorrectly sending results to the LIS that contain "<96>" in the comment field. Most LIS try to convert "<96>" into a symbol which causes the checksum to fail because Panther is counting them as individual characters.
Seen so far with results for the LDT-SARS-CoV-2 (SARS PCR) and GBS assays.
No workaround at this time in Panther. SW is looking into the issue.
Instruct customers/LIS that they will need to have the LIS treat "<96>" as for individual characters and not convert to a symbol.
Example: <- 1C|5|I|^icrfu <96> IC is negative.|I<CR>B1<CR><LF>
ASTM American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) is an international standards organization that develops and publishes voluntary technical standards. 1381/1394 Logs:
“<- 1C|5|I|^icrfu <96> IC is negative.|I<CR>B1<CR><LF>

when verifying all results under Results Tab, some results will not cross

2285407
Password
A customer
reported that every time they logged into an instrument at their site, they
were prompted to reset their password. It was determined that this is related
to Panther Link, which shares operator account information with all
instruments in the same Data Sharing Group.
This
is a defect that occurs when the expiration of a password is set to 0.
When the user sets this value to 0 the data is shared to other instruments
with a null value for the expiration. The receiving instruments see this null
value and because of the defect, set the expiration to the current time.
Requiring the user to go to each instrument and update the password.
The
workaround is to ensure the expiration of a user’s password is never set to 0.

Fluids
Customer
reported that both of the universal fluid kits (A&B) were marked as In
Use long after one of the kits should have no longer been In Use. Customer is
not able to change either of the fluid kits during assay processing because
both are In Use.
This
is a rare issue that can only occur in a very specific timeframe when SW is
scheduling the disposal of a leading prime MTU at the same time waste unload
(during assay processing) is happening. In this situation it is possible that
the disposal of the lead prime MTU is skipped and this results in the empty
fluid kit remaining in the ‘in use’ state. Unfortunately when this occurs the
empty fluid kit is unable to be replaced. There is no workaround for this
once it occurs. The operator will have to wait until processing has completed
before that kit can be replaced. This issue can occur in both 7.1 and 7.2 SW.
The anomaly has been scheduled to be fixed in v7.4 software
No
workaround at this time.
UFP.EvaluateInUseKitsLocation

(tells you the RTR and RTP for each bottle in a fluid kit)

Software exception
Customer likely recently completed a PC reboot, and a message will read "Assay reagent racks are located in different lane positions after the maintenance reboot. Reagent kits need to be reloaded to confirm kit information". If the operator ignores this message and proceeds with loading different kits, SW exception errors may pop up and/or incorrect ML# can be assigned to a worklist if it is the same assay/same lane, but different LN.
The workaround is to ensure customer does not load or unload reagents during a maintenance reboot, as instructed in the Ops Manual. To clear the error, customer can unload all racks and restart.
If customer runs into this again:
- Remind operator and site of proper process when “Allow Reagents to remain loaded during Maintenance Restart” is enabled.
- Clear error, unload all racks and restart instrument.
Another fix is upgrading to v7.2.5.

7.2
trax release
2467984
Worklist
A reagent
kit used on day one was removed but samples run the next day were on the original
WL from day one.
- The anomaly is related to the Allow
Reagents to Remain Loaded During Maintenance Restart feature and can only
happen on systems that have this feature enabled.
- Only TMA kits that were left
onboard through a maintenance restart could be impacted.
- Issue is not tied to the samples
themselves so any impacted samples can be safely retested.
- SW Dev was unable to identify a way
to prevent this from happening though fortunately this error has proven to be
rare.
This could be avoided by disabling the ‘allow
reagents to remain loaded’ configuration but this issue is so uncommon, and
the benefit to having this configuration enabled is so great, that it’s not
worth it. So my recommendation would be to continue to use the system as
intended. There is still a risk that this could happen but the chances so
remote that it’s not worth the cost to avoid.

## SW 7.1 - Fusion Software Exception After Assigning LDT Control
id="mc-main-content">
SW 7.1 - Fusion Software Exception After Assigning LDT Control
Software Exception After Assignment on LDT Control
Issue:
Customer experienced a SW exception shortly after assignment on an LDT Control.
MKS:
2099423
Root Cause:
- User manually deletes the test orders that were assigned via sample defaults.
- Shortly after, the user selects the sample to be assigned as a control.
- The UI thinks that test orders are still available to be deleted and attempts to do so.
- The test orders have already been deleted, though, and thus the Sequence contains no elements error occurs because UI expected the command to return the deleted DBIds.
Workaround:
A workflow change could help to mitigate this issue. The customer is using sample defaults to assign the test orders, which forces them to delete the test orders and thus helps to lead to this exception.
- Turn off sample defaults when loading the rack with controls. Turn back on after loading the rack.
- Load the rack with controls first, delete the test orders, load all remaining specimen racks, and then assign as an LDT control.
The key is that we need to give some time for the delete to successfully take place and propagate to the UI, or to eliminate the delete by turning off sample defaults.

## SW 7.1 - Software Exception - Test Orders Must Have an Associated User
id="mc-main-content">
SW 7.1 - Software Exception - Test Orders Must Have an Associated User
TestOrders Filtered by Not Processed Today
Issue:
Looking at the logs, the error is the same and occurs at the same time, during the PC reboot maintenance. It looks like it has something to do with test orders that were not processed today. Error message appears below:
Looking at the activity logs, the instrument is doing the following prior to the exception TestOrders filtered by Not Processed Today .
MKS:
1946160
Root Cause:
Dealing with the LIS Laboratory Information System. sending the Panther test orders right when the LIS connection is available. They start sending us test orders before a user is even able to login, which causes the SW exception that test orders must have an associated user. An upgrade would be the best path. To confirm, these errors should not cause a crash of the system.
Workaround:
NA Does not Cause the Instrument to Crash

## SW 7.1 - Fusion-Samples Not Turning Green When Adding Test Orders
id="mc-main-content">
SW 7.1 - Fusion-Samples Not Turning Green When Adding Test Orders
MKS: 2045725, 2078738, 2078766
Issue
The operator wanted to re-process a specimen which had been flagged with a VVFS. They unloaded the rack and reloaded it to re-process the specimen. At this time, the front-end MTU had not yet completed the handoff to Fusion. The system allowed them to add an additional test order to the specimen, which is okay if the front-end is not set to be invalidated. Thus, both PCR test orders were invalidated by the system. They also experienced an anomaly within the UI which looks to be the original reported issue.
They reloaded the rack and the system SW incorrectly allowed them to add an additional PCR test order to the specimen which was set to be invalidated.
The UI also experienced a defect regarding display of the test order in the rack details screen. The additional test order added was considered a replicate. When a replicate is created against a front-end that has already been pipetted, IC will copy the pipetting time from the front-end. UI sees that that pipetting time is from before when the sample was loaded and excludes it intentionally. Basic steps to reproduce below.
Load a sample and let it begin processing a PCR test order.
Unload and reload the rack.
Add an additional PCR test order, the sample display will remain white.
The system did not unschedule/remove the back-end tests when the front-end was invalidated. This is a downstream effect of defect 1 and does not need to be identified in the logs. Mainly we feel this shouldn’t be done as it is a waste of consumables.
Workaround
If the customer would like to re-process specimens which have been flagged during front-end processing, they must wait for the containing MTU to complete front-end processing. Unfortunately, there is no notification to the operator when this occurs so we recommend that they wait until the invalid PCR test order has completed processing.
Resolution
All defects will be fixed in a future software version. No target yet.
MKS
2045725
2078738
2078766
Log Entries
Reference #s:
- 174103 - DbID of front end that gets the VVFS flag
- 174104 - DbID of first SARS-CoV-2 PCR test
- 174252 - DbID of new SARS-CoV-2 test added through UI
Original front end fails on a sample dispense and gets a VVFS flag.
2020-05-12
18:54:23,783|[ProcessEvent]|StaticHelperMethods|ProcessManagement|Info|Normal|PipettorDispense Sample (ID=12311) samples= 174103/13307858A , MTU=19 MTU BarcodeID=1966464128 tube=3: LLD result=LldPositive LLD height=101 pressure signal result=OK second LLD result=NoLiquidDetected second LLD height=0
2020-05-12
18:54:23,970|[TOS]|TestOrderManager|OrderManagement|Info|Problem|<<TestOrderManager.OnAssignResultFlag: FlagEventArgs: Flag VVFS to 174103 , AreOrdersToRelease: False
Sample reloaded
2020-05-12
19:49:42,644|[LM]|BayManager|Loading|Info|Normal|Position=0, barcode=13307858A, read status=TubeBarcode
User attempted to add a new SARS-CoV-2 test
2020-05-12 19:49:53,666|[UI]|SubPageHost.xaml|PantherUI|Info|Normal|Show[151]: UI_Activity Modal dialog activated: GenProbe.Panther.UI.SubPages. AddTestRequestPage
2020-05-12 19:50:01,125|[85]|BaseService|UICommunication|Info|Normal|ReagentsSamplesService. AddTestOrders (NewTOR 118169, 13307858A ,F;, LDT-SARS-CoV-2 , 1, 1, False)
At this point the bad front end test is still riding around. It's status is pipetted but it's not part of a started MTU on the sidecar and consequently RadiumIC (in PcrTestOrderFactor.GetAvailablePCRFrontEndTestOrder) sees it as a front end that can be reused for the newly added test.
This is a defect—we should check for failing flags before attempting to piggy back on an in-process front end.
2020-05-12
19:50:01,173|[85]|PcrTestOrderFactory|SidecarOrderMan|Info|Normal|PcrTOF.CreateTestOrders: Found usable parent test 174103/Pippeted . Parent pcr tests = 1, new pcr test = 1, requested replicates 1
2020-05-12
19:50:01,173|[85]|PcrTestOrderFactory|SidecarOrderMan|Info|Normal|PcrTOF.CreateTestOrders: Will send request to add new replicates to the parent test 174103. Parent pcr tests = 1, new pcr test = 1, requested replicates 1
Then we add the replicate and copy the pipetting time from the parent (in SidecarTestOrderManager.ProcessNewReplicateRequests).
2020-05-12
19:50:01,838|[TOS]|SidecarTestOrderManager|SidecarOrderMan|Info|Normal|~~SCTOM.ProcessNewReplicateRequests: Received request to add new PCR test 174252 to parent 174103
UI gets the notifications that the sample has updated and correctly excludes the old test order. However, it also excludes the new test orders because it doesn't think it’s from the current load of the sample (with SampleViewItem.LoadTestOrders calling IsFromCurrentLoad). It's looking at that copied pipetting time and sees that it's earlier than when the sample was loaded. This is a defect.
2020-05-12
19:50:04,110|[UI]|SampleViewItem|PantherUI|Info|Normal|LoadTestOrders[2217]: TO excluded : sampleID=13307858A LoadTime=05/13/2020 00:49:42 : testorder Assay=LDT-SARS-CoV-2, Status=Pippeted, PipettingTime=05/12/2020 23:54:13, CompletionTime=05/13/2020 02:13:17
2020-05-12

2020-05-12
19:50:04,110|[UI]|SampleViewItem|PantherUI|Info|Normal|LogTestOrderCounts[2520]: dbID=118169 SampleID=13307858A Pending=0 [TMA:0/PCR:0] Scheduled=0 InProcess=0 Completed=0 Error=0 Reflex=0 Total=0 - pipettingErrorReported=False

## Troubleshooting with Service Software
id="mc-main-content">
Troubleshooting with Service Software
This topic describes commands, data, and options available in Panther's Service Software.
-
When using Service Software Tool, Universal fluid usage is not tracked.
-
Recommendations:
Use a different set of Universal Fluids when priming and/or dispensing during Service Software Tool usage. Load original Universal Fluids when returning Panther Instrument to customer.
or
Use customer’s current loaded Universal Fluids when priming and/or dispensing during Service Software Tool usage BUT load a new set of Universal Fluids when returning Panther instrument to customer.
-
Service software – firmware version and sensors should be able to be read without initializing the module.

The FSE Password Login dialog box appears.

!G9x53rvic3y

Click OK .
The PANTHER FSE Shield appears.

Each tab has a Main and a Parameter subtab. Some tabs also have Move, Sub-Module, Teach, and Error Memory subtabs:
Main – Main control for that module:
Move – Opens control screen for that module movements.
Sub Module – Additional control screen for modules with multiple sub modules.
Parameter – Will display individual module firmware version.
Teach – Allows manual teaching of mid-bay modules.
Error Memory – Not used unless specified in technical bulletins.
1. Distributor – Main Tab – Initialize
Each Main screen has a Common Control located in this area. There are three icons:
Initialize – All modules that interact with the selected module tab, Complete System – All modules, Individual Modules – Entire module or sub-module.
Get Module Firmware – will display individual module firmware version.
Get Module Status – will display individual module status.
NOTE: If there are multiple modules, a select Device section will be to the right of the Common Control.

Linear Distributor – Move Tab
-
Distributor Single Movement to – Single click will move the Linear Distributor to that location. Double clicking will make the Linear Distributor load or unload an MTU.
-
Next MTU Action – Displays LD MTU presence state to determine what the distributor will do with the single movement command (Pick/ Place). Pick: indicates empty LD. Place: indicates MTU present. Unknown: LD is not initialized. Next MTU action changes depending on current state. If MTU is present in LD, it will place. If no MTU is in LD, it will pick.
-
Luminometer – [Open] [Close] Opens or Closes the Luminometer door.
-
Input Queue – [Unlock Drawer] Unlocks MTU drawer. [Push MTU] Advances MTU pusher.
-
Output Queue – Dispose MTU - Aspirate and dispose of all MTUs in the Output Queue. (vacuum pump needs to be turned on for the aspiration to work).
-
Distributor Repetition Movement - Available Positions – All the positions the distributor can move to.
-
Movement List – Lists positions in the order that the distributor will move to. Action indicates – shows if position will be performed once or twice (this column will be blank, x or xx).
-
Add Pos. – [>>] moves highlighted selection from available positions to the movement list.
-
Action
[None] Will perform only x/z/theta action. No hook movement, e.g., no picking or placing.
[Once X] – Will perform the Next MTU Action once per cycle.Twice XX – Will perform the Next MTU Action twice.
[Twice XX] – Will perform two Next MTU Actions. For example, if action is set to “XX” and there MTU is present in LD, next MTU Action indicating ‘place’ upon execute, the LD will place MTU in position, then pick MTU back in LD.
-
Item – [Up][Down] Moves the Delete – Removes selected position from the list.highlighted position in movement list up or down [Delete] removes selected position from the list.
-
MTU Barcode – Checkbox enables scanning MTU barcode.
-
Execute – Starts the cycle and will move the distributor to all of the selected positions in the movement list repetitively until stopped or cancelled. Clear List clears all positions from the Movement List.
